body.text: Abhidharmasamuccayabhāṣyam
body.translated_text: <s>Abhidharmasamuccayabhāṣya</s> (Commentary on the Compendium of Higher Doctrine)

body.text: I [lakṣaṇasamuccayo nāma prathamaḥ samuccayaḥ]
body.translated_text: I. [The First Compendium, entitled the Compendium of Characteristics (<s>Lakṣaṇasamuccaya</s>)]

body.text: oṃ namo ratnatrayāya /
body.translated_text: Oṃ, homage to the Three Jewels.

body.text: kimarthamidaṃ śāstramārabdham / skandhādīnārabhya kati kasmādityevamādiṣu cintāsthāneṣu kauśalyakaraṇārtham / tathāhyanena kauśalyena dvividho 'nuśaṃso labhyate - manaskārānuśaṃsaṃḥ sāṃkathyaviniścayānuśaṃsaśca / tatra manaskārānuśaṃsaḥ śamathānukūlyādvipaśyanāvṛddhayānukūlyācca veditavyaḥ / śamathānukūlyaṃ punareṣu sthāneṣu kṛtakauśalasya niḥsaṃdehatayā yatheṣṭamālaṃbane aikāgrayayogena sukhaṃ cittasamādhānataḥ / vipaśyanāvṛddhayānu kūlyaṃ bahubhiḥ prakāraiḥ jñeyaparīkṣayā prajñāprakarṣagamanataḥ / sāṃkathyaviniścayānuśaṃsa eṣu sthāneṣu kuśalasya sarvapraśnavyākaraṇaśaktiyogādvaiśāradyapratilaṃbhato draṣṭavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: For what purpose was this treatise undertaken? For the purpose of producing skill in such areas of investigation as: beginning with the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) and so forth, how many are there, why, and so on. For indeed, through such skill, a twofold benefit is obtained: the benefit of mental attention (<s>manaskāra</s>) and the benefit of the resolution of discussions (<s>sāṃkathyaviniścaya</s>). Therein, the benefit of mental attention should be understood as being conducive to <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and conducive to the growth of <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight). Conduciveness to <s>śamatha</s> means that for one who has gained skill in these topics, being free from doubt, there is ease of mental concentration (<s>samādhi</s>) through one-pointed application to any object of one's choice. Conduciveness to the growth of <s>vipaśyanā</s> means the attainment of excellence in <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) through examining the knowable in many ways. The benefit of the resolution of discussions should be seen in one who is skilled in these topics obtaining confidence (<s>vaiśāradya</s>) through the capacity to answer all questions.

body.text: pañcākārātmavastūdbhāvanatāmupādāyetyatracaturākāramātmano vastvityātmavastu / pañcamaṃ tvātmalakṣaṇameva vastvityātmavastviti veditavyam / saparigrahadehagrahaṇena bāhyasyādhyātmikasya ca rūpaskandhasya grahaṇaṃ veditavyam / vedanādīnāmupabhogāditvaṃ tallakṣaṇanirdeśe jñāpayiṣyate / tadāśrayātmasvavastu vijñānam, teṣāṃ saparigrahadehādīnāmāśrayamātmalakṣaṇaṃ vastvityarthaḥ / tathāhi loke prāyeṇa vijñāne ātmagrāhaḥ, śeṣeṣvātmīyagrāha iti //
body.translated_text: 'By way of bringing about the self-entity (<s>ātmavastu</s>) in five aspects' — here, 'the entity of the self in four aspects' means <s>ātmavastu</s>; but the fifth, the characteristic of the self itself is the entity, and should be understood as <s>ātmavastu</s>. By the term 'body with its possessions' (<s>saparigrahadeha</s>), one should understand the grasping of the <s>rūpaskandha</s> (form aggregate), both external and internal. The nature of <s>vedanā</s> (feeling) and others as enjoyment and so forth will be indicated in the exposition of their characteristics. <s>Vijñāna</s> (consciousness) is the entity of the self as their support; the meaning is that the self-characteristic which is the support of the body with its possessions and so forth is the entity. For indeed, in the world, the grasping of self (<s>ātmagrāha</s>) generally pertains to consciousness, while the grasping of 'mine' (<s>ātmīyagrāha</s>) pertains to the rest.

body.text: dehaparigrahābhyāmiti cakṣu[rādī] ndriyaṣaṭkena rūpādiviṣayaṣaṭkena ca / ṣaḍākāro 'tīto vartamānaścopabhogo vijñānaṣaṭkam, tasya dhāraṇamāśrayālaṃbana bhāvataḥ / ityevaṃ taddhā raṇatvena dvādaśānāmindriyaviṣayāṇāṃ dhātutvam /
body.translated_text: 'By the body and its possessions' means by the group of six sense-faculties beginning with the eye and by the group of six objects beginning with form. The six-fold past and present enjoyment is the group of six <s>vijñānas</s> (consciousnesses); their maintenance is through being their support and object. Thus, the <s>dhātu</s>-nature of the twelve sense-faculties and objects is by way of their being the maintainers of that. The

body.text: vijñānānāṃ punarupabhogalakṣaṇa dhāraṇatvena dhātutvaṃ veditavyam / yathātītapratyutpannāḥ cakṣurādaya upabhogalakṣaṇadhārakā naivamanāgatāḥ - 2 //
body.translated_text: <s>dhātu</s>-nature of the <s>vijñānas</s> (consciousnesses) should be understood as maintaining them through the characteristic of enjoyment. Just as past and present eyes and so forth are maintainers of the characteristic of enjoyment, so too the future ones are not [currently maintaining] — 2.

body.text: āyadvāramātratvādindriyārthamātragrahaṇena dvādaśaivāyatanāni vyavasthā pitāni, na tūpabhogalakṣaṇaṃ vijñānaṣaṭkamiti //
body.translated_text: Because they are merely doors of approach and so forth, by grasping only the sense-faculties and objects, only twelve <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases) are established, and not the six groups of consciousness characterized by enjoyment.

body.text: upādānaṃ chando rāgaśca / tatra chando 'bhilāṣaḥ, rāgo 'dhyavasānam / chandenānāgatamātmabhāvamabhilāṣamukhenopādatte, yenānāgatān skandhānabhinirvarttayati / rāgena vartamānamātmabhāvamadhyavasānamukhenopādatte, yena vartamānān skandhānna parityajati / tasmādetadeva dvayamupādānamityucyate / tatra skandhavannirdeśa iti / upādānena yuktāstasmātsopādānadharmā iti veditavyam //
body.translated_text: <s>Upādāna</s> (clinging) consists of desire (<s>chanda</s>) and attachment (<s>rāga</s>). Therein, <s>chanda</s> is longing, and <s>rāga</s> is resolution. Through desire, one clings to the future self-existence through the mode of longing, by which one produces future <s>skandhas</s>. Through attachment, one clings to the present self-existence through the mode of resolution, by which one does not abandon the present <s>skandhas</s>. Therefore, it is precisely this pair that is called <s>upādāna</s> (clinging). The expression 'like the <s>skandhas</s>' therein means: they are conjoined with <s>upādāna</s>, hence they should be understood as <s>sopādāna dharmas</s> (phenomena with clinging).

body.text: sparśena rūpāṇāmanyathībhāvo veditavyaḥ / yā deśe ityabhi mukhapradeśe / idaṃ cedaṃ cetyasthiśaṃkalādikaṃ jñeyavastusabhāgaṃ pratibimbam / evaṃ caivaṃ ceti varṇasaṃsthānabhedaiḥ citrīkārateti tathāsaṃjñā / śubhānāṃ karmaṇāṃ sukho 'nubhavaḥ phalavipākaḥ / aśubhānāṃ duḥkhaḥ / ubhayeṣāmaduḥkhāsukhaḥ / tathāhi śubhānāmaśubhānāṃ vā vipāka ālayavijñānaṃ nityamupekṣayaiva saṃprayuktaṃ bhavati / saiva cātropekṣā vipākaḥ / sukhaduḥkhayostu vipākajatvādvipākopacāraḥ / dṛṣṭaśrutatamavijñātānarthāniti dṛṣṭaṃ yacca kṣuṣānubhūtam, śrutaṃ yacchrotreṇānubhūtam, mataṃ yatsvayamabhyūhitamevaṃ caivaṃ ca bhavitavyamiti, vijñātaṃ yatpratyātmamanubhūtamiti / vyavaharatītyabhilāpaiḥ prāpa[ya]tītyarthaḥ // nānāvasthāsu ceti sukhaduḥkhādyāsu //
body.translated_text: By contact, the alteration of material forms is to be understood. 'In a certain place' means in the region directly in front. 'This and this' — such as bones and chains, etc. — is a reflected image resembling the object to be known. 'In such and such ways' means that it is variegated through differences of color and shape; hence it is called such (<s>saṃjñā</s>). The pleasant experience of wholesome <s>karmas</s> is the fruition result (<s>phalavipāka</s>); of unwholesome ones, it is painful; of both (mixed), it is neither-painful-nor-pleasant. For indeed, the fruition of wholesome or unwholesome actions is the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (storehouse consciousness), which is always associated with equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>) alone. And that very equanimity here is the fruition. But pleasure and pain, being produced from fruition, are figuratively called fruition. 'Objects that are seen, heard, thought, and cognized' — 'seen' is what is experienced through the eye; 'heard' is what is experienced through the ear; 'thought' (<s>mata</s>) is what one has inferred by oneself, thinking 'it must be thus and thus'; 'cognized' is what is experienced in one's own personal experience. 'Engages in' means communicates through verbal expressions. 'In various conditions' means in conditions of pleasure, pain, and so forth.

body.text: yena cakṣuṣā rūpāṇi dṛṣṭavānityatītavijñānopabhogadhārakatvena dhātutva darśayati / paśyatīti vartamānavijñānopabhogadhārakatvena / yacca tasya cakṣuṣo bījamupacitamālayavijñānaṃ yata āyatyāṃ cakṣunirvartiṣyate, vaipākyaṃ ca yato nirvṛttam, tadapi dvividhaṃ bījaṃ cakṣurdhāturityucyate, cakṣuṣo hetutvāt / yaccakṣurdhātoḥ rūpe ādhipatyamiti rūpīndriyādhipatyena bāhyaviṣayanirvartanāt /
body.translated_text: 'By which eye one has seen forms' — this shows the <s>dhātu</s>-nature through being the maintainer of the enjoyment of past consciousness. 'Sees' shows it through being the maintainer of the enjoyment of present consciousness. And that seed which has been accumulated in the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (storehouse consciousness) as the seed of that eye, from which the eye will be produced in the future, and the fruition from which it was produced — that twofold seed too is called the eye-element (<s>cakṣurdhātu</s>), because it is the cause of the eye. 'The eye-element's sovereignty over form' means that through the sovereignty of the material sense-faculty, external objects are produced.

body.text: taddhātuvaddraṣṭavyaṃ tacca yathāyogamiti yena cakṣuṣā rūpāṇi drakṣyati yacca tadbījamityevamādi yojayitavyam //
body.translated_text: 'It should be seen like that element' and 'in the appropriate manner' — 'by which eye one will see forms' and 'that which is its seed' — thus should one connect the meaning.

body.text: catvāri ca mahābhūtānyupādāyeti / kathamupādāyarūpam / catvāri mahābhūtānyupādāya jananasaṃniśrayapratiṣṭhopastaṃbhopabṛṃhaṇahetutvena / jananādi hetutvaṃ punarbhūtānāmupādāyarūpe pañcavidhaṃ hetutvamadhikṛtya / utpattihetutvaṃ tairvinā tadanutpatteḥ / vṛttihetutvaṃ bhūtāni pratyākhyāyopādāyarūpasya pṛthagdeśāvaṣṭambhasāmarthyābhāvāt / anuvṛttihetutvaṃ bhūtavikāreṇa tatpratiṣṭhitopādāyarūpavikriyāgamanāt / sthitihetutvaṃ sadṛśotpattikāle bhūtairupādāyarūpasaṃtānasyānupacchedayogena saṃdhāraṇāt / upacayahetutvaṃ vṛttikāle bhūtairūpādāyarūpāpyāyanāditi /
body.translated_text: 'Having taken up the four great elements' — how is derived form (<s>upādāyarūpa</s>) so called? It is because the four great elements are taken up as causes of generation, support, foundation, sustenance, and nourishment. The five-fold causality of the elements in relation to derived form is as follows: the causality of generation, because without them it does not arise; the causality of maintenance, because without the elements, derived form lacks the capacity to occupy a separate location; the causality of continuance, because through the transformation of the elements, the derived form established upon them undergoes transformation; the causality of stability, because at the time of similar arising, by the elements maintaining the continuum of derived form without interruption; the causality of augmentation, because at the time of maintenance, the elements nourish the derived form.

body.text: nīlādīnāṃ pañcaviṃśatīnāṃ rūpāṇāṃ vyavasthānaṃ ṣaḍbhirākārairveditavyam / lakṣaṇataḥ saṃniveśato 'nugrahopaghātataḥ kriyāsaṃniśrayataḥ kriyālakṣaṇataḥ maṇḍanataśca caturṇā daśānāmaṣṭānāmekaikasya ca yathākramam / tatrābhyavakāśastadanyaprativārakaspraṣṭavyarahito yo deśaḥ / nabho yadupariṣṭānnīlaṃ dṛśyate //
body.translated_text: The establishment of the twenty-five forms beginning with blue should be understood through six aspects: through their characteristics, arrangement, benefit and harm, dependence on action, characteristics of action, and adornment — respectively for the groups of four, ten, eight, and one each, in order. Therein, space (<s>ābhyavakāśa</s>) is that place which is free from obstruction by anything else and from tangible contact. The sky (<s>nabhas</s>) is that which appears blue above.

body.text: śabdavyavasthānaṃ lakṣaṇato 'nugrahopaghātataḥ hetuprabhedato deśanāprabhedato vyavahāraprabhedataśca / lakṣaṇataḥ śrotrendriyagrāhyo yo 'rtha iti / deśanāprabhedato lokaprasiddhādayastrayaḥ / śeṣaṃ yathāyogaṃ veditavyam / tatropāttamahābhūtahetukastadyathā vākchabdaḥ / anupāttamahābhūtahetukastadyathā vṛkṣaśabdaḥ / tadubhayastadyathā hastamṛdaṅgaśabdaḥ / lokaprasiddho laukikabhāṣāsaṃgṛhītaḥ / siddhopanīta āryerdeśitaḥ / parikalpitastīrthyerdeśitaḥ / āryānāryavyāvahārikau tudṛṣṭādīnaṣṭau vyavahārānadhikṛtya veditavyau //
body.translated_text: The establishment of sound should be understood through its characteristics, through benefit and harm, through classification of causes, through classification of teaching, and through classification of usage. Through characteristics: it is the object grasped by the ear faculty. Through classification of teaching: three types, beginning with what is commonly known in the world. The rest should be understood as appropriate. Therein, sound caused by great elements that are appropriated (by sentient beings) — for example, vocal sound. Sound caused by great elements that are not appropriated — for example, the sound of a tree. Sound caused by both — for example, the sound of a hand-drum. Commonly known in the world means included in ordinary worldly language. Introduced by the accomplished means taught by the Noble Ones (<s>āryas</s>). Fabricated means taught by heretics (<s>tīrthyas</s>). The conventional usages of the Noble Ones and non-Noble Ones should be understood with reference to the eight kinds of usage beginning with 'seen' and so forth.

body.text: gandhavyavasthānaṃ svalakṣaṇato 'nugrahopaghātataḥ prabhedataśca // rasavyavasthānamapyevameva veditavyam // tatra sahajo gandhaścandanādonām, sāṃyogiko dhūpayuktyadīnām, pāriṇāmikaḥ pakvaphalādīnāmiti /
body.translated_text: The establishment of smell should be understood through its own characteristic, through benefit and harm, and through classification. The establishment of taste should also be understood in the same way. Therein, natural smell is that of sandalwood and such things; compound smell is that of mixtures with incense and the like; transformed smell is that of ripened fruits and such.

body.text: spraṣṭavyaikadeśavyavasthānamāmarśanata ātulanataḥ sparśanata āpīḍanataḥ saṃsargato dhātuvaiṣamyasāmyataśca / abvāyusaṃsargācchītam /
body.translated_text: The establishment of certain tangible objects should be understood through touching, through weighing, through tactile contact, through pressure, through combination, and through the imbalance and balance of the bodily constituents (<s>dhātus</s>). Coldness arises from the combination of water and wind.

body.text: appṛthavīsaṃsargātpicchalam / viśrāmo balamūrjā ca dhātusāmyāt / ūrjā punarvaiśāradyaṃ veditavyam / tṛptirubhayathā / śeṣā jighatsādayo dhātuvaiṣamyādveditavyāḥ //
body.translated_text: Sliminess arises from the combination of water and earth. Rest, strength, and energy arise from the balance of the constituents. Energy should be understood as confidence. Satiation is of both kinds (physical and mental). The remaining ones, beginning with hunger, should be understood as arising from the imbalance of the constituents.

body.text: ābhisāṃkṣepikaṃ paramāṇurūpam / ābhyavakāśikaṃ tadeva yathoktaṃ tadanyaprativārakaspraṣṭavyarahitam / sāmādānikamavijñaptirūpam / parikalpitaṃ pratibimbarūpam / vaibhūtvikaṃ vimokṣadhyāyigocaraṃ yadrūpam /
body.translated_text: The comprehensive form is atomic form (<s>paramāṇurūpa</s>). The spatial form is the same as described — that which is free from obstruction by anything else and from tangible contact. The undertaking form is <s>avijñaptirūpa</s> (non-informative form). The imagined form is reflected form (<s>pratibimbarūpa</s>). The form produced by supernatural power is that form which is the object of those who meditate on liberation (<s>vimokṣa</s>).

body.text: vedanāskandhavyavasthānamāśrayataḥ svabhāvata āśrayasaṃkalanataḥ saṃkleśavyavadānataśca / tatra rūpāśrayasaṃkalanataḥ kāyikīvedanāvyavasthānam / arūpyāśrayasaṃkalanataścaitasikīvedanāvyavasthānam / saṃkleśataḥ sāmiṣādīnām, vyavadānato nirāmiṣādīnāṃ vyavasthānaṃ veditavyam / tattṛṣṇāviyukteti visaṃyuktā visaṃyogyānukūlā ca veditavyā //
body.translated_text: The establishment of the <s>vedanāskandha</s> (feeling aggregate) should be understood through its basis, through its intrinsic nature, through the combination of its bases, and through defilement and purification. Therein, the establishment of bodily feeling is through the combination with the material basis. The establishment of mental feeling is through the combination with the immaterial basis. Defilement pertains to feelings with bait (<s>sāmiṣa</s>) and so forth; purification pertains to those without bait (<s>nirāmiṣa</s>) and so forth. 'Separated from craving' should be understood as dissociated from craving and conducive to dissociation from craving.

body.text: avyavahārakuśalasyāśikṣitabhāṣatayā rūpe saṃjñā bhavati na tu rūpamiti / tasmādanimittasaṃjñetyucyate / animittadhātusamāpannasya rūpādisarvanimittāpagate 'nimitte nirvāṇe saṃjñānimittasaṃjñā / bhavāgrasamāpannasyāpaṭutvenālaṃbanānimittīkaraṇādanimittasaṃjñā / parīttaḥ kāmadhātuḥ nikṛṣṭa tvāt / mahadgato rūpadhātustata utkṛṣṭatvāt / apramāṇe ākāśa vijñānānantyāyatane 'paryantatvāt / tasmāttadālaṃbanāḥ saṃjñāḥ parīttādisaṃjñā veditavyāḥ /
body.translated_text: For one who is not skilled in conventional usage, through untrained speech, there arises a perception of form, but not 'this is form.' Therefore it is called signless perception (<s>animittasaṃjñā</s>). For one who has attained the signless element, the perception of the sign of <s>nirvāṇa</s>, which is devoid of all signs such as form, is perception of the signless (<s>animittasaṃjñā</s>). For one who has attained the summit of existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>), because of the inability to clearly apprehend the object due to dullness, it is signless perception. The limited (<s>parītta</s>) is the <s>kāmadhātu</s> (desire realm), because of its inferior nature. The extensive (<s>mahadgata</s>) is the <s>rūpadhātu</s> (form realm), because it is superior to that. The immeasurable (<s>apramāṇa</s>) applies to the spheres of infinite space and infinite consciousness, because of their boundlessness. Therefore, the perceptions related to those objects should be understood as limited perception and so forth.

body.text: vedanāsaṃjñāvarjyānāṃ sarveṣāṃ caitasikānāṃ cittaviprayuktānāṃ ca saṃskāraskandhalakṣaṇatve cetanāmātrasyaiva tannidaśe grahaṇaṃ tatpūrvakatvāditareṣāmiti kāraṇajñāpanārthamāha - yayā kuśalatvāya cetayata ityevamādi / tatra kuśalā vakṣyamāṇāḥ śraddhādayaḥ / saṃkleśā rāgādayaḥ kleśopakleśāḥ / avasthābhedataḥ cetanāpreritasaṃskārāvasyāsu prajñaptāḥ cittaviprayuktāḥ saṃskārāḥ //
body.translated_text: The characteristic of the <s>saṃskāraskandha</s> (formation aggregate) is all mental factors (<s>caitasikas</s>) except <s>vedanā</s> (feeling) and <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), as well as the factors dissociated from mind (<s>cittaviprayukta</s>). Among these, in the indication of this aggregate, only <s>cetanā</s> (volition) is mentioned, to convey the reason that the others are preceded by it. Hence it says: 'by which one wills toward the wholesome' and so forth. Therein, wholesome factors are the forthcoming ones such as faith (<s>śraddhā</s>). Defiled factors are the afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>) and secondary afflictions (<s>upakleśas</s>) such as attachment (<s>rāga</s>). Through differences of states, the <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) impelled by <s>cetanā</s> and designated in various states are the <s>cittaviprayukta saṃskāras</s> (formations dissociated from mind).

body.text: cetanādīnāṃ caitasikānāṃ lakṣaṇataḥ karmataśca nirdeśo veditavyaḥ / tatra cetanāyāḥ cittābhisaṃskāro manaskarmeti lakṣaṇanirdeśaḥ / kuśalākuśalāvyākṛteṣu cittapreraṇakarmiketi karmanirdeśaḥ / tathāhi
body.translated_text: The exposition of mental factors (<s>caitasikas</s>) beginning with <s>cetanā</s> (volition) should be understood through their characteristics and functions. Therein, the characteristic-exposition of <s>cetanā</s> is: mental construction (<s>cittābhisaṃskāra</s>), which is mental action (<s>manaskarma</s>). Its function-exposition is: it has the function of impelling the mind toward the wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate. For indeed,

body.text: yathābhisaṃskāraṃ kuśalādiṣu dharmeṣu cittasya pravṛttirbhavatīti / ālaṃbane cittadhāraṇaṃ tatraiva punaḥ punarāvarjanaṃ veditavyam / ata eva samādhilābhī mana(ḥ) saṃskāralābhītyucyate / vijñānotpattāvindriyasya sukhādivedanotpattyanukūlo yo vikārastadākāraḥ sparśo veditavyaḥ / tattadupasaṃhitā kartukāmateti darśanaśravaṇādisarvakriyecchāsaṃgrahārtham / yathāniścayaṃ dhāraṇā evametannānyathetyadhimuktiḥ / ata eva tatpradhāno 'nyaiḥ saṃhartu na śakyate saṃstutaṃ vastu pūrvānubhūtaṃ veditavyam / avikṣepakarmikatvaṃ punaḥ smṛterālaṃbanābhilapane sati cittāvikṣepatāmupādāya / cittasyaikāgratāvikṣepaḥ / jñānasaṃniśrayadānaṃ samāhitacittasya yathābhūtajñānāt / saṃśayavyāvartanaṃ prajñayā dharmān pravicinvato niścayalābhāt / astitve 'bhisaṃpratyayākārā śraddhā / guṇatve prasādākārā / śakyatve 'bhilāṣākārā, śakyaṃ mayā prāptuṃ niṣpādayituṃ veti / hryādayaḥ sugamatvānna vibhajyante / upapattiprātilambhikaṃ śrutacintāmayaṃ bhāvanāmayaṃ ca yathākramaṃ vipākāgamādhigamarūpaṃ veditavyam / pratisaṃkhyāprajñā dhairyasahitā / sthāmavānvīryavānutsāhī dṛḍhaparākramo 'nikṣiptadhuraḥ kuśaleṣu dharmeṣvityevamādisūtrapadāni yathākramaṃ saṃnāhādiṣvabhyutsāhavastuṣu yojayitavyāni / paripūraṇaṃ yathā maulaṃ praveśaḥ / niṣpādanaṃ tasyaiva suparikarmakṛtatvam / sarvāvaraṇaniṣkarṣaṇaṃ tadvaśenāśrayaparivṛttito draṣṭavyam / sarvakuśalabhāvanāyā vīryādipūrvakatvātteṣvapramādaprajñapti / sāsravā dharmā āsravā āsravasthānīyāśca viṣayā iha veditavyāḥ / cittasamatādibhirupekṣāyā ādimadhyāvasānāvasthā vyākhyātāḥ / tathāhyupekṣayā yuktaṃ cittaṃ layādiveṣamyābhāvādāditaḥ samam / tato 'nabhisaṃskāreṇa vahanātpraśaṭham / tataḥ saṃkleśāśaṅkābhāvādanābhogāvasthitamiti / a vihiṃsā pyadveṣāvyatirekāt prajñaptisatī veditavyā / duḥkhasaṃjananakarmaka iti tṛṣṇāvaśena pañcopādānaskandha nirvartanāt / asparśavihāra āghātacittasya duḥkhavihārāt / agauravaṃ guruṣu guṇavatsu ca stabdhatā / duḥkhotpattiḥ
body.translated_text: the mind's engagement in wholesome and other <s>dharmas</s> occurs according to mental construction. Holding the mind on the object means directing it again and again to that very thing. Hence one who has obtained <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) is said to have obtained mental formation. Contact (<s>sparśa</s>) should be understood as the transformation that is conducive to the arising of feelings such as pleasure in the sense-faculty upon the arising of consciousness, and its aspect. 'Desire to do what is associated with this and that' is for the purpose of including all desires for action such as seeing, hearing, and so forth. Conviction (<s>adhimukti</s>) is holding according to one's determination: 'it is exactly thus and not otherwise.' Hence what is principally characterized by that cannot be shaken by others — the remembered thing should be understood as previously experienced. The function of non-distraction of <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) is: when there is the naming of an object, taking up the non-distraction of the mind. One-pointedness of mind is non-distraction (<s>avikṣepa</s>). Giving the support of knowledge means: from the as-it-is knowledge of one whose mind is concentrated. The removal of doubt is: from gaining certainty when one discriminates <s>dharmas</s> through <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom). Faith (<s>śraddhā</s>) has the aspect of conviction in existence; the aspect of clarity in regard to qualities; the aspect of aspiration in regard to capacity — 'I can attain it, I can accomplish it.' <s>Hrī</s> (self-respect) and others are not analyzed because of their easy comprehensibility. That which is obtained by birth, that which arises from hearing and reflection, and that which arises from meditation — these should be understood respectively as having the nature of fruition, learning, and realization. Reflective wisdom with steadfastness. One who is strong is vigorous, enthusiastic, of firm exertion, one who does not cast off the burden in wholesome <s>dharmas</s> — such sūtra passages should be connected in order with the objects of enthusiasm beginning with the armor and so forth. Fulfillment is like the root — the entrance. Accomplishment is its being well-prepared. The extraction of all obstructions is to be seen through the transformation of the basis (<s>āśrayaparivṛtti</s>) by its power. Because all wholesome cultivation is preceded by vigor and so forth, <s>apramāda</s> (non-heedlessness) is designated in regard to these. <s>Sāsrava dharmas</s> (phenomena with outflows) — the outflows and what serves as the basis for outflows, and objects, should be understood here. Through the equality of mind and so forth, the initial, middle, and final stages of <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity) are explained. For indeed, the mind engaged in equanimity is initially even (<s>sama</s>) due to the absence of imbalance from torpor and the like; then flowing (<s>praśaṭha</s>) because it flows without fabrication; then abiding without effort (<s>anābhoga</s>) because there is no apprehension of defilement. <s>Avihiṃsā</s> (non-harming) should be understood as a designation that is not separate from non-hatred (<s>adveṣa</s>). Its function of generating suffering means: through the force of craving, one produces the five aggregates of clinging. Discomfort of abode is: from the painful abiding of an angry mind. Disrespect is rigidity toward teachers and those possessing qualities. The arising of suffering

body.text: punarbhavotpattirvedi tavyā / mithyāniścayairviparītaṃ jñānam / vicikitsā saṃśayaḥ / saṃkleśotpattiḥ rāgādikleśasamudācāraḥ / tatsaṃniśrayadānaṃ mūḍhasya sarvakleśapravṛtteriti / ratneṣu vimatirmārgasatye nirodhasatye ca yathāyogam / tayā kuśalapakṣe 'pravṛttiralabdhaniścayasyānārambhāt //
body.translated_text: should be understood as the arising of renewed existence (<s>punarbhava</s>). Wrong knowledge is knowledge that is inverted through wrong determinations. <s>Vicikitsā</s> is doubt. The arising of defilement is the occurrence of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) such as attachment and so forth. The giving of their support means: because all afflictions operate in one who is deluded. Doubt regarding the jewels pertains to the truth of the path and the truth of cessation, as appropriate. Through that, there is non-engagement in the wholesome side, because one who has not gained certainty does not undertake action.

body.text: madhyamā pratipacchāśvatocchedagrāhavarjitaṃ pratītyasamutpādajñānam / śīlavrataṃ kudṛṣṭipūrvakaṃ veditavyama / śramavaiphalyaṃ tenāniryāṇāt / nāsti dattaṃ nāstīṣṭaṃ nāsti kṛtaṃ nāsti sucaritaṃ nāsti duścaritamityayaṃ hetvapavādaḥ / nāsti duścaritasucaritānāṃ karmaṇāṃ phalavipāka iti phalāpavādaḥ / nāstyayaṃ loko nāsti paraloko nāsti mātā nāsti pitā nāsti sattva upapāduka iti kriyāpavādaḥ, lokāntaragamanāgamanakriyāyā bījādhānakriyāyāḥ pratisaṃdhibandhakriyāyāścāpavādāt / na santi loke 'rhanta ityevamādi sadvastunāśanam / tadanyadyat kiṃcidviparītadarśanaṃ tanmithyāparikalpanaṃ veditavyam / kuśalamūlasamucchedo viśiṣṭāyā eva mithyādṛṣṭerna sarvasyāḥ /
body.translated_text: The middle path (<s>madhyamā pratipad</s>) is the knowledge of dependent arising (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>), free from the grasping of eternalism and annihilationism. Clinging to rites and vows (<s>śīlavrata</s>) should be understood as preceded by wrong views. The futility of effort is because there is no liberation through it. 'There is nothing given, nothing offered, nothing done, no good conduct, no bad conduct' — this is the denial of causes (<s>hetvapavāda</s>). 'There is no fruition result of actions of good and bad conduct' — this is the denial of results (<s>phalāpavāda</s>). 'There is no this world, no other world, no mother, no father, no spontaneously born beings' — this is the denial of action (<s>kriyāpavāda</s>), because it denies the action of going to and coming from other worlds, the action of planting seeds [of karma], and the action of establishing a new rebirth-connection (<s>pratisaṃdhi</s>). 'There are no <s>Arhats</s> in the world' and so forth — this is the destruction of existing things. Whatever other inverted views there may be, those should be understood as wrong conceptualization (<s>mithyāparikalpanā</s>). The cutting off of wholesome roots pertains only to the distinguished wrong view, not to all [wrong views].

body.text: pañcaskandhātmake jñeye ātmātmīyasvabhāvasamāropikā satkāyadṛṣṭiḥ / ātmanityānityaviśeṣasamāropikāntagrāhadṛṣṭiḥ / kudṛṣṭāvagratā samāropako dṛṣṭiparāmarśaḥ / tatraiva śuddhisamāropakaḥ śīlavrataparāmarśaḥ / ekā yadbhūyaseti mithyāvikalpikā yā nāvaśyamapavādikatvāt / lakṣaṇato dvābhyāmantagrāhamithyādṛṣṭibhyām, saparivārataḥ sarvābhyaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> (view of the perishable body) is that which superimposes the nature of self (<s>ātman</s>) and what belongs to self (<s>ātmīya</s>) upon the knowable that consists of the five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates). <s>Antagrāhadṛṣṭi</s> (extreme view) superimposes the distinctions of the self as permanent or impermanent. <s>Dṛṣṭiparāmarśa</s> (clinging to views) superimposes primacy upon wrong views. <s>Śīlavrataparāmarśa</s> (clinging to rites and vows) superimposes purification upon those very [wrong views]. One [view], being predominant, involves wrong conceptualization but is not necessarily denialist — [this is] because [wrong view] is not invariably of the denialist type. By their characteristics, [the cutting off of wholesome roots is] through two — extreme view and wrong view; with their retinue, through all [five views].

body.text: rūpādayo nātmā, tadvilakṣaṇatvāt na hi te ātmalakṣaṇā iti / na teṣvātmā, anityatādoṣāt / na hyāśrayābhāve āśritaṃ bhavatīti / na rūpavānātmā, asvātantryadoṣaprasaṅgāt / na tebhyo 'nyatrātmā, nirdehatādoṣāt / na hi vinā dehenā tmaparikalpa upalabhyata iti / asvātantryatādoṣaḥ teṣvavaśavartanāt / athaivaṃvidhamātmānaṃ
body.translated_text: Form and the rest are not the self, because they have different characteristics — for they do not have the characteristics of the self. Nor is the self in them, because of the fault of impermanence — for when the support is absent, the supported cannot exist. Nor is the self the possessor of form, because of the consequent fault of lack of independence. Nor is the self elsewhere than them, because of the fault of bodilessness — for without a body, the conceptualization of self is not observed. The fault of lack of independence is because [the self would be] subject to the power of those [aggregates]. Now, if someone were to conceptualize such a self

body.text: kaścitparikalpayet tathāpi nopapadyate 'rūpādika ātmā, ayatnato mokṣadoṣāt / dehādibandhanābhāve hi svarasenaiva mokṣaḥ syāditi //
body.translated_text: even so it would not be tenable that form and the rest are the self, because of the fault of liberation without effort — for in the absence of bondage to the body and so forth, liberation would occur spontaneously.

body.text: rūpāmātmeti samanupaśyati vedanāṃ saṃjñāṃ saṃskārān vijñānamātmeti samanupaśyatītyetāḥ pañcātmadṛṣṭayaḥ / śeṣāḥ pañcadaśātmīyadṛṣṭayaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'One regards form as the self, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness as the self' — these are the five views of self (<s>ātmadṛṣṭi</s>). The remaining are the fifteen views of 'mine' (<s>ātmīyadṛṣṭi</s>).

body.text: rūpavān yāvadvijñānavāniti saṃbandhenātmīyatā, sā hi tatsaṃvandhāttadvān bhavatīti / ātmīyaṃ rūpaṃ yāvadvijñānamiti vaśavarttyātmīyatāmupādāya, yasya hi yadvaśena vartate dāne viniyoge vā tasya tadātmīyamityucyate / rūpe yāvadvijñāne ātmetyavinirbhāgavṛttyātmīyatā, ayamātmāeṣvanusṛto vistṛtaḥ prakṣipto 'ṅgāṅgānusārigata iti parikalpanāt //
body.translated_text: 'Possessing form' up to 'possessing consciousness' — this is the sense of 'mine' through connection, for through its connection with that, one becomes a possessor of that. 'Form belongs to the self' up to 'consciousness [belongs to the self]' — this takes up the sense of 'mine' through having power over it, for that over which one has power in giving or employing is said to belong to that [self]. 'The self is in form' up to 'in consciousness' — this is the sense of 'mine' through undifferentiated activity, because of the conceptualization that 'this self is extended into these, spread out, cast into them, following limb by limb.'

body.text: anirūpitavastukatvaṃ punā rūpamityevamādilakṣaṇaṃ nirūpayata ātmadṛṣṭeranavakāśāt / tadyathā rajjuṃ sarpato gṛhṇāti kaścit sahasā, na punā rajjuriti nirūpayaṃstāṃ sarpato gṛhṇīyāditi //
body.translated_text: The uninvestigated nature of the entity [is such that]: when one investigates the characteristics such as 'form' and so forth, there is no room for the view of self (<s>ātmadṛṣṭi</s>). Just as someone might suddenly grasp a rope as a snake, but upon investigating it as a rope, would not grasp it as a snake.

body.text: krodhādayaḥ prajñaptisanto veditavyāḥ, pratighātādivyatirekeṇābhāvāt // tadūrdhvamiti krodhādūrdhvam / akṣāntirapakārāmarṣaṇam / dharmataiṣā yadavadyaṃ praticchādayataḥ kaukṛtyam, ataścāsparśavihāra iti / uccapragāḍhapāruṣyavacanaṃ paramarmaghaṭṭanayogena pratyakṣaravāditā / asaṃlekho mātsaryeṇānupayujyamānānāmapyupakaraṇānāṃ saṃnicayādveditavyaḥ / bhūtadoṣavimālanā anyenānyasya pratisaraṇaṃ veditavyam / samyagavavādalābhaparipanthakarmakatvaṃ yathābhūtamātmānamanāviṣkṛtyāvavādāyogyatvāt / dīrghāyuṣkalakṣaṇagrahaṇaṃ tadvikalpanādamaravitarkapūrvakaṃ jīvitamadotpatteḥ / anyatamānyatamā sāsravā saṃpattiḥ kulavalarūpamedhābuddhibhogaiśvaryādikā veditavyā / rāgāṃśikaṃ nāndīsaumanasyaṃ saṃkliṣṭo harṣaviśeṣaḥ / śubhanimittamanusarato rāgānukūlaṃ pūrvahasitaramitakrīḍitānusmaraṇāt cittasyānupaśamo veditavyaḥ kausīdyasaṃniśrayadānakarmakatvamaśraddadhānasya
body.translated_text: Anger (<s>krodha</s>) and the rest should be understood as existing by designation (<s>prajñaptisat</s>), because they do not exist apart from hostility (<s>pratigha</s>) and so forth. 'From that onwards' means from anger onwards. Intolerance (<s>akṣānti</s>) is the inability to endure harm. It is the nature [of things] that remorse (<s>kaukṛtya</s>) arises for one who conceals a fault; hence it results in uncomfortable abiding. Loud, intense, and harsh speech, through the method of striking at another's vital points, is verbal retaliation word by word. Hoarding (<s>asaṃlekha</s>) should be understood as the accumulation of provisions through miserliness, even when they are not being used. Concealing real faults is to be understood as attributing one thing to another. Obstructing the gain of proper instruction is because, by not revealing oneself as one truly is, one becomes unfit for admonition. Grasping at the sign of longevity is because, from conceptualizing that, preceded by the reasoning of immortality, intoxication with life arises. Any one of the various defiled fortunes — family, strength, beauty, intelligence, wisdom, possessions, sovereignty, and so forth — should be understood [as the basis for intoxication]. The joy and mental satisfaction that is a portion of attachment (<s>rāga</s>) is a defiled form of elation. Mental restlessness should be understood as pursuing the sign of the attractive, in conformity with attachment, through recollecting previous laughter, amusement, and play. The function of providing support for laziness (<s>kausīdya</s>) is that of one without faith (<s>aśraddadhāna</s>)

body.text: prayogacchandābhāvāt / asaṃviditā kāyavākcittacaryābhikramapratikramādiṣu samyagapratyavekṣitatayā veditavyā / evaṃ hyasya karaṇīyākaraṇīyājñānā dāpattayo bhavantīti //
body.translated_text: because of the absence of desire for application. Lack of introspective awareness (<s>asaṃprajanya</s>) should be understood as the failure to properly examine one's bodily, verbal, and mental conduct in approaching, departing, and so forth. For in this way, through ignorance of what should and should not be done, transgressions arise.

body.text: svabhāvavikṣepaḥ pañcavijñānakāyāḥ, prakṛtyaivādhyātmaṃ samādhātumaśakyatvāt / bahirdhāvikṣepaḥ śrutādikuśale prayuktasya tadālaṃbanādbahiḥ kāmaguṇeṣu cittagamanaṃ veditavyam / adhyātmavikṣepaḥ samādhiprayuktasyaiva taccyutikarau layauddhatyamāsvādanā ca / nimittavikṣepaḥ pare māṃ guṇavattayā saṃbhāvayiṣyantītyetannimittametadartha kuśalaprayuktasya śanaiḥ tatparihāṇito veditavyaḥ / dauṣṭhulya vikṣepo 'haṃkārādidauṣṭhulyavaśādutpannotpanneṣu sukhādiṣu vediteṣvahaṃ mama asmīti vā karaṇāt kuśalapakṣāpariśuddhito veditavyaḥ / āditastathodgrahaṇamudgrahaḥ / vyavakiraṇā tadūrdhvaṃ tena cittasaṃtānasya miśrībhāvaḥ / nimittīkāraḥ tasyaiva veditasya punaḥ punaścitrīkāro veditavyaḥ / manaskāravikṣepaḥ samāpattyantaraṃ vā samāpadyamānasya dhyānāntaraṃ vā saṃśrayataḥ pūrvasmāddhyutthānato veditavyaḥ / vairāgyaparipanthakarmaka ityupakleśātmakaṃ vikṣepamadhikṛtya //
body.translated_text: Distraction of intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāvavikṣepa</s>) consists of the five groups of consciousness (<s>pañcavijñānakāya</s>), because by their very nature they are incapable of internal concentration. External distraction (<s>bahirdhāvikṣepa</s>) should be understood as the going of the mind outward toward the five strands of sensual pleasure while one is engaged in wholesome [activities] such as learning and so forth, away from that [wholesome] object. Internal distraction (<s>adhyātmavikṣepa</s>) pertains to one who is engaged in <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) — it consists of sinking (<s>laya</s>) and excitation (<s>auddhatya</s>), which cause falling from it, and savoring (<s>āsvādanā</s>). Distraction through signs (<s>nimittavikṣepa</s>) should be understood as the gradual decline [from practice] of one engaged in the wholesome for the purpose and with the sign that 'others will esteem me as virtuous.' Distraction through unsuitability (<s>dauṣṭhulyavikṣepa</s>) should be understood as the impurity of the wholesome side, because under the power of unsuitability such as ego-grasping and so forth, whenever pleasant and other feelings arise, one thinks 'I,' 'mine,' or 'I am.' Grasping (<s>udgraha</s>) is the initial apprehension in that manner. Scattering (<s>vyavakiraṇā</s>) is the subsequent mixing of the mental continuum by that. Elaboration (<s>nimittīkāra</s>) should be understood as the repeated diversification of that very feeling. Distraction of attention (<s>manaskāravikṣepa</s>) should be understood as arising from a previous [attainment] when one enters another attainment or resorts to another <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation). 'Having the function of obstructing dispassion' refers to distraction that is of the nature of secondary afflictions (<s>upakleśa</s>).

body.text: middhanimittaṃ tadyathā daurbalyam, śramaḥ, kāyagauravaḥ, andhakāranimittasya manasikaraṇam, sarvārambhāṇāmadhyupekṣaṇam punaḥ punastatkālanidrābhyāsaḥ, mantrabalena parainidropasaṃhārastathā saṃvāhanādibhirveti / mohāṃśika iti samādhito viśeṣaṇārtham / kuśalā(di)bhāvavacanaṃ na tvavaśyaṃ mohātmaka iti kṛtvā / kāla iti rātryā madhyame yāme / akālastato 'nyaḥ / yuktaṃ kāle yathānujñam, akāle 'pi glānasya karmaṇyatārtha vā / ayuktastato 'nyaḥ / kṛtyātipattisaṃniśrayadānamupakleśātmakasya middhasya veditavyaḥ / anabhipretaṃ karaṇamabhipretapūrvikā sucaritaduścaritakriyā, anabhipretaṃ karaṇaṃ parairbalādavaṣṭabhya kāryamāṇasya kleśābhibhavādvā yathāyogaṃ veditavyam / mohāṃśika ityupakleśasaṃgṛhītaḥ / kāle yāvanna prativiramati, akāle tadūrdhvam / yuktaṃ sthāne, ayuktamasthāne / cetanāṃ vā niśritya prajñāṃ vetyanabhyūhābhyūhāvasthāyāṃ yathākramam /
body.translated_text: The causes of torpor (<s>middha</s>) are as follows: weakness, fatigue, heaviness of body, attending to the sign of darkness, neglecting all undertakings, repeated habitual sleeping at those times, the withdrawal [into sleep] of others through the power of mantras, and also through massage and the like. 'Having a portion of delusion (<s>moha</s>)' is for the purpose of distinguishing it from <s>samādhi</s>. The statement of its being wholesome and so forth means it is not necessarily of the nature of delusion. 'Timely' means during the middle watch of the night. 'Untimely' is other than that. 'Appropriate' means when timely and as permitted; even when untimely, for the sake of fitness when one is ill. 'Inappropriate' is other than that. Providing the support for the transgression of duties should be understood as pertaining to torpor that is of the nature of secondary afflictions. Unintended action is the performance of good and bad conduct preceded by [good] intention; unintended action should also be understood as being compelled by others through force, or being overpowered by afflictions, as appropriate. 'Having a portion of delusion' means included among the secondary afflictions. [For torpor:] as long as it does not cease at the proper time, and beyond that at improper times. 'Appropriate' is in the proper place; 'inappropriate' is in an improper place. Whether based on volition (<s>cetanā</s>) or on wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) — [these correspond] respectively to the states of non-deliberation and deliberation.

body.text: paryeṣaṇākārā manaso 'bhijalpanā vitarkaḥ pratyavekṣaṇākārā manaso 'bhijalpanānuvicāra iti // tāveva vitarkavicārau saṃvadhyete, audārikasūkṣmavyavasthānādanayoḥ //
body.translated_text: Investigation (<s>vitarka</s>) is the mental discourse in the mode of inquiry; examination (<s>vicāra</s>) is the mental discourse in the mode of scrutiny. These very <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s> are established [respectively] because of their coarse and subtle classification.

body.text: tadyathālobhasya lobhaprahāṇam, śraddhāyā āśraddhayaprahāṇam / rāgapratipakṣo vairāgyam, tasya paripanthakaraṇam, tasya tena tadutpattāvantarāyakaraṇāt / evaṃ krodhādīnāmapyupakleśānāṃ maitryādyātmīyaratipakṣāntarāyakaraṇaṃ veditavyam //
body.translated_text: For example, the abandonment of greed is through [the antidote of] non-greed, and the abandonment of faith is through lack of faith. Dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) is the antidote of attachment (<s>rāga</s>); [the secondary affliction's] function of obstructing that [antidote] is because it creates an obstacle to the arising of that [antidote] through that [affliction]. Similarly, the obstruction of the respective antidotes such as loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) and so forth by the secondary afflictions beginning with anger (<s>krodha</s>) should be understood.

body.text: cittaviprayuktānāṃ saṃskārāṇāmadhiṣṭhānataḥ svabhāvataḥ prajñaptitaśca nirdeśo veditavyaḥ / asaṃjñisamāpattinirodhasamāpattī bhūmito 'pi niḥsaraṇavihārasaṃjñāpūrvakābhyāṃ manaskārābhyāmapi nirdiṣṭe / āsaṃjñikaṃ manaskāravarjyairebhireva / śeṣā adhiṣṭhānādibhistribhireva /
body.translated_text: The exposition of the formations dissociated from mind (<s>cittaviprayukta saṃskāras</s>) should be understood through [their] basis, intrinsic nature, and designation. The attainment of non-perception (<s>asaṃjñisamāpatti</s>) and the attainment of cessation (<s>nirodhasamāpatti</s>) are also explained through [their] level (<s>bhūmi</s>) and through two types of mental attention — that preceded by the perception of emergence and that preceded by the perception of abiding. The state of non-perception (<s>āsaṃjñika</s>) [is explained] by these same [factors] excluding mental attention. The remaining [dissociated formations are explained] by only three — basis and so forth.

body.text: tatra kuśalākuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāmityadhiṣṭhānanirdeśaḥ / ācayāpacaya iti svabhāvanirdeśaḥ / tathāhyācaye 'dhimātraiḥ śraddhādibhiḥ samanvāgata ityucyate / apacaye sati mṛdubhiriti / prāptiḥ pratilambhaḥ samāgama iti prajñaptiriti prajñaptinirdeśaḥ / evamanyeṣvapi yathāyogaṃ yojayitavyam //
body.translated_text: Therein, 'of wholesome and unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>' is the exposition through basis. 'Accumulation and diminution' (<s>ācaya-apacaya</s>) is the exposition through intrinsic nature. For indeed, in the case of accumulation, one is said to be 'endowed with intense faith and so forth'; in the case of diminution, 'with mild [faith and so forth].' 'Acquisition' (<s>prāpti</s>), 'obtainment' (<s>pratilambha</s>), and 'convergence' (<s>samāgama</s>) are designations — this is the exposition through designation. Thus, in the case of others also, [the exposition] should be applied as appropriate.

body.text: śubhakṛtsnavītarāgasyeti tṛtīyadhyānavītarāgasya / uparyavītarāgasyeti caturthadhyānāvītarāgasya / niḥsaraṇasaṃjñāpūrvakeṇeti mokṣasaṃjñāpūrvakeṇa / asthāvarāṇāmiti pravṛttivijñānasaṅgṛhītānām / nirodha iti samāpatticittakṛtaḥ kālāntaramasthāvaracittacaittasamudācāranirodho āśrayasyāvasthāviśeṣo nirudhyate 'neneti kṛtvā / nirodhasamāpattāvuparyavītarāgasyetyavacanai bhavāgravīta rāgasyārhato 'pi tatsaṃbhavāt / tadekatyānāṃ ca sthāvarāṇāmiti kliṣṭamanaḥsaṃgṛhītānām / ete ca samāpattī bhūmitaḥ manaskārato 'dhiṣṭhānataḥ svabhāvataḥ prajñaptitaśca nirdeṣṭe āsaṃjñikaṃ manaskāravarjairebhireva / śeṣā adhiṣṭhānādibhistribhireva //
body.translated_text: 'Of one who has become dispassionate toward the <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s> [realm]' means of one who has become dispassionate toward the third <s>dhyāna</s>. 'Of one who has not become dispassionate toward what is above' means of one who has not become dispassionate toward the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>. 'Preceded by the perception of emergence' means preceded by the perception of liberation. 'Of the non-stable ones' means those included in the active consciousness (<s>pravṛttivijñāna</s>). 'Cessation' is the cessation of the occurrence of non-stable mental factors produced by the mind of the attainment at a later time — it is a special state of the basis, because it is that by which [mental activity] is ceased. In the attainment of cessation, the omission of 'one who has not become dispassionate toward what is above' [is because] even an <s>Arhat</s> who has become dispassionate toward the summit of existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>) can attain it. 'And of certain stable ones' means those included in the afflicted mind (<s>kliṣṭamanas</s>). These two attainments are explained through level, mental attention, basis, intrinsic nature, and designation; the state of non-perception [is explained] by these same [factors] excluding mental attention; the remaining [dissociated formations are explained] by only three — basis and so forth.

body.text: nikāyasabhāga ekajanmikaḥ skandhasaṃtānaḥ / sthitikālaniyama iyantaṃ kālamanenāsmin nikāyasabhāge 'vasthātavyaṃ varṣaśataṃ varṣasahasraṃ veti karmakṛtaḥ sāmarthyaviśeṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Nikāyasabhāga</s> (class-homogeneity) is the continuum of aggregates belonging to a single birth. The determination of the duration of existence is a special capacity produced by <s>karma</s>: 'for this duration one must remain in this class-homogeneity — a hundred years or a thousand years.'

body.text: tasmistasmin sattvanikāya iti devamanuṣyādiṣu sattvajātiṣu / ātmabhāvasadṛśatāyāmityekajātīyatāyām /
body.translated_text: 'In this and that class of beings' (<s>sattvanikāya</s>) means among the types of beings such as gods, humans, and so forth. 'In the similarity of self-existence' means in the homogeneity of one kind.

body.text: bāhyasyāpi rūpasya jātimattve nikāyasabhāgamātragrahaṇaṃ sattvasaṃtāne lakṣaṇaprajñaptijñāpanārtham / bāhyaṃ hi rūpaṃ saṃvarttavivarttaprabhāvitamā dhyātmikāstu jātijarādiprabhāvitā iti / prabandhavināśo maraṇaṃ veditavyam / ete ca jātyādayo na pratikṣaṇaṃ veditavyāḥ kiṃtarhi prabandhāvasthāsviti /
body.translated_text: Even though external form possesses species-nature, the mention of mere class-homogeneity is for the purpose of indicating the characteristics and designations within the continuum of beings. For external form is governed by cosmic formation and dissolution, whereas internal [form] is governed by birth, aging, and so forth. Death should be understood as the destruction of the continuum. And these [factors] beginning with birth should not be understood as occurring at each moment, but rather in the stages of the continuum.

body.text: svabhāvādhivacanaṃ cakṣuḥ śrotraṃ devo manuṣya ityevamādi / viśeṣādhivacanaṃ sarvasaṃskārā anityāḥ sarvasattvā mariṣyantītyevamādi / tadubhayāśrayeṣvi ti svabhāvaviśeṣādhivacanāśrayeṣvakṣareṣu a i u ityevamādiṣu / etāvacca sarvaṃ yaduta svabhāvo viśeṣastadubhayavyavahāraśca, tatsarvamebhiranuvyavahriyata iti / ata ete nāmapadavyañjanakāyā vyavasthāpitāḥ / paryāyākṣaraṇatāmupādāyeti yathā cakṣuścakṣurityetasmātparyāyādanyeṣvapi netrākṣinayanalocanādiṣu paryāyāntareṣu kṣarati, tairapi tatsaṃjñānāt / naivaṃ a ityetadakṣaraṃ a ityetaṃ paryāyaṃ mukttvā paryāyāntareṇa śakyate jñāpayitum, ataḥ paryāyākṣaraṇādakṣarāaṇi / kṣaraṇaṃ punargamanaṃ veditavyam //
body.translated_text: A name designating intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāvādhivacana</s>) is like 'eye,' 'ear,' 'god,' 'human,' and so forth. A name designating a qualification (<s>viśeṣādhivacana</s>) is like 'all formations are impermanent,' 'all beings will die,' and so forth. 'Based on both of those' means in the syllables (<s>akṣaras</s>) that are the basis of names designating intrinsic nature and qualifications — such as 'a,' 'i,' 'u,' and so forth. And this is the totality [of language]: namely, the intrinsic nature, the qualification, and the conventional usage of both — all of this is expressed through these [syllables]. Therefore, the collections of names (<s>nāmakāya</s>), sentences (<s>padakāya</s>), and syllables (<s>vyañjanakāya</s>) are established. 'Because of flowing through synonyms' means: just as 'eye' (<s>cakṣus</s>), from this synonym, flows (<s>kṣarati</s>) to other synonyms as well — such as <s>netra</s>, <s>akṣi</s>, <s>nayana</s>, <s>locana</s>, and so forth — because by those too, that [same thing] is cognized. But the syllable 'a' cannot be indicated by any synonym other than the synonym 'a'; therefore, because of non-flowing through synonyms, [they are called] syllables (<s>akṣara</s>, 'non-flowing'). 'Flowing' (<s>kṣaraṇa</s>) should be understood as 'going.'

body.text: prabandhānupacchede pravṛttivyavasthānamekasmin kṣaṇe vyavacchinne vā tadupacārābhāvāt hetuphalanānātvamiṣṭasya phalasya sucaritamaniṣṭasya duścaritamityevamādi / phalānāṃ pṛthak pṛthaganyonyahetukatvam / hetuphalasārūpyamanyatve 'pi yadyasya phalaṃ yujyate / tadyathā dānasya bhogasaṃpadityevamādi / ekaikasyaiva pravṛttirayugapatpravṛttirveditavyā / hetuphalasya prabandhena pravṛttau satyāṃ yattatra hetuphalamutpannaniruddhaṃ so 'tītaḥ kāla iti prajñapyate, yadanutpannaṃ so 'nāgataḥ kālaḥ, yadutpannāniruddhaṃ sa pratyutpannaḥ kāla iti / hetuphalasya digvyāptau deśopacāraḥ / rūpasaṃgṛhītaṃ cātra hetuphalaṃ veditavyamarūpiṇāṃ digvyāpanasāmarthyābhāvāt / pratyekaśo bhede saṃkhyetyabhinnaikātmakatve dvitrisaṃkhyādyanupapatteḥ / hetuphalapratyayānāṃ
body.translated_text: The establishment of occurrence is in the non-interruption of the continuum — [even] when interrupted at a single moment, because of the absence of figurative usage for that. The diversity of causes and results: of a desired result, the cause is good conduct; of an undesired result, bad conduct — and so forth. The results individually have different causes for one another. The similarity of cause and result is because, even though different, whichever result is appropriate for whichever [cause] — for example, the prosperity of enjoyments is [the result] of generosity (<s>dāna</s>), and so forth. The occurrence of each [cause-result] should be understood as non-simultaneous occurrence. When there is the occurrence of cause and result in a continuum, that causal result therein which has arisen and ceased is designated as past time; that which has not yet arisen is future time; that which has arisen but not ceased is present time. When cause and result pervade a direction, there is the figurative usage of location. And here, the cause-and-result should be understood as included in form (<s>rūpa</s>), because formless [dharmas] lack the capacity to pervade a direction. Number is through the individual differentiation [of things], because in the absence of differentiated individual identity, the enumeration of two, three, and so forth would be untenable. Of the conditions of causes, results, and <s>pratyayas</s>

body.text: samavadhānaṃ tadyathā vijñānākhyasya hi hetuphalasyendriyāparibhedo vipayābhāsagamanaṃ tajjñānaṃ manaskārapratyupasthānaṃ ceti / evamanyatrāpi yojitavyam //
body.translated_text: the coming together [of conditions] — for example, for the causal result called consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>): the non-deterioration of the sense-faculty, the approaching of the appearance of the object, the cognition of that [object], and the presence of attention (<s>manaskāra</s>). Thus, in other cases also, [the conditions] should be connected [accordingly].

body.text: ityevamete cittaviprayuktāḥ saṃskārāṇāṃ dharmāṇāmavasthāsu prajñapanātsarve prajñaptisanto veditavyāḥ / tatra kuśalākuśalādyācayāpacayāvasthāyāmekaḥ / cittacaitasikāpravṛttyavasthāyāṃ trayaḥ / sthityavasthāyāmekaḥ / sādṛśyāvasthāyāmekaḥ / lakṣaṇāvasthāyāṃ catvāraḥ / vyavahārāvasthāyāṃ trayaḥ / alābhāvasthāyāmekaḥ / hetuphalāvasthāyāṃ śeṣā iti / hetuphalaṃ punaratra sarva saṃskṛtaṃ veditavyam / tato 'nyasyotpādāddhetuḥ / anyatastadutpādāt phalamiti //
body.translated_text: Thus, these <s>cittaviprayukta</s> (mind-dissociated) [formations] are all to be understood as designations in the states of <s>saṃskāra dharmas</s> (conditioned phenomena). Among them, one pertains to the state of accumulation and diminution of wholesome, unwholesome, and other [factors]; three pertain to the state of non-occurrence of <s>citta</s> (mind) and <s>caitasikas</s> (mental factors); one pertains to the state of duration; one pertains to the state of similarity; four pertain to the state of characteristics; three pertain to the state of conventional usage; one pertains to the state of non-obtaining; and the remainder pertain to the state of cause and effect. Furthermore, here cause and effect should be understood as all that is <s>saṃskṛta</s> (conditioned). From the arising of something other than that, it is a cause; from the arising of that from something else, it is an effect.

body.text: skandhādīnāṃ samudācāre tadbījaparipuṣṭirvāsanetyucyate / sarvabījakaṃ teṣāmeva skandhādīnāmutpattibījairyuktatvāt / ālīyante tasmin dharmā bījataḥ, sattvā vātmagrāheṇetyālayavijñānam / pūrvakarmanirmitatvāt vipākavijñānam / punaḥ punaḥ pratisaṃdhibandhe ātmabhāvopādānā dādānavijñānam / tatpunaretaccittamityucyate, sarvadharmavāsanācittatvāt //
body.translated_text: When the <s>skandhas</s> and so forth are active, the nourishment of their seeds is called <s>vāsanā</s> (habitual impregnation). It is <s>sarvabījaka</s> (containing all seeds) because it possesses the seeds for the production of those very <s>skandhas</s> and so forth. <s>Dharmas</s> cling to it by way of seeds, and sentient beings cling by way of self-grasping — thus it is called <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (storehouse consciousness). Because it is fashioned by former <s>karma</s>, it is called <s>vipākavijñāna</s> (resultant consciousness). Because it appropriates a personal existence at each successive rebirth-connection, it is called <s>ādānavijñāna</s> (appropriating consciousness). Furthermore, this is called <s>citta</s> (mind), because it is impregnated by the <s>vāsanās</s> of all <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: tadetadālayavijñānamastīti kathaṃ vijñāyate / yasmāttena vinā
body.translated_text: How is it known that this <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (storehouse consciousness) exists? Because without it,

body.text:
upāttamādi spaṣṭatvaṃ bījaṃ karma na yujyate /
kāyiko 'nubhavo 'citte samāpattī cyutistathā //
body.translated_text:
Appropriation, initial [arising], clarity, seed-nature, <s>karma</s>, are not tenable;
bodily experience, mindless attainment, and death likewise [are not tenable].

body.text: etasyāścoddānagāthāyā vibhāgastadyathā viniścayasaṃgrahaṇyāma ṣṭābhirākārairālayavijñānasyāstitā pratyetavyā / tadyathāntareṇālayavijñānaṃ āśrayopādānāsaṃbhavataḥ ādipravṛtyasaṃbhavataḥ spaṣṭapravṛttyasaṃbhavato bījatvāsaṃbhavataḥ karmāsaṃbhavataḥ kāyikānubhavāsaṃbhavatācittakasamāpattyasaṃbhavato vijñānacyutyasaṃbhavataśca //
body.translated_text: The analysis of this summary verse is as follows: as stated in the <s>Viniścayasaṃgrahaṇī</s>, the existence of <s>ālayavijñāna</s> is to be recognized through eight aspects, namely: without <s>ālayavijñāna</s>, (1) the appropriation of a basis (<s>āśrayopādāna</s>) would be impossible, (2) initial functioning (<s>ādipravṛtti</s>) would be impossible, (3) clear functioning (<s>spaṣṭapravṛtti</s>) would be impossible, (4) seed-nature (<s>bījatva</s>) would be impossible, (5) <s>karma</s> would be impossible, (6) bodily experience (<s>kāyikānubhava</s>) would be impossible, (7) mindless attainment (<s>acittakasamāpatti</s>) would be impossible, and (8) the departure of consciousness at death (<s>vijñānacyuti</s>) would be impossible.

body.text: kena kāraṇenāśrayopādānaṃ na yujyate / āha pañcabhiḥ kāraṇaiḥ / tathāhi ālayavijñānaṃ pūrvasaṃskārahetukam / cakṣurādipravṛttivijñānaṃ punarvartamānapratyayahetukam / yathoktam indriyaviṣayamanaskāravaśādvijñānānāṃ pravṛttirbhavatīti vistareṇa / idaṃ prathamaṃ kāraṇam / api ca kuśalākuśalāḥ ṣaḍvijñānakāyā upalabhyante / idaṃ dvitīyaṃ kāraṇam / api ca ṣaṇṇāṃ vijñānakāyānāṃ sā jātirnopalabhyate yāvyākṛtavipākasaṃgṛhītā syāt / idaṃ tṛtīyaṃ kāraṇam / api ca pratiniyatāśrayāḥ ṣaḍvijñānakāyāḥ pravartante, tatra yena yenāśrayeṇa yadvijñānaṃ pravartate tadeva tenopāttaṃ syādavaśiṣṭasyānupāttateti na yujyate, upāttatāpi na yujyate vijñānavirahitatayā / idaṃ caturtha kāraṇam / api ca punaḥ punarāśrayasyopādāna doṣaḥ prasajyate / tathāhi cakṣurvijñānamekadā pravartate ekadā na pravarttate evamavaśiṣṭāni / idaṃ pañcamaṃ kāraṇam / iti pūrvakarmapravarttamānapratyahetuto 'pi kuśalākuśalato 'pi tajjātyanupalaṃbhato 'pi pratiniyatāśrayato 'pi punaḥ punarupādānadoṣato 'pi na yujyate //
body.translated_text: For what reason is the appropriation of a basis (<s>āśrayopādāna</s>) not tenable [without <s>ālayavijñāna</s>]? It is stated: for five reasons. Namely, <s>ālayavijñāna</s> has past <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) as its cause, while the <s>pravṛttivijñānas</s> (active consciousnesses) beginning with visual consciousness are conditioned by present sense objects. If <s>ālayavijñāna</s> does not exist, who would appropriate the objects that serve as the basis for <s>dharmas</s> born from <s>saṃskāras</s>, existing in the interval between active consciousnesses? Moreover, one who has gone to the lower realms would not at all be included within those <s>pravṛttivijñānas</s>. Nor would there necessarily be an abiding in accordance with reality in the lower realms. And since there is no <s>vipāka</s> (maturation) in the lower realms, there would be abiding in one's own nature like space and so forth. Furthermore, when two consciousnesses appear, for something that has the nature of appearance to be mutually dependent — such dependence without [an independent basis] is not tenable.

body.text: kena kāraṇenādipravṛttisaṃbhavo na yujyate / sa cetkaścidvadedyadyālaya vijñānamasti tena dvayoḥ vijñānayoḥ yugapatpravṛttirbhaviṣyati / sa idaṃ syādvacanīyaḥ - adoṣa eva bhavāndoṣasaṃjñī / tathāhi bhavatyeva dvayorvijñānayoryugapatpravṛttiḥ / tatkasya hetoḥ / tathāhyekatyasya yugapadradṣṭukāmasya yāvadvijñātukāmasyādita itaretaravijñānapravṛttirna yujyate / tathāhi tatra manaskāro 'pi nirviśiṣṭa indriyamapi viṣayo 'pi //
body.translated_text: For what reason is the initial arising (<s>ādipravṛtti</s>) not tenable [without <s>ālayavijñāna</s>]? Suppose someone were to say: if <s>ālayavijñāna</s> exists, then two consciousnesses would function simultaneously, and <s>manovijñāna</s> (mental consciousness) would necessarily accompany <s>cakṣurvijñāna</s> (visual consciousness); due to no difference in accumulation between the two, there would be no occasion when even <s>devas</s> (gods) among beings could remain stable. The reply is: it is not necessarily the case that the two always function simultaneously through the force of deliberate attention. <s>Manovijñāna</s> operates sequentially, being similar to its immediately preceding object-support. Moreover, <s>manovijñāna</s> functions even regarding present objects because it arises from the seeds of that [<s>ālayavijñāna</s>].

body.text: kena kāraṇenāsatyāṃ yugapadvijñānapravṛttau manovijñānasya cakṣurādivijñānasahānucarasya spaṣṭatvaṃ na saṃbhavati / tathāhi yasmin samaye 'tītamanubhūtaṃ viṣayaṃ samanusmarati tasmin samaye 'vispaṣṭo manovijñānapracāro bhavati na tu tathā vartamānaviṣayo manaḥpracāro 'vispaṣṭo bhavati / ato 'pi yugapatpravṛttirvā yujyate 'vispaṣṭatvaṃ vā manovijñānasya //
body.translated_text: For what reason, in the absence of simultaneous functioning of consciousnesses, is the clarity (<s>spaṣṭatva</s>) of <s>manovijñāna</s> — which accompanies <s>cakṣurvijñāna</s> (visual consciousness) and the like — not possible? Namely, the grasping of particular objects by <s>cakṣurvijñāna</s> is through the power of <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight), not of <s>manas</s> (mind), because <s>cakṣurvijñāna</s>, being free from conceptual construction, does not have the form of <s>vipaśyanā</s>. If, however, through the power of <s>vipaśyanā</s>, <s>manovijñāna</s> grasps particular objects, then without the functioning of <s>ālayavijñāna</s>, clarity of object-support for <s>manovijñāna</s> accompanying <s>cakṣurvijñāna</s> is possible through the power of training. And through the power of training, four consciousnesses can grasp simultaneously.

body.text: kena kāraṇena bījatvaṃ na saṃbhavati ṣaṇṇāṃ vijñānakāyānāmanyonyam / tathāhi kuśalānantaramakuśalamutpadyate, akuśalānantaraṃ kuśalam, tadubhayānantaramavyākṛtam, hīnadhātukānantaraṃ madhyadhātukam, madhyadhātukānantaraṃ praṇītadhātukam, evaṃ praṇītadhātukānantaraṃ yāvaddhīnadhātukam, sāsravānantaramanāsravam, anāsravānantaraṃ
body.translated_text: For what reason is seed-nature (<s>bījatva</s>) not possible among the six <s>vijñānakāyas</s> (consciousness-groups) mutually? Namely, immediately after a wholesome [state], an unwholesome [state] arises; immediately after an unwholesome [state], a wholesome [state]; immediately after a defiled [state], an indeterminate [state]; immediately after a determinate [state], a defiled [state]; immediately after a contaminated [state],

body.text: sāsravam, laukikānantaraṃ lokottaram, lokottarānantaraṃ laukikam / na ca teṣāṃ tathā bījatvaṃ yujyate / dīrghakālasamucchinnāpi ca saṃtatiścireṇa kālena pravartate, tasmādapi na yujyate //
body.translated_text: a contaminated [state arises]; immediately after a mundane [state], a supramundane [state]; immediately after a supramundane [state], a mundane [state]. And seed-nature among them in that manner is not tenable. Moreover, being the seed of everything is not tenable due to the operation of what is contrary over a long period and immediately preceding. Without <s>ālayavijñāna</s>,

body.text: kena kāraṇenāsatyāṃ yugapadvijñānapravṛttau karma na saṃbhavati / tathāhi samāsataścaturvidhaṃ karma - bhājanavijñaptirāśrayavijñaptirahamiti vijñaptirviṣayavijñaptiśceti / etā vijñaptayaḥ kṣaṇe kṣaṇe yugapatpravartamānā upalabhyante / na caikasya vijñānasyaikasmin kṣaṇe idamevaṃrūpaṃ vyatibhinnaṃ karma yujyate //
body.translated_text: for what reason, in the absence of simultaneous functioning of consciousnesses, is <s>karma</s> not possible? Namely, in brief, <s>karma</s> is fourfold: the representation of the receptacle-world (<s>bhājanavijñapti</s>), the representation of personal existence (<s>ātmabhāvavijñapti</s>), the representation of enjoyment (<s>bhogavijñapti</s>), and the representation of action (<s>kriyāvijñapti</s>). These four kinds of <s>karma</s>, having the form of object-representation, are accomplished by <s>pravṛttivijñāna</s> (active consciousness). However, not all action-object-representations in every activity are established in their own nature without <s>ālayavijñāna</s>.

body.text: kena kāraṇenāsatyālayavijñāne kāyiko 'nubhavo na yujyate / tathāhyekatyasya yoniśo vāyoniśo vā cintayato vānuvitarkayato vā samāhitacetaso vāsamāhitacetaso vā ye kāye kāyānubhavā utpadyante 'nekavidhā bahunānāprakārāste na bhaveyurupalabhyante ca / tasmādapyastyālayavijñānam //
body.translated_text: For what reason is bodily experience not tenable without <s>ālayavijñāna</s>? Namely, when someone thinks or reflects wisely or unwisely, an experience of such a kind arises dependent on the body. And for one whose mind is distracted, feelings of heat, cold, pleasure, suffering, and so forth arise — is this through <s>ālayavijñāna</s> or not?

body.text: kena kāraṇe nāsatyālayavijñāne 'cittā samāpattirna saṃbhavati / tathāhya saṃjñisamāpannasya vā nirodhasamāpannasya vā vijñānameva kāyādapakrāntaṃ syāt / nānapakrāntaṃ tataḥ kālakriyaiva bhavet / yathoktam bhagavatā - "vijñānaṃ cāsya kāyādanapakrāntaṃ bhavatī"ti //
body.translated_text: For what reason is mindless attainment (<s>acittasamāpatti</s>) not possible without <s>ālayavijñāna</s>? Namely, for one who has attained the <s>asaṃjñisamāpatti</s> (attainment of non-perception) or the <s>nirodhasamāpatti</s> (attainment of cessation), there would be one [remaining] consciousness. Because both of these do not exist as an entity without a support. And if both these attainments were accompanied by consciousness, [the latter] would not be called the attainment beyond cessation. Because there is equality between the two in terms of the abiding of <s>ālayavijñāna</s>, but not in terms of active manifestation. Even the varied stream of subtle consciousness experiences obstruction through the cessation of just one consciousness of twofold nature.

body.text: kena kāraṇenāsatyālayavijñāne cyutirapi na yujyate / tathāhi cyavamānasya vijñāna mūrdhvadehaṃ vā śotikurvan vijahāti, adhodehaṃ vā / na ca manovijñānaṃ kadācinna pravartate / ato 'pyālayavijñānasyaiva dehopādāna kasya vigamāddehaśītatā upa[la]bhyate dehāpratisaṃvedanā ca / na tu manovijñānasya / ato 'pi na yujyate //
body.translated_text: For what reason is death (<s>cyuti</s>) also not tenable without <s>ālayavijñāna</s>? Namely, the consciousness of the dying person departs, making the upper part of the body cold, or the lower part. In a body that is conscious, there is undisputed agreement [about this]. But in a body devoid of consciousness, that one-sided position is not tenable.

body.text: mano nirvacanata ālaṃbanataḥ saṃprayogataḥ pravṛttikālataśca nirdiṣṭaṃ veditavyam / mārgasaṃmukhībhāve tadabhāvaḥ, paramārthajñānasyātmadṛṣṭisamudācāreṇātyantavirodhāt / tadūrdhvamālayavijñānātpravṛttiḥ, śaikṣasyāprahīṇatvāt / asaṃjñisamāpattito
body.translated_text: <s>Manas</s> (mental faculty) should be understood as described by way of its etymology (<s>nirvacana</s>), its object-support (<s>ālambana</s>), its association (<s>saṃprayoga</s>), and its time of operation (<s>pravṛttikāla</s>). When facing the path, there is its absence, and because there is absence in the ultimate sense at the time of eradication. But how is it known that its continuity exists? Because without it, the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions)

body.text: nirodhasamāpatteḥ śāntataratvaṃ tadasamudācārādeva veditavyam / samanantaraniruddhaṃ mano 'numatamiti kṛtvānantaraṃ matamityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: The greater tranquility of <s>nirodhasamāpatti</s> (attainment of cessation) should be understood precisely from the non-manifestation of that [<s>manas</s>]. Since the immediately preceding ceased <s>manas</s> is accepted, what follows immediately is called <s>manas</s>, because <s>manovijñāna</s> (mental consciousness) dependent on it is corrupted by the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) associated with <s>kliṣṭamanas</s> (defiled mind). It is also called immediate (<s>ānantarya</s>) because it serves as the basis for the mental activity that crushes present afflictions.

body.text: vijñānasyāśrayata ālaṃbanataḥ svabhāvataśca vyavasthānaṃ veditavyam //
body.translated_text: The establishment of <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) should be understood by way of its basis (<s>āśraya</s>), its object-support (<s>ālambana</s>), and its intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāva</s>).

body.text: dhātvāyatanānāṃ nāsti pṛthaglakṣaṇavyavasthānam, skandhanirdeśa eva cakṣurādīnāmuktalakṣaṇatvāt / tasmātskandhebhya eva niṣkṛṣya dhātavo vyavasthāpyante, dhātubhya āyatanāni //
body.translated_text: There is no separate establishment of the characteristics of <s>dhātus</s> (elements) and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense bases), because the characteristics of the eye and so forth have already been stated in the exposition of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates). Therefore, why is there a separate exposition of <s>dhātus</s> and <s>āyatanas</s> apart from the <s>skandhas</s>? It is stated: the separate exposition of the container and what is contained is not meaningless; nor is the separate exposition of <s>manas</s> (mind) and its activity, because the noble <s>dharmas</s> are not undifferentiated from others. Moreover, it is for the purpose of differentiating what is subtle and to be fully known.

body.text: yattu skandhairasaṃgṛhītamasaṃskṛtaṃ tadaṣṭadhāvyavasthāpya iti / tathatāyāstraividhyamāśrayaprakārabhedānna svabhāvabhedāditi veditavyam / ananyathīma vatā sadaiva bhāvanāṃ nirātmatayā draṣṭavyā / saṃkleśāpracāratāmupādāyeti tenālabanena saṃkleśavastunaḥ saṃkleśaśūnyīkaraṇāt / yadāpi saṃkliṣṭetyucyate tadāpyāgantukastatropakleśo veditavyaḥ / katamaḥ punarāgantukastatropakleśaḥ / anapoddhṛtagrāhyagrāhakabījasya paratantracittasya dvayākārā pravṛttiḥ / na dharmatā cittasya / prakṛtiprabhāsvarā hi sarvadharmāṇāṃ dharmateti / nimittāni rūpaṃ vedanā yāvadbodhiriti prapañcitāni, teṣāṃ tatropaśamādanimittam / bhūtaṃ yadaviparītam, tasya koṭiḥ paryantaḥ, nairātmyātpareṇa tattvāparyepaṇāt / ākāśaṃ rūpābhāva iti rūpasyava viparyayeṇābhāvalakṣaṇo yo dharmo manovijñānaviṣayastadākāśam / manovijñānaviṣayatva punaḥ dharmadhātvadhikāratvena veditavyam / rūpasyaivetyavadhāraṇādvedanādisādhāraṇāstathatāpratisaṃkhyāpratisaṃkhyāni[ro]dhānityatāḥ paryudāsyante / śaśavipāṇādīnāmatyantamabhāvo na teṣāṃ viparyayeṇa vijñāyate / yasmātta evātyantaṃ na saṃbhavantīti / te 'pi śaśaviṣāṇādayo nāsyaiva vidyamānasya rūpasya viparyayeṇa,
body.translated_text: As for that which is <s>asaṃskṛta</s> (unconditioned), not included in the <s>skandhas</s>, it is established as eightfold. The threefold nature of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) is due to differences in basis and mode, not due to differences in intrinsic nature. The differences in basis are three: <s>prakṛtivisuddhi</s> (natural purity), <s>dhātu</s> (element), and <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness). Furthermore, it is said

body.text: vedanādisādhāraṇatvāt / tasmādrūpasyaiva viparyayeṇetyucyate / abhāvalakṣaṇavacanena vedanādonāmarūpiṇāṃ paryudāsaḥ / na hi te 'bhāvalakṣaṇā iti / yo nirodho na ca visaṃyoga ityanuśayāsamuddhātāt / viparyayādvisaṃyogaḥ //
body.translated_text: because [it is] common to <s>vedanā</s> (feeling) and so forth. Therefore it is said, 'conversely, of <s>rūpa</s> (form) alone.' By the statement of the characteristic of absence, there is the exclusion of the formless, namely <s>vedanā</s> and the rest. Activity is the functioning of <s>vedanā</s> and so forth, and that should be understood as belonging to <s>cetanā</s> (volition). As for <s>ākāśa</s> (space), both of these — the characteristic of absence and the absence of activity — are natural to it. For the others, [these characteristics are] produced through conditioning. What is that which is obstructed, such that the characteristic of non-obstruction is [the definition of] <s>ākāśa</s>? It is nothing whatsoever; rather, without which there would be the nature of non-establishment in itself — that is its characteristic. The absence of a support means the revealing of non-establishment.

body.text: dvayamidaṃ prahātavyam - kleśāśca tadāśrayabhūtaṃ ca vastu veditam / tatpunarveditaṃ dvividham - vaikārikamavaikārikaṃ ca, sukhaduḥkhamaduḥkhāsukhaṃ ca yathākramam / tatra kleśaprahāṇāt pratisaṃkhyānirodhavyavasthānam / dvividhaveditaprahāṇādyathākramamāniñjyasya saṃjñāvedayitanirodhasya ca vyavasthānam / tatra kleśaprahāṇaṃ tatpakṣadauṣṭhulyāpagamādāśrayaparivṛttiḥ, veditaprahāṇaṃ tatpratipakṣabhūtāyāḥ samāpatterāvaraṇāpagamādāśrayaparivṛttiḥ / ata eva dvitīye dhyāne duḥkhanirodhasyāsaṃskṛtā[vya]vasthānam, vaikārikasya veditasyāśeṣamaprahāṇāt //
body.translated_text: This twofold [category] is to be abandoned: the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) and the object known as their basis. That which is known is again twofold: changeable and unchangeable. That which is not abandoned by the <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) arising in meditative absorption or the supramundane <s>prajñā</s> obtained subsequently is permanent. Likewise is <s>nirvāṇa</s> for one not in meditative absorption. Even for one in absorption, not in every respect, for the personal attainment of one not in absorption is not [wholly] eliminated.

body.text: rūpaskandhena daśarūpiṇo dhātavaḥ saṃgṛhītāḥ, dharmadhātunā sa eva, mana āyatanena sapta vijñānadhātava ityevaṃ sarvadharmāstrayo bhavanti //
body.translated_text: Ten material <s>dhātus</s> (elements) are included in <s>rūpaskandha</s> (the aggregate of form); that very [remainder is included] in <s>dharmadhātu</s> (the element of phenomena); seven consciousness <s>dhātus</s> are included in <s>manāyatana</s> (the mind base) — thus all <s>dharmas</s> are included in the five <s>skandhas</s>. Because there is nothing included in <s>dhātus</s> and <s>āyatanas</s> that is not [included in the five <s>skandhas</s>], there is nothing not included in the five <s>skandhas</s>.

body.text: evaṃ vyavasthāpiteṣu skandhadhātvāyataneṣvānuṣaṃgikametadvayutpādyate //
body.translated_text: When the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense bases) have been established in this way, the following incidental points are elucidated.

body.text: cakṣuḥśrotraghrāṇānāṃ pratyekaṃ dvitve sati kathaṃ dhātūnāṃ naikaviṃśatitvam / yadyapi caiṣāṃ dvitvaṃ na tu dhātvantaratvam, lakṣaṇasādharmyeṇobhayoścakṣurlakṣaṇatvāt, kṛtyasādharmyeṇobhayoścakṣurvijñānakṛtyatvāt / evaṃ śrotraghrāṇayoryojyam / dvayordvayostu nirvṛttirāśrayaśobhārtham / evaṃ suvibhaktasamobhayapārśva āśrayaḥ śobhano nānyathā //
body.translated_text: Given that the eye, ear, and nose each have a pair, how are the <s>dhātus</s> twenty-one [rather than more]? Although these are indeed paired, they are not different <s>dhātus</s>. Because there is multiplicity among things of the same class, but not difference in <s>dhātu</s>. Otherwise, even with the division of atoms, there would be difference in <s>dhātu</s>.

body.text: kimekaikameva cakṣurniśritya cakṣurvijñānamutpadyate nityamāhosviddva api / dve apītyucyate, spaṣṭagrahaṇāt / yathā dvayoścakṣuṣorunmiṣitayoḥ rūpagrahaṇaṃ spaṣṭaṃ bhavati na tathaikasminneveti / tadyathā ekasminnapavarake dvayoḥ pradīpayorekaṃ prabhāpratānaṃ spaṣṭataraṃ dvau pradīpau niśritya varttate / tadvadatrāpi nayo draṣṭavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Does <s>cakṣurvijñāna</s> (visual consciousness) always arise dependent on only one eye, or on both? It is said: on both, because of clearer apprehension. Just as one consciousness arises from the capacity of both [eyes], so too when one [eye] has that same capacity, there is no difference.

body.text: ekaikenendriyadvāreṇa vicitraviṣayapratyupasthāne tatprakāreṣu kiṃ krameṇa vijñānānyutpadyante āhosyidyugapadekam / yugapadekameva vicitrākāraṃ vijñānaṃ veditavyam / jihvāsaṃprāpte kavaḍe jihvākāyavijñānayornityaṃ yugapadutpattirveditavyā //
body.translated_text: When diverse objects are present at a single sense door, do consciousnesses arise sequentially with respect to those varieties, or simultaneously as one? It is said: simultaneously. Because it is not tenable that what has turned away from the former [object] would be restricted to the subsequent object-support.

body.text: śabdasyoccheditvānna deśāntareṣvaparāparotpattisaṃtānena deśāntaragamanamasti kiṃtarhi sakṛt / yathā svaprade śamavaṣṭabhya pradīpapratānavat śabdapratānasyotpādo draṣṭavyaḥ / yattvāsannatiraskṛtasya śabdasyāspaṣṭaṃ śravaṇaṃ bhavati tacchabdasya pratighātitvādāvaraṇasauṣiryasvalpoktito veditavyam //
body.translated_text: Because sound is perishable, it does not travel to other places through a continuum of successive arising in different locations; rather, it occurs just once. Just as [a consciousness] grasps [the sound] by being established in its own region, so for another [at a distance], because of having no connection with that region, it does not [arise].

body.text: ṣaṇṇāṃ vijñānānāṃ kati vijñānāni savikalpakāni katyavikalpakāni / tribhistāvadvikalpaiḥ manovijñānamekaṃ savikalpakam / trayo vikalpāḥsvabhāvavikalpo 'nusmaraṇavikalpo 'bhinirūpaṇāvikalpaśca / tatra svabhāvavikalpaḥ pratyutpanneṣu saṃskāreṣvanubhūyamāneṣu yaḥ svalakṣaṇākāro vikalpaḥ / anusmaraṇavikalpo yo 'nubhūtapūrvasaṃskārākāraḥ / abhinirūpaṇāvikalpo yo 'tītānāga tapratyutpanneṣu viparokṣeṣvabhyūhanākāro vikalpaḥ // api khalu sapta vikalpāḥ ālaṃbane svarasavāho vikalpaḥ sanimitto 'nimittaḥ paryeṣakaḥ pratyavekṣakaḥ kliṣṭo 'kliṣṭaśca vikalpaḥ / tatra ādyo vikalpaḥ pañca vijñānakāyāḥ, acitrayitvālaṃbanaṃ yathāsvaṃ viṣayeṣu svarasenaiva vahanāt / sanimittaḥ svabhāvānusmaraṇavikalpo vartamānātītaviṣayacitrīkaraṇāt / animitto 'nāgataviṣayo manorathākāro vikalpaḥ śeṣā abhinirūpaṇāvikalpasvabhāvā veditavyāḥ / tathāhyekadābhyūhamānaḥ paryeṣate, ekadā pratyavekṣate, ekadā kliṣṭo bhavati, ekadākliṣṭa iti //
body.translated_text: Of the six <s>vijñānas</s> (cognitions), how many are <s>savikalpaka</s> (conceptual) and how many are <s>avikalpaka</s> (non-conceptual)? To begin with, <s>manovijñāna</s> (mental cognition) alone is <s>savikalpaka</s> by means of three <s>vikalpas</s> (conceptualizations). The three <s>vikalpas</s> are: <s>svabhāvavikalpa</s> (intrinsic conceptualization), <s>anusmaraṇavikalpa</s> (recollective conceptualization), and <s>abhinirūpaṇāvikalpa</s> (investigative conceptualization). Among these, <s>svabhāvavikalpa</s> is that conceptualization which has the character of apprehending the particular mark (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) when presently conditioned phenomena (<s>saṃskāras</s>) are being experienced. <s>Anusmaraṇavikalpa</s> is that which has the character of previously experienced <s>saṃskāras</s>. <s>Abhinirūpaṇāvikalpa</s> is that conceptualization which has the character of conjecturing (<s>abhyūhana</s>) about past, future, and present things that are beyond direct perception. Furthermore, there are seven <s>vikalpas</s>: spontaneous engagement with the object (<s>svarasavāha</s>), with-sign (<s>sanimitta</s>), without-sign (<s>animitta</s>), searching (<s>paryeṣaka</s>), examining (<s>pratyavekṣaka</s>), afflicted (<s>kliṣṭa</s>), and unafflicted (<s>akliṣṭa</s>) conceptualization. Among these, the first <s>vikalpa</s> belongs to the five <s>vijñānakāyas</s> (sense-cognition groups), because they engage spontaneously in their respective sense-objects without elaborating upon the object. The with-sign type is <s>svabhāva</s> and <s>anusmaraṇa</s> conceptualization, because it elaborates upon present and past objects. The without-sign type is conceptualization directed toward future objects, having the character of wishful imagination (<s>manoratha</s>).
