The remaining ones should be understood as having the nature of <s>abhinirūpaṇāvikalpa</s>. For thus, when conjecturing, one sometimes searches, sometimes examines, sometimes it is afflicted, and sometimes unafflicted.

body.text: yadā rūpādiprativijñaptikaṃ vijñānaṃ tatkena kāraṇena cakṣurādivijñānamityucyate na rūpādibhijñānamiti / pañcavidhavigrahopapatteḥ rūpādivacanānupapattiḥ / kathamiti / cakṣuṣi vijñānaṃ cakṣurvijñānam, āśrayadeśe vijñānotpattitaḥ, sati ca tasmistadbhāvāt / tathāhi sati cakṣuṣi cakṣurvijñānamavaśyamutpadyate anandhānāmanandhato 'ndhakārasyāpi darśanāt / na rūpe satyavaśyam, andhānāmadarśanāditi / cakṣuṣā vijñānaṃ cakṣuvijñānam, tadvaśenāvikṛte 'pi rūpe vijñānasya vikriyāgamanatvāt / tadyathā kāmalavyādhyupahatena
body.translated_text: When cognition corresponds to form and other [objects], for what reason is it called '<s>cakṣurvijñāna</s>' (eye-cognition) and so forth, rather than 'form-cognition' (<s>rūpavijñāna</s>) and so forth? Because of the applicability of a fivefold argument, the designation by 'form' and so forth is untenable. How so? [First:] Cognition in the eye is <s>cakṣurvijñāna</s>, because cognition arises at the locus of its support (<s>āśraya</s>), and because when that [support] exists, that [cognition] occurs. For when the eye exists, <s>cakṣurvijñāna</s> necessarily arises — since those who are not blind see even darkness from the state of not being blind. But when form exists, [cognition] does not necessarily [arise], since the blind do not see. [Second:] Cognition by means of the eye is <s>cakṣurvijñāna</s>, because even when the form is unaltered, change in cognition occurs due to the influence of [the eye]. Just as by an eye afflicted with the disease of jaundice

body.text: cakṣuṣā nīlādirūpeṣvapi pītadarśanameva bhavatīti / cakṣuṣo vijñānaṃ cakṣurvijñānam, vijñānabījānubandhāccakṣuṣastannirvṛtteḥ / cakṣuṣe vijñānam, tasmai hitāhi[ta]tvāt / tathāhi vijñānasaṃprayuktenānubhavenendriyasyānugraha upaghāto vā bhavati, na viṣayasyeti / cakṣurvijñānaṃ cakṣurvijñānam, ubhayoḥ sattvasaṃkhyātatvāt na tvavaśyaṃ rūpasyeti //
body.translated_text: even with regard to blue and other forms, only a yellow appearance occurs. [Third:] Cognition belonging to the eye is <s>cakṣurvijñāna</s>, because consciousness arises from the eye through the connection of the seeds of cognition (<s>vijñānabīja</s>) with the eye. [Fourth:] Cognition for the eye is <s>cakṣurvijñāna</s>, because it is beneficial or harmful to that [eye]. For the experience (<s>anubhava</s>) associated with cognition produces either benefit or harm to the sense faculty, not to the object. [Fifth:] Eye-cognition is <s>cakṣurvijñāna</s> [as a <s>karmadhāraya</s> compound], because both [eye and cognition] belong to the category of sentient being (<s>sattvasaṃkhyāta</s>), but form does not necessarily [belong to that category].

body.text: kiṃ tāvaccakṣū rūpāṇi paśyatīti veditavyamatha vijñānam / naikaṃ nāparaṃ paśyatīti veditavyam, nirvyāpāratvāt dharmāṇām / sāmagrayāṃ tu satyāṃ darśanaprajñaptiḥ / api khalu ṣaḍbhirākāraiḥ cakṣuṣo rūpadarśane prādhānyaṃ veditavyaṃ na vijñānasya / katamaiḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ / utpattikāraṇa (ta)ḥ, cakṣuṣastadutpatteḥ / tatpadasthānataḥ, darśanasya cakṣurāśrayaṇāt / acalavṛttitaḥ, cakṣuṣo nityamekajātīyatvāt / svatantravṛttitaḥ, pratikṣaṇamutpattipratyayasāmagryanapekṣatvāt / śobhāvṛttitaḥ, tenāśrayaśobhanāt / āgamataḥ, "cakṣuṣā rūpāṇi dṛṣṭve" ti vacanāt / etacca yathoktaṃ sarva vijñānasya na saṃbhavatīti / calavṛttitvaṃ tvasya bahuprakārotpattito veditavyam //
body.translated_text: Now, should it be understood that the eye sees forms, or that consciousness [sees]? It should be understood that neither the one nor the other sees, because [both are] devoid of activity (<s>nirvyāpāra</s>) and because [their relationship is one of] defining characteristic and cause. The eye is the defining characteristic for the arising of cognition. And because cognition has an object-support (<s>sālambana</s>), that becomes the defining characteristic of the eye's 'seeing.' But for those who hold that 'the one who sees does not know, and the one who knows does not see' — they are refuted by the very fact that the cognitions of seeing and knowing are not mutually distinct. And that [position] is not correct, because the cognition of seeing is not different [from knowledge]; for the cognition of seeing and the cognition of knowing are not different from each other.

body.text: yathā dhātuṣvāyataneṣu cāsaṃskṛtaṃ vyavasthāpitamevaṃ kasmānna skandheṣvapi vyavasthāpitam / skandhārthāsaṃbhavāt / rūpādīnāmatītādiprakārābhisaṃkṣepeṇa rāśyarthaḥ skandhārtho nirdiṣṭaḥ / sa ca nityasya na saṃbhavatīti na skandheṣvasaṃskṛtavyavasthānam //
body.translated_text: Just as the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>) is established in the <s>dhātus</s> (elements) and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), why is it not also established in the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates)? Because the defining characteristic of the <s>skandhas</s> is exclusively that of being aggregational in nature (<s>saṃcayātmaka</s>), through the characteristic of production (<s>abhinirharaṇa</s>). Production is the cause and accumulation is the result. Since these two are necessarily mutually entailed, the <s>skandhas</s> are exclusively aggregational in nature. But the unconditioned is not aggregational in nature, because when the unconditioned serves as a support (<s>āśraya</s>), despite possessing [factors for] non-investigation, investigation arises — just as in the case of knowledge, where there is no obstruction through having a different object-support among the two [factors of] object-support and basis, but [obstruction occurs] through a deficiency in the basis.

body.text: kena kāraṇena ta eva dharmā skandhadhātvāyatanamukhaiḥ pṛthagdeśitāḥ / vineyānāṃ samāsavyāsanirdeśakauśalyotpādanārtham / tathāhi skandhanirdeśe ye rūpavijñāne samāsena nirdiṣṭe te dhātvāyataneṣvekādaśadhā / saptadhā ca bhittvā vyāsena
body.translated_text: For what reason are those same <s>dharmas</s> taught separately through the frameworks of <s>skandha</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātu</s> (elements), and <s>āyatana</s> (sense-bases)? For those to be trained (<s>vineya</s>) who are inclined toward either concise or extensive instruction, and who are confused in the respective applications (<s>yoga</s>) of the basis (<s>sthāna</s>) of delusion about self (<s>ātmamoha</s>) —

body.text: nirdiṣṭe yathāyogam / ye tu tatra vedanādayo vyastāḥ te dhātvāyataneṣu dharmadhātvāyatanatvena samastā iti / api khalu lakṣaṇamātravyavasthānataḥ skandhanirdeśaḥ, grāhyagrāhakagrahaṇavyavasthānato dhātunirdeśaḥ, grahaṇāya dvārabhūtasya grāhyagrāhakamātrasya vyavasthānata āyatananirdeśo veditavyaḥ / samāptamānuṣaṃgikam //
body.translated_text: they are taught as appropriate in due order. Moreover, those [factors] such as <s>vedanā</s> (feeling) and others which are listed separately there [in the <s>skandhas</s>] are grouped together in the <s>dhātus</s> and <s>āyatanas</s> as the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (element of phenomena) and <s>dharmāyatana</s> (sense-base of phenomena). Since they are separated in the <s>skandhas</s> but not elsewhere, they should not be understood as being separate substantial entities (<s>dravyāntara</s>). Others, however, speak with reference to the six-element (<s>ṣaḍdhātu</s>) level. For those in whom no confusion arises through the <s>dhātu</s> and <s>āyatana</s> framework when the <s>dharmas</s> are taught in detail — why is there a separate teaching of the <s>rūpa</s> and other <s>skandhas</s> for them, when the establishment of the unconditioned [already] exists in the <s>dhātus</s> and <s>āyatanas</s>? And that which is not included in the <s>skandhas</s> — how does he explain [this]? Because it is devoid of qualities (<s>nirguṇa</s>). The meaning is: it is devoid of all qualities. When merely hearing of its existence constitutes its 'quality,' but since no [actual] quality is found in it, it is said to be in every respect a mere name (<s>nāmamātra</s>).

body.text: ataḥ paraṃ mūlagranthasyaivārthanirdeśo draṣṭavyaḥ / arhataścaramaṃ cakṣuḥ parinirvāṇakāle paścimam / tatra dhātuḥ, cakṣurantarasyāhetutvāt / ārūpyopapannasya pṛthagjanasya cakṣurheturiti tataḥ pracyutya rūpiṇi dhātāvupapadyamānasya yasmādālayavijñānasaṃniviṣṭāccakṣurbījācca kṣurnirvartiṣyate, na tvāryasya punaranāgamanāditi // kāyadhāturna kāya ārūpyopapannasya pṛthagjanasya yaḥ kāyadhāturityetadatra vaktavyam, aṇḍagatādīnāṃ kāyasaṃbhavāt pranaṣṭakāyasya cājīvi[ta]svāditi // syānmanodhāturna mana ityatrāsaṃjñisamāpanna syāgrahaṇam, kliṣṭamanaḥsadbhāvāt //
body.translated_text: From this point onward, one should see the explanation of the meaning of the root text (<s>mūlagrantha</s>) itself. 'The last eye of an <s>arhat</s>' means: at the time of <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, the final [eye]. 'The pair of <s>āyatanas</s>' means the eye sense-base (<s>cakṣurāyatana</s>) and the form sense-base (<s>rūpāyatana</s>). 'Three <s>dhātus</s> of two aspects' [refers to the three types]. 'Immediately after <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, three equal ones without remainder' — these are the three that cease without continuation.

body.text: jāto bhūtaḥ nirvṛtti vṛddhi cādhikṛtya yathākramam // ārūpyāvacareṇa manasārūpyāvacarān svabhūmikānanāsravāṃśca dharmān vijānātītyāryaśrāvakamadhikṛtya / bāhyakaḥ pṛthagjanaḥ svabhūmikāneva vijānātīti / iha dhārmikastu kaścitpūrvaśrutaparibhāvanāvaśādūrdhvabhūmikānapyālaṃbate tadutpādanārtham //
body.translated_text: Born, become, produced, and grown — with reference to [these stages] respectively. By means of the mind (<s>manas</s>) belonging to the formless realm (<s>ārūpyāvacara</s>), the <s>dharmas</s> of the formless realm, those of one's own level, and those of lower levels are [cognized] without material support; 'final' refers to those for whom there is absolutely no form.

body.text: yathā rūpaṃ tathānubhava iti sukhādivedanīyādindriyārthadvayātsukhādivedanotpatteḥ / yathā vedayate tathā saṃjānīta iti yathānubhavaṃ nimittodgrahaṇāt / yathā saṃjānīte tathā cetayati yathāsaṃjñaṃ karmābhisaṃskaraṇāt / yathā cetayate tathā vijñānaṃ tatra tatropagaṃ bhavatīti yathābhisaṃskāraṃ viṣayeṣu gatyantareṣu ca vijñānapariṇāmāt //
body.translated_text: Just as there is form, so there is experience (<s>anubhava</s>) — because feelings of pleasure and so forth arise from the pair of faculty (<s>indriya</s>) and object (<s>artha</s>) which are to be felt as pleasure and so forth. Just as one feels, so one perceives (<s>saṃjānāte</s>) — because <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception) is occasioned by feelings of pleasure and so forth. The sign (<s>nimitta</s>) of <s>saṃjñā</s> is the accurate recognition corresponding to each cognition; <s>saṃjñā</s> operates accordingly because of such correspondence. <s>Manaskāra</s> (attention) and <s>cetanā</s> (volition) also — among the four that are not included in the external <s>āyatanas</s>, these are mental factors (<s>caitta</s>) and that which is dissociated from them is [classified as] internal.

body.text: yatra saṃkliśyate vyavadāyate ceti sendriye kāye / yenānubhaveneti sāmiṣanirāmiṣādyena yathākramam / yena nimittagrahaṇābhisaṃskāreṇetyayoniśo yoniśaśca pravṛttena / yatsaṃkliśyate vyavadāyate ceti cittadauṣṭhulyādauṣṭhulyopapattitaḥ //
body.translated_text: Where one is defiled and where one is purified — this refers to the body endowed with sense faculties (<s>sendriya kāya</s>). By which experience — this refers to [feelings] with and without material bait (<s>sāmiṣa</s>, <s>nirāmiṣa</s>) and so forth, respectively. That it has an object-support, and that which is dominant with respect to the faculty — the word '<s>rūpa</s>' in '<s>rūpāyatana</s>' is to be understood as a designation (<s>saṃjñā</s>) by the force of extending [the term] <s>rūpa</s> to include even the formless realm (<s>nirūpāvacara</s>).

body.text: ekādaśavidhāttṛṣṇāprakārādrūpādīnāmatītādiprakāravyavasthāna veditavyam / sā punaḥ apekṣātṛṣṇā abhinandanātṛṣṇā adhyavasānatṛṣṇā āmatṛṣṇā viṣayatṛṣṇā kāmatṛṣṇā samāpattitṛṣṇā duścaritaduḥkhatṛṣṇā sucaritasukhatṛṣṇā viprakṛṣṭatṛṣṇā sanikṛṣṭatṛṣṇā ca / asyāḥ tṛṣṇāyā ālaṃbanatvena yathākramamatītādayaḥ prakārā yojitavyāḥ / aparaḥ paryāyaḥ / utpannānutpannabhedato grāhakagrāhyabhedato bahirmukhāntarmukhabhedataḥ kliṣṭākliṣṭabhedato viprakṛṣṭasaṃnikṛṣṭabhedataśvātītādīni yathāyogaṃ veditavyāni / tatrotpannamatītaṃ pratyutpannaṃ ca / anutpannamanāgatam / vahirmukhamasamāhitabhūmikam / antarmukhaṃ samāhitabhūmikam / śiṣṭaḥ sugamatvānna vibhaktaḥ / duḥkhavaipulyalakṣaṇatāmupādāyeti rūpādisaṃniśrayeṇa jātthādiduḥkhapratānāt / saṃkleśabhārodvahanaṃ rūpādyāśritatvāt kleśādisaṃkleśasya / tadyathā loke yena śarīrapradeśena bhāra uhyate tatra skandhopacāro dṛṣṭaḥ, skandhena bhāramuddhahatīti //
body.translated_text: From the eleven kinds of <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving), the establishment of form and other [objects] as past and so forth should be understood. Moreover, that [craving] is threefold: <s>apekṣātṛṣṇā</s> (craving of longing), <s>abhinandanātṛṣṇā</s> (craving of delight), and <s>tatratṛṣṇā</s> (craving for that [state]). The objects of <s>tṛṣṇā</s> are fourfold. The object of <s>tṛṣṇā</s> concerning form and the other twenty-one <s>dhātus</s> should be seen as one [category]. The three realms (<s>traidhātuka</s>) constitute the second. The three times — past, future, and present — constitute the third. Internal and external constitute the fourth. All of this is [distinguished] by way of different synonymous expressions (<s>paryāya</s>).

body.text: sarvadharmabījārtha iti hetvarthamadhikṛtyālayavijñāne / kāryakāraṇabhāvadhāraṇamaṣṭādaśasu dhātuṣu ṣaṇṇāṃ vijñānadhātūnāmindriyārthadhātūnāṃ, ca yathākramam / sarvaprakāradharmasaṃgrahaṇena sūtrāntaranirdiṣṭānāṃ pṛthivīdhātvādīnāmanyeṣāmapi dhātūnāmeṣvevāṣṭādaśasu yathāyogaṃ saṃgrahaṇādveditavyam //
body.translated_text: 'Containing the seeds of all <s>dharmas</s>' — with reference to its causal meaning (<s>hetvartha</s>), this pertains to the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (store-consciousness). 'Maintaining the cause-and-effect relationship' pertains to the eighteen <s>dhātus</s>. 'Of the door and of what stands at the door' — this also pertains to the eighteen <s>dhātus</s> alone.

body.text: bījārthaḥ sarvaprakāradharmasaṃgrahārthaścāyatanārtho 'pi veditavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: The meaning of seed (<s>bījārtha</s>) and the meaning of encompassing <s>dharmas</s> of all kinds should also be understood as the meaning of <s>āyatana</s> (sense-base).

body.text: rūpādānāṃ phenapiṇḍo pamatvamasato riktataḥ tucchato 'sārataśca
body.translated_text: Of form and the rest, the foam-lump (<s>phenapiṇḍa</s>) [analogy and so forth] should be understood from the proclamation of [their] insubstantiality, emptiness, hollowness, and essencelessness

body.text: khyānādveditavyam / eteṣāṃ punaḥ sūtrapadānāmartha ātmaśucisukhanityaviparyāsapratipakṣeṇa yathākramamanātmatāmupādāyetyevamādibhiḥ padarveditavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: . Furthermore, the meaning of these <s>sūtra</s>-passages serves as the antidote to the fourfold error (<s>viparyāsa</s>) of [grasping at] self, purity, pleasure, and permanence, respectively. Even though the foam-lump [analogy] has the function of indicating and [revealing] cause, how should the analysis of compactness (<s>ghanavinirbheda</s>) be understood? Thus: the sense faculty and the object, the eye-cognition of those, <s>sparśa</s> (contact), the <s>vedanā</s> (feeling) born from that — this is the analysis of the compactness of the <s>skandhas</s>. The practice of <s>aśubhā</s> (foulness contemplation), <s>kāyānusmṛti</s> (mindfulness of the body), <s>nirveda</s> (disenchantment), <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), and the attainment of the true nature of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmatāsamāpatti</s>) — these exhaust [the path] completely.

body.text: kathaṃ kati kimarthibhiriti praśnatrayavyavasthāpanaṃ lakṣaṇavastusaṃmohayoḥ samāropasya ca prahāṇārtham /
body.translated_text: 'How, how many, and for whom' — the establishment of this triad of questions is for the purpose of eliminating the superimposition (<s>samāropa</s>) of confusion about characteristics (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) and entities (<s>vastu</s>). 'How' is the indication of characteristics. 'How many' is the indication of entities. 'For whom' is for the purpose of eliminating confusion about characteristics and entities. Superimposition is grasping in one way, and its elimination is [accomplished] in another way.

body.text: tatra kathaṃ dravyasaditi dravyasato lakṣaṇanirdeśena tatsaṃmohaḥ prahīyate / sarvāṇi dravyasantītyanena vastusaṃmohaḥ prahīyate ātmadravyābhiniveśatyājanārthamityanena samāropaḥ prahīyate / evamanyatrāpi yojyam / abhilāpanirapekṣa indriyagocarastadyathā rūpaṃ vedanetyevamādikaṃ nāmnācitrayitvā yasyārthasya grahaṇaṃ bhavati / tadanyanirapekṣastadyathārthāntaramanapekṣya yatra tadbuddhirbhavati / na yathā ghaṭādiṣu rūpādīnapekṣya ghaṭādibuddhiriti //
body.translated_text: There, 'how is something substantially existent (<s>dravyasat</s>)?' — through the indication of the characteristics of the substantially existent, the confusion about that is eliminated. 'All are substantially existent' and so forth. 'How [are factors of] defilement (<s>saṃkleśa</s>) and purification (<s>vyavadāna</s>)?' — through the indication of their characteristics, confusion about them is eliminated. Through [indicating] the intrinsic characteristics (<s>svarūpalakṣaṇa</s>) of factors of defilement and purification, confusion about entities is eliminated. And superimposition is eliminated — [that is,] the superimposition of one <s>dharma</s> upon another, as for example [superimposing] consciousness upon the eye.

body.text: saṃkleśālaṃbanaṃ saṃvṛtisat saṃkleśavṛttyarthena / ātmā saṃkleśasya nimittamityabhiniveśatyājanārtham //
body.translated_text: The object-support of defilement is <s>saṃvṛtisat</s> (conventionally existent), in the sense of being the domain of defilement's operation. 'The self is the cause of defilement' — this is for the purpose of abandoning the clinging [to self]; that is its illustration. And that which is the cause and object-support for the purification of those [beings] — defilement was taught first because it defiles in the context of defilement. Purification [is taught] first [in another sense] because those to be trained (<s>vineya</s>) seek purification.

body.text: viśuddhaye ālaṃbanaṃ paramārthasat paramajñānagocarārthena / sarvāṇi ṣaramārthasantītiti tathatāvyatirekātsarvadharmāṇām //
body.translated_text: The object-support for purification is <s>paramārthasat</s> (ultimately existent), in the sense of being the domain of the highest knowledge (<s>paramajñāna</s>). 'All are ultimately existent' — this means that apart from <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), because the intrinsic nature of all <s>dharmas</s> is not other than that, [their independent nature] is non-existent. That conventional [reality] is superimposed as 'existent' — this is to be fully known (<s>parijñeya</s>). For when there is the superimposition of conventional [reality], its intrinsic nature is not found; thus, the two truths (<s>satyadvaya</s>) are the characteristics of all <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: yena saṃkliśyate vyavadāyate ceti rāgādibhiścetasikaiḥ śraddhādibhiśceti veditavyam / yā ca tatrāvastheti rūpacittacetasikāvasthāsu prajñaptāścittaviprayuktāḥ saṃskārāḥ / yacca vyavadānamityasaṃskṛtaṃ vyavadānaṃ veditavyam / tacca yathāyogam / punastrayodaśavidhasya vijñānasya yo viṣayaḥ tajjñeyamanena pradarśitam / tatpunaḥ śrutamayaṃ jñānaṃ cintāmayaṃ jñānaṃ laukikabhāvanāmayaṃ jñānaṃ paramārthajñānaṃ paracittajñānaṃ dharmajñānam anvayajñānaṃ duḥkhajñānaṃ samudayajñānaṃ nirodhajñānaṃ mārgajñānaṃ kṣayānutpādajñānaṃ mahāyānajñānaṃ ca / ete 'nye ca yathākramamadhimuktijñānādīni veditavyāni / tatra paracittajñānaṃ parātma jñānam, parātmacittaviṣayāt / dharmajñānamadharajñānam, satyeṣvādita
body.translated_text: 'By which one is defiled and purified' — this should be understood as by mental factors such as <s>rāga</s> (attachment) and others, and by <s>śraddhā</s> (faith) and others. And the state (<s>avasthā</s>) therein should be understood. When one investigates the intrinsic nature, that entity which is the ultimate limit of reality (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>) — that itself is what is meant by <s>paramārthasat</s> (ultimately existent). That entity by which defilement and purification occur, [when understood as] otherwise-becoming — this is the indicating cause (<s>upalakṣaṇahetu</s>). Because conceptual construction (<s>kalpanā</s>) is applicable in [establishing] causality, [this knowledge] is not non-conceptual (<s>nirvikalpaka</s>). Through the cultivation of [seeing things as] distinct entities, there is no single-aspect nature, since [the knowledge arises] precisely from the non-conceptual

body.text: utpādāt / anvayajñānamūrdhvajñānam, dharmajñānādūrdhvamutpādāt / vidūṣaṇāyāsamutthāpanāyānutpāde jñāne niṣṭhāyāṃ mahārtheṣu jñānaṃ tadvidūṣaṇajñānaṃ yāvanmahārthajñānamiti yojayitavyam / mahārthatvaṃ punaḥ svaparārthatvāt //
body.translated_text: . <s>Anvayajñāna</s> (inferential knowledge) is higher knowledge (<s>ūrdhvajñāna</s>), because it arises after <s>dharmajñāna</s> (knowledge of dharmas). Knowledge [arising] when there is non-production for the purpose of refutation and exertion — [this is knowledge of non-arising]. Direct realization (<s>sākṣātkāra</s>) is <s>abhisamaya</s> (comprehension), because of the uniform nature of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), and it is shared [by all noble ones]. The distinction of <s>kṣānti</s> (patient acceptance) [is that it is] a special knowledge endowed with the purpose of accumulated realization. And thus, when there is a single knowledge of the elimination of the clearly defined characteristic through the practice of knowledge, that becomes the one true knowledge (<s>tattvajñāna</s>), by the power of its own function. <s>Kṣānti</s>, in brief, is dominated by <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight), because of the application of analytical investigation. <s>Jñāna</s> (knowledge), on the other hand, is dominated by <s>śamatha</s> (calm), because it has the characteristic of equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>). The extension of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) that occurs in between successive moments of inspiration (<s>saṃvega</s>) regarding preceding objects —

body.text: tatra avikalpanataḥ pañcabhirvijñānakāyaiḥ / vikalpanataḥ manovijñānena / hetuta ālayavijñānam / pravṛttitastadanyadvijñānam nimittata indriyārthāḥ / naimittikato vijñānāni / vipakṣapratipakṣataḥ sarāgaṃ vigatarāgaṃ sadveṣaṃ vigatadveṣamityevamādi / sūkṣmaprabhedataḥ saptavidhadurvijñānavijñaptibhedāt / saptavidhādurvijñānā vijñāptistadyathā asaṃviditavijñaptiḥ bhājanavijñaptiḥ, sarvakālamaparicchinnākāratvāt citrākāravijñaptirekasyāneka ākāro vicitraśceti durvyavasthāpanādasyāḥ sūkṣmatvam / sahabhāvavijñaptirekakālotpannāti vijñānāni kathaṃ pṛthagyathāsvaṃ viṣayaṃ paricchindantīti durvyavasthāpanātsūkṣmatvam / sūkṣmatvamiti sarvatrādhikṛtaṃ veditavyam / vipakṣapratipakṣalaghuparivṛttivijñaptiḥ kathaṃ rāgādisamastabandhanaṃ cittaṃ tanmuhureva sakṛdvītarāgādikaṃ bhavatīti / vāsanāvijñaptiḥ kathaṃ karmabhiḥ samudācaradbhiḥ cittaṃ vāsyate, na ca tasmādanyā sā vāsanā, nāpi tanmātrameva, phaladānaṃ ca prati krameṇa vṛttilābha iti / pratisaṃdhivijñaptiḥ kathamanekaprakārātmabhāvanirvartakakarmaparibhāvitaṃ sadvijñānaṃ tathāpyaparisphuṭāyāṃ maraṇāvasthāyāṃ sahasā prabuddhayānyatarakarmavāsanāmanyatarasyāṃ gatau pratisaṃdhi vadhnānīti / muktavijñaptiḥ kathamarhataścittaṃ paramaṃ niṣprapañcaṃ dharmatāprāptaṃ saṃsārocitasarvaprakārasāśravacaryā samatikrāntamanenākāreṇa vartata iti durvyavasthāpanādasyāḥ sūkṣmatvaṃ veditavyam / draṣṭādigrahaṇena draṣṭā śrotā ghrātā svādayitā spraṣṭā vijñātā cetyeṣāṃ grahaṇaṃ veditavyam //
body.translated_text: There, with respect to non-conceptualization, [consciousness is understood] through the five groups of consciousness (<s>vijñānakāya</s>); with respect to conceptualization, through mental consciousness (<s>manovijñāna</s>); as cause, [through] the <s>ālaya-vijñāna</s> (store consciousness); as functioning, [through] the consciousness other than that; as signs, [through] the sense faculties and objects; as effects, [through] the consciousnesses; as obstacle and antidote, [consciousness is] with desire, without desire, with hatred, without hatred, and so forth; as subtle distinction, from the division of the seven types of hard-to-cognize cognition (<s>durvijñāna-vijñapti</s>). The seven types of hard-to-cognize cognition are as follows: (1) unperceived cognition (<s>asaṃvidita-vijñapti</s>), (2) receptacle cognition (<s>bhājana-vijñapti</s>)—because at all times it has an undiscriminated aspect; (3) variegated cognition (<s>citrākāra-vijñapti</s>)—its subtlety is due to the difficulty of establishing that a single [consciousness] has multiple, variegated aspects; (4) co-existent cognition (<s>sahabhāva-vijñapti</s>)—its subtlety is due to the difficulty of establishing how consciousnesses arising at a single time can each separately discriminate their own respective objects. The term 'subtlety' should be understood as applying throughout [all these types]. (5) Cognition of rapid alternation between obstacle and antidote (<s>vipakṣa-pratipakṣa-laghu-parivṛtti-vijñapti</s>)—how can the mind, totally bound by desire and so forth, in a single instant become free from desire and so forth? (6) Habitual impression cognition (<s>vāsanā-vijñapti</s>)—how is the mind perfumed by active karmas, when that perfuming is neither different from the mind nor identical with it alone, and how does it gradually attain functioning toward the giving of fruit? (7) Rebirth-linking cognition (<s>pratisaṃdhi-vijñapti</s>)—how does existing consciousness, cultivated by karmas producing various types of existence, nevertheless at the unclear moment of death, suddenly, by awakening a particular karmic impression, link rebirth in a particular destiny? Liberated cognition (<s>mukta-vijñapti</s>)—how does the mind of an <s>Arhat</s>, supremely free from proliferation, having attained the nature of reality (<s>dharmatā</s>), having transcended all modes of defiled conduct habituated by <s>saṃsāra</s>, function in this manner? Its subtlety should be understood from the difficulty of establishing this. By the expression 'seer and so forth,' one should understand the inclusion of the seer, hearer, smeller, taster, toucher, and knower.

body.text: abhijñeyaṃ ṣaṇṇāmabhijñānāṃ viṣaya / gamanaviśeṣaprabhāvitatvādṛddhayabhijñāyāstadviṣayasya saṃkrāntito 'bhijñeyatvam /
body.translated_text: The object of superknowledge (<s>abhijñeya</s>) is the domain of the six superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>). Because the superknowledge of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhi-abhijñā</s>) is brought about by a special mode of going, the superknowability of its domain is [established] through transference (<s>saṃkrānti</s>).

body.text: sarāgādinimittajñānāccaritapraveśāt / atītajanmaparaṃparāgamanajñānādāgatitaḥ / anāgatotpattigamanajñānāt gatitaḥ / traidhātukanirmokṣopāyajñānānnisaraṇataḥ / sarvāṇyabhijñeyānyantyānāṃ tisṛṇāṃ savaṃviṣayatvāt /
body.translated_text: Through the knowledge of signs such as desire and so forth, [there is] penetration into [a person's] conduct (<s>carita</s>). Through knowledge of the succession of past lives, [it is knowable] by origin (<s>āgati</s>). Through knowledge of future births, [it is knowable] by destiny (<s>gati</s>). Through knowledge of the means of liberation from the three realms, [it is knowable] through escape (<s>nisaraṇa</s>). All are objects of superknowledge because the last three [superknowledges] have all [these] as their domain.

body.text: tatra rūpīti rūpaṃ tasya dharmasyātmasvabhāvastasmādasau rūpī, na tu rūpāntareṇa yuktatvāt / yāvaduktaṃ syādrūpasvabhāva iti / bhūtāśrayato 'pīti rūpāntarayogādapi rūpitvamiti darśayati, upādāyarūpasya bhūtarūpeṇa yogādbhatarūpāṇāṃ ca parasparamiti / nāndīsamudaya iti nāndyeva yasya samudayastadrūpi, na tu yathā vedanādīnāṃ pūrvikā ca nāndo samudayaḥ, pratyutpannaśca sparśādiriti / sapradeśataḥ sāvayavatvāt / deśavyāptito dikṣu pratyāsparaṇāt / deśopadeśato 'muṣyāṃ diśīti vyavadeṣṭuṃ śakyatvāt deśagocarataḥ kasmiścitpradeśe sthitasyālaṃbanībhāvāt / dvayasamagocarataḥ sattvadvayasya kasmiścitpradeśe sthitasyālaṃ vanobhāvāt / dvayasamagocarataḥ sattvadvayasya samamālaṃ vanībhāvānna tvevamarūpiṇo yathātmānubhavaṃ paraiḥ parigrahītumaśakyatvāditi / saṃbandhataścakṣurvijñānā dīnāmapi paryāyeṇa rūpitvam, rūpīndriyasaṃbandhāt / anubandhata ārūpyāṇāṃ pṛthagjanānāṃ rūpabījānubandhāt / prarūpaṇato vitarkavicārāṇāmālaṃbanaprarūpaṇāt / vyābādhanataḥ pañcānāṃ skandhānāṃ pāṇyādisaṃsparśaiḥ śokādibhiśca yathāyogaṃ rūpaṇāt bādhanādityarthaḥ / saṃprāpaṇato deśanāyā arthanirūpaṇāt / saṃcayavyavasthānataḥ paramāṇorūrdhvarūpasya sāvayavavyavasthānāt / bahirmukhataḥ kāmāvacarasya rūpasya kāmaguṇatṛṣṇāsaṃbhūtatvāt / antarmukhato rūpāvacarasya rūpasya samāpatticittatṛṣṇāsaṃbhūtatvādata evāsya manomayatvaṃ veditavyam / āyatataḥ pṛthagjanasya pūrvāntāparāntayoḥ paryantavyavasthānābhāvāt / paricchinnataḥ śaikṣasya rūpasya paryantīkṛtasaṃsāratvāt / tatkālato 'śaikṣarūpasya pratyutatpannabhavamātrāvaśeṣāt /
body.translated_text: Here, 'having form' (<s>rūpī</s>) means that form (<s>rūpa</s>) is the intrinsic nature (<s>ātma-svabhāva</s>) of that <s>dharma</s>; therefore it is 'having form'—not through a different form, because that would be illogical. Up to what was stated as 'having the nature of form.' 'Also from the basis of the great elements (<s>bhūta</s>)'—this shows that there is form-nature also through connection with another form: derived form (<s>upādāya-rūpa</s>) through its connection with elemental form, and elemental forms mutually with each other. 'Having delight as origination' (<s>nāndī-samudaya</s>): that whose origination is delight itself has that form-nature—not as in the case of feeling etc., where both prior delight is the origination and present contact etc. 'Having a location' (<s>sapradeśa</s>): because of having parts. 'Pervading a location': because of spreading in the directions. 'Being indicable by location': because it can be designated as 'in that direction.' 'Having location as its domain': because it can serve as an object while situated in some place. 'Having a domain common to two': because it serves equally as an object for two beings—but this is not so for the formless, because [formless experience] cannot be grasped by others as one experiences it oneself. 'Through connection': visual consciousness etc. also have form-nature in a secondary sense, through their connection with form-possessing sense faculties. 'Through latent connection': beings in the formless realm who are ordinary persons, through the latent connection with seeds of form. 'Through description': because thought (<s>vitarka</s>) and investigation (<s>vicāra</s>) describe their object. 'Through affliction': because the five aggregates are molded or afflicted by contacts with hands etc. and by grief etc., as appropriate—this is the meaning. 'Through bringing about understanding': because teaching ascertains the meaning. 'Through aggregate arrangement': because form above [the level of] an atom is established as having parts. 'Through being outward-directed': because desire-realm form arises from craving for sense-pleasures. 'Through being inward-directed': because form-realm form arises from craving for attainment-consciousness; hence its mind-made nature should be understood. 'Through extensiveness': because for an ordinary person there is no establishment of limits in the past and future. 'Through being limited': because the form of a learner (<s>śaikṣa</s>) has its <s>saṃsāra</s> bounded. 'Through being of that time only': because the form of a non-learner (<s>aśaikṣa</s>) [i.e., <s>Arhat</s>] has only the present existence remaining.

body.text: nidarśanato buddhādirūpasya saṃdarśanamātratvādaniṣpannatāmupādāya // tatra sarvāṇi rūpīṇi vyāvādhanarūpitvena / yathāyogaṃ śeṣairveditavyam / bahirmukhatādayastu ṣaḍ rūpibhedā vedanādisādhāraṇā veditavyāḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Through illustration': because the form of <s>Buddhas</s> etc., being merely a display, is taken as non-produced. // Among these, all [<s>dharmas</s>] are 'having form' by virtue of the form of afflicting (<s>vyāvādhana-rūpa</s>). The rest should be understood as applicable. But the six kinds of form-nature beginning with 'outward-directed' should be understood as common to feeling (<s>vedanā</s>) and so forth.

body.text: śiṣṭasya rūpivat prabheda iti / iti katham / yathā rūvitadātmato 'pīti vistareṇa rūpītyuktaṃ tathā sanidarśanatadātmato 'pi sanidarśanaṃ vistareṇa yojayitavyam / tatra sarvāṇi sanidarśanāni sarvanidarśanasaṃbandhādinārūpiṇāmapi sanidarśanatvāt //
body.translated_text: The distinction of the rest [should be understood] like [the analysis of] 'having form.' How so? Just as 'having form' was explained in detail as 'having form by its own nature also,' so 'visible' (<s>sanidarśana</s>) should be construed in detail as 'visible by its own nature also.' Among these, all are 'visible' because even formless [<s>dharmas</s>] have visibility through their connection with all-indication and so forth.

body.text: āvṛṇotyāvri yata iti gamanapratibandhārthena / āvṛṇotītyetāvati vaktavye āvriyate ceti vacanaṃ prabhādirūpasya sapratighatvavyavasthāpanārtham / taddhyāvriyata eva nāvṛṇotītyeṣā tasya jātireṣa svabhāva ityarthaḥ / paramāṇorūrdhvamityekasya paramāṇorapratighatvāt / yanna samādhivaśavarti rūpamiti samādhivaśena vartamānasyāpratighatvāt samacittakadevatāvata / prakopapadasthānaṃ yatrāśraya ālaṃbane vā dveṣa utpadyate / anena ca sapratighārthena sarvāṇisapratighāni / yathāyogaṃ veti śeṣaiḥ //
body.translated_text: 'It obstructs and is obstructed' (<s>āvṛṇoti āvriyate</s>)—this is in the sense of obstruction to movement. When it suffices to say 'it obstructs,' the additional statement 'and is obstructed' is for the purpose of establishing the resistance-nature (<s>sapratighatva</s>) of light and other such forms. For that [light etc.] is indeed obstructed but does not itself obstruct—this is its kind, this is its nature; that is the meaning. 'Above an atom' (<s>paramāṇu</s>): because a single atom has no resistance. 'Form that is not under the power of concentration (<s>samādhi</s>)': because that which operates under the power of concentration has no resistance, like deities of equanimous mind. 'A basis for arousal of agitation': where hatred arises toward the support or the object. By this meaning of 'having resistance,' all are resistant. 'As applicable'—by the remaining [categories].

body.text: āsravatadātmata āsravāṇāṃ sāsravatvamāsravasvabhāvena yuktatvāt / āsravasaṃbandhatastatsahabhuvāṃ citacaittānāṃ cakṣurādīnāṃ cāsravasaṃprayuktatvādāsrava [śraya]tvācca yathākramam / āsravabandhataḥ kuśalasāsravāṇāṃ tadvaśena punarbhavanirvartanāt / āsravānubandhato 'nyabhūmikānāmapyanyabhūmikāsravadauṣṭhulyāśrayatvāt / āsravānukūlyata iti kleśadauṣṭhulyānugatatve 'pi nirvedyabhāgīyānāmanāsravatvavyavasthāpanārtham, sarvabhavavaimukhyena
body.translated_text: 'With outflows by their own nature' (<s>āsrava-tad-ātma</s>): the contaminated nature of the outflows (<s>āsrava</s>) themselves is because they are endowed with the nature of outflows. 'Through connection with outflows': because the co-existent mental [factors] (<s>citta-caitta</s>), consciousness, and the eye etc. are respectively associated with outflows and serve as the basis of outflows. 'Through bondage of outflows': because wholesome contaminated [<s>dharmas</s>] produce further existence under their power. 'Through latent connection with outflows': because <s>dharmas</s> of other levels also serve as the basis for the bad disposition (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>) of outflows belonging to other levels. 'Through being favorable to outflows': this is for the purpose of establishing the uncontaminated nature of the [practices] belonging to the portion of definite separation (<s>nirvedha-bhāgīya</s>), even though they are accompanied by the bad disposition of defilements, because of their being turned away from all existence—

body.text: tatpratipakṣatvāt / āsravānvayato 'rhatāṃ skandhānāṃ paurvajānmikakleśasaṃbhūtatvāt // pañcaskandhāḥ sāsravāḥ / pañcadaśa ghātavo 'ntyāṃstrīn hitvā / daśāyatanānyantye dve hitvāḥ / trayāṇāṃ dhātūnāṃ dvayoścāyatanayoḥ pradeśaḥ saparivāramāryamārgamasaṃskṛtaṃ ca hitvā //
body.translated_text: because they are the antidote to those [outflows]. 'Through descent from outflows': because the aggregates (<s>skandha</s>) of <s>Arhats</s> are produced from defilements of previous lives. // The five aggregates are contaminated (<s>sāsrava</s>). Fifteen elements (<s>dhātu</s>), excluding the last three. Ten sense bases (<s>āyatana</s>), excluding the last two. A portion of three elements and two sense bases, excluding the noble path together with its retinue, and the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>).

body.text: śastrādānādiraṇahetavo rāgādayo raṇāḥ / yāvanti sāsravāṇi tāvanti saraṇāṇītyevamādi tadānubaṃdhyārthena veditavyam //
body.translated_text: Desire (<s>rāga</s>) and so forth are 'strife' (<s>raṇa</s>) because they are causes of strife such as taking up weapons and so forth. 'As many as are contaminated, that many have strife'—this and so forth should be understood in the sense of what is bound to [strife].

body.text: punarbhavādhyavasānahetavo rāgādaya āmiṣam / kathaṃ dveṣasya - punarbhavādhyavasānahetutvam / vyāvadānikadharmadveṣeṇa punarbhavādhyavasānāt //
body.translated_text: Desire and so forth are 'bait' (<s>āmiṣa</s>) because they are causes of adherence to further existence (<s>punarbhava</s>). How is hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>) a cause of adherence to further existence? Through hatred of purifying <s>dharmas</s>, there is adherence to further existence.

body.text: kāmaguṇādhyavasānahetavo rāgādayo gredhaḥ / kīdṛśena dveṣeṇa tadadhyavasānam / naiṣkramyadveṣeṇa //
body.translated_text: Desire and so forth are 'greed' (<s>gredha</s>) because they are causes of adherence to sense-pleasures (<s>kāmaguṇa</s>). Through what kind of hatred is there such adherence? Through hatred of renunciation (<s>naiṣkramya</s>).

body.text: kāmakāreṇa saṃmukhībhāvo vimukhībhāvaśca nāsaṃskṛtasya saṃbhavati nityatvāt / naivasaṃskṛtanāsaṃskṛtasya dvayāvyatirekādyaduktam - dvayamidaṃ saṃskṛtaṃ cāsaṃskṛtaṃ ceti / tatkathaṃ dvayamevameva bhavatīti / kāmakārasaṃmukhībhāvārthena saṃskṛtameveti vaktavyam / karmakleśānabhisaṃskṛtatārthenāsaṃskṛtameveti / na dvayādvayatiricyate //
body.translated_text: Facing toward and turning away at will do not occur for the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>), because it is permanent. Nor for what is neither conditioned nor unconditioned, because it does not deviate from the two, as was stated: 'This twofold [classification] is the conditioned and the unconditioned.' How then is the twofold [classification] only thus? It should be said that [something] is conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>) in the sense of being what can be faced toward at will, and unconditioned in the sense of not being fashioned by <s>karma</s> and defilements (<s>kleśa</s>). The twofold does not exceed the twofold.

body.text: tatpratibhāsamiti traidhātukaparyāpannākāram, tathatādipratibhāsasyaikāntenānucitatvena lokottaratvāt / skandhānāmekadeśaṃ samyagjñānasaṃgṛhītaṃ lokottarapratibhāsāṃśca pṛṣṭhalabdhān sthāpayitvā / taccāsaṃskṛtaṃ ca sthāpayitvā trayāṇāṃ dhātūnāṃ dvayoścāyatanayoḥ pradeśo draṣṭavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Having that appearance' means having the aspect included in the three realms, because the appearance of suchness (<s>tathatā</s>) etc. is absolutely supramundane (<s>lokottara</s>) due to being entirely unhabituated [to the three realms]. Setting aside the portion of the aggregates that is included in correct knowledge, the supramundane appearances, and the subsequently-obtained [wisdoms], and setting aside that [correct knowledge] and the unconditioned, a portion of three elements (<s>dhātu</s>) and two sense bases (<s>āyatana</s>) should be seen [as mundane].

body.text: traidhātukapratipakṣa āryamārgaḥ / sa punaḥ śrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ nityādicaturvidhaviparyāsapratipakṣatvādaviparyāsanirvikalpatayā nirvikalpaḥ / bodhisattvānāṃ rūpādisarvadharmaprapañcapratipakṣatvānniṣprapañcanirvikalpatayā nirvikalpaḥ / asaṃskṛtaṃ tu sarvavikalpāpasthānānnirvikalpaḥ /
body.translated_text: The noble path (<s>ārya-mārga</s>) is the antidote to the three realms. For <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, it is non-conceptual (<s>nirvikalpa</s>) through the non-conceptuality of non-distortion (<s>aviparyāsa</s>), because it is the antidote to the four kinds of distortion (<s>viparyāsa</s>) beginning with [the distortion of] permanence. For <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, it is non-conceptual through the non-conceptuality of non-proliferation (<s>niṣprapañca</s>), because it is the antidote to the proliferation of all <s>dharmas</s> beginning with form. The unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>), however, is non-conceptual because of the absence of all concepts.

body.text: ādyutpannaṃ pratisaṃdhikāle / prabandhotpannaṃ tata ūrdhvam / upacayotpannaṃ caturvidhenopacayena svapnāhārabrahmacaryasamāpattihetukena / āśrayatvotpannamadhyātmakamindriyam / vikārotpannaṃ sukhā divedanotpattau tadanukūla indriyapariṇāmaḥ / paripākotpannaṃ jīrṇāvastham / hānyutpannaṃ sugateścyutvādurgatāvutpadyamānasya / viśeṣotpannaṃ viparyayāt / prabhāsvarotpannaṃ krīḍāpramoṣakāṇāṃ manaḥpradūṣakāṇāṃ nirmāṇaratīnāṃ paranirmitavaśavartināṃ rūpārūpyāvacarāṇāṃ ca devānāṃ pramodabāhulyādbhogeṣu vihāre ca svavaśavarttanādyathāyogam / aprabhāsvarotpannaṃ tadanyat / saṃkrāntyutpannaṃ gamanāvasthāyām / sabījotpannamarhataścaramān skandhān varjayitvā / abījotpannaṃ caramāḥ skandhāḥ / pratibimbavibhutvanidarśanotpannaṃ jñeyaṃ vastu sabhāgaṃ vaimokṣikaṃ tāthāgataṃ ca rūpaṃ yathākramam / paraṃparotpannaṃ janmaprabandhe / kṣaṇabhaṅgotpannaṃ pratikṣaṇaṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ lakṣaṇam / saṃyogaviyogotpannaṃ priyāpriyasaṃyogaviyogāvasthāyāṃ cittasya ca sarāgavigatarāgādyavasthāyām / avasthāntarotpannaṃ kalalādyavasthāsu vyādhyādyavasthāsu ca / cyutopapādotpannaṃ sattvalokaḥ / saṃvartavivartotpannaṃ bhājanalokaḥ / pūrvakālotpannaṃ pūrvakālabhavaḥ / maraṇakālotpannaṃ maraṇakālabhavaḥ / antarotpanamantarābhavaḥ / pratisaṃdhikālotpannamupapattibhavaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Initially arisen' (<s>ādyutpanna</s>): at the time of rebirth-linking (<s>pratisaṃdhi</s>). 'Arisen in continuity' (<s>prabandhotpanna</s>): from then onward. 'Arisen through growth' (<s>upacayotpanna</s>): through four kinds of growth—caused by sleep, food, celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>), and meditative attainment (<s>samāpatti</s>). 'Arisen as basis' (<s>āśrayatvotpanna</s>): the internal sense faculty. 'Arisen through transformation' (<s>vikārotpanna</s>): when pleasant and other feelings arise, the corresponding transformation of the sense faculties. 'Arisen through maturation' (<s>paripākotpanna</s>): the state of aging. 'Arisen through decline' (<s>hānyutpanna</s>): for one who, having fallen from a happy destiny, is born in an unfortunate destiny. 'Arisen through distinction' (<s>viśeṣotpanna</s>): the reverse [of the above]. 'Arisen as luminous' (<s>prabhāsvarotpanna</s>): for the gods of the <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>, <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s>, and the form and formless realms—because of their abundance of delight, and because in enjoyments and dwelling they operate under their own control, as applicable. 'Arisen as non-luminous' (<s>aprabhāsvarotpanna</s>): the rest [of beings] other than those. 'Arisen through transference' (<s>saṃkrāntyutpanna</s>): in the state of movement. 'Arisen with seed' (<s>sabījotpanna</s>): excluding the final aggregates of an <s>Arhat</s>. 'Arisen without seed' (<s>abījotpanna</s>): the final aggregates [of an <s>Arhat</s>]. 'Arisen as reflection, pervasiveness, and illustration' (<s>pratibimba-vibhutva-nidarśanotpanna</s>): the knowable object, the similar form, the liberative form, and the <s>Tathāgata</s> form, respectively. 'Arisen in succession' (<s>paraṃparotpanna</s>): in the continuum of births. 'Arisen through momentary destruction' (<s>kṣaṇabhaṅgotpanna</s>): the characteristic of conditioned things at each moment. 'Arisen through union and separation' (<s>saṃyoga-viyogotpanna</s>): in the state of union with and separation from the pleasant and unpleasant, and in the states of the mind with desire, without desire, and so forth. 'Arisen through change of state' (<s>avasthāntarotpanna</s>): in the embryonic stages beginning with <s>kalala</s>, and in the states beginning with illness. 'Arisen through death and rebirth' (<s>cyutopapādotpanna</s>): the world of beings (<s>sattvaloka</s>). 'Arisen through contraction and expansion' (<s>saṃvarta-vivartotpanna</s>): the receptacle world (<s>bhājanaloka</s>). 'Arisen in the prior time' (<s>pūrvakālotpanna</s>): the existence of the prior time. 'Arisen at the time of death' (<s>maraṇakālotpanna</s>): the existence of the time of death. 'Arisen in the intermediate [state]' (<s>antarotpanna</s>): the intermediate existence (<s>antarābhava</s>). 'Arisen at the time of rebirth-linking' (<s>pratisaṃdhikālotpanna</s>): birth-existence (<s>upapattibhava</s>).

body.text: rūpasaṃskāraskandhaikadeśa itīndriyalakṣaṇaḥ saṃprayuktalakṣaṇaśca yathākramam / dharmadhātvāyatanaikadeśaḥ saṃprayuktasvabhāvaḥ / bhoktātmā iṣṭāniṣṭānāṃ viṣayāṇāmupalaṃbhārthena veditavyaḥ / aprāptagrāhakaṃ cakṣuḥ śrotraṃ manaśca / prāptagrāhakaṃ tadanyadindriyam / svalakṣaṇasya vartamānasya pratyekaṃ pratiniyatasya viṣayasya grāhakaṃ pañcendriyajam / svasāmānyalakṣaṇasya
body.translated_text: 'A portion of the form and formations aggregates' (<s>rūpa-saṃskāra-skandha</s>): [this refers to] the characteristic of faculties (<s>indriya</s>) and the characteristic of association (<s>saṃprayukta</s>), respectively. 'A portion of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> and dharma-sense-base': [this has] the nature of association. 'The experiencer, the self' (<s>bhoktā ātmā</s>) should be understood in the sense of perceiving pleasant and unpleasant objects. The eye, ear, and mind are apprehenders of what is not reached [i.e., distant objects]. The other sense faculties are apprehenders of what is reached [i.e., objects in contact]. That born of the five sense faculties apprehends [objects having] their own particular characteristics, present, and individually determinate. Of [objects having both] particular and general characteristics—

body.text: sarvakālasya sarvasya viṣayasya grāhakaṃ ṣaṣṭhendriyajam // pratyayasāmagrayā vijñānasyotpattimadhikṛtya prajñaptyāṃ grāhakopacāro veditavyaḥ, na tu bhūtārthena vyāpāratvād dharmāṇāmiti /
body.translated_text: of all times and of all objects, the apprehender is that born of the sixth faculty [i.e., mental consciousness]. // The metaphorical usage of 'apprehender' in designation should be understood with reference to the arising of consciousness through the totality of conditions (<s>pratyaya-sāmagrī</s>), but not in a real sense, because <s>dharmas</s> do not have [real] activity.

body.text: yattāvadgrāhakaṃ grāhyamapi tat cakṣurādīnāmapi manovijñānena grāhyatvāt / grāhakagocara evetyavadhāraṇaṃ caitasikavyudāsārtham //
body.translated_text: Now, that which is an apprehender (<s>grāhaka</s>) is also apprehendable (<s>grāhya</s>), because even the eye and other [faculties] are apprehendable by mental consciousness. The restrictive particle in 'only the domain of the apprehender' is for the purpose of excluding mental factors (<s>caitasika</s>).

body.text: śrutacintāmayatadanudharmapratipattisaṃgṛhītasyābahirmukhatvam, niṣyandadharmahetukatvāt, tadvaśena nirvāṇādyālaṃbanato draṣṭavyam / niṣyandadharmaḥ punarbuddhādīnāmadhigamānvayā deśanā veditavyā / catvāro dhātavo ghrāṇavijñānadhāturgandhadhāturjihvāvijñānadhātuḥ rasadhātuśca / dve āyatane gandharasāyatane tadanyeṣāmekadeśaḥ kāmadhātusaṃgṛhītaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Non-outward-directedness' (<s>abahirmukhatva</s>) of that which is included in [wisdom] born of learning (<s>śruta</s>) and reflection (<s>cintā</s>) and in the practice in accordance with that <s>dharma</s>—because it is caused by the outflow-<s>dharma</s>-cause (<s>niṣyanda-dharma-hetu</s>). It should be seen as having <s>nirvāṇa</s> etc. as its object through its power. The outflow-<s>dharma</s> should further be understood as the teaching that follows upon the realization of the <s>Buddhas</s> etc. The four elements (<s>dhātu</s>) are: the olfactory-consciousness element, the odor element, the gustatory-consciousness element, and the taste element. The two sense bases (<s>āyatana</s>) are the odor and taste sense bases. A portion of the others is included in the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>).

body.text: daśānāṃ dhātūnāmiti saptānāṃ vijñānadhātūnāṃ rūpaśabdadharmadhātūnāṃ ca / caturṇāmāyatanānāmiti rūpaśabdamanodharmāyatanānām //
body.translated_text: 'Of the ten elements' means of the seven consciousness-elements and the form, sound, and dharma elements. 'Of the four sense bases' means of the form, sound, mind, and dharma sense bases.

body.text: hetuphalopayogata ityutpannatvānniruddhatvācca yathākramam / saṃkleśavyavadānakāritrasamatikrāntata iti pratyutpannarāgādiśraddhādivaccittasaṃkleśavyavadānasāmarthyābhāvāt / hetuparigrahavināśato vāsanāṃ sthāpayitvā vinaṣṭatvāt / phalasvalakṣaṇabhāvābhāvato vartamāne kāle tadāhitavāsanāsadbhāvāttadādhāyakadravyābhāvācca / smarasaṃkalpādīnāṃ nimittatvamālaṃbanamātra bhāvādaveditavyam / sarveṣāmekadeśo 'nāgatapratyutpannāsaṃskṛtavarjaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Through the utilization of cause and effect' means respectively because of having arisen and having ceased. 'Having surpassed the activity of defilement and purification' means because of the absence of the capacity for mental defilement and purification, unlike present attachment and so forth and faith and so forth. 'Through the destruction of the appropriation of causes' means because, having deposited the habitual impregnation (<s>vāsanā</s>), [the cause] has perished. 'Through the absence of the own-characteristic nature of the result' means because in the present time, the deposited habitual impregnation does not [actually] exist [as the result], and the substance that deposited it is also absent. The causality of memory, thought, and so forth should be understood as being merely an object-support. A portion of all [dharmas], excluding the future, the present, and the unconditioned.

body.text: hetau satyanutpannata ityasaṃskṛtādviśeṣaṇārtham, taddhayanutpannamapi sanna hetumaditi / labdhasvalakṣaṇato 'nirvṛttasvabhāvatvāt / hetuphalānupayogatastadbījasyākṛtakṛtyatvāt tasya cānutpannatvāt //
body.translated_text: 'Being unarisen when the cause exists' is for the purpose of distinguishing [the future] from the unconditioned, for that [unconditioned] too, though unarisen, exists but does not have a cause. 'Having obtained its own characteristic' means because [the future] has an unaccomplished nature. 'Through the non-utilization of cause and effect' means because its seed has not accomplished its purpose and because it has not yet arisen.

body.text: hetuphalopayogānupayogataḥ punaranivartyatvādasthitatvācca / atītānāgataprabhāvananimittataḥ pratyutpannamadhiṣṭhāyātītānāgataprajñapteḥ / yattāmavasthāṃ
body.translated_text: 'Through both the utilization and non-utilization of cause and effect' means further because of its irreversibility and non-abiding. 'Through being the cause for the manifestation of the past and the future' means because the designation of past and future is based upon the present. 'That which [will attain] that state'

body.text: prāpsyati tadanāgatam / yatprāptaṃ tadatītamiti / kāritrapratyupasthānataścakṣurādīnāṃ vijñānāśrayādibhāvāt //
body.translated_text: 'will attain is the future; that which has been attained is the past.' 'Through the presence of activity' means because the eye and so forth function as the basis of consciousness and so forth.

body.text: atītanirdeśādhikāreṇedamapi jñāpyate - kimartha bhagavatātītādīnyeva trīṇi kathāvastūni vyavasthāpitāni na nirvāṇamiti / nirvāṇasya pratyātmavedanīyatayā nirabhilāpyatāmupādāya kathayitumaśakyatvādityarthaḥ, dṛṣṭaśrutamatavijñātavyavahārāṇāṃ bhūtabhavyavartamānādhiṣṭhānatvāt /
body.translated_text: In the context of the exposition of the past, this also is made known: for what purpose did the <s>Bhagavān</s> establish only three topics of discourse (<s>kathāvastu</s>) — past and so forth — and not <s>nirvāṇa</s>? The meaning is: because <s>nirvāṇa</s>, being to be personally experienced, is inexpressible and therefore impossible to discourse about, since the conventional usages of 'seen, heard, thought, and cognized' have their basis in the past, future, and present.

body.text: daśānāṃ dhātūnāṃ vijñānadhātūnāṃ rūpaśabdadharmadhātūnāṃ ca / caturṇāmāyatanānāṃ rūpaśabdamanodharmāyatanānām / teṣveveti śraddhādiṣu / prakṛtyāpratisaṃkhyāyeti svarasena, vinā kalyāṇamitrādibalenetyarthaḥ / ruciḥ saṃtiṣṭhata iti na kevalaṃ rucirevopapattiprātilambhikā kiṃ tarhi saha taiḥ śraddhādibhiriti / kuśalasya bhāvanā sarve śrutamayādayaḥ kuśalā dharmāveditavyāḥ / svargāḍhyakulopapattiparigrahābhyāmabhyudayahetuṃ darśyati / vyavadānānukalyaparigraheṇa prāptihetumiti / vidūṣaṇāpratipakṣādayaḥ parastānnirdekṣyante /
body.translated_text: Of ten <s>dhātus</s> (elements) — the consciousness elements, the form-element, the sound-element, and the <s>dharmadhātu</s>. Of four <s>āyatanas</s> (sense bases) — the form, sound, mind, and <s>dharma</s> sense bases. 'In those very' means in faith and so forth. 'Naturally, without analytical cessation' means spontaneously, without the force of a spiritual friend and so forth — that is the meaning. 'Inclination abides' means that it is not merely inclination that is obtained at birth, but rather together with faith and so forth. 'The cultivation of the wholesome' — all wholesome <s>dharmas</s> arising from learning and so forth should be understood. Through the appropriation of rebirth in heaven and wealthy families, the cause of worldly prosperity is shown. Through the appropriation of what is favorable to purification, the cause of attainment [of liberation is shown]. Corruption, non-antidotes, and so forth will be explained later.

body.text: tadanyaḥ kleśopakleśo duścaritasamutthāpaka iti sa punaryaḥ kāmā[va]caro 'naiḥsargikaḥ, naiḥsargikastu yo duścaritasamutthāpakaḥ so 'ku[śa]laḥ / tadanyo nivṛtāvyākṛto veditavyaḥ / hiṃsāpūrvakaṃ caityaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati yatrorabhramahiṣādayo hanyante / kudṛṣṭipūrvakaṃ yatrānaśanādibhiḥ puṇyārthino varārthinaśca kliśyanta iti / ākṣepakaṃ vā paripūrakaṃ veti durgatimadhikṛtya / sugatau tu paripūrakameva, yenātropapanno dāridrayādikaṃ vyasanaṃ pratyanubhavati / kuśalāntarāyikā dharmā abhīkṣṇaṃ gaṇasaṃnipātādayaḥ //
body.translated_text: The other afflictions and secondary afflictions that give rise to misconduct — among these, that which belongs to the desire realm and is non-liberative, and that which is non-liberative and gives rise to misconduct, is unwholesome. What is other than that should be understood as obstructed-indeterminate (<s>nivṛtāvyākṛta</s>). 'Preceded by violence, one establishes a shrine (<s>caitya</s>)' means where sheep, goats, buffaloes, and so forth are slaughtered. 'Preceded by wrong views' means where those seeking merit or boons are tormented through fasting and so forth. 'Either projecting or completing' refers to the lower destinies. But for the happy destinies, it is completing only — by which one, having been reborn here, experiences the misfortune of poverty and so forth. <s>Dharmas</s> that obstruct the wholesome are frequent assembly gatherings and the like.

body.text: aṣṭau dhātavaścakṣuḥ śrotraghrāṇājihvākāyagandharasaspraṣṭavyadhātavaḥ / aṣṭāvāyatanāni tānyeva / aduṣṭāprasannacitasyeti kuśalākuśalaviparyayaṃ darśa[ya]ti / taireva parigṛhītā iti tadākāratvena manojalpasukhavṛttatvāt / teṣāmevābhilāpavāsaneti nāma kāyādibhiścitavāsanāyatyāmabhilāpapravṛttaye / tatparigṛhīteścittacaitasikairdharmairyatsamutthāpitamityapraduṣṭāprasannacittasya nāmādyabhilāpākārai[ḥ] / akliṣṭākuśalacetaso yadyasya
body.translated_text: Eight <s>dhātus</s> (elements): the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, smell, taste, and tangible-object elements. Eight <s>āyatanas</s> (sense bases) are those very same. 'Of a mind that is neither corrupted nor clear' shows the converse of wholesome and unwholesome. 'Appropriated by those very [names]' means because [consciousness] operates easily through mental discourse in the form of those [names]. 'The habitual impregnation of expression of those very [names]' means name-collections and so forth, for the future operation of expression through impregnation accumulated by body and so forth. 'That which is produced by the mind and mental factors appropriated by those' means through the modes of expression of names and so forth, of a mind that is neither corrupted nor clear. If, for one whose mind is neither afflicted nor unwholesome,

body.text: na kliṣṭaṃ nāpi kuśalaṃ ceto bhavati, tata airyāpathikādyavyākṛtaṃ bhavatyanyathā kuśalākuśalaṃ yathāyogamiti / yathāpi tadapratisaṃkhyāyeti kuśalatvādviśepayati, akliṣṭacitta ityakuśalatvāt / pratisaṃkhyāya bhaiṣajyaṃ niṣevate sarvavyādhipratipakṣeṇārogyārtham / adhigamaniṣyandato 'vyākṛtaṃ nirmāṇacittaṃ sahajāmiti yaiścittacaitasikaiḥ vikrīḍanārthaṃ nirmāṇaṃ nirmemīyate / sattvahitārtha tu kuśalaṃ veditavyamiti // nidarśanataḥ kuśalādikaṃ yadbuddhādayo vineyārthavaśātsaṃdarśayanti / aku[śa]lasya kathaṃ saṃdarśanam / corādi nirmāya tadanyasattvabhīṣaṇārtha karacaraṇaśiraśchedādisaṃdarśanāt //
body.translated_text: the mind is neither afflicted nor wholesome, then it becomes indeterminate in the manner of deportment and so forth; otherwise, it is wholesome or unwholesome as appropriate. 'Without analytical [cessation]' also distinguishes from wholesomeness; 'of unafflicted mind' from unwholesomeness. 'Having analyzed, one resorts to medicine' — for the purpose of health through the antidote to all diseases. 'As the outflow of attainment, the indeterminate transformation-mind (<s>nirmāṇacitta</s>) and its concomitants' means those mind and mental factors by which transformation is created for the purpose of sport. But for the purpose of benefiting beings, it should be understood as wholesome. 'By way of demonstration' — that which <s>Buddhas</s> and others demonstrate for the sake of those to be trained, as wholesome and so forth. How is the unwholesome demonstrated? By creating [the appearance of] thieves and so forth, and demonstrating the cutting of hands, feet, and heads to frighten other beings.

body.text: avītarāgasyeti pradeśavairāgyeṇāpyayuktasyāsamādhilābhina ityarthaḥ / itarathā hyanāgamyaṃ kāmapratisaṃyuktaṃ prāpnuyāt / saha samādhilābhāt prahāṇābhirativipakṣabhūtasya dauṣṭhu[lya]sya prahāṇāt pradeśavairāgyamastīti veditavyam / bāhyaṃ tviha rūpādikamavītarāgakarmādhipatyanirvṛttatvāt kāmapratisaṃyuktam / sarvasattvasādhāraṇakarmādhipatyasaṃbhūtavacanamavītarāgakarmaṇā rūpārūpyāvacareṣvapi vījino 'stitvāt / catvāro dhātavo gandharasaghrāṇajihvāvijñānadhātavaḥ / dve āyatane gandharasāyatane / tadanyeṣāmekadeśaḥ rūpārūpyāvacarānāsravavarjaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Of one who has not become dispassionate' means one who is not endowed even with partial dispassion, that is, one who has not obtained <s>samādhi</s> (concentration). Otherwise, one would arrive at the <s>anāgamya</s> (preliminary meditation) being associated with the desire realm. It should be understood that together with the attainment of <s>samādhi</s>, there is partial dispassion through the abandonment of the unsuitability (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>) that is the opponent of the joy of abandonment. But external [dharmas] such as form and so forth are here associated with the desire realm because they are produced under the sovereignty of <s>karma</s> of one who has not become dispassionate. The statement of being produced under the sovereignty of <s>karma</s> common to all beings is because even in the form and formless realms, the seed of the <s>karma</s> of one not yet dispassionate exists. Four <s>dhātus</s>: the smell, taste, nose-consciousness, and tongue-consciousness elements. Two <s>āyatanas</s>: the smell and taste sense bases. A portion of the others, excluding those belonging to the form and formless realms and the uncontaminated.

body.text: caturo dhātūn dve cāyatane sthāpayitvānantaroktāni / tadanyeṣāṃ skandhadhātvāyatanānāmekadeśaḥ kāmarūpyāvacarānāsravavarjyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Setting aside those four elements and two sense bases just mentioned, a portion of the remaining <s>skandhas</s>, <s>dhātus</s>, and <s>āyatanas</s>, excluding those belonging to the desire realm, form realm, and the uncontaminated.

body.text: caturṇā skandhānāṃ vedanādīnām / trayāṇāṃ dhātūnāṃ manodharmamanovijñānadhātūnām / dvayorāyatanayormanodharmāyatanayoḥ / pradeśaḥ kāmarūpāvacarānāsravavarjyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Of four <s>skandhas</s> — feeling (<s>vedanā</s>) and so forth. Of three <s>dhātus</s> — the mind-element, <s>dharma</s>-element, and mind-consciousness-element. Of two <s>āyatanas</s> — the mind and <s>dharma</s> sense bases. A portion, excluding those belonging to the desire realm, form realm, and the uncontaminated.

body.text: ekadeśavairāgyaṃ bhūmimadhikṛtya yāvadaṣṭamasya kleśaprakārasya prahāṇāt / sakalavairāgyaṃ nava [ma]sya prahāṇāt / satkāyavairāgyaṃ vā punaradhikṛtya śaikṣasyaikadeśavairāgyamaśaikṣasya sakalavairāgyaṃ veditavyam / prativedhavairāgyaṃ darśanamārgeṇa / upaghātavairāgyaṃ laukikena mārgeṇa / samuddhātavairāgyaṃ lokottareṇeti veditavyam / daśavairāgyāṇītyatra prātikūlyārtho vairāgyārtho veditavyo nāvaśyaṃ prahāṇārthaḥ / uccataraṃ sthānaṃ prāptavato nihīnesthāne ityuccataraṃ nagaraśraiṣṭhayādisthānaṃ prāptavato grāmamahattarādisthāne nihīne / bālānāṃ nirvāṇa iti tasya śāntatvājñānāt satkāyābhiṣvaṅgācca / pratilabdhadarśanamārgasya traidhātuka iti saṃskāraduḥkhatāṃ parijñātavataḥ sarvasāsrava[va]stunirvedāt / prakṛtyā vairāgyaṃ prakṛtivairāgyaṃ yāvatprahāṇena vairāgyaṃ prahāṇavairāgyamiti padavigrahajātirveditavyā //
body.translated_text: Partial dispassion (<s>ekadeśavairāgya</s>) with respect to a level (<s>bhūmi</s>) is through the abandonment of up to the eighth type of affliction. Complete dispassion (<s>sakalavairāgya</s>) is through the abandonment of the ninth. Or again, with respect to the perishable body (<s>satkāya</s>), partial dispassion pertains to the learner (<s>śaikṣa</s>) and complete dispassion to the non-learner (<s>aśaikṣa</s>). Penetrating dispassion (<s>prativedhavairāgya</s>) is through the path of seeing (<s>darśanamārga</s>). Suppressive dispassion (<s>upaghātavairāgya</s>) is through the mundane path. Eradicating dispassion (<s>samuddhātavairāgya</s>) should be understood as through the supramundane path. 'The ten dispassions' — here, the meaning of dispassion should be understood as aversion, not necessarily as abandonment. 'Of one who has obtained a higher position, in a lower position' means of one who has obtained a higher position such as city chief and so forth, in a lower position such as village headman. 'Of the immature toward <s>nirvāṇa</s>' means because of not knowing its peaceful nature and because of attachment to the perishable body (<s>satkāya</s>). 'Of one who has obtained the path of seeing, toward the three realms' means because of disgust toward all contaminated things, having fully comprehended the suffering of conditioned existence (<s>saṃskāraduḥkhatā</s>). 'Dispassion by nature is natural dispassion' up to 'dispassion through abandonment is abandonment-dispassion' — this type of word-analysis should be understood.

body.text: mokṣaprayuktasya kuśalaṃ śaikṣamiti saṃbhṛtasaṃbhārāvasthāyāḥ prabhṛtimokṣārtha prayuktasya veditavyam / saṃbhṛtasaṃbhārāvasthā punarādhigāmikamokṣabhāgīyāvasthā veditavyā / daśānāṃ dhātūnāṃ vijñānarūpaśabdadharmadhātūnām / caturṇāmāyatanānāṃ rūpaśabdamanodharmāyatanānām /
body.translated_text: 'The wholesome of one engaged in liberation is the learner's (<s>śaikṣa</s>)' should be understood as pertaining to one engaged for the sake of liberation from the stage of having accumulated the requisites onward. The stage of having accumulated the requisites should be understood as the state of the portion conducive to liberation leading to attainment. Of ten <s>dhātus</s> — the consciousness-elements, form-element, sound-element, and <s>dharmadhātu</s>. Of four <s>āyatanas</s> — the form, sound, mind, and <s>dharma</s> sense bases.

body.text: śikṣāyāṃ niṣṭhāgatasyetyadhiśīlamadhicittamadhiprajñaṃ ca śikṣāyāṃ niṣṭhāgatasyārhata ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Of one who has reached the culmination of training' means of an <s>Arhat</s> who has reached the culmination of the training in higher morality (<s>adhiśīla</s>), higher mind (<s>adhicitta</s>), and higher wisdom (<s>adhiprajñā</s>).

body.text: pṛthagjanasya kuśalādikamiti mokṣaprayuktavarjasya / sa hi śikṣāyā[ma]bhiśikṣaṇācchaikṣa ucyata iti / śaikṣasya kliṣṭāvyākṛtamityatra kliṣṭamakuśalaṃ nivṛtāvyākṛtaṃ ca yathāsaṃbhavam / avyākṛtaṃ punaranivṛtāvyākṛtaṃ veditavyam //
body.translated_text: 'The wholesome and so forth of the ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>)' means of one not engaged in liberation. For one is called a 'learner' (<s>śaikṣa</s>) because of training in the training. 'The afflicted and indeterminate of the learner' — here, 'afflicted' means unwholesome and obstructed-indeterminate, as applicable. 'Indeterminate' should be understood as unobstructed-indeterminate.

body.text: parikalpitā kliṣṭā dṛṣṭirasaddharmaśravaṇapūrvikā pañca daṣṭayaḥ / parikalpitagrahaṇaṃ sahajasatkāyāntagrāhadṛṣṭivyudāsārtham / antagrāhadṛṣṭiḥ kīdṛśī sahajā / ucchedadṛṣṭiryato 'bhisamayaprayuktasyottrāso bhavatyatha kastarhi me ātmeti / dṛṣṭisthānaṃ dṛṣṭisahabhuvo dharmāstadvījaṃ ca tathaiva vicikitsāsthānamapi veditavyam / ye ca dṛṣṭau vipratipannāḥ kleśopakleśā iti ye dṛṣṭimukhena pravṛttā tadālaṃbanāśca rāgādayaḥ / sarveṣāmekadeśo bhāvanāprahātavyānāsravavarjaḥ //
body.translated_text: The conceptually constructed (<s>parikalpita</s>) afflicted views are the five views preceded by hearing wrong doctrine (<s>asaddharma</s>). The qualification 'conceptually constructed' is for the purpose of excluding the innate (<s>sahaja</s>) view of the perishable body and extreme view. What is the innate extreme view like? It is the annihilationist view, because terror arises for one engaged in penetration (<s>abhisamaya</s>): 'Then who indeed is my self?' The basis of views consists of the <s>dharmas</s> coexistent with views and their seeds; similarly, the basis of doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>) should also be understood. 'The afflictions and secondary afflictions that are opposed to views' means those such as attachment and so forth that operate through the gateway of views and have those [views] as their object-support. A portion of all, excluding those to be abandoned by cultivation and the uncontaminated.

body.text: darśanaprahātavyāviparyayeṇa sāsravā iti parikalpitakliṣṭadṛṣṭayādikādanye sāsravā ityarthaḥ / atra punaḥ sāsravagrahaṇena nirvedhabhāgīyānāmapi grahaṇaṃ veditavyaṃ dauṣṭhulyānubandhārthena / sarveṣāmekadeśaḥ darśanaprahātavyānāsravavarjaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Contaminated by the converse of what is to be abandoned by seeing' means those contaminated [dharmas] other than the conceptually constructed afflicted views and so forth. Here, moreover, by the mention of 'contaminated,' the inclusion of the faculties conducive to penetration (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>) should also be understood, for the purpose of the connection with unsuitability (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>). A portion of all, excluding those to be abandoned by seeing and the uncontaminated.

body.text: skandhānāmekadeśo 'prahātavyaḥ, lokottaro mārgastatpṛṣṭalabdhaśca / daśānāṃ [dhātūnāṃ caturṇā cāyatanānām (ekadeśa) iti] sa cā saṃskṛtaṃ ca / kīdṛśo rūpaśabdadhātū na prahātavyau / aśaikṣasya kuśala kāyavākkarmasvabhāvau /
body.translated_text: A portion of the <s>skandhas</s> is not to be abandoned — the supramundane path and that which is subsequently obtained from it. Of ten <s>dhātus</s> and four <s>āyatanas</s>, [a portion] — that [uncontaminated dharma] and the conditioned. What kind of form-element and sound-element are not to be abandoned? Those that are of the nature of the bodily and verbal actions of the non-learner's (<s>aśaikṣa</s>) wholesome [conduct].

body.text: avidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārā ityevamādi / tatra asmin satīdaṃ bhavati nirīhapratyayotpattitāmupādāya / sati kevalaṃ pratyaye phalaṃ bhavati, na tu phalotpādanaṃ prati pratyayasya kācidīhetyarthaḥ / asyotpādādidamutpadyate anityapratyayotpattitāmupādāya, na hyanutpādikāraṇāt kiṃcidutpadyamānaṃ kārya siddhamiti kṛtvā / avidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārā ityevamādi samarthapratyayotpattitāmupādāya nirīhakatvānityatve 'pi sati na yataḥ kutaścit pratyayāt sarvameva phalamutpadyate, kiṃtarhi samarthāt / tadyathāvidyātaḥ saṃskārā yāvajjātito jarāmaraṇamiti //
body.translated_text: 'Conditioned by ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), formations (<s>saṃskāras</s>) [arise]' and so forth. Therein, 'when this exists, that comes to be' takes up the production [of the result] from a condition without effort (<s>nirīha</s>). The meaning is: when there is merely a condition, the result comes to be, but the condition has no effort directed toward the production of the result. 'From the arising of this, that arises' takes up the production from an impermanent condition — for an effect being produced from a non-arising cause would not be established. 'Conditioned by ignorance, formations [arise]' and so forth takes up the production from a competent condition — although [conditions are] effortless and impermanent, not every result arises from any condition whatsoever; rather, [it arises] from a competent [condition]. For example, from ignorance [arise] formations, up to: from birth [arise] aging and death.

body.text: yānyavidyādīni dvādaśāṅgāni vibhaktāni tānyeva punaḥ samasya catvāryaṅgāni bhavantyākṣepā ṅgādīni / etāvacca pravṛttinirdeśe nirdeṣṭavyam yaduta hetukāle yenākṣipyate yaccākṣipyate phalakāle yenābhinirvartyate yaccābhinirvatyate tadetatsarvamebhiraṅgainirdiṣṭaṃ veditavyam / tatra ākṣepakāṅgamavidyāsaṃskārā vijñānaṃ ca, anāgatajanmābhinirvṛttaye satyeṣvajñānapūrvakeṇa karmaṇā cittavāsanārthena / ākṣiptāṅgaṃ nāmarūpaṃ ṣaḍāyatanaṃ sparśo vedanā ca, tayā cittavāsanayā nāmarūpādīnā māyatyāṃ pūrvotarasaṃniśrayakrameṇābhinirvṛtaye bījapuṣṭitaḥ / abhinirvartakāṅgaṃ tṛṣṇā upādānaṃ bhavaśca, aprahīṇakāmādi tṛṣṇādivasena kāmādiṣu sucaritaduścaritaprakāraratipūrvakeṇa chandarāgeṇa sopādāne vijñāne sati maraṇāvasthāyāṃ phaladānaṃ prati chandarāgānurūpyāntarakarmavāsanābhimukhībhāvāt / abhinirvṛttyaṅgaṃ jātirjarāmaṇaṃ ca, tena prakāreṇa karmāntaravāsanābhimukhye satyanyatarasmin gatiyonyādibhedabhinne nikāyasabhāge yathākṣipte nāmarūpādinirvṛtteḥ / jātijarāmaraṇavacanaṃ saṃskṛtalakṣaṇatrayādhikāreṇodvejanārtham /
body.translated_text: Those very twelve limbs beginning with ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) that have been analyzed, when combined again, become four limbs beginning with the projecting limb. And this is what must be indicated in the exposition of occurrence: namely, at the time of the cause, that by which [a new existence] is projected and that which is projected; and at the time of the result, that by which [it] is actualized and that which is actualized — all of this should be understood as indicated by these limbs. Therein, the projecting limb (<s>ākṣepāṅga</s>) consists of ignorance, formations, and consciousness — for the actualization of future birth, through action preceded by non-knowledge, for the purpose of impregnating the mind with <s>vāsanā</s> (habitual tendencies). The projected limb (<s>ākṣiptāṅga</s>) consists of name-and-form (<s>nāmarūpa</s>), the six sense bases (<s>ṣaḍāyatana</s>), contact (<s>sparśa</s>), and feeling (<s>vedanā</s>) — through that mental impregnation, for the actualization of name-and-form and so forth in the future in the order of successive dependence, through the nourishment of the seed. The actualizing limb (<s>abhinirvartakāṅga</s>) consists of craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>), clinging (<s>upādāna</s>), and becoming (<s>bhava</s>) — because for one who has not abandoned craving for sensual pleasures and so forth, through desire and attachment (<s>chandarāga</s>) preceded by delight in the manner of good and bad conduct regarding sensual pleasures and so forth, when there is consciousness with clinging, at the time of death, the intermediate <s>karma</s>-impregnation corresponding to desire and attachment turns toward [the next existence] for the bestowal of its fruit. The actualized limb (<s>abhinirvṛttyaṅga</s>) consists of birth (<s>jāti</s>) and aging-and-death (<s>jarāmaraṇa</s>) — because, in that manner, when the intermediate <s>karma</s>-impregnation has turned [toward a destiny], name-and-form and so forth are actualized in whatever class-homogeneity (<s>nikāyasabhāga</s>) was projected, differentiated by the distinctions of destiny, mode of birth, and so forth. The mention of 'birth, aging, and death' is for the purpose of evoking revulsion, in the context of the three characteristics of the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛtalakṣaṇa</s>).

body.text: jarāmaraṇasyaikāṅgakaraṇaṃ vināpi jarāṃ maraṇasaṃbhavāt / na tvevaṃ jarāyujāyāṃ yonau vinā nāmarūpādibhiḥ ṣaḍāyatanādīnāṃ saṃbhava ityeṣāṃ pṛthagaṅgīkaraṇaṃ veditavyam //
body.translated_text: The combining of aging and death into one limb is because death is possible even without aging. But it is not the case that in the womb-born mode of birth, the six sense bases and so forth are possible without name-and-form and so forth — therefore, the separate enumeration of these [as distinct limbs] should be understood.

body.text: aṅgapratya[yatvavya]vasthānaṃ caturaḥ pratyayānadhikṛtya / tatra tāvadavidyā saṃskārāṇāṃ pūrvotpannāvāsanato hetupratyayaḥ, tatparibhāvitasaṃtānotpannānāṃ karmaṇāṃ punarbhavābhisaṃskaraṇasāmarthyāt tatkālasamudācāriṇī / āvedhataḥ samanantarapratyayaḥ, tadākṣepakaviśeṣeṇa saṃskārasrotānupravṛtteḥ / manaskārata ālaṃbanapratyayaḥ, mūḍhāvasthāyā agratādibhirayoniśomanaskārālaṃbanībhāvāt / sahabhāvato 'dhipatipratyayaḥ, tadādhipatyena tatsaṃprayuktāyāścetanāyā viparītālaṃbanābhisaṃskaraṇāt /
body.translated_text: The establishment of the limbs as conditions is with reference to the four <s>pratyayas</s> (conditions). Therein, first, ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) is the causal condition (<s>hetupratyaya</s>) of formations through the impregnation previously produced — because of the capacity of the actions produced in the continuum cultivated by that [ignorance] to fashion renewed existence, [ignorance] operates at the time of those [actions]. It is the immediately preceding condition (<s>samanantarapratyaya</s>) through penetration — because the stream of formations continues in accordance with the specific projection by that [ignorance]. It is the object-support condition (<s>ālaṃbanapratyaya</s>) through attention — because in the state of delusion, [ignorance] becomes the object-support of unwise attention through grasping and so forth. It is the dominant condition (<s>adhipatipratyaya</s>) through coexistence — because under its dominance, the volition (<s>cetanā</s>) associated with it fashions [experience] with an inverted object-support.

body.text: avidyā bhave sattvān saṃmohayati, tadāvṛtteḥ pūrvāntāparāntamadhyāntānāṃ yathābhūtāparijñānāt / yata evaṃ vicikitsati - kiṃ nvahamabhūvamati[te] 'dhvanyāhosvinnābhūvamityevamādi / pratyayaśca bhavati saṃskārāṇām tadvaśena punarbhavikakarmopacayāt / saṃskārā gatiṣu sattvāna vibhajanti, karmavaśena sattvānāṃ gatyantaragamanavaicitryāt / pratyayāśca bhavanti vijñānasya vāsanāyāḥ, āyatyā nāmarūpābhinirvṛttaye bījapoṣaṇāt / vijñānaṃ karmabandhaṃ dhārayati, saskārā hitavāsanāsahotpatteḥ / pratyayaśca bhavati nāmarūpasya, mātuḥ kukṣau vijñānāvakrāntyā nāmarūpavivṛddhigamanāt / nāmarūpamātmabhāvaṃ sattvān grāhayati tannivṛttyā sattvānāṃ nikāyasabhāgāntarabha janāt / nāmarūpādīnāṃ ṣaḍāyatanādipratyayabhāvaḥ pūrvāṅgasaṃniśrayeṇottarāṅganirvṛttito draṣṭavyaḥ / ṣaḍāyatanamātmabhāvaparipūriṃ
body.translated_text: <s>Avidyā</s> (ignorance) causes confusion in beings regarding existence, because due to its obstruction there is no true understanding of the past, future, and middle periods; hence one doubts thus — 'Did I indeed exist?' regarding that time, 'Or did I not exist?' and so forth. It is also a condition of <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations), because under its power there is accumulation of karma leading to rebirth. The <s>saṃskāras</s> distribute beings among the <s>gatis</s> (destinies), because through the power of karma there is diversity in beings' passage to different destinies. They are also conditions of the imprinting of <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness), because they nourish the seeds for the future production of <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form). <s>Vijñāna</s> carries the karmic bond, because the consciousness-link arises together with the imprints deposited by the <s>saṃskāras</s>. It is also a condition of <s>nāmarūpa</s>, because through the descent of consciousness into the mother's womb, name-and-form proceed to develop. <s>Nāmarūpa</s> causes beings to grasp a personal existence, because through its functioning beings take birth in different classes of beings. The condition-relationship of <s>nāmarūpa</s> and the rest to <s>ṣaḍāyatana</s> (six sense bases) and so forth should be understood as the arising of each subsequent link depending on the preceding link. The <s>ṣaḍāyatana</s> causes beings to grasp the full development of their personal existence

body.text: ca sattvān grāhayati, tannivṛttāvindriyāntarāvaikalyāt / pratyayaśca bhavati sparśasya / sparśo viṣayopabhoge sattvān pravartayati, tanmukhena sukhavedanīyāditrividhaviṣayopabhogāt / pratyayaśca bhavati vedanāyāḥ / vedanā janmopabhoge ca sattvān pravartayati, tadadhiṣṭhāneneṣṭādikarmavipākopabhogāt / pratyayaśca bhavati tṛṣṇāyāḥ, tatsaṃprayogādyabhilāṣamukhena tṛṣṇotpatteḥ / tṛṣṇā janmani sattvānākarṣati, tadvaśena janmāntarasroto 'nupacchedāt / pratyayaśca bhavatyupādānasya, āsvādaprārthanāmukhena kāmādiṣu chandarāgapravṛtteḥ / upādānaṃ punarbhavādānāya sopādānaṃ ca sattvānāṃ vijñānaṃ karoti, narakādigativiśiṣṭapunarbhavapratisaṃdhaye karmavāsanāniyamāt / pratyayaśca bhavati bhavasya, tadvaśena saṃskāravāsanayovṛttilābhāt / bhavaḥ punarbhave sattvānabhimukhīkaroti, anantaragatyantarāvāhanāt pratyayaśca bhavati jāteḥ, tato nikāyasabhāgāntaranirvṛtteḥ / jātirnāmarūpādyānupūrvyā sattvānabhinirvartayati, uttarottarāvasthāntarāvāhanāt / pratyayaśca bhavati jarāmaraṇasya, jātau satyāṃ tatprabandhasyānyathātvavināśasaṃbhavāt / jarāmaraṇaṃ punaḥpunarvayaḥ pariṇāmena jīvitapariṇāmena ca sattvān yojayati, yauvanāyuṣovināśena yojanāt //
body.translated_text: and this is because through its functioning there is no deficiency in the various sense faculties. It is also a condition of <s>sparśa</s> (contact). <s>Sparśa</s> engages beings in the enjoyment of objects, because through it there is enjoyment of three kinds of objects — those to be experienced as pleasant and so forth. It is also a condition of <s>vedanā</s> (feeling). <s>Vedanā</s> engages beings in birth and enjoyment, because based on it there is enjoyment of the ripened results of karma such as the desirable and so forth. It is also a condition of <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving), because through association with feeling, craving arises by way of longing. <s>Tṛṣṇā</s> draws beings toward birth, because under its power the stream toward future births is not cut off.
