It is also a condition of <s>upādāna</s> (clinging), because through the desire for enjoyment, attachment and passion arise toward sense pleasures and the rest. <s>Upādāna</s> makes the consciousness of beings endowed with clinging for the purpose of taking up future existence, because there is a determination of karmic imprints for the reunion with future existence distinguished by destinies such as the hells and so forth. It is also a condition of <s>bhava</s> (existence), because under its power the imprints of the formations obtain their function. <s>Bhava</s> turns beings toward future existence, because it brings about passage to a subsequent destiny without interval. It is also a condition of <s>jāti</s> (birth), because from it arises the production of a different class of beings. <s>Jāti</s> brings beings into manifestation through the successive stages of name-and-form and so forth, because it conveys one to ever-subsequent states. It is also a condition of <s>jarāmaraṇa</s> (aging-and-death), because when birth exists, the alteration and destruction of that continuum become possible.

body.text: vijñānasya karma[saṃ]kleśasaṃgrahaṇaṃ saṃskāravāsanāprabhāvitatvādvijñānāṅgasyaḥ
body.translated_text: The gathering of karmic defilement by <s>vijñāna</s> is because the consciousness-link is empowered by the imprints of the <s>saṃskāras</s>. The gathering of defilement through the birth-link is because prior to that it is caused by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). Because of the connection of the imprints of karma and defilements, there is the gathering of both karma and defilements.

body.text: niṣkartṛkārtha īśvarādikartṛrahitatvāt / sahetukārtho 'vidyādihetukatvāt / niḥsatvārthaḥ svayamanātmatvāt / paratantrārthaḥ pratyayādhīnatvāt / nirīhakārthaḥ pratyayānāṃ nirvyāpāratvāt / anityārtho 'śāśvatatvāt / kṣaṇikārtha utpattikālāt pareṇānavasthānāt / hetuphalaprabandhānupacchedārthaḥ kāraṇakṣaṇa nirodhasamakālaṃ kāryakṣaṇotpādāt /
body.translated_text: The meaning of 'without an agent' is because it is devoid of a creator such as <s>Īśvara</s> and the like. The meaning of 'having causes' is because it is caused by <s>avidyā</s> and the rest. The meaning of 'without a self' is because <s>vijñāna</s> and the rest are devoid of a self. The meaning of 'having those conditions and no other conditions' is that the <s>saṃskāras</s> are conditioned by <s>avidyā</s> and not by <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> (view of the self-existing body), and so forth.

body.text: anurūpahetuphalaparigrahārthaḥ sarvataḥ sarvasyāsaṃbhavāt / vicitrahetuphalārtho 'nekaikajātīyātkāraṇādekānekajātīyakāryotpatteḥ / pratiniyatahetuphalārthaḥ saṃtānāntarāphalanāt //
body.translated_text: The meaning of 'grasping cause and effect in accordance' is because it is impossible that everything arises from everything. The meaning of 'having diverse causes and effects' is because of the distinctiveness of cause and effect — from not understanding the results such as the wholesome and so forth in the three types of the morally indeterminate. 'Three divisions' means three sections, with reference to the wholesome and other <s>dharmas</s> in sequential cause-and-effect order. 'Of six kinds' is by virtue of the prior operation of the six <s>āyatanas</s> (sense bases). This analysis of the three groups excluding the cause should be examined.

body.text: punarebhirevārthaḥ pratītyasamutpādasya pañcavidhaṃ gāmbhīrya veditavyam / hetugāmbhīrya viṣamahetvahetuvādapratipakṣena dvābhyāmarthābhyām / lakṣaṇagāmbhīrya nirātmakatayaikārthena / utpattigāmbhīrya pratyayebhyaḥ phalotpattāvapyatatkṛtatayā dvābhyāmarthābhyām / sthitigāmbhīryamavyavasthitānāṃ sthityābhāsanāddvābhyāmarthābhyām / pravṛttigāmbhīryaṃ hetuphalapravṛttidurvijñānatvāccaturbhirarthairiti //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, with these very meanings, the fivefold profundity of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) should be understood: profundity of cause, profundity of effect, profundity of the non-destruction of the results of action, profundity of 'neither self-made nor other-made,' and profundity of the dependent nature being merely <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena).

body.text: antareṇa eva kartāraṃ karma kriyā cāsti tatphalopabhogaścetyayamatra karmaphalāvipraṇāśo veditavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Even without an agent, there is action and activity and the enjoyment of its results — this is the meaning of the profundity of the non-destruction of the results of action. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s> on the rejoicing in merit, so here too it is said that <s>vijñāna</s> carries karma. It carries it, moreover, principally.

body.text: na svayaṃkṛto dharmo 'nutpannasyābhāvādyenāsau kriyeta / na parakṛtaḥ pratyayānāmakartṛkatvāt / nobhayakṛta etenaiva kāraṇadvayena / nāsvayaṃkārāpa[ra]kārahetusamutpannaḥ hetupratyayānāṃ phalotpattau sāmarthyāt // aparaḥ paryāyaḥ / na svayaṃkṛtaḥ pratyayāpekṣaṇāt / na parakṛtaḥ satsvapi pratyayeṣu nirvījasyānutpādāt / nobhayakṛtastadubhayonirīhakatvāt / nāhetusamutpanno bījapratyayānāṃ śaktisadbhā[vā]diti / bhavati hyapi-
body.translated_text: A <s>dharma</s> is not self-made, because that which has not yet arisen does not exist and so could not create itself. It is not made by another, because without mutual dependence among the conditions, no single condition exists in isolation.

body.text:
svabījatvānna parataḥ na svayaṃ tadapekṣaṇāt /
niśceṣṭatvānna ca dvābhyāṃ tacchakternāpyahetutaḥ // iti /
body.translated_text:
Because it arises from its own seed it is not from another; because it depends on that, it is not from itself;
because both are inert, it is not from both; since it is empty of that, it indeed arises from that [dependent origination].

body.text: na svayaṃ na parato dvividhakoṭipratikṣepe 'pi gambhīraḥ pratītyasamutpādaḥ syāt prāgeva yatra catasro 'pi koṭayaḥ pratikṣipyante, tasmādetasya paramagāmbhīrya veditavyam //
body.translated_text: Even though both alternatives — 'not from self' and 'not from another' — are rejected, <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> is profound; since even dual agency is without conceptual construction, it is even more profound. Therefore, it is the arising of emptiness as the dependent nature being merely <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: vijñānotpattiprabhedataścakṣuḥpratītyarūpāṇi cotpadyate cakṣurvijñānamityevamādi / vyutpattiprabhedataḥ satvalokamadhikṛtya, avidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārā ityevamādi / bāhyavasyotpattiprabhedato bījaṃ pratītyāṅkuraḥ, aṅkuraṃ pratītya kāṇḍaḥ / tathā nāpatrapuṣpaphalāni yojyāni / saṃvartavivartaprabhedataḥ sarvasattvasādhāraṇakarmādhipatyaṃ pratītya mahāpṛthivyādīnāmutpādāt / āhāropastambhaprabhedataścatura āhārān pratītya traidhātuke satvānāmavasthānāt / iṣṭāniṣṭagativibhāgaprabhedataḥ sucaritaduścarite pratītya sugatidurgatigamanāt / viśuddhiprabhedato mokṣabhāgīyāni pratītya nirvedhabhāgīyotpattito yāvaddarśanabhāvanāmārgānupūrvyārhattvaprāptitaḥ, parato vā ghoṣaṃ pratītyādhyātmaṃ ca yoniśo manaskāraṃ samyagdṛṣṭistato yāvatsarvāsravakṣaya iti / prabhāvaprabhedato 'dhigamaṃ pratītyābhijñādayo vaiśeṣikā guṇā iti / ebhiḥ prabhedaivistareṇa saṃskārāṇāṃ pratītyasamutpādo 'nusartavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: From the classification of the arising of <s>vijñāna</s> — 'dependent on the eye and visible forms, eye-consciousness arises' and so forth — this is due to the distinction of the object-conditions of the substantial. From the classification of the <s>bhūtas</s> (great elements) and derived form, it is of eleven kinds due to the distinction between what is natural to karma and what is adventitious.

body.text: saṃ
body.translated_text: 'Forward and reverse order of defilement' — with reference to the sequence of arising, the forward order is '<s>avidyā</s> conditions the <s>saṃskāras</s>' and so forth. With reference to the sequence of cessation, the reverse order should be understood as 'from the cessation of <s>avidyā</s>, cessation of the <s>saṃskāras</s>' and so forth.

body.text: kleśānulomapratiloma iti pravṛtyānupūrvīmadhikṛtya, avidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārā ityevamādyanulomanirdeśaḥ / jarāmaraṇaṃjarāmara[ṇa]samudayo [jarāmaraṇanirodho] jarāmaraṇanirodhagāminī pratipaditi satyavyavasthānamadhikṛtya pratilomanirdeśo veditavyaḥ /
vyavadānānulomapratilomata iti
body.translated_text: 'Forward and reverse order of purification' — as follows: 'from the cessation of <s>avidyā</s>, cessation of the <s>saṃskāras</s>' and so forth is the forward order of purification. The same in reverse order is 'from the cessation of the <s>saṃskāras</s>, cessation of <s>vijñāna</s>' and so forth.

body.text: tadyathāvidyānirodhāt saṃskāranirodha ityevamādi vyavadānānulomanirdeśaḥ / kasminnasati na jarāmaraṇaṃ bhavati kasya nirodhājjarāmaraṇanirodha iti pratilomanirdeśataḥ //

hetupratyaya ālayavijñānaṃ kuśalavāsanā ca sāsravānāsravāṇāṃ ca saṃskārāṇāṃ yathākramam / ālayavijñānaṃ punardvividham - vaipākikamābhisaṃskārikaṃ ca / tatra vaipākikamupapattiprātilambhikānāṃ hetupratyayaḥ / ābhisaṃskārikaṃ prāyogikānāmāyatyāṃ cālayavijñānāntarasya hetupratyayo draṣṭavyaḥ / ābhisaṃskārikaṃ punarālayavijñānaṃ tajjānmikapravṛttivijñānasamudācāravāsitaṃ veditavyam / kuśalavāsanā mokṣabhāgīyānāṃ vāsanā
body.translated_text: The <s>hetupratyaya</s> (causal condition) is <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (storehouse consciousness) and <s>kuśalavāsanā</s> (wholesome imprints); it establishes that these are respectively the <s>kāraṇahetu</s> (efficient cause) of conditioned phenomena both with and without outflows, in due order. Furthermore, the other five kinds — for the wholesome, the wholesome <s>sahabhūhetu</s> (co-existent cause), <s>sabhāgahetu</s> (homogeneous cause), <s>sarvatragahetu</s> (universal cause), and <s>vipākahetu</s> (retributive cause) for all levels — and so forth

body.text: draṣṭavyā / teṣāṃ lokottarābhyupagamaniṣyandadharmanaimittikatastadvāsanāyā lokottaradharmahetutvaṃ veditavyam //
body.translated_text: should be understood. Among these, the supramundane practice-result and causal <s>dharmas</s> and their imprints serve as the cause for projecting supramundane imprints. Although they share a common nature, because they are determined as either wholesome or unwholesome, they are not <s>vipākahetu</s> — this should be examined in detail elsewhere.

body.text: api khalu svabhāvato 'pītyevamādinā ṣaḍḍhetavo hetupratyaya iti darśayati / tatra svabhāvataḥ prabhedataśca kāraṇahetorvyavasthānam / śeṣaiḥ padaiḥ yathākramaṃ sahabhūsaṃprayuktasabhāgasarvatragavipākahetūnāṃ vyavasthānaṃ veditavyam /
body.translated_text: Moreover, by the statement 'also by intrinsic nature' and so forth, the six <s>hetus</s> (causes) are shown to be the <s>hetupratyaya</s>. Among these, the six causes are: <s>kāraṇahetu</s> (efficient cause), <s>sahabhūhetu</s> (co-existent cause), <s>sabhāgahetu</s> (homogeneous cause), <s>sarvatragahetu</s> (universal cause), <s>vipākahetu</s> (retributive cause), and <s>naimittikahetuh</s> (occasional cause).

body.text: hetusvabhāvamadhikṛtya kāraṇahetuvyavasthānātsarvahetavaḥ kāraṇahetāvantarbhūtā veditavyāḥ / sahāyādiviśeṣaprabhāvanārtha tu pṛthagvyavasthānam /
body.translated_text: With reference to the intrinsic nature of causes, because of the establishment of <s>kāraṇahetu</s>, it is demonstrated that all causes are included within <s>kāraṇahetu</s>. Through the inclusion of all causation there is a definite principle. However, the definite establishment of <s>kāraṇahetu</s>-status does not hold for what is merely possible everywhere. In brief, the unobstructed cause and the cause operating through initiative and the like — this establishes the twofold nature of <s>kāraṇa</s> (causation) from the standpoint of meaning.

body.text: kāraṇahetuprabhede vijñānasāmagrayādikaṃ yannirdiṣṭamudāharaṇamātraṃ taddraṣṭavyam, tayā diśānyasyāpi tajjātīyasyābhyūhanārtham / tatra utpattikāraṇaṃ tataḥ kāryasyābhūtvā prādurbhāvāt / sthitikāraṇamutpannasya prabandhānupacchedāt / dhṛtikāraṇaṃ pātapratibandhāt / prakāśanakāraṇamāvṛtasyābhivyañjanāt / vikārakāraṇaṃ tatsaṃtānasyānyathātvāpādanāt / viyogakāraṇaṃ saṃbandhasya dvaidhīkaraṇāt / pariṇatikāraṇaṃ tadavayavānāṃ deśāntarasaṃcaraṇāt / saṃpratyayakāraṇaṃ tena viparokṣānumānāt / saṃpratyāyanakāraṇaṃ tena samyaṅniścayāt / prāpaṇakāraṇaṃ tenādhigamāt / vyavahārakāraṇaṃ yathānāmadheyaṃ nimittodgrahaṇenābhiniviśyānuvyavaharaṇāt / apekṣākāraṇamanyatrecchotpattinimittatvāt / ākṣepakāraṇaṃ tadanvayāvasthāntaraparāparabhāvina āvedhakatvāt / ābhinirvṛttikāraṇamanantarabhāvino janakatvāt / parigrahakāraṇaṃ svabījotpādina upodvalatvāt / āvāhanakāraṇaṃ tadānukūlyenākarṣaṇāt / pratiniyamakāraṇaṃ bhinnasvabhāvatayānyonyaphalatvāt / sahakārikāraṇaṃ svakāryanirvartane
body.translated_text: Regarding the varieties of <s>kāraṇahetu</s>, the aggregate of consciousness and so forth that is indicated should be understood as merely illustrative. The twofold condition of consciousness — as object-support and as cause — is according to its varieties. The cause of each individual thing should be understood through the door of producing <s>dharmas</s> such as impermanence and the like.

body.text: kāraṇāntarāpekṣaṇāt / virodhikāraṇaṃ vidhnakaraṇāt / avirodhikāraṇaṃ tadviparyayeṇa veditavyam //
body.translated_text: This is because of dependence on other conditions. <s>Virodhikāraṇa</s> (obstructive causation) is because of creating obstruction. <s>Avirodhikāraṇa</s> (non-obstructive causation) is the opposite of that — because in the form of a complete assembly of conditions, the result is produced immediately thereafter.

body.text: tadyathā bhūtāni bhautikaṃ ceti yathāsaṃbhavaṃ na tvavaśyaṃ sarvatra saṃghāte catvāri mahābhūtāni bhavanti rūpādikaṃ vā bhautikam / ityato yadyatrāsti tattena sahotpadyate nānyonyaṃ vineti //
body.translated_text: For example, the <s>bhūtas</s> (great elements) and <s>bhautika</s> (derived matter) — this is as the case may be, not necessarily in every instance. And in a composite, the two are mutually causes of each other, because the second arises from the first.

body.text: sahāyanaiyamyena sahabhūheturvyavasthāpitaḥ / bhūtāni bhautikaṃ cetyudāharaṇamātrametadveditavyam, cittacaitasikānāmanyonyamavinābhāvaniyamāt / yadyevaṃ saṃprayuktahetoḥ pṛthagvyavasthānaṃ na prāpnoti, cittacaitasikānāṃ sahabhūhetāvantarbhāvāt / yadyapyetadevaṃ tathāpyanyenārthena / ye dharmāḥ sahabhāvenālaṃbanaṃ pratipadyante nānyatama vaikalyena te saṃpratipattitaḥ saṃprayuktakaheturvyavasthāpyate, na sahabhāvamātreṇa, tadyathā cittai caitasikāśca //
body.translated_text: The <s>sahabhūhetu</s> (co-existent cause) is established by the invariable association of companions. The example of the <s>bhūtas</s> and <s>bhautika</s> should be understood as merely illustrative.

body.text: pūrvabhāvitānāmiti pūrvābhyastānāṃ pūrvaṃ samudācaritānāmityarthaḥ / yā aparānte uttarottarā puṣṭataratamā pravṛttiriti taiḥ paripoṣitabījānāṃ tadanvayānāmanāgate kāle viśiṣṭotpattito draṣṭavyā / evamayaṃ sabhāgahetuḥ sadṛśānāṃ puṣṭinimittatvena vyavasthāpitaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Of those previously cultivated' means of those previously practiced, those previously engaged in — this is the meaning. That which in the future depends on those is the <s>sabhāgaphala</s> (homogeneous result) and outflow-nature. This is because what is of the same kind progressively develops further and further.

body.text: sarvatragaheturna kevalaṃ sadṛśasyaiva puṣṭaye kiṃ tarhi yasya kasyacidrāgādeḥ kleśasyābhyāsena sarveṣāṃ dveṣādīnāṃ prabandhapuṣṭayā dṛḍhīkāro bhavatyato vandhanagāḍhīkaraṇānmokṣaprāptiparipanthārthenāsya vyavasthānaṃ veditavyam //
body.translated_text: The <s>sarvatragahetu</s> (universal cause) serves not merely to nourish what is similar to itself, but rather becomes a cause that accompanies everywhere any <s>rāga</s> (passion) and so forth, even of the wholesome, because it abandons the assemblage of its own cause. Just as in the world, universally spreading diseases are like seeds, so it is.

body.text: vipākahetuḥ punarāyatyāmekāntavisadṛśasyaivānivṛttāvyākṛtasyātmabhāvasaṃgra hītavyavipākasyākṣepakatvāt parigrahārthena vyavasthāpitaḥ / kuśalasāsravagrahaṇamanāsravāṇāṃ janmavirodhitvenānākṣepakatvāt //
body.translated_text: The <s>vipākahetu</s> (retributive cause) produces in the future only what is entirely dissimilar — the <s>anivṛttāvyākṛta</s> (unobstructed-indeterminate) that is included in one's personal existence. Even though the <s>kāraṇahetu</s> is not differentiated, its establishment is through its distinctive particular result.

body.text: nairantaryasamanantarato 'pīti nāvaśyaṃ kṣaṇanairantarya kiṃtarhi cittāntaranairantaryamapyatra nairantarya draṣṭavyam / itarathā hyacittikasamāpattau vyutthānacittasya samāpatticittaṃ na samanantarapratyayaḥ syāt / bhavati ca / tasmādekasmin saṃtāne paścimasya cittasya pūrvakaṃ cittaṃ cittāntareṇānantaritaṃ
body.translated_text: 'From immediate contiguity' — this does not necessarily mean momentary contiguity, but rather mental contiguity; because from the immediately preceding mental state the subsequent mental state arises.

body.text: samanantarapratyayaḥ / yathā cittamevaṃ caitasikā api veditavyāḥ / sabhāgavisabhāgacittacaittotpattisama[na]ntarato 'pīti kuśalāḥ cittacettāḥ kuśalānāṃ sabhāgānāmakuśalāvyākṛtānāṃ ca visabhāgānāmanantarotpannānāṃ samanantarapratyayaḥ / evaṃ kuśalāvyākṛtāḥ svānyaprakārāṇāṃ yojayitavyāḥ / tadyathā kāmāvacarā kāmāvacarāṇāṃ rūpārūpyāvacarānāsravāṇāṃ cānantarotpannānāṃ samanantarapratyayaḥ / evaṃ rūpāvacarādayo 'pi pṛthagpṛthagrūpāvacarādonāṃ kāmāvacarādīnāṃ cā[na]ntarotpannānāmiti yojayitavyam //
body.translated_text: This is the <s>samanantarapratyaya</s> (immediately contiguous condition). Just as with <s>citta</s> (mind), so too the <s>caitasikas</s> (mental factors) should be understood. 'From the immediately contiguous arising of similar and dissimilar mind and mental factors' means that wholesome mind and mental factors are the <s>samanantarapratyaya</s> for those that arise immediately after — both the similar wholesome ones and the dissimilar unwholesome and indeterminate ones. Likewise, the unwholesome and indeterminate should be applied to their own and other types. For example, those belonging to the <s>kāmāvacara</s> (desire realm) are the <s>samanantarapratyaya</s> for those that arise immediately after in the desire realm, the <s>rūpāvacara</s> (form realm), the <s>ārūpyāvacara</s> (formless realm), and the uncontaminated. Likewise, those belonging to the form realm and so forth should each be applied separately to those of the form realm and so forth, and also to those of the desire realm and so forth that arise immediately after.

body.text: kiṃ khalu sarvasya cintasyānantaraṃ sarva cittamutpadyate, ahosvidasti pratiniyamaḥ / astītyucyate / avaitasya cittasyānantaramidaṃ cedaṃ ca cittamutpadyata ityucyamāne bahuvaktavyaṃ jāyate / tasmātsāmānyena cittotpattau lakṣaṇamātraṃ vyavasthāpyate / tadyathā daśabhirbalaiścittasyotpādo veditavyaḥ - paricayabalena chandabalena prayogabalena samāpattibalena ''vedhabalena hetubalena viṣayabalena smṛtibalena manaskārabalena pratisaṃdhibalena ca / paricayabalaṃ punastrividham - mṛdu madhyamadhimātraṃ ca / samāpattisthitivyutthānanimittānāmanupalakṣitatvānmṛdu / upalakṣitānāṃ svaparicitta tvānmadhyam / suparicitatopalakṣitatvādadhimātram / tatra mṛdunā paricayabalena dhyānārūpyāṇāma[nu]pūrvyasamāpattirveditavyā / madhyena vyutkrāntakasamāpattirekāntarikayogena / adhimātreṇa yatheṣṭaṃ sarvāṇi vā vyutkrāmyānulomaṃ pratilomaṃ ca samāpattirveditavyā / chandabalena dvitīyadhyānalābhī prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ samāpanno yadyākāṃkṣati dvitīyadhyānabhūmikaṃ vyutthānacittamāmukhīkarotyatha nā kāṃkṣati kāmāvacaraṃ kuśalamanivṛtāvyākṛtaṃ vā / evamanyatrāpi vistareṇa yojyam / prayogabalena kāmāvacarasya kuśalasyavānantaraṃ tatprathamato rūpāvacaraṃ cittamutpadyate / anāgamyasya kuśalasyānantaraṃ maulam / maulasya kuśalasyānantaraṃ dvitīyadhyānasamāpannakamityevamādi vistareṇa yāvadbhavāgrāt veditavyam / samāpattibalena śuddhakaṃ samāpannasya kadācicchuddhakamevotpadyate
body.translated_text: Does every mental state arise immediately after every other mental state, or is there a definite restriction? It is said that there is. If one were to specify that after such-and-such a mental state this and that mental state arises, there would be far too much to say. Therefore, only the general characteristics of mental arising are established. The arising of mind should be understood through ten powers: the power of familiarity, the power of intention, the power of effort, the power of attainment, the power of penetration, the power of cause, the power of object, the power of mindfulness, the power of attention, and the power of rebirth-connection. The power of familiarity is threefold — weak, medium, and strong. It is weak when the signs of attainment, abiding, and emergence are not discerned. It is medium when they are discerned but only somewhat familiar. It is strong when they are well-practiced and fully discerned. With weak power of familiarity, the sequential attainment of the <s>dhyānas</s> and <s>ārūpyas</s> (formless states) should be understood. With medium power, the skip-attainment with the practice of alternation. With strong power, the attainment in forward and reverse order, skipping at will through all or any. Through the power of intention, one who has attained the second <s>dhyāna</s> and is established in the first <s>dhyāna</s> — if they wish it, they direct the emergence-consciousness to the level of the second <s>dhyāna</s>; if they do not wish it, it becomes wholesome of the desire realm or unobstructed-indeterminate. This should be applied in detail elsewhere as well. Through the power of effort, immediately after the wholesome of the desire realm, a form-realm mental state arises for the first time. Immediately after the wholesome of the preliminary stage, a fundamental stage arises. Immediately after the wholesome of the fundamental stage, that of the second <s>dhyāna</s> attainment arises — and so forth in detail up to the peak of existence. Through the power of attainment, for one established in the pure attainment, sometimes

body.text: kadācitkliṣṭam / āvedhavalena samādhervyutthāya caratastāvatsamāhitabhūmikaṃ cittam[a]samāhitakṣaṇānantaravyatibhinnamanuvartate yāvattadvirodhikleśasamudācārātparihīṇa iti / tadvirodhi kleśasaṃprayuktasya punaścittasya hetvādibhiśca turbhirbalaiḥ samudācāro veditavyaḥ - tatra tāvaddhetubalena yadyavaśyaṃ bhūmiparihāṇisaṃvartanīyamāvaraṇaṃ pūrvamupacitaṃ bhavati, viṣayabalena yadi rāgādyutpatyanukūlaḥ śubhādinimittaḥ prabhāvotkaṭaviṣaya ābhāsasamāgato bhavati, smṛtivalena yadi smaraṇasaṃkalpairatītānviṣayān prapañcayati, manaskārabalena yadi mīmāṃsāmanaskāreṇānyatarānyataracchubhanimittaṃ manasikarotīti / pratisaṃdhibalena nava maraṇacittānyātmabhāvatṛṣṇāsaṃprayuktāni triṣu dhātuṣupratyekaṃ kāmarūpārūpyāvacarāṇi / tatra kāmadhātoścyutvā kāmadhātāveva pratisaṃdhi vadhnataḥ kāmāvacaramātmabhāvatṛṣṇāsaṃprayuktaṃ maraṇacittaṃ veditavyam / rūpārūpyadhātvoḥ pratisaṃdhi badhnato rūpārūpyāvacaram / tathā rūpārūpyadhātubhyāṃ cyutvā tatra vānyatra votpadyamānasya ṣaṭcittāni yojayitavyāni / sā punarātmabhāvatṛṣṇā sahajānirūpitālaṃbanānivṛtāvyākṛtā ca / ātmabhāvajātiścāsyāḥ prakārāparicchedenālaṃbanaṃ veditavyam / tadvaśenā[na]ntaraṃ pṛthagjanānāmantarābhavapratisaṃdhiḥ / āryāṇāmapyavītarāgāṇāṃ maraṇakāle yāvadaspaṣṭasaṃjñāvasthāṃ na gacchati tāvadasau tṛṣṇā samudācarati / te tvenāṃ paricchidya pratipakṣeṇābhinigṛhṇanti / vītarāgāṇāṃ tvāryāṇāṃ pratipakṣasya valīyastvānnaivāsau samudācaratyaprahīṇāpi satī / tadanuśayavaśena tu teṣāṃ pratisaṃdhiḥ / antarābhavapratisaṃdhikṣaṇaḥ punarnityamanivṛtāvyākṛta eva vipākatvāt / tata ūrdhva kuśalo 'pyakuśalo
body.translated_text: sometimes defiled. Through the power of penetration, for one who has emerged from <s>samādhi</s> and moves about, the mind of the concentrated level continues through the moments of non-concentration without interruption, until it is lost through the arising of an opposing defilement. The arising of a mental state associated with that opposing defilement should be understood through four powers including the power of cause and the rest. Among these, first through the power of cause, that which

body.text: 'pyavyākṛto 'pi yathāsaṃbhavam, cyuticittaṃ sthāpayitvā / antarābhavacyuticittaṃ tu nityaṃ kliṣṭaṃ maraṇabhavavat / upapattipratisaṃdhiḥ punarnityamanivṛtāvyākṛta eveti veditavyam / bodhisattvānāṃ tu praṇidhānabalenopapadyamānānāṃ maraṇacittādikamekāntena sarva kuśalaṃ veditavyam / samāptaḥ samanantara pratyayaprasaṅgaḥ //
body.translated_text: even indeterminate, as the case may be, excluding the death-consciousness. However, the death-consciousness in the intermediate existence is always defiled, as in the case of the death-existence. Rebirth-connection at the time of birth should be understood as always being <s>anivṛtāvyākṛta</s> (unobstructed-indeterminate). But for <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who take rebirth through the power of their vows, the death-consciousness and so forth should be understood as entirely wholesome in all cases. The <s>samanantarapratyaya</s> section is completed.

body.text: paricchinnaviṣayālaṃbanataḥ pañcānāṃ vijñānakāyānāmālaṃbanam, pratiniyataviṣayatvāt pañcānāṃ vijñānakāyānām / aparicchinnaviṣayālaṃbanataḥ manovijñānasyālaṃbanam, sarvadharmaviṣayatvānmanovijñānasya / acitrīkāraviṣayālaṃbanato 'vyutpannasaṃjñānāṃ manovijñānasyālaṃbanam, nāmato 'kṣarīkartumaśakyatvāt / citrīkāraviṣayālaṃbanatastadviparya[yā]dveditavyam / savastukaviṣayālaṃbanato dṛṣṭimasmimānaṃ tatsaṃprayuktāṃśca dharmān sthāpayitvā tadanyeṣāmālaṃbanam / avastukaviṣayālaṃbanataḥ sthāpitānāmālaṃbanam, ātmādhiṣṭhānatvāt / vastvālaṃbanato 'nāsravālaṃbanān visabhāgadhātubhūmisarvatragānanivāritavastukāṃścātītānāgatālaṃbanān sthāpayitvā tadanyeṣāmālaṃbanam / parikalpālaṃbanataḥ sthāpitānāmālaṃbanam, svaparikalpamātrālaṃbanāt / viparyastālaṃbanaṃ nityādyākārāṇām / aviparyastālaṃbanamanityādyākārāṇām / savyāghātālaṃbanamaprahīṇajñeyāvaraṇānām / avyāghātālaṃbanaṃ prahīṇajñeyāvaraṇānāmiti //
body.translated_text: From the standpoint of having a limited range of objects, the <s>ālambana</s> (object-support) of the five <s>vijñānakāyas</s> (consciousness-groups), because the five consciousness-groups have determinate objects. From the standpoint of having an unlimited range of objects, the object-support of <s>manovijñāna</s> (mental consciousness), because mental consciousness has all <s>dharmas</s> as its objects. From the standpoint of objects that are not conceptually elaborated, the object-support of the mental consciousness of those with undeveloped perception, because names cannot be formed into syllables.

body.text: ālaṃbanapratyaye viniścayaḥ - lakṣaṇato 'pi prabhedato 'pi sthitito 'pi parijñānato 'pi prahāṇato 'pyālavanavyavasthānaṃ veditavyam //
body.translated_text: The determination regarding the <s>ālambanapratyaya</s> (object-condition) — the establishment of the object-support should be understood from the standpoint of characteristics, from the standpoint of classification, from the standpoint of status, from the standpoint of full understanding, and from the standpoint of abandonment.

body.text: kathaṃ lakṣaṇataḥ / yo 'rthastatpratibhāsānāṃ cittacaitasikānāṃ dharmāṇāmutpattinimittama, te cotpannāstadarthābhiniveśavyavahārapratyātmāvagamāya bhavanti tadālaṃbanalakṣaṇam //
body.translated_text: How from the standpoint of characteristics? Whatever object is the cause for the arising of mind and mental factors that have it as their appearance — and those, once arisen, function for the engagement, conventional usage, and personal realization regarding that object — that is the characteristic of the object-support.

body.text: kathaṃ prabhedataḥ / asadālaṃbanaṃ tadyathā viparyastānāṃ cittacaitasikānāmatītānāgatasvapnapratirbibamāyādyālaṃbanaṃ ca / sadālaṃbanaṃ tadanyeṣām / anālaṃbanamālaṃbanaṃ rūpaṃ cittaviprayuktā asaṃskṛtaṃ ca / sālaṃbanamālaṃbanaṃ cittacaitasikā dharmāḥ / samyaktvālaṃbanaṃ tadyathā kuśalam /
body.translated_text: How from the standpoint of classification? A non-existent object-support, such as the object-support of distorted mind and mental factors — objects of the past, the future, dreams, reflections, illusions, and so forth. An existent object-support is that of the others. An object-support that does not take objects includes form, factors dissociated from mind, and the unconditioned. An object-support that takes objects includes mind and mental factors. A correct object-support is, for example, the wholesome.

body.text: mithyātvālaṃbanaṃ tadyathā kliṣṭam / naivasamyakratvanamithyātvālaṃbanaṃ tadyathānivṛtāvyākṛtam / yoniśa ālaṃbanaṃ tadyathā kuśalānāṃ cittacaitasikānām / ayoniśa ālaṃbanaṃ tadyathā kliṣṭānām / naivayoniśonāyoniśastadvinirmuktānām / sabhāgamālaṃbanaṃ tadyathā kuśalādīnāṃ kuśalādīni svabhūmikānāṃ ca svabhūmikaṃ sāsravāṇāṃ ca sāsravamanāsravāṇāṃ cānāsravam / visabhāgamālaṃbanaṃ tadyathā kuśalādīnāmakuśalādīnyanyabhūmikānāṃ cānyabhūmikaṃ sāsravānāsravayoścānāsravasāsravam / nānātvamālaṃbanaṃ tadyathā savitarkavicārāṇāṃ cittacaitasikānām / ekatvamālaṃbanaṃ tadyathāvitarkāvicārāṇām / vibhūtyālaṃbanaṃ tadyathāsaṃjñikaprāyogikānāṃ cittacaitasikānāmākāśavijñānānantyāyatanikānāṃ ca / abhisaṃkṣiptaṃ sūkṣmamālaṃbanaṃ tadyathākiṃcanyāyatanikānām / paryantikaṃ sūkṣmamālaṃbanaṃ tadyathā naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanikānām / kleśa ālaṃbanaṃ tenālaṃbyata iti kṛtvā / dharma ālaṃbanaṃ tadyathāryāṇāṃ nāmakāyapadakāyavyañjanakāyāḥ / artha ālaṃbanaṃ tadāśrito 'rthaḥ / parīttamālaṃbanaṃ tadyathā śrāvakayānam / vipulamālaṃbanaṃ tadyathā mahāyānam / nimittamālavanaṃ tadyathā śamathapragrahopekṣānimittāni / animittamālaṃbanaṃ tadyathā nirvāṇaṃ bhavāgrayaṃ ca / tattvamālaṃbanaṃ tadyathā tathatā ṣoḍaśānāṃ cākārāṇāṃ satyāni / vaihārikamālaṃbanaṃ tadyathā nirodhasamāpattiḥ / vaśavartyālaṃbanaṃ tadyathā vimokṣādīnāṃ sarvākārajñatāvasānānāṃ guṇānām / kṣaṇikamālaṃbanaṃ tadyathāśaikṣāṇāṃ tajjanmikameva / anuvartyālaṃbanaṃ tadyathā buddhabodhisattvānām //
body.translated_text: An erroneous object-support is, for example, the defiled. An object-support that is neither correct nor erroneous is, for example, the <s>anivṛtāvyākṛta</s> (unobstructed-indeterminate). A methodical object-support is that of wholesome mind and mental factors. An unmethodical object-support is that of defiled ones. Neither methodical nor unmethodical is that of those freed from both. A similar object-support is, for example, the wholesome and so forth for the wholesome and so forth, and those of one's own level for those of one's own level.

body.text: kathaṃ sthititaḥ / ālaṃbanasyāpariniṣpattitastathā vyavasthāpanāt / caturbhiśca kāraṇairapariniṣpannamālaṃbanaṃ veditavyam - viruddhavijñānanimittatayā,
body.translated_text: How from the standpoint of status? Because of the non-establishment of the object, such is the determination. The object-support should be understood as non-established for four reasons: because it is the cause for conflicting cognitions,

body.text: a[n]ālaṃbanavijñānopalabdhyā, yatnamantareṇāviparyāsaprasaṅgatayā, trividhajñānānuvartanatayā ca / tataśca grāhakasyāpyapariniṣpattiḥ / trividhaṃ jñānaṃ vaśitājñānaṃ vipaśyanājñāna nirvikalpajñānaṃ ca / tatra caturṇā kāraṇānāmudāharaṇāni /
body.translated_text: because cognition without an object is observed, because without effort there would be the consequence of non-distortion, and because it accords with three types of knowledge. From this, the non-establishment of the apprehender as well follows. The three types of knowledge are: knowledge through mastery, knowledge through <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight), and non-conceptual knowledge. Here are illustrations of the four reasons:

children.translated_text: and <s>devas</s> (gods), respectively — from the difference of mind regarding the same object, the non-establishment of the object is maintained.
Likewise regarding the past and so forth, in dreams, and in the two types of reflections,
because of the non-existent object-support and from the application of that object-support —
if the object were truly established as an object, non-conceptual knowledge would be impossible;
and because of its absence, the attainment of <s>Buddhahood</s> would not be possible at all.
When a <s>Bodhisattva</s> has attained mastery, through the power of aspiration,
such transformation in earth and the rest is observed in the case of meditators.
For the wise one here who has accomplished investigation and attained <s>samādhi</s>,
in the mental engagement with all <s>dharmas</s>, and also from the appearance of objects as such —
indeed, in the non-conceptual operation of knowledge, and also from the appearance of all objects,
the non-existence of the object is to be understood, because of the non-existence of that from the standpoint of <s>vijñapti</s> (representation).

body.text: kathaṃ parijñānataḥ / lakṣaṇaprabhedasthitīnāṃ yathābhūtajñānataḥ //
body.translated_text: How from the standpoint of full understanding? Through the knowledge of the characteristics, classifications, and status as they truly are.

body.text: kathaṃ prahāṇataḥ / śrāvakayānamahāyānābhyāmāśrayaparivṛttitaḥ / śrāvakayānāśrayaparivṛttyā skandhadhātvāyatanālaṃbanebhyo vimokṣo na tu teṣu vibhutvalābhaḥ / mahāyānāśrayaparivṛttyā tūbhayamiti / samāpta ālaṃbanapratyaye yathāgranthaṃ viniścayaḥ /
body.translated_text: How from the standpoint of abandonment? Through the transformation of the basis by means of the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> and the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. Through the transformation of the basis by the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s>, there is liberation from the object-supports of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense bases), but not the attainment of sovereignty over them. Through the transformation of the basis by the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, however, both are achieved. The determination of the <s>ālambanapratyaya</s> according to the text is completed.

body.text: pratiṣṭhādhipatitaḥ vāyumaṇḍalādīnyammaṇḍalādīnām, bhājanalokaḥ sattvalokasya, bhūtāni bhautikānām, indriyāṇi vijñānānāmityevamādi / āvedhādhipatitaḥ sarvasattvasādhāraṇaṃ karma bhājanalokasya, paurāṇaṃ sāsravakarma vipākasyetyevamādi sahabhāvādhipatitaḥ cittaṃ caitasānām, manaskāraḥ cittasya, sparśī vedanāyā ityevamādi / ataḥ paraṃ dvāviśati mindriyāṇyadhikṛtyādhipativyavasthānaṃ veditavyam / tatra viṣayādhipatitaḥ cakṣuḥśrotraghrāṇajihvākāyamanaindriyānām, tadādhipatyena rūpādyabhinirvṛtteḥ /
body.translated_text: From the standpoint of dominant support: the wind-circle and the rest for the water-circle and the rest; the receptacle world for the world of sentient beings; the <s>bhūtas</s> (great elements) for <s>bhautikas</s> (derived matter); the sense faculties for the <s>vijñānas</s> (consciousnesses) — and so forth. From the standpoint of dominant penetration: the karma shared by all sentient beings for the receptacle world; former contaminated karma for the maturation-result — and so forth. From the standpoint of dominant co-existence: <s>citta</s> (mind) for the <s>caitasas</s> (mental factors); <s>manaskāra</s> (attention) for the mind; <s>sparśa</s> (contact) for the mind —

body.text: prasavādhipatitaḥ strīpuruṣendriyayoḥ, tadādhipatyena garbhāvakramaṇāt / sthānādhipatito jīvitendriyasya, tadvaśena nikāyasabhāgasthānāt / phalopabhogādhipatitaḥ sukhaduḥkhasaumanasyopekṣendriyāṇām, tadadhiṣṭhāneneṣṭāniṣṭavipākapratisaṃvedanāt / laukikaviśudhyadhipatitaḥ śraddhāvīryasmṛtisamādhiprajñendriyāṇām, taiḥ kleśaviṣkambhaṇāt / lokottaraviśudhyadhipatito 'nājñātamājñāsyāmīndriyasyājñendriyasyājñātāvīndriyasya ca vyavasthānaṃ veditavyam, tairanuśayasamudghātāditi //
body.translated_text: From the standpoint of dominant procreation, of the female and male faculties, because through their dominance there is the descent into the womb. From the standpoint of dominant abiding, of the life faculty, because under its power there is continuity within a class of beings. From the standpoint of dominant enjoyment of results, of the faculties of pleasure, pain, mental happiness, and equanimity, because through them there is the experience of desirable and undesirable <s>vipāka</s> (maturation). From the standpoint of dominant mundane purification, of the faculties of faith, vigor, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom, because through them the defilements are suppressed. From the standpoint of dominant supramundane purification, the establishment of the faculty of 'I shall come to know what is not yet known,' the faculty of perfect knowledge, and the faculty of one who has fully known should be understood, because through them the latent tendencies are eradicated.

body.text: vijñānāvirahitatatsādṛśyendriyaviṣayaprabandhotpattitaḥ sabhāgaṃ veditavyam, vijñānasahitasya vijñānasādṛśyenendriyasya viṣayeṣu prabandhenotpatteḥ vijñānavṛttisādṛśyārthena tadindriyaṃ sabhāgamityucyate / vijñānavirahitasvasādṛśyaprabandhotpattitastatsabhāgam, vijñānena viprayuktasyendriyasya svātmasādṛśyena prabandhotpattirindriyalakṣaṇasādṛśyārthena tatsabhāgaṃ veditavyam / rūpaskandhaikadeśaścakṣurādipañcendriyalakṣaṇaḥ / pañca rūpīṇi dhātvāyatanāni cakṣurādīnītyeva /
body.translated_text: The <s>sabhāga</s> (similar) should be understood from the arising in continuity of sense faculties and objects similar to those not separated from consciousness — because the sense faculty that is accompanied by consciousness arises in continuity with respect to objects by means of similarity to consciousness, and in the sense of similarity to the activity of consciousness, that faculty is called <s>sabhāga</s>. The <s>tatsabhāga</s> (corresponding) should be understood from the arising in continuity through similarity to itself of that which is separated from consciousness — because the sense faculty that is dissociated from consciousness arises in continuity through similarity to its own nature, and in the sense of similarity to the characteristic of the faculty, it is called <s>tatsabhāga</s>. A portion of the <s>rūpaskandha</s> (form aggregate) has the character of the five faculties beginning with the eye. The five material <s>dhātus</s> (elements) and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense bases) are simply the eye and the rest.

body.text: vedanotpattyāśrayarūpata iti yadrūpamāśritya vedanotpadyate tadupāttamityucyate / rūpaskandhaikadeśaḥ sādhiṣṭhānendriyasaṃgahītaḥ / pañca rūpīṇi dhātvāyatanāni cakṣurādīni / caturṇāṃ caikadeśaḥ rūpagandharasaspraṣṭavyānāmindriyāvinirbhāgī //
body.translated_text: From the standpoint of the form that serves as the basis for the arising of feeling — whatever form depending on which feeling arises, that is called 'appropriated.' A portion of the <s>rūpaskandha</s> is included in the faculties together with their basis. The five material <s>dhātus</s> and <s>āyatanas</s> are the eye and the rest. And a portion of the four — form, smell, taste, and tangibles — is inseparable from the faculties.

body.text: viṣayagrahaṇādhipatitaścakṣurādīnāṃ ṣaṇṇām, tadādhipatyena rūpādyālaṃbane cittacaitapravṛteḥ / kulaprabandhādhipatitaḥ strīpuruṣendriyayoḥ, tataḥ putrapautrādyanvayapravṛtteḥ / śeṣaṃ yathādhipatipratyaye nirdiṣṭaṃ tathānugantavyam / rūpaskandhaikadeśaścakṣuḥ śrotraghrāṇajihvākāyastrīpuruṣendriyalakṣaṇaḥ / saṃskāraskandhaikadeśo jīvitaśraddhāvīryasmṛtisamādhiprajñendriyalakṣaṇaḥ / dvādaśa dhātava indriyavijñānadhātavaḥ / ṣaḍāyatanānyādhyātmikāni / dharmadhātvāyatanaikadeśaśca jīvitendriyaṃ sukhādīni śraddhādāni pañca //
body.translated_text: From the standpoint of dominant object-apprehension, of the six beginning with the eye, because through their dominance <s>citta</s> (mind) and <s>caittas</s> (mental factors) engage with objects such as form and the rest. From the standpoint of dominant family-continuity, of the female and male faculties, because from them there is the continuation of the lineage of sons, grandsons, and so forth. The remainder should be understood as indicated in the <s>adhipatipratyaya</s> (dominant condition) section. A portion of the <s>rūpaskandha</s> has the character of the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, female, and male faculties. A portion of the <s>saṃskāraskandha</s> (formations aggregate) has the character of the life, faith, vigor, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom faculties. Twelve <s>dhātus</s> are the faculty-elements and consciousness-elements. Six <s>āyatanas</s> are the internal ones. And a portion of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> and <s>dharmāyatana</s> comprises the life faculty, pleasure and the rest, and the five beginning with faith.

body.text: duḥkhā vedanā duḥkhātmikā satī svenaiva lakṣaṇena duḥkhaduḥkhatāḥ / tadutpattinimittabhūtāstvindriyārthāstatsaṃprayuktāśca duḥkhavedanīyatvādduḥkhaduḥkhatā draṣṭavyā //
body.translated_text: Painful feeling, being of the nature of suffering, is <s>duḥkhaduḥkhatā</s> (the suffering of suffering) by its very own characteristic. However, the sense faculties and objects that are the conditions for its arising, and the <s>dharmas</s> associated with it, should be understood as <s>duḥkhaduḥkhatā</s> because they are to be experienced as suffering.

body.text: sukhāyā vedanāyāstadvedanīyānāṃ ca dharmāṇāṃ vipariṇāmena daurmanasyotpādāt tadvipariṇatirvipariṇāmaduḥkhatā / tatra cānunayena cittasya vipariṇamanaṃ vipariṇāmaduḥkhatā veditavyā / yathoktamavadīrṇo vipariṇatena citteneti //
body.translated_text: The transformation of pleasant feeling and of the <s>dharmas</s> to be experienced as pleasant, producing mental distress through their alteration — that transformation is <s>vipariṇāmaduḥkhatā</s> (the suffering of change). In that context, the alteration of the mind through attachment should be understood as <s>vipariṇāmaduḥkhatā</s>. As it is said: 'one is dejected by a mind that has changed.'

body.text: aduḥkhāsukhā vedanālayavijñānasaṃprayuktā tadvedanīyāśca saṃskārā duḥkhavipariṇāmaduḥkhatayodauṣṭhulyenānugatatvāttena duḥkhatādvayenāvinirmuktatvādekadā duḥkhāvasthāṃ bhajante ekadā sukhāvasthāṃ, na nityakālamaduḥkhāsukhāvasthā eva bhavanti / tasmādanityatānubandhārthenāyogakṣematvātsaṃskāraduḥkhatā veditavyā / skandhānām / trayāṇāṃ dhātūnāṃ manodharmamanovijñānadhātūnām / dvayoścāyatanayormanodharmāyatanayoḥ / ekadeśaṃ sthāpayitvānāsravalakṣaṇam, tadanyāni sarvāṇīti //
body.translated_text: Neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling associated with <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (storehouse consciousness), and the formations to be experienced as such, are <s>saṃskāraduḥkhatā</s> (the suffering of conditioned existence) because they are accompanied by the unwholesome disposition of the suffering of suffering and the suffering of change — since they are not free from those two kinds of suffering, at one time they partake of the state of suffering and at another time of the state of pleasure; they do not remain perpetually in the state of neither-pain-nor-pleasure alone. Therefore, <s>saṃskāraduḥkhatā</s> should be understood because of the accompaniment of impermanence, hence the absence of security — of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates); of three <s>dhātus</s>: the <s>manodhātu</s>, <s>dharmadhātu</s>, and <s>manovijñānadhātu</s>; and of two <s>āyatanas</s>: the <s>manas</s> and <s>dharma</s> sense bases. Excluding a portion having the character of the uncontaminated, all the rest are included.

body.text: akuśalasya kuśalasāsravasya cāyatyā sasaṃprayogamālayavijñānaṃ vipākaḥ / atastena vipākena tadubhayaṃ savipākamityucyate / skandhānām / daśānāṃ dhātūnāṃ vijñānarūpaśabdadharma dhātūnām / caturṇā cāyatanānāṃ rūpaśabdamanodharmāyatanānām / ekadeśo 'vyākṛtānāsravavarjaḥ / ālayavijñānāttadanyattu cakṣurādikaṃ ca sukhaduḥkhādikaṃ ca tadvipākrajamityākhyāṃ labhate tato jātamiti kṛtvā /
body.translated_text: The <s>vipāka</s> (maturation) of the unwholesome and the wholesome-with-outflows is, in the future, the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> together with its associates. Therefore, because of that maturation, both of those are said to be 'having maturation.' Of the <s>skandhas</s>. Of ten <s>dhātus</s>: the consciousness, form, sound, and <s>dharma</s> elements. And of four <s>āyatanas</s>: the form, sound, <s>manas</s>, and <s>dharma</s> sense bases. The portion excludes the indeterminate and the uncontaminated. Other than the <s>ālayavijñāna</s>, the eye and the rest and pleasure and pain and the rest obtain the designation of being 'born from that maturation' because they are born from it.

body.text: pariṇatitaḥ pāriṇāmikaḥ kavaḍīkāra āhāraḥ, pariṇāmakāle indriyamahābhūtapoṣaṇāt / viṣayato vaiṣayikaḥ sparśāhāraḥ, iṣṭaviṣayā dhiṣṭhānena sparśenāśrayānugrahaṇāt / āśāta āśikaḥ manaḥ saṃcetanāhāraḥ, abhipretavastuprativaddhāśāvaśenāśrayānugrahaṇāt / upādānata aupādānikaḥ vijñānamāhāraḥ, ālayavijñānopādānavaśenātmabhā vopasthānāt / tathāhi tadviyukta āśrayaḥ pūtībhavatīti /
body.translated_text: From the standpoint of transformation, the <s>kavaḍīkārāhāra</s> (material nutriment) is transformative, because at the time of transformation it nourishes the sense faculties and great elements. From the standpoint of objects, <s>sparśāhāra</s> (contact-nutriment) pertains to objects, because through contact based on desirable objects there is support of the physical basis. From the standpoint of aspiration, <s>manaḥsaṃcetanāhāra</s> (mental-volition nutriment) pertains to wishes, because through the aspiration bound to desired objects there is support of the physical basis. From the standpoint of appropriation, <s>vijñānāhāra</s> (consciousness-nutriment) pertains to appropriation, because through the appropriation by <s>ālayavijñāna</s> there is the maintenance of the personal existence. For indeed, the physical basis separated from that becomes putrid.

body.text: punaścatvāro 'pyāhārāḥ samasya caturbhiḥ prabhedairvyavasthāpyante / tadyathā aśuddhāśrayasthitikaḥ kāmāvacarāṇāṃ pṛthagjanānām, sakalabandhanatvāt / śuddhāśuddhāśrayasthitikaḥ śaikṣāṇāṃ rūpārūpyāvacarāṇāṃ ca pṛthagjanānām, sāvaśeṣavandhanatvāt / śuddhāśrayasthitiko 'rhatām, sarvabandhanavinirmuktatvāt / sthitisāṃdarśiko buddhānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ ca mahāprabhāvaprāptānām, āhāravaśena sthitiriti saṃdarśanamātratvāt //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, all four nutriments are established equally through four classifications. Namely: sustaining an impure basis — for ordinary beings of the <s>kāmāvacara</s> (desire realm), because of being fully bound. Sustaining a pure-and-impure basis — for trainees and ordinary beings of the <s>rūpāvacara</s> (form realm) and <s>ārūpyāvacara</s> (formless realm), because of having remaining bonds. Sustaining a pure basis — for <s>Arhats</s>, because of being completely freed from all bonds. Merely demonstrating sustenance — for <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have attained great power, because the sustenance through nutriment is merely a display.

body.text: asaṃskṛtaikadeśaḥ niṣpannasvabhāvaḥ sottaramiti nirvāṇaṃ muktvā, tasya sarvadharmāgratvādiśuddhāyāśca tathatāyāstallakṣaṇatvāt //
body.translated_text: A portion of the unconditioned, the <s>pariniṣpannasvabhāva</s> (perfected nature), is said to have something beyond — excluding <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, because <s>Nirvāṇa</s> is the foremost of all <s>dharmas</s> and so forth, and because pure <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) has that characteristic.

body.text: samāsataḥ prabhedastrividhaḥ, trividhaṃ svabhāvamadhikṛtya pudgalanairātmyanayena veditavyaḥ / tatra parikalpitaḥ svabhāvaḥ skandhādīnyadhiṣṭhāyāvidyamāna ātmādisvabhāvo yaḥ parikalpitaḥ / paratantraḥ svabhāvastānyeva skandhādīni yatrāsāvātmadyabhūtavikalpaḥ pravṛttaḥ / pariniṣpannaḥ svabhāvo bhāvābhāvaviyuktalakṣaṇā hi tathatā, skandhādiṣvātmādyabhāvanairātmyāstitālakṣaṇatvāt //
body.translated_text: In summary, the classification is threefold, and should be understood with reference to the three natures through the approach of <s>pudgalanairātmya</s> (selflessness of persons). Among these, the <s>parikalpitasvabhāva</s> (imagined nature) is the non-existent nature of self and so forth that is imagined by superimposing upon the <s>skandhas</s> and the rest. The <s>paratantrasvabhāva</s> (dependent nature) is those very <s>skandhas</s> and the rest in which the unreal conceptualization of self and so forth operates. The <s>pariniṣpannasvabhāva</s> (perfected nature) is <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) characterized by the separation from existence and non-existence, because it has the character of the selflessness consisting in the non-existence of self and so forth in the <s>skandhas</s> and the rest.

body.text: lakṣaṇaprabhedo dharmāṇāṃ svabhāvamadhikṛtya, rūpaṃ vedanetyevamādi / prakāra[pra]bhedo viśeṣamadhikṛtya, dravyasantaḥ prajñaptisanta ityevamādi / āśrayaprabhedaḥ pratyātmabhāvaṃ skandhādīnāṃ nānātvamadhikṛtya /
body.translated_text: Classification by characteristics pertains to the intrinsic nature of <s>dharmas</s> — form, feeling, and so forth. Classification by type pertains to distinctions — substantially existent, conceptually existent, and so forth. Classification by basis pertains to the diversity of the <s>skandhas</s> and the rest with respect to each individual existence.

body.text: saṃtatiprabheda ekasminapyātmabhāve skandhādīnāṃ pratilakṣaṇamanyathātvamadhikṛtya //
body.translated_text: Classification by continuity pertains to the moment-by-moment alteration of the <s>skandhas</s> and the rest even within a single personal existence.

body.text: bahirmukhaprabhedo yadbhūyasā kāmāvacara iti bhūyograhaṇaṃ niṣpandadharmahetukaśrutacintāmayavyudāsārtham // samāptaḥ prabhedaḥ //
body.translated_text: The externally directed classification, insofar as it is predominantly of the <s>kāmāvacara</s> (desire realm) — the word 'predominantly' is for the purpose of excluding those caused by the <s>dharmas</s> of non-agitation and by hearing and reflection. The section on classification is completed.

body.text: lakṣaṇasaṃgraheṇa rūpaskandho rūpaskandhenaiva saṃgṛhīto vistareṇa yāvaddharmāyatanaṃ dharmāyata[ne]naiva / dhātusaṃgraheṇa sarvāṇi skandhadhātvāyatanānyālayavijñānena saṃgṛhītāni, sarveṣāṃ tatra bījato 'stitvāt / jātisaṃgraheṇa skandhaiḥ rāśyādyarthayuktā rūpādayaḥ sarve saṃgṛhītā vilakṣaṇā apyanyonyaṃ svalakṣaṇenaikajātīyatvāt / evaṃ dhātubhiścāyatanaiścopabhogadhāraṇārthayuktā āyadvārārthayuktāścakṣurādayaḥ saṃgṛhītā veditavyāḥ / avasthāsaṃgraheṇa skandhā ekajātīyā api sukhādyavasthāṃ niyamayya sukhāvasthāḥ sukhāvasthaireva saṃgṛhītā na duḥkhādyavasthaiḥ / evaṃ duḥkhāvasthāduḥkhāsukhāvasthāśca tadavasthai[re]va saṃgṛhītāḥ / yathā skandhā evaṃ dhātava āyatanāni ca / sahāyasaṃgraheṇa rūpaskandhaḥ saha tadāśritairvedanādibhiḥ sahāyairgṛhyamāṇaḥ pañcabhiḥ skandhaiḥ saṃgṛhītaḥ / evaṃ vedanādayāpi pratyekaṃ saparivārā gṛhyamāṇāḥ pañcabhiḥ skandhaiḥ saṃgṛhītā bhavanti / tathā dhātava āyatanāni ca saparivārāṇi pratyekaṃ sarvardhātubhirāyataneśca saṃgṛhītāni veditavyāni / ekadeśasaṃgraheṇa śīlaskandho rūpaskandhaikadeśena saṃgṛhītaḥ / samādhiprajñāskandhau saṃskāraskandhaikadeśena / kāmavyāpādahiṃsādhātavo dharmadhātvekadeśena saṃgṛhītāḥ / ākāśānantyāyatanādīni manodharmāyatanaikadeśena saṃgṛhītāni / evaṃ kṛtvā yāvanto dharmāḥ skandhadhātvāyatanaiḥ saṃgṛhītāḥ sūtrāntareṣu teṣāmanyatamasaṃgraha ekadeśasaṃgraho veditavyaḥ / sakalasaṃgraheṇa duḥkhaskandhaḥ pañcabhirupādānaskandhaiḥ saṃgṛhītaḥ, kāmadhāturaṣṭādaśabhirdhātubhiḥ, asaṃjñi sattvāyatanaṃ daśabhirāyatanaṃgandharasāyatanavarjaiḥ saṃgṛhītam / evaṃ kṛtvā yāvanto dharmāḥ skandhadhātvāyatanaṃḥ saṃgṛhītāḥ sūtrāntareṣu teṣāmaśeṣataḥ saṃgrahaḥ sakalasaṃgraho veditavyaḥ / itaretarasaṃgraheṇa skandhāḥ pratyekaṃ dhātubhirāyatanaiśca saṃgṛhītāḥ, yathāyogamevaṃ dhātavaḥ skandhāyatanarāyatanāni skandhadhātubhiḥ saṃgṛhītāni [iti] vistareṇāvagantavyam //
body.translated_text: By inclusion through characteristics, the <s>rūpaskandha</s> (form aggregate) is included by the form aggregate itself, and in detail up to the <s>dharmāyatana</s> by the <s>dharmāyatana</s> itself. By inclusion through <s>dhātu</s> (element), all <s>skandhas</s>, <s>dhātus</s>, and <s>āyatanas</s> are included in the <s>ālayavijñāna</s>, because all exist there in seed-form. By inclusion through class, all form and the rest — included in the <s>skandhas</s> which have the meaning of a heap and so forth — are included mutually even when of different characteristics, because they are of one class by their own characteristics. Likewise, those included in the <s>dhātus</s> and <s>āyatanas</s>, having the meaning of sustaining and enjoyment, and having the meaning of being doors of arising — the eye and the rest — should be understood as included. By inclusion through state, even the <s>skandhas</s> of one class, when their state is determined as pleasure and so forth, those in the state of pleasure are included only by those in the state of pleasure, not by those in the state of pain and so forth. Likewise, those in states of pain and neither-pain-nor-pleasure are included only by those in those same states. As with the <s>skandhas</s>, so too the <s>dhātus</s> and <s>āyatanas</s>. By inclusion through companions, the <s>rūpaskandha</s>, when taken together with feeling and the rest that depend on it as companions, is included in all five <s>skandhas</s>. Likewise, feeling and the rest, each taken with their retinue, are included in all five <s>skandhas</s>. Similarly, the <s>dhātus</s> and <s>āyatanas</s>, each with their retinue, should be understood as included in all the <s>dhātus</s> and <s>āyatanas</s>. By partial inclusion, the moral-conduct aggregate is included in a portion of the <s>rūpaskandha</s>. The concentration and wisdom aggregates are included in a portion of the <s>saṃskāraskandha</s>. The elements of desire, malice, and harm are included in a portion of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>. The sphere of infinite space and the rest are included in a portion of the <s>manas</s> and <s>dharmāyatana</s>. In this way, however many <s>dharmas</s> are included in the <s>skandhas</s>, <s>dhātus</s>, and <s>āyatanas</s>, the inclusion of any one of those in other <s>sūtras</s> should be understood as partial inclusion. By complete inclusion, the aggregate of suffering is included in the five aggregates of clinging; the desire realm in eighteen <s>dhātus</s>; the realm of non-perceptive beings in ten <s>āyatanas</s> excluding the smell and taste sense bases. In this way, however many <s>dharmas</s> are included in the <s>skandhas</s>, <s>dhātus</s>, and <s>āyatanas</s>, their exhaustive inclusion in other <s>sūtras</s> should be understood as complete inclusion. By mutual inclusion, the <s>skandhas</s> are each included in the <s>dhātus</s> and <s>āyatanas</s>; accordingly, the <s>dhātus</s> are included in the <s>skandhas</s> and <s>āyatanas</s>; and the <s>āyatanas</s> are included in the <s>skandhas</s> and <s>dhātus</s> — this should be understood in detail.

body.text: saṃgrahalakṣaṇaṃ punarlokaprasiddhasaṃgrahānusāreṇa ṣaḍidvadhaṃ draṣṭavyam / tatpunaḥ katamat / padasthānasaṃgraho yathā jambūdvīpasaṃgṛhītā manuṣyāḥ, araṇyasaṃgṛhītā mṛgā iti loke ucyate tathehāpi cakṣurādibhiḥ cakṣurvijñānādīnāṃ saṃgraho veditavyaḥ / nibandhasaṃgraho yathā rajjvādinā kāṣṭhabhārādikasya tathā kāyena cakṣurādonāmindriyāṇām / tulyārthasaṃgraho yathā samānasarvaprayojanānāṃ visrambhiṇāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ parasparaṃ tarthakālaṃbanapravṛttānāṃ saṃprayuktānāmānyonyam / upādānasaṃgraho yathā svāminā ātmīyataḥ parigrahītādīnā dāsādīnāṃ tathālayavijñānenātmabhāvasya / avisārasaṃgraho yathā ghaṭenodakasya tathā samādhinā tadanyeṣāṃ cittacaitasikānām / abhisaṃkṣepa[saṃ]graho yathā samudreṇa nadīnāṃ tathā rūpaskandhena cakṣurādonāmiti / tadatrābhisakṣapasaṃgrahamadhikṛtyakādaśavidhaḥ saṃgraho veditavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: The characteristic of inclusion, furthermore, should be understood as sixfold, following the worldly conventions of inclusion. What then is that? Inclusion by location — just as in the world it is said 'humans are included in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>' and 'deer are included in the forest,' so here too the inclusion of eye-consciousness and the rest by the eye and the rest should be understood. Inclusion by binding — just as a bundle of wood is bound by a rope and the rest, so the faculties of the eye and the rest by the body. Inclusion by common purpose — just as among trustworthy people who share all purposes there is mutual support, so among associated mind and mental factors that operate at the same time with the same object, there is mutual inclusion. Inclusion by appropriation — just as servants and the rest are taken up by a master as his own, so the personal existence is appropriated by the <s>ālayavijñāna</s>. Inclusion by containment — just as water is contained by a pot, so mind and mental factors other than <s>samādhi</s> are contained by <s>samādhi</s>. Inclusion by condensation — just as rivers are condensed by the ocean, so the eye and the rest are condensed by the <s>rūpaskandha</s>. Here, with reference to inclusion by condensation, the elevenfold inclusion should be understood.

body.text: paramāṇudeśe sarveṣāṃ deśināmityekaparamāṇuparyāpannānāṃ rūpādīnāmavinirbhāgaḥ samānadeśatvena veditavyaḥ / paramāṇorūrdhva sarveṣāṃ deśināṃ miśrībhāvaḥ tadyathā kaluṣe pānīye appṛthivīparamāṇūnāṃ paramparam / deśināmeva samudāyināmanyonyaṃ samavadhānaṃ tadyathā bhittau mṛtpiṇḍena mṛtpiṇḍāntarasya / sahabhāvasaṃ[pra]yoga ekātmabhāve kṣaṇikānāṃ skandhādīnām / kṛtyānuṣṭhānasaṃprayoga ekasmin prayojane prayuktānāmanyonyam / saṃpratipattisaṃprayogaḥ parabhāvena na svabhāvena tadyathā cittaṃ cittāntareṇa na saṃprayujyate, vedanā vedanāntareṇetyavamādi / na viruddhayostadyathā rāgadveṣayoḥ kuśalākuśalayorvetyevamādi / na visadṛśakālayostadyathā vartamānānāgatayoratītavartamānayorvā / na visabhāgadhātubhūmikayostadyathā kāmāvacararūpāvacarayoḥ prathamadvitīyadhyānabhūmikayorvetyevamādi / sarvatragaḥ saṃpratipattisaṃprayoga vedanādīnāṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ sarvāsvavasthāsveṣāṃ vinānyonyamabhāvāt / ucitastadekatyānāṃ ca śaikṣāśaikṣāṇāmityekāntalaukikānāṃ kuśalānāmakuśalāvyākṛtānāṃ ca yathāsaṃbhavam / ādyataduttarāṇāmityapūrvajātīyatvena prathamakṣaṇotpannānāṃ dvitīyādikṣaṇotpannānāṃ ca lokottarāṇāmanucitatvajñāpanārtham //
body.translated_text: In the region of a single <s>paramāṇu</s> (atom), the inseparability of all things having location, such as form and the rest included within a single atom, should be understood as having the same location. Above the level of the atom, the intermixture of all things having location — for example, in turbid water, the atoms of water and earth interpenetrate one another. The mutual aggregation of things having location that are in combination — for example, a lump of clay joined to another lump of clay in a wall. The association of co-existence is of the momentary <s>skandhas</s> and the rest within a single personal existence. The association through functional activity is the mutual association of those engaged in a single purpose. The association through correspondence is by other-nature and not by self-nature — for example, <s>citta</s> (mind) is not associated with another <s>citta</s>, feeling is not associated with another feeling, and so forth. Not between what is opposed — for example, between <s>rāga</s> (passion) and <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion), or between wholesome and unwholesome, and so forth. Not between those of different times — for example, between the present and the future, or between the past and the present. Not between those of different realms and levels — for example, between the <s>kāmāvacara</s> (desire realm) and <s>rūpāvacara</s> (form realm), or between the first and second <s>dhyāna</s> levels, and so forth. The universal correspondence-association is that of feeling and the other five in all states, because without one another they do not exist. The customary association is that of certain trainees and non-trainees — that is, of those exclusively mundane, the wholesome, the unwholesome, and the indeterminate, as the case may be. 'Of those first and their successors' — this is to indicate the non-customary nature of those born at the first moment as a new class, and those born at the second and subsequent moments, among the supramundane.

body.text: samanvāgamo lakṣaṇataḥ pūrvavattadyathā kuśalādīnāṃ dharmāṇāmācayāpacaye prāptiḥ pratilambhaḥ samanvāgama iti prajñaptiḥ / bījasamanvāgama iti kāmadhātau jātau bhūtastraidhātukaiḥ kleśopakleśaiḥ samanvāgata ityavītarāgaṃ pṛthagjanamadhikṛtyaitadvaiditavyam / vītarāgastu tatrordhvaṃ vā jāto yato bhūmervītarāgastadbhūmikairasamanvāgataḥ samanvāgataśca, pratipakṣeṇopahatatvādasamuddhātitatvāccānuśayato yathākramam / upapattiprātilambhikaṃśca kuśalariti yatra jātastadbhūmikaireva / traidhātukapratipakṣalābhīti lokottaramārgalābhī / yasya yasya prakārasya pratipakṣa utpanna iti bhāvanāprahātavyasyādhimātrādeḥ kleśasya / tasya tasya bījasamanvāgamenāsamanvāgato 'nuśayataḥ samuddhātitatvāt / vaśitāsamanvāgamaḥ prāyogikānāṃ kuśalānāmiti śrutamayādīnāṃ satyapi bīje tadabhyāsakṛtāṃ tajjanmikīṃ bījapuṣṭimantareṇa saṃmukhīkartumaśakyatvāt / tadekatyānāṃ cāvyākṛtānāṃ śaṃlpasthānikanairmāṇikacittaprabhṛtīnām //
body.translated_text: Possession (<s>samanvāgama</s>) is, in terms of characteristics, as before — namely, in the accumulation and diminution of wholesome and other <s>dharmas</s>, acquisition (<s>prāpti</s>), obtainment (<s>pratilambha</s>), and possession (<s>samanvāgama</s>) are designations. Seed-possession (<s>bījasamanvāgama</s>) should be understood with reference to an ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) who has not become dispassionate and who, born in the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>), is a being possessed of the afflictions and secondary afflictions of all three realms. But one who has become dispassionate, whether born there or above — from whichever level one has become dispassionate, one is no longer possessed of [the afflictions] belonging to that level, yet is still possessed [of them] as latent tendencies (<s>anuśaya</s>), respectively because [those afflictions have been] damaged by the antidote and because they have not been eradicated. And as for the wholesome [dharmas] obtained at birth — [one is possessed] only of those belonging to the level where one has been born. One who has obtained the antidote to the three realms is one who has obtained the supramundane path. 'Of whatever type of affliction the antidote has arisen' refers to the afflictions to be abandoned by cultivation (<s>bhāvanāprahātavya</s>), beginning with the intense. One is not possessed of the seed-possession of that particular [affliction], because it has been eradicated as a latent tendency. Mastery-possession (<s>vaśitāsamanvāgama</s>) of the applied wholesome [dharmas] — such as those arising from learning and so forth — is because even though the seed exists, without the nourishment of the seed through repeated practice in that very birth, [those dharmas] cannot be brought to manifestation. And [this applies] to certain indeterminate [dharmas] such as the mind of transformation (<s>nirmāṇacitta</s>) produced through conceptualization and the like.

body.text: mokṣahetuvaikalyādātyantika eṣāṃ hetvasamanvāgama iti / mokṣaprāptihetvasamanvāgama ityarthaḥ / kaḥ punarmokṣaprāptihetuḥ / yasyaivaṃ tathatāyāṃ kleśadauṣṭhulyaṃ saṃniviṣṭaṃ bhavati tatsati pratipakṣānukūlapratyayalābhe śakyate samuddhātayitum, sa bhavyatā rthena heturityucyate / viparyayāddhetuvaikalyaṃ veditavyam //
body.translated_text: 'Because of the deficiency of the cause for liberation, the non-possession of the cause is ultimate for these' — the meaning is: the non-possession of the cause for attaining liberation. What then is the cause for attaining liberation? When, in the <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) of a being, the unsuitability (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>) of afflictions is so embedded that, given the obtaining of conditions favorable to the antidote, it can be eradicated — that, in the sense of capacity (<s>bhavyatā</s>), is called the 'cause.' The deficiency of the cause should be understood as the opposite.

body.text: II satyaviniścayo nāma dvitīyaḥ samuccayaḥ
body.translated_text: II. The Determination of the Truths (<s>Satyaviniścaya</s>), the Second Compendium

body.text: tatsattvajanmato janmādhiṣṭhānataśceti yaśca jāyate sattvalokaḥ, yatra ca jāyate bhājanaloke, tadubhayaṃ duḥkha mityuktaṃ bhavati / yaśca sattvaloko yaśca bhājanalokaḥ karmakleśajanitaḥ karmakleśādhipateya ityābhyāṃ tayoḥ sattvabhājanalokayorduḥkhatvakāraṇaṃ jñāpayati //
body.translated_text: 'From the birth of those beings and from the basis of birth' — the sentient world (<s>sattvaloka</s>) that is born, and the receptacle world (<s>bhājanaloka</s>) in which it is born — both of these are said to be suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>). 'The sentient world and the receptacle world are produced by <s>karma</s> and afflictions, having <s>karma</s> and afflictions as their dominant [conditions]' — by these [two statements], [the text] indicates the cause of the suffering of both the sentient world and the receptacle world.

body.text: api khalu jātirduḥkhamityevamādi pūrvaṃ samasya duḥkhasatyalakṣaṇaṃ vyutpādyādhunā duḥkhasatyamārabhya sūtroktasya nirdeśasyārtha vibhaktumārabhate //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, 'birth is suffering' and so forth — having first summarized and explained the characteristic of the truth of suffering, [the text] now begins to analyze the meaning of the exposition stated in the <s>sūtras</s>, starting from the truth of suffering.

body.text: jātirduḥkhaṃ saṃvādaduḥkhatāṃ tadanyadukhasvāśrayatāṃ copādāyeti mātuḥ kukṣāvāmapakvāśayayorantarāle āsīnasya niṣkrāmato vā kukṣervividhāśucidravyāsaṃpīḍāṅgasaṃmardaduḥkhānubhavanārthena, jātau satyāṃ jarādiduḥkhābhyanuṣaṅgārthena ca yathākramam //
body.translated_text: 'Birth is suffering' should be understood with reference to the suffering of contact (<s>saṃvāda</s>) and the suffering of being the basis for other suffering — namely, for one seated between the stomach and the intestines in the mother's womb, or for one emerging from the womb, for the purpose of experiencing the suffering of being pressed against various impure substances and of limbs being crushed; and because when there is birth, suffering of aging and so forth follows — respectively in order.

body.text: ṣaṭ samānānyaṣṭau bhavanti vipariṇatidukhaṃ tridhā kṛtvā //
body.translated_text: Six [characteristics] are common; [when] the suffering of transformation is made threefold, there are eight.

body.text: jātyādibhirduḥkhaduḥkhatāparidīpanavacanaṃ duḥkhavedanīyadharmasvalakṣaṇārthena / priyavināmāvādinā vipariṇāmaduḥkhatāparidīpanavacanaṃ prāptāprāptasukhavedanīyadharmavipariṇatisvalakṣaṇārthena / pañcopādānaskandhā duḥkhamityanena
body.translated_text: The statement illuminating the suffering of suffering (<s>duḥkhaduḥkhatā</s>) through birth and so forth is for the purpose of the own-characteristic of <s>dharmas</s> that are experienced as painful. The statement illuminating the suffering of transformation (<s>vipariṇāmaduḥkhatā</s>) through separation from the beloved and so forth is for the purpose of the own-characteristic of the transformation of <s>dharmas</s> experienced as pleasant, whether obtained or not yet obtained. By 'the five aggregates of clinging are suffering'

body.text: saṃskāraduḥkhatāparidīpanavacanaṃ dvayāvinirmokṣānityetā nubandhayogakṣemārthena //
body.translated_text: the statement illuminating the suffering of conditioned existence (<s>saṃskāraduḥkhatā</s>) is for the purpose of the impermanent bondage to the two [types of suffering], the connection with insecurity, and the well-being [that is threatened].

body.text: jātirdukhamityevamādi saṃvṛtisatyena dukham, laukikajñānaviṣayatvāt / pañcopādānaskandhā duḥkhamiti paramārthasatyena dukham, saṃniveśatathatāmukhena lokottarajñānaviṣayatvāt //
body.translated_text: 'Birth is suffering' and so forth is suffering according to conventional truth (<s>saṃvṛtisatya</s>), because it is the domain of worldly knowledge. 'The five aggregates of clinging are suffering' is suffering according to ultimate truth (<s>paramārthasatya</s>), because through the gateway of the <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) of the composite, it is the domain of supramundane knowledge.

body.text: duḥkhasāmānyalakṣaṇe yairākārairyogine duḥkhasatyaṃ vyavacārayanti, tadyathānityato duḥkhataḥ śūnyato 'nātmataśca //
body.translated_text: Regarding the general characteristics of suffering — the aspects by which practitioners (<s>yogins</s>) determine the truth of suffering are: as impermanent, as suffering, as empty, and as non-self.

body.text: tatra dvādaśavidhena lakṣaṇenānityaṃ duḥkhasatyaṃ veditavyam / tatpuna rasallakṣaṇaṃ yathā nāsti sarvadā duḥkhasatyamā[tmā]tmoyasvabhāvamiti yo 'rthaḥ so 'rtho 'nityaṃ duḥkhasatyamiti / akārasya pratiṣedhārthatvāt nityaśabdasya ca sarvakālārthatvāditi / vināśalakṣaṇaṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ bhūtvābhāvaḥ / vipariṇatilakṣaṇaṃ prabandhāsādṛśyena pravṛttiḥ / viyogalakṣaṇaṃ tadavastheṣveva vastuṣu svabhāvavaśitvabhraṃśaḥ kvacitparaiḥ svīkaraṇamapi veditavyam / saṃnihitalakṣaṇaṃ yattadānīmevānubhūyamānānityatā / dharmatālakṣaṇaṃ yāmavaśyamanubhaviṣyati / kṣaṇalakṣaṇamātmalābhānantaramavaśyavināśitā / prabandhalakṣaṇamanādimati saṃsāre ājavaṃjavībhāvena vṛttiḥ / vyādhijarāmaraṇalakṣaṇaṃ dhātuvaiṣamyaṃ khalityādikaṃ sthitikālāvedhopayogaśca / cittacittākāravṛttilakṣaṇaṃ vipakṣapratipakṣāvasthānāvasthitatvam / bhogasaṃpattilakṣaṇaṃ sarvalaukikasamṛddho nāmanātyantikatayā durantatvam / bhājanasaṃvartavivartalakṣaṇaṃ mahāpṛthivyādināmagnyādibhiḥ punaḥ punarvināśa[ta] utpādataśca, agnyambuvāyusaṃvartanībhirdahanakledanaśoṣaṇātmikābhiryathākramam / prathamadvitīyatṛtīyadhyānasthānāvasāne lokasaṃniveśe saṃvṛtte tadūrdhvaṃ yānyavaśiṣyante dvitīyatṛtīyacaturthadhyānasyānāntarāṇi tāni tāsāṃ śīrṣāṇi veditavyāni / caturthadhyānabhūmikānāṃ tarhi vimānānāṃ kena saṃvartavivartaḥ / na kena cidbāhyena, taireva tu sarvairjāyamānaiḥ saha tāni vimānāni nirvartante cyavamānaiḥ saha
body.translated_text: Therein, the truth of suffering should be understood as impermanent through twelve characteristics. The essential characteristic: that the truth of suffering does not exist at all times as possessing a self-nature — this meaning is [conveyed by] 'the truth of suffering is impermanent,' because the prefix 'a-' has the meaning of negation and the word 'nitya' (permanent) has the meaning of 'at all times.' The characteristic of destruction: the non-existence after having existed of conditioned things. The characteristic of transformation: occurrence with dissimilarity in the continuum. The characteristic of separation: the loss of sovereignty over one's own nature in regard to those very things remaining in those very states; in some cases, appropriation by others should also be understood. The characteristic of proximity: impermanence that is being experienced at that very moment. The characteristic of natural law (<s>dharmatā</s>): that which one will inevitably experience. The characteristic of momentariness: inevitable destruction immediately upon obtaining self-existence. The characteristic of the continuum: functioning in an uninterrupted back-and-forth manner in beginningless <s>saṃsāra</s>. The characteristic of disease, aging, and death: imbalance of the bodily constituents (<s>dhātus</s>), baldness and the like, and the utilization of the duration's termination of existence. The characteristic of the modes of mind and mental factors: instability due to being in the conditions of opposition and antidote. The characteristic of the fortune of enjoyments: all worldly prosperity, because of its non-ultimate nature, being interminable [in its suffering]. The characteristic of the formation and dissolution of the receptacle [world]: the repeated destruction and production of the great earth and so forth by fire and so forth — through the fire-dissolution, water-dissolution, and wind-dissolution, which are respectively of the nature of burning, moistening, and drying. At the end of the [cosmic] abiding in the realms of the first, second, and third <s>dhyānas</s>, when the world-system has been dissolved, those [realms] that remain above, immediately adjacent to the second, third, and fourth <s>dhyānas</s>, should be understood as the upper limits of those [dissolutions]. As for the celestial mansions of beings belonging to the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> level — by what [means] is their formation and dissolution? Not by any external [cause], but rather those mansions come into being together with all those beings as they are born, and

body.text: tāni nirudhyanta iti / sa eva teṣāṃ saṃvartavivarto veditavyaḥ / yaiḥ kalpasya niryāṇaṃ bhavatīti parisamāptirbhavatītyarthaḥ / eko 'ntarakalpo 'pakarṣaḥ vivartakāle ekānnaviṃśati[ta]maḥ / aṣṭādaśa utkarṣāpakarṣāḥ / tata ūrdhvameka utkarṣaḥ paścimaḥ / āyukṣayānmaraṇaṃ kālacyutimadhikṛtya yāvadākṣepamāyuṣaḥ parisamāptatvāt / puṇyakṣayādakālacyuti[madhikṛtya] samāpattyāsvādanatayā tadāyurākṣepakakarmabhāvanopadhātāt / karmakṣayātprabandhacyutimadhikṛtya, tasminnāyatane upapadyāparaparyāyavedanīyakarmaṇa upayuktatvādabhāvādvā tatra bhūyo 'nutpattito veditavyam //
body.translated_text: they cease together with those [beings] as they pass away — that very [process] should be understood as their formation and dissolution. 'By whom the exhaustion of the <s>kalpa</s> occurs' means its completion comes about — that is the meaning. One intermediate <s>kalpa</s> (<s>antarakalpa</s>) of decline is the nineteenth during the period of dissolution. Eighteen are the [kalpas of] increase and decrease. Above those, one final [kalpa] of increase. 'Death from the exhaustion of lifespan' — with reference to timely death (<s>kālacyuti</s>), because the projected lifespan has been fully exhausted. 'Death from the exhaustion of merit' — [with reference to] untimely death (<s>akālacyuti</s>), because through savoring the attainments, the <s>karma</s> that projected the lifespan is not nourished through cultivation. 'Death from the exhaustion of <s>karma</s>' — with reference to death in the continuum, because in that realm of existence, the <s>karma</s> to be experienced in a subsequent life has been utilized, or because of its absence, there is no further arising there — this should be understood.

body.text: aṣṭākāraṃ vā duḥkhamiti saṃbādhaduḥkhatādi / utpādāṃśikī anityatā abhūtvā bhāvaḥ, sa ca duḥkhapakṣyāṇāṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ bādhanātmakaḥ / iti tāmanityatāṃ pratītya duḥkhaduḥkhatā prajñāyate / vyayāṃśikī bhūtvābhāvaḥ, sa ca sukhapakṣyāṇāṃ saṃskārāṇāmanabhipretaḥ / iti tāṃ pratītya vipariṇāmaduḥkhatā prajñāyate / sadauṣṭhulyānāṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ prabandhenodayo 'pyanabhipretaḥ, vyayo 'pīti tadubhayāṃśikīmanityatāṃ pratītya saṃskāraduḥkhatā prajñāyate / saṃskārānityatāṃ saṃskāravipariṇāmatāṃ ca saṃdhāyoktam - mayā yatkiṃcidveditamidamatra duḥkhasyetyayamaduḥkhāsukhasya sukhasya ca veditasya duḥkha vacane 'bhisaṃdhirveditavyaḥ / duḥkhasya tu veditasya duḥkhatvena prasiddhatvālloke na tatra punarabhisaṃdhirucyata iti / yeṣu cānityeṣu saṃskāreṣu jātyādikaṃ prajñāyate [teṣām] anityatvāt duḥkhamityabhisaṃdhirveditavyaḥ / anyathā mārgo 'pyanityatvādduḥkhaṃ syāditi //
body.translated_text: 'Or suffering is eightfold' refers to the suffering of constriction and so forth. The impermanence pertaining to arising is coming-into-being after not having existed, and that is of the nature of afflicting conditioned things belonging to the suffering side. Thus, dependent on that impermanence, the suffering of suffering (<s>duḥkhaduḥkhatā</s>) is recognized. The impermanence pertaining to destruction is non-existence after having existed, and that is unwanted by conditioned things belonging to the happiness side. Thus, dependent on that, the suffering of transformation (<s>vipariṇāmaduḥkhatā</s>) is recognized. The arising of conditioned things that are ever burdened with unsuitability (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>) in their continuum is also unwanted, and their destruction is also [unwanted] — thus, dependent on the impermanence pertaining to both aspects, the suffering of conditioned existence (<s>saṃskāraduḥkhatā</s>) is recognized. With reference to the impermanence of formations and the transformability of formations, [the <s>Bhagavān</s>] stated: 'Whatever I have experienced, that is [included] herein among suffering' — this intention should be understood as the statement that [what is experienced as] neither-suffering-nor-pleasure and [what is experienced as] pleasure are also suffering. But what is experienced as suffering, being well-known in the world as suffering, need not be specifically intended again. And in regard to those impermanent formations in which birth and so forth are recognized, the intention should be understood as: 'Because of the impermanence of those [formations], they are suffering.' Otherwise, the path too, being impermanent, would be suffering.

body.text: śūnyatālakṣaṇaṃ nityādilakṣaṇasyātmanaḥ saṃskārebhyo 'rthāntarabhūtasya teṣvabhāvaḥ / teṣāṃ ca saṃskārāṇāṃ nityakālaṃ tadrahitaprakṛtikalakṣaṇasya
body.translated_text: The characteristic of emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) is the non-existence, among the formations, of a self that possesses characteristics such as permanence and so forth and that is a separate entity from those [formations]. And the existence of selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>) — [namely,] the natural characteristic of those very formations as being perpetually devoid of that [self] —

body.text: nairātmyasya bhāvastadubhayaṃ śūnyatetyucyate / svabhāvaśūnyatā parikalpitaṃ svabhāvamu[pā]dāya, tasya svalakṣaṇenaivābhāvāt / tathābhāvaśūnyatā paratantraṃ svabhāvamupādāya, tasya yena yena prakāreṇa parikalpyate tena tena prakāreṇābhāvāt / prakṛtiśūnyatā pariniṣpannaṃ svabhāvamupādāya tasya śūnyatāprakṛtikatvāt //
body.translated_text: both of those together are called emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>). Emptiness of own-nature (<s>svabhāvaśūnyatā</s>) is with reference to the imagined own-nature (<s>parikalpita svabhāva</s>), because it does not exist by its own characteristic. Emptiness of existence (<s>tathābhāvaśūnyatā</s>) is with reference to the dependent own-nature (<s>paratantra svabhāva</s>), because in whatever manner it is imagined, in that manner it does not exist. Natural emptiness (<s>prakṛtiśūnyatā</s>) is with reference to the perfected own-nature (<s>pariniṣpanna svabhāva</s>), because its nature is emptiness itself.

body.text: anātmalakṣaṇaṃ punasteṣāmeva saṃskārāṇāmātmavādibhiḥ parikalpitenātmalakṣaṇenānātmalakṣaṇatā //
body.translated_text: The characteristic of non-self (<s>anātman</s>) is the selflessness of those very formations in regard to the self-characteristic imagined by the proponents of self (<s>ātmavādins</s>).

body.text: vināśādilakṣaṇānityatā prasiddhā, kṣaṇikalakṣaṇā tu na prasiddhā sarvasaṃskārāṇāmataḥ sā prasādhayitavyā / tatra cittacaitasikānāṃ kṣaṇikatvaṃ loke prasiddhamataḥ tenāprasiddhaṃ rūpasya kṣaṇikatvaṃ prasādhyate / kathamiti / cittopāttatāmupādāya, kṣaṇikena hi cittena kāya upātta / kenārthena / cittaikayogakṣematāmupādāya, tathāhi kāyaḥ savijñānaka eva samudāgacchati vijñānāpakrāntyā ca pūtībhavati / tasmāccittenaikayogakṣematvāttadivāsya kṣaṇikatvaṃ veditavyam / kiṃ ca cittāśrayatāmupādāya, cittasya hi [vi]kāreṇa kāyasya vikāro dṛśyate sukhaduḥkharāgadveṣādyavasthāsu / ataḥ pratikṣaṇaṃ vikāriṇaścetaso 'nuvidhānāt kāyasya kṣaṇikatvaṃ siddham / cittādhipatyasaṃbhūtatāmupādāya, cittasya hi sendriyaḥ kāya āśrayaḥ prasiddhaḥ, yasya ca ya utpatyāśrayo nāsau svavināśamantareṇa tasyāśrayībhavandṛṣṭaḥ / tadyathāgnyaṃkurādīnāmindhanabījādikaḥ / tasmātpratikṣaṇaṃ cittasyāśrayabhāvātpratikṣaṇameva vinaśyatīti siddham / cittasyādhipatyasaṃbhūtatāmupādāya, sarvaṃ hyādhyātmikabāhyaṃ rūpaṃ cittasyādhipatyena saṃbhavati / ataḥ kāraṇasya kṣaṇikatvātkāryasya kṣaṇikatvaṃ veditavyam, ye hetavo ye pratyayāḥ rūpasyātpādāya te 'pyanityāḥ, anityān khalu hetupratyayān pratītyotpannaṃ rūpaṃ kuto nityaṃ bhaviṣyatīti sūtrapadānusāreṇa / cittavaśavarttitāṃ copādāya, prabhāvaviśiṣṭasya ca cittasya
body.translated_text: Impermanence characterized by destruction and so forth is well-established, but the momentary characteristic (<s>kṣaṇikalakṣaṇa</s>) of all formations is not well-established; therefore, it must be demonstrated.
