Therein, the momentariness of mind and mental factors is well-known in the world; therefore, through that, the momentariness of form, which is not well-established, is demonstrated. How? First, through being appropriated by the mind (<s>cittopāttatā</s>) — for the body is appropriated by the mind, which is momentary. In what sense? Through sharing the same fortune as the mind (<s>cittaikayogakṣematā</s>) — for indeed the body functions only when endowed with consciousness, and upon the departure of consciousness it putrefies. Therefore, because of sharing the same fortune as the mind, its momentariness should be understood just like [the mind's]. Furthermore, through being the support of the mind (<s>cittāśrayatā</s>) — for transformation of the body is observed corresponding to the transformation of the mind, in the states of pleasure, suffering, attachment, aversion, and so forth. Therefore, since the body follows the mind that transforms at each moment, the momentariness of the body is established. Through being produced under the dominance of the mind (<s>cittādhipatyasaṃbhūtatā</s>) — for it is well-established that the body with its sense faculties is the support of the mind, and whatever is the support for the arising of something is never seen to become its support without undergoing its own destruction. For example, fuel and seeds are [the supports] for fire and sprouts. Therefore, since [the body] serves as the support of the mind at each moment, it is established that it perishes at each moment. Through being produced under the dominance of the mind — for all form, both internal and external, comes into being under the dominance of the mind. Therefore, from the momentariness of the cause, the momentariness of the effect should be understood — 'those causes and those conditions for the arising of form are also impermanent; how could form produced in dependence on impermanent causes and conditions be permanent?' — following this <s>sūtra</s> passage. And through being subject to the control of the mind — for form is under the control of the mind endowed with special power,

body.text: rūpaṃ vaśe vartate, tena yatheṣṭaṃ pariṇāmāt / ataḥ pratikṣaṇamanyathādhimokṣe satyanyathotpādātkṣaṇikatvasiddhiḥ / api khalu ante vikāropalabdhitāmupādāya, na hi pratikṣaṇaprakṛtivikāritāmantareṇākasmiko rūpasyānte vikāro yuktaḥ, sa copalabhyate / tasmātsvāsāṃtānikapratikṣaṇavikārābhivṛddhihetukatvādantyasya rūpavikārasya kṣaṇikaṃ rūpamiti siddham / utpannasya cānapekṣya pratyayaṃ svarasavināśitāmupādāya, sarvasyotpannasya vināśaḥ pratyayamanapekṣya svarasenaiva bhavati / ataḥ pratyayāntaranirapekṣo 'vaśyaṃbhāvī vināśa utpannamātrasyaiva bhāvasya na bhavati paścādbhatīti [na] kiṃcidviśeṣaṇamasti / tasmātsarveṇa vināśinotpannamātreṇa vinaṣṭamiti siddhaṃ kṣaṇikatvam //
body.translated_text: because [the mind] transforms [form] as it wishes. Therefore, when there is a different resolve at each moment, from the arising of something different [at each moment], momentariness is established. Furthermore, through the observation of deterioration at the end (<s>ante vikāropalabdhitā</s>) — for without momentary natural transformation, a sudden deterioration of form at the end would not be reasonable, yet it is observed. Therefore, because the final deterioration of form is caused by the progressive increase of momentary transformation within one's own continuum, it is established that form is momentary. And through the spontaneous destruction of what has arisen without depending on conditions (<s>utpannasya svarasavināśitā</s>) — for the destruction of everything that has arisen occurs spontaneously without depending on [additional] conditions. Therefore, destruction that is inevitable and independent of other conditions belongs to what has just arisen — there is no distinguishing characteristic [that it comes about] 'later.' Therefore, since everything that is subject to destruction has perished at the very moment of its arising, momentariness (<s>kṣaṇikatva</s>) is established.

body.text: ekapradeśāśrayibhāvārtha upādāyārthaḥ, bhūtadeśanirapekṣasya pṛthak svatantravṛttitāsāmārthyābhāvāt / asti samudāya ekabhautikastadyathā śuṣko mṛtpiṇḍaḥ / asti dvibhūtikaḥ sa evārdraḥ / asti tribhūtikaḥ sa evoṣṇaḥ / asti sarvabhūtikaḥ sa evārdra uṣṇaśca mṛtpiṇḍo gamanāvasthāyāmiti / asti samudāya ekopādāyarūpikastadyathā prabhā / dvyupādāyarūpikastadyathā śabdagandho vāyuḥ / tryupādāyarūpikastadyathā dhūmaḥ, tasya rūpagandhaspraṣṭavyaviśeṣaprabhāvitatvāt / spraṣṭavyaviśeṣaḥ punaratra laghutvaṃ veditavyam / caturupādāyarūpikastadyathā guḍapiṇḍaḥ / pañcopādāyarūpikastadyathā sa eva saśabdaḥ / itya[nya]trāpi yadyatropalabhyate bhūtaṃ bhautikaṃ vā tatra tadastīti veditavyaṃ nānyatra /
body.translated_text: The meaning of 'derived' (<s>upādāya</s>) is being dependent on a partial basis, because [derived form] lacks the capacity to function independently apart from the actual elements (<s>bhūtas</s>). There is a combination of a single element — for example, a dry lump of clay. There is a two-element [combination] — the same when moist. There is a three-element [combination] — the same when hot. There is an all-element [combination] — the same moist and hot lump of clay in a state of motion. There is a combination of a single derived form (<s>upādāyarūpa</s>) — for example, radiance. Of two derived forms — for example, sound and smell, or wind. Of three derived forms — for example, smoke, because it is produced by the special qualities of form, smell, and tangibility. The special tangibility here should be understood as lightness. Of four derived forms — for example, a lump of molasses. Of five derived forms — the same when accompanied by sound. Thus, in any other case as well, whatever element or derived form is found in any [combination], it should be understood as existing there and not elsewhere.

body.text: niḥśarīraḥ paramāṇuriti niḥsvabhāvo vyavasthānamātramityarthaḥ, apakarṣamaryādābhāvāt / buddhyā paryantabhedatastu paramāṇuvyavasthānaṃ buddhyā yāvānavayapāpakarṣaparyantaḥ śakyate prabhettuṃ tāvatā paramāṇuvyavasthānaṃ kriyate / kiṃ punaḥ kāraṇaṃ yadevaṃ niḥśarīro 'pi paramāṇurvyavasthāpyate / piṇḍasaṃjñāvibhā[va]natāmupādāya, avayavaśo hi buddhyā bhidyamāne rūpe sarvametadekaṃ rūpamiti piṇḍasaṃjñā vigacchati, yataḥ pudgalanairātmyapraveśasyānukūlyaṃ bhavatīti /
body.translated_text: 'The bodiless atom' (<s>paramāṇu</s>): meaning it has no intrinsic nature, it is a mere designation—because there is no limit to reduction. But the establishment of the atom through the limit of intellectual analysis [means]: the atom is established to the extent that the intellect is able to analyze the ultimate limit of the reduction of parts. What then is the reason that even a bodiless atom is established? For the sake of dispelling the perception of a mass (<s>piṇḍasaṃjñā</s>). For when form is analyzed by the intellect part by part, the perception of a mass—[thinking] 'all this is one form'—disappears, from which there comes favorability for entering into the selflessness of the person (<s>pudgalanairātmya</s>).

body.text: rūpadravyāpariniṣpattipraveśatāṃ copādāya, evaṃ hi buddhyā bhidyamānaṃ rūpaṃ na kiṃcidbhavatīti matvā rūpadravyasyāpariniṣpattiṃ praviśati, yato vijñaptimātrāvatāreṇa dharmanairātmyapraveśasyānukūlyaṃ bhavatīti //
body.translated_text: And for the sake of entering into the non-establishment of the substance of form (<s>rūpadravya</s>). For thus, thinking 'form, when analyzed by the intellect, becomes nothing,' one enters into the non-establishment of the substance of form, from which, through entering into 'representation-only' (<s>vijñaptimātra</s>), there comes favorability for entering into the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmanairātmya</s>).

body.text: vipuladuḥkhamasaṃlikhitaṃ kāmāvacaramanupacitakuśalamūlānām, sarvaduḥkhatāgatiyoniprabhāvitatvāt kāmadhātoranupacittakuśalamūlatvenānāvṛtaṃ sarvagatigamanatvācca yathākramaṃ tadvipulamasaṃlikhitaṃ ca veditavyam saṃlikhitaṃ tadevotpannamokṣabhāgīyānām, avaśyaṃ parinirvāṇaniyamāt / saṃlikhitāsaṃlikhitaṃ tadeva kāmāvacaraṃ duḥkhaṃ laukikavairāgyāvaropitakuśalamūlānām, duḥkhaduḥkhatādisamatikramaniyamitatvādanātyantikatvācca yathākramam / evaṃ madhyāsaṃlikhitādīni yathāyogaṃ yojayitavyāni / mahāsaṃlekhapratyupasthānamanekasattvasaṃtānikaduḥkhāpanayanapratyupasthānāt //
body.translated_text: 'Vast and unerased suffering' of the desire realm (<s>kāmāvacara</s>) belongs to those whose roots of merit (<s>kuśalamūla</s>) are uncultivated—because it is brought about by all forms of suffering, destinies, and kinds of birth in the desire realm, because having uncultivated roots of merit it is unobstructed, and because of going to all destinies; thus it should be understood as 'vast' and 'unerased' respectively. 'Erased' is that very [suffering] of those in whom the portion leading to liberation (<s>mokṣabhāgīya</s>) has arisen, because they are certainly determined for <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. 'Erased and unerased' is that very desire-realm suffering of those who have planted roots of merit through worldly detachment (<s>laukikavairāgya</s>), because they are determined to transcend the suffering of suffering (<s>duḥkhaduḥkhatā</s>) etc., but not ultimately—respectively. Likewise, 'moderate, unerased' and so forth should be construed as applicable. 'The presentation of the great erasure': because of the presentation of the removal of suffering from the continuities of many beings.

body.text: kuśalādicittasya maraṇamityātmasnehasaṃprayuktāccyuticittāpavargāvasthāmadhikṛtya veditavyam / manomaya upapādukatvena, cittamātrahetukatvāt / gandharvo gandhenārvaṇāt gandhānusāreṇo papattideśa[ga]manādityarthaḥ / paraṃ saptāhaṃ tiṣṭhatyantareṇa ca cyavate yadyupapattipratyayān labhate / atha na labhate saptāhātpareṇa cyutvā punarantarābhava eva nivartate / evaṃ yāva[t] saptakṛtvaḥ tataḥ pareṇa ekadā ca vyāvartate yadi tadavasthā syādyatropapattipratya[ya] / balavanta āmukhībhūtā bhavanti caturthadhyānalābhino 'rhattvābhimānino bhikṣostadbhūmikāntarābhavābhinirvṛttau mokṣāpavādi kamithyādṛṣṭipratilambhānnārakāntarābhavābhinirvṛttivat / tatrasthaśca karmopacinoti, pūrvāvedhavaśena kuśalādicetanāsamudācārāt / sabhāgāṃśca sattvānpaśyati yaiḥ saha pūrva tatkuśalamakuśalaṃ vā caritaṃ bhavati taiḥ saha vartamānamātmānaṃ svapna iva saṃjānīte / yatra cāsāvupapanno tatpūrvakālabhavākṛtirnirvartate / tata ūrdhvamindriyābhinirvṛttiryathā pratītyasamutpāda iti nāmarūpādyānupūrvyā / yathoktam -
body.translated_text: 'The death of a mind that is wholesome etc.': this should be understood with reference to the state of cessation of the death-consciousness (<s>cyuticitta</s>) that is associated with self-attachment. 'Mind-made' (<s>manomaya</s>): because of being born spontaneously (<s>upapāduka</s>), because it is caused by mind alone. '<s>Gandharva</s>': because of feeding on odor—meaning it goes to the place of birth following odors. It remains for at most seven days, and in the meantime it passes away if it obtains the conditions for birth. But if it does not obtain them, having passed away after seven days, it returns again to the intermediate existence (<s>antarābhava</s>) itself. Thus [this continues] up to seven times; thereafter it turns away at once if the condition obtains where the conditions for birth become strong and come to the fore—as in the case of a monk who has attained the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> and conceives himself to be an <s>Arhat</s>: when the intermediate existence of that level is produced, through the acquisition of the wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>) that denies liberation, a hellish intermediate existence is produced. And while in that [intermediate state], one accumulates <s>karma</s>, through the occurrence of wholesome and other volitions under the power of previous impressions. And one sees beings of similar kind—those with whom one previously practiced that wholesome or unwholesome [conduct]; together with them one perceives oneself as if in a dream. And where one is born, the form of the prior existence continues. From then onward, the development of the sense faculties follows as in <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), according to the sequence beginning with <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form). As stated:

body.text:
kalalaṃ prathamaṃ bhavati kalalājjāyate 'rbudam /
arbudājjāyate peśī peśīto jāyate dhanam //
body.translated_text: First there is the <s>kalala</s> (embryonic fluid); from the <s>kalala</s> arises the <s>arbuda</s> (rounded mass); from the <s>arbuda</s> arises the <s>peśī</s> (fleshy lump); from the <s>peśī</s> arises the <s>ghana</s> (solid mass).

body.text:
ghanātpraśākhā jāyante keśalomanakhādayaḥ /
indriyāṇi ca rūpīṇi vyañjanādyanupūrvaśaḥ //
body.translated_text: From the <s>ghana</s> arise the limbs (<s>praśākhā</s>)—hair, body-hair, nails, and so forth; and the material sense faculties, and the marks and other features, in due sequence.

body.text: samudayasatyaṃ yato duḥkhaṃ samudeti / tatpunaḥ katamat / kleśāḥ kleśādhipateyaṃ ca karma iti sāsravamityarthaḥ / yadyevaṃ kimartha bhagavatā tṛṣṇaiva samudayanirdeśe nirdiṣṭā / sarvatragatvena prādhānyāt / tṛṣṇā vastusarvatragā prāptāprāptasarvātmabhāvaviṣayavastuvyāpanāt / prāpte ātmabhāve tṛṣṇā, aprāpte paunarbhavikī / prāpteṣu viṣayeṣu [nandīrāgasahagatā / aprāpteṣu viṣayeṣu] tatratatrābhinandinī veditavyā / avasthāsarvatragā duḥkhaduḥkhatāditryavastheṣu saṃskāreṣvanuga[ta]tvāt / tatra duḥkhaduḥkhatāvastheṣu prāpteṣu viyogatṛṣṇā, aprāpteṣvasaṃyogatṛṣṇā / vipariṇāmaduḥkhatāvastheṣu aviyogatṛṣṇā saṃyogatṛṣṇā ca, prāptāprāptabhedāt / saṃskāraduḥkhatāvastheṣu saṃmohatṛṣṇā, kleśadauṣṭhulyaprabhāvitatvādaduḥkhāsukhavedanāprabhāvitatvācca / ālayavijñānaṃ viśeṣeṇa saṃskāraduḥkhatāvasthaṃ tatra cātmasaṃmohasukhena tṛṣṇā pravṛttā veditavyā / adhvasarvatragā triṣvapyadhvasvanugatatvāt / atīte tāvadadhvanyapekṣākāreṇānugatā, anāgate abhinandanākāreṇa, pratyutpanne adhyavasānākāreṇa / dhātusarvatrikā traidhātukaspharaṇātkāmarūpārūpyatṛṣṇābhiḥ / eṣaṇāsarvatrikā tayā kāmabhavamithyābrahmacaryaiṣaṇāt / kāmaiṣaṇayā kāmadhātoraparimucyamānastatraiva duḥkhaṃ nirvartayati / tathā bhavaiṣaṇayā rūpārūpyadhātvoḥ dukhaṃ nirvartayati / mithyābrahmacaryaiṣaṇayā saṃsārādaparimucyamānastatra saṃsaratīti / prakārasarvatrikā śāśvatocchedaprakārānugatatvādbhavavibhava tṛṣṇābhyām //
body.translated_text: The truth of origination (<s>samudayasatya</s>) is that from which suffering arises. What then is that? Defilements (<s>kleśa</s>) and <s>karma</s> under the dominance of defilements—meaning 'contaminated' (<s>sāsrava</s>). If so, why did the <s>Bhagavān</s> teach only craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) in the exposition of origination? Because of its predominance through being all-pervasive. Craving is object-pervasive (<s>vastusarvatragā</s>)—because it pervades all objects, whether one's own existence is attained or unattained. For attained existence there is craving; for unattained existence there is craving for further birth (<s>paunarbhavikī</s>). For attained objects, [craving] is accompanied by delight and passion (<s>nandīrāga</s>); for unattained objects, it should be understood as delighting here and there. It is state-pervasive (<s>avasthāsarvatragā</s>)—because it follows conditioned phenomena in the three states of the suffering of suffering (<s>duḥkhaduḥkhatā</s>) etc. In the state of the suffering of suffering, when attained, there is craving for separation; when unattained, craving for non-conjunction. In the state of the suffering of change (<s>vipariṇāmaduḥkhatā</s>), there is craving for non-separation and craving for conjunction, according to the distinction of attained and unattained. In the state of the suffering of conditioned existence (<s>saṃskāraduḥkhatā</s>), there is craving of delusion (<s>saṃmohatṛṣṇā</s>), because it is brought about by the bad disposition of defilements and because it is brought about by neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. The <s>ālaya-vijñāna</s> (store consciousness) is particularly in the state of the suffering of conditioned existence; therein craving should be understood as operating through the pleasure of self-delusion. It is time-pervasive (<s>adhvasarvatragā</s>)—because it follows through all three times: with respect to the past, it follows in the mode of longing; with respect to the future, in the mode of anticipation; with respect to the present, in the mode of adherence. It is realm-pervasive (<s>dhātusarvatrikā</s>)—because it pervades the three realms through cravings for the desire realm, form realm, and formless realm. It is quest-pervasive (<s>eṣaṇāsarvatrikā</s>)—through craving for sense-pleasures, for existence, and for wrong celibacy. Through the quest for sense-pleasures, one who is not freed from the desire realm produces suffering right there. Likewise, through the quest for existence, one produces suffering in the form and formless realms. Through the quest for wrong celibacy, one who is not freed from <s>saṃsāra</s> continues to wander therein. It is mode-pervasive (<s>prakārasarvatrikā</s>)—because it follows the modes of eternalism and annihilationism, through cravings for existence (<s>bhavatṛṣṇā</s>) and for non-existence (<s>vibhavatṛṣṇā</s>).

body.text: dṛṣṭeḥ prañcākāro bhedaḥ - satkāyadṛṣṭirantagrāhadṛṣṭimithyādṛṣṭiḥ dṛṣṭiparāmarśaḥ śīlavrataparāmarśa iti //
body.translated_text: The fivefold division of views (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>): the view of the real self (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), the view of extreme positions (<s>antagrāhadṛṣṭi</s>), wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>), attachment to views (<s>dṛṣṭiparāmarśa</s>), and attachment to rules and rituals (<s>śīlavrataparāmarśa</s>).

body.text: apraśāntalakṣaṇatā kleśānāṃ sāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ veditavyam / sā punaḥ ṣaḍākārā tadyathā vikṣepāpraśāntatā viparyāsāpraśāntatā auddhatyāpraśāntatā styānamiddhāpraśāntatā pramādāpraśāntatālajjāpraśāntatā ca //
body.translated_text: The characteristic of non-pacification (<s>apraśāntalakṣaṇatā</s>) should be understood as the general characteristic of the defilements. That is of six aspects, namely: non-pacification through distraction (<s>vikṣepa</s>), non-pacification through distortion (<s>viparyāsa</s>), non-pacification through restlessness (<s>auddhatya</s>), non-pacification through torpor and drowsiness (<s>styānamiddha</s>), non-pacification through heedlessness (<s>pramāda</s>), and non-pacification through shamelessness (<s>alajjā</s>).

body.text: kleśānuśayaścāprahīṇo bhavatīti tatpakṣasya dauṣṭhulyasyāsamudghāti tatvāt / kleśasthānīyaśca dharma ābhāsagato bhavati raṃjanīyādiḥ / tatra cāyo niśomanaskāraḥ pratyavasthito bhavatīti tasminviṣaye śubhanimittādyudgrāhako rāgādyutpattyanukūlaḥ //
body.translated_text: And the latent defilement (<s>kleśānuśaya</s>) remains unabandoned because the bad disposition (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>) on its side has not been uprooted. And the <s>dharma</s> that takes the place of the defilement appears in the guise [of something desirable], such as the attractive and so forth. And unwise attention (<s>ayoniśo manaskāra</s>) is established there—that is, it grasps the sign of beauty (<s>śubhanimitta</s>) etc. in that object and is favorable to the arising of desire (<s>rāga</s>) and so forth.

body.text: avidyā dṛṣṭivicikitsā ūrdhvabhūmyālaṃbanā api santi na punarāsāṃ sā bhūmiḥ sākṣādālaṃbanaṃ veditavyaṃ yathā svabhūmiḥ, tatparikalpamukhapravṛttatvāt tu tadālaṃbanavyavasthānaṃ veditavyam / tatrāvidyā ūrdhvabhūmyālaṃbanā yā dṛṣṭisaṃprayuktā / dṛṣṭiḥ satkāyadṛṣṭi sthāpayitvā, na hi parabhūmikān saṃskārānahamityabhiniviśamāno dṛṣṭa iti / ūrdhvabhūmikasya tu kleśasyādhobhūmirālaṃbanaṃ na bhavati, tato vītarāgatvāt / nirodhamārgālaṃbanasya tau nālaṃbanam, lokottareṇa jñānena tatpṛṣṭhalabdhena vā pratyātmavedanīyatvāt / tat parikalpitaṃ tvasyālaṃbanamiti vaktavye tatparikalpastvasyālaṃbanamiti vacanam, tadavyatirekātparikalpitasya //
body.translated_text: Ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), views (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>), and doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>) also have objects belonging to higher levels, but those levels should not be understood as their direct object-support in the way their own level is, because they operate through the door of conceptual construction regarding those [levels]—thus the establishment of them as having those objects should be understood. Among these, the ignorance that has objects of higher levels is that which is associated with views. Views [with higher-level objects] exclude the view of the real self (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), for one does not cling to conditioned phenomena of other levels [thinking] 'this is I.' But a defilement of a higher level does not have a lower level as its object, because one is free from attachment to that [lower level]. For one whose object is cessation (<s>nirodha</s>) and the path (<s>mārga</s>), those [cessation and path] are not its object-support, because they are to be personally experienced through supramundane knowledge or its subsequently-obtained [wisdom]. Rather, it should be said that its conceptual construction of those is its object—the statement says 'its conceptual construction is its object' because the conceptually constructed is not different from [the act of] conceptual construction.

body.text: rāgaḥ pratidhena na saṃ[pra]yujyate, ekāntaviruddhayorekatra vṛttyayogāt / vicikitsayāpi na saṃ[pra]yujyate, na hi vicikitsāvyavasthitabuddhiradhyavasyatīti / śiṣṭaistvasya mānādibhiraviruddhatvātsaṃprayogo veditavyaḥ / pratigho mānena dṛṣṭyā ca na saṃprayujyate, na hi yo yatra vastuni pratihatastena sa unnatiṃ gacchati tadvā saṃtīrayituṃ śaknotīti, evamanyadapi yojayitavyam // krodhādaya anyonyaṃ na saṃprayujyanta iti viruddhā viruddhairna saṃ[pra]yujyante / tadyathā rāgāṃśikāḥ pratighāṃsikaiḥ / aviruddhāstu kleśavadeva saṃprayujyanta iti
body.translated_text: Desire (<s>rāga</s>) is not associated with aversion (<s>pratigha</s>), because two absolutely opposed [mental factors] cannot function together in one [mind-moment]. Nor is it associated with doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>), for one whose understanding is established in doubt does not make firm determination. But its association with the remaining [defilements] such as pride (<s>māna</s>) etc. should be understood, because they are not contradictory. Aversion is not associated with pride or views (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>), for one who is repelled by a certain thing does not become elated regarding it, nor is one able to consider it with regard [to a view]—and so forth should be applied similarly. // Anger (<s>krodha</s>) and the other [secondary defilements] are not mutually associated—[that is,] contradictory ones are not associated with contradictory ones. For example, those belonging to the desire-group are not [associated] with those belonging to the aversion-group. But non-contradictory ones should be understood as associated, just like the [primary] defilements themselves.

body.text: veditavyam / āhrīkyānapatrāpyaṃ sarvatrākuśale saṃprayujyate, svaparanirapekṣatāmantareṇākuśalasatsamudācārā saṃbhavāt / evaṃ styānādayaḥ sarvatra kliṣṭe yojayitavyāḥ, akarmaṇyādikamantareṇa kliṣṭatvā saṃbhavāditi //
body.translated_text: This should be understood. Shamelessness (<s>āhrīkya</s>) and lack of moral dread (<s>anapatrāpya</s>) are associated with all unwholesome [states], because without disregard for self and others, the occurrence of unwholesome [states] would be impossible. Likewise, torpor (<s>styāna</s>) and the other [universal defilements] should be applied as present in all defiled [states], because without non-workability (<s>akarmaṇya</s>) and the like, the occurrence of defilement would be impossible.

body.text: yadyena prakāreṇa yasmin vastuni saṃprayojayati tannirdeśena saṃyojananirdeśo veditavyaḥ / kiṃ saṃyojayati / anunayasaṃyojanaṃ tāvattraidhātukarāgasvabhāvaṃ saṃyojayati / kena prakāreṇa saṃyojayati / tadvataḥ traidhātukānudvege satyakuśalasamudācarataḥ kuśalāsamudācarataśca / kasmin saṃyojayati / āyatyāṃ duḥkhābhinirvṛttau / evaṃ pratighasaṃyojanādiṣu yojayitavyaḥ / avidyāsaṃyojanena saṃprayukto duḥkhadharmān samudayadharmānnādhyavasyati, phalahetubhūtānsāsravānsaṃskārāstadādīnavāparijñānāt / dṛṣṭisaṃyojanena saṃprayukto mithyāni saraṇaṃ paryeṣata ityaha mokṣo mama mokṣo muktaśca nityo bhaviṣyāsyucchetsyāmi veti, na ca bauddhānāmasti mokṣa iti / parāmarśasaṃyojanena saṃ[pra]yukto mithyāniḥsaraṇopāyaṃ kalpayatyabhiniviśate, āryāṣṭāṅgaṃ mārgaṃ hitvā satkāyadṛṣṭayā tatpūrvakeṇa ca śīlavratena śuddhipratyayanāt //
body.translated_text: The teaching of fetters (<s>saṃyojana</s>) should be understood through the indication of what, in what manner, and in what thing [a fetter] binds. What does the fetter of attraction (<s>anunayasaṃyojana</s>) bind? Being of the nature of desire for the three realms, it binds. In what manner does it bind? By the absence of disenchantment toward the three realms in one who has it, and by the non-occurrence of wholesome [states] together with the occurrence of unwholesome [states]. In what does it bind? In the future production of suffering. The same should be applied to the fetter of aversion (<s>pratighasaṃyojana</s>) and so forth. One associated with the fetter of ignorance (<s>avidyāsaṃyojana</s>) does not comprehend the <s>dharmas</s> of suffering and the <s>dharmas</s> of origination—the contaminated conditioned phenomena that are cause and fruit—because of not fully understanding their dangers. One associated with the fetter of views (<s>dṛṣṭisaṃyojana</s>) seeks wrong refuge—saying 'this is my liberation, my liberation, and once liberated I shall be eternal' or 'I shall be annihilated,' and 'the Buddhists have no liberation.' One associated with the fetter of clinging (<s>parāmarśasaṃyojana</s>) imagines and clings to wrong means of escape—abandoning the noble eightfold path and [instead] placing confidence in purification through the view of the real self (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) and the rules and rituals based upon it.

body.text: rāgādibandhanaivipariṇāmaduḥkhatādibandhanavacanaṃ sukhādivedanānuśayitatvāt / bāhyena hi bandhanena baddho dvayaṃ na labhate - gantuṃ ca na labhate, āsīno 'pi yatheṣṭamabhipretaceṣṭāyāṃ kāmakāraṃ na labhate / tatsādharmyeṇādhyātmikaṃ rāgādibandhanaṃ veditavyam //
body.translated_text: The statement of the bond of desire (<s>rāga</s>) etc. as 'the bond of the suffering of change (<s>vipariṇāmaduḥkhatā</s>) etc.' is because it is accompanied by the latent tendency toward pleasant and other feelings. For one bound by an external bond does not obtain two things: one cannot go freely, and even while seated, one does not obtain freedom of desired movement and activity. By analogy with that, the internal bond of desire etc. should be understood.

body.text: kāmaiṣaṇāyā aviratasya kāmarāgapratighānuśayāvanuśayā te, tanmukhena tayoḥ puṣṭigamanāt / mithyā mokṣaṃ mokṣopāyaṃ ca santīrayantīti yathākramaṃ tisṛbhirdṛṣṭibhirdvābhyāṃ ca parāmarśābhyāṃ yathā saṃyojaneṣūktamiti //
body.translated_text: For one who has not ceased from the quest for sense-pleasures (<s>kāmaiṣaṇā</s>), the latent tendencies (<s>anuśaya</s>) of desire-attachment (<s>kāmarāga</s>) and aversion (<s>pratigha</s>) are the latent tendencies, because through that door those two gain nourishment. [Non-Buddhists] consider a wrong liberation and wrong means to liberation—respectively through three views (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>) and two attachments (<s>parāmarśa</s>), as stated in [the section on] fetters.

body.text: ṣaḍ rāgādīn kleśān sthāpayitvā tadanyaḥ kliṣṭaścaitasikaḥ saṃskāraskandhaḥ krodhādiko veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Setting aside the six defilements beginning with desire (<s>rāga</s>) etc., the other defiled mental factor (<s>caitasika</s>) of the formations aggregate (<s>saṃskāraskandha</s>) should be understood as beginning with anger (<s>krodha</s>) and so forth.

body.text: kuśalapakṣāntarāyāya yogināṃ punaḥpunarudvegena cittaṃ paryavanahyantīti paryavasthānāni / kuśalapakṣaḥ punaryathākālaṃ śamathapragrahopekṣānimittabhāvanā tatsaṃniśrayaśca brahmacaryādiśuddhisaṃgṛhītaṃ śīlam / tatra śamathakāle styānamiddhamantarāyaṃ karoti, ādhyātmaṃ saṃkṣepāvāhanāt / pragrahakāle auddhatyakaukṛtyam, bahirdhā vikṣepāvāhanāt / upekṣākāle īrṣyāmātsaryam, tadvataḥ parātmasaṃpattyamarśagrahamukhena muhurmuhuścittakaṃpanāt / śīlaviśuddhikāle āhvīkyānapatrāpyam, tadubhayavataḥ sarvathāpattisthāneṣvalajjanāditi //
body.translated_text: They are called 'engulfments' (<s>paryavasthāna</s>) because they repeatedly engulf the minds of practitioners (<s>yogin</s>) with agitation, obstructing the wholesome side. The wholesome side means: the cultivation of calm-abiding (<s>śamatha</s>), exertion (<s>pragraha</s>), equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>), and signs (<s>nimitta</s>) at the appropriate times, and morality (<s>śīla</s>) included in the purity of celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>) etc. that depends on these. Among these, at the time of calm-abiding, torpor and drowsiness (<s>styānamiddha</s>) creates an obstacle, by bringing about internal contraction. At the time of exertion, restlessness and regret (<s>auddhatyakaukṛtya</s>) [creates an obstacle], by bringing about external distraction. At the time of equanimity, jealousy and miserliness (<s>īrṣyāmātsarya</s>) [create an obstacle], because in one who has these, the mind trembles again and again through grasping at the consideration of the success of others and oneself. At the time of purification of morality, shamelessness (<s>āhrīkya</s>) and lack of moral dread (<s>anapatrāpya</s>) [create an obstacle], because one who has both of these feels no embarrassment whatsoever at occasions of transgression.

body.text: saṃkleśavyavadānaguṇavaiguṇyārthena yathākramamoghayogavyavasthānaṃ veditavyam / āśritāśrayasaṃbandhayogeneti dṛṣṭayaugha āśritaḥ, avidyaugha āśrayaḥ, saṃmohe sati mokṣatadupāyaviparītaṃ saṃtīraṇāt //
body.translated_text: The establishment of floods (<s>ogha</s>) and yokes (<s>yoga</s>) should be understood in terms of the qualities and deficiencies of defilement (<s>saṃkleśa</s>) and purification (<s>vyavadāna</s>), respectively. 'Through the connection of the supported and the support': the flood of views (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>) is the supported, and the flood of ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) is the support, because in the presence of delusion one considers liberation and its means in a distorted manner.

body.text: dṛṣṭiśīlavratopādānābhyāṃ tīrthyā anyonyaṃ vivadanti, tatrānekamatyāt / ātmavādopādāne[na] tvanyonyaṃ na vivadanti, ātmano 'stitvaṃ prati sarveṣāṃ matasāmyāt / ātmavādopādānena tīrthyāihadhārmikaiḥ sārddhaṃ vivadanti, eṣāṃ nairātmyavāditvāt //
body.translated_text: Through the grasping (<s>upādāna</s>) of views and of rules and rituals, non-Buddhist teachers (<s>tīrthya</s>) quarrel with one another, because of their many different opinions regarding those. But through the grasping of the self-doctrine (<s>ātmavāda</s>), they do not quarrel with one another, because all of them share the same opinion regarding the existence of a self. Through the grasping of the self-doctrine, however, the non-Buddhist teachers quarrel with the followers of this [Buddhist] teaching, because these [Buddhists] hold the doctrine of selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>).

body.text: abhidhyādayaḥ kāyagranthā iti na rūpakāyasyaite granthā veditavyāḥ kiṃtarhi samāhitacittasvabhāvasya kāyasya parigranthārthena granthāḥ / pṛthagdṛṣṭisaṃniśrayeṇedameva satyaṃ moghamanyadityabhiniviśya jñeyaṃ saṃtīrayatāmayoniśo jñeyasaṃtīraṇahetoḥ cittaṃ vikṣipyate / kuto vikṣipyate / samāhitacittasya yathābhūtajñānadarśanataḥ //
body.translated_text: Covetousness (<s>abhidhyā</s>) and the other 'bodily knots' (<s>kāyagrantha</s>) should not be understood as knots of the physical body (<s>rūpakāya</s>), but rather as knots in the sense of binding the body whose nature is the concentrated mind (<s>samāhitacitta</s>). By relying on various views and clinging to 'only this is true, everything else is false,' when one considers the knowable (<s>jñeya</s>) through unwise consideration of the knowable, the mind is distracted. From what is it distracted? From the knowledge-and-vision of things as they really are (<s>yathābhūtajñānadarśana</s>) belonging to one whose mind is concentrated.

body.text: kuśalapakṣasyāsaṃprakhyānāya cittaṃ nivṛṇvantīti nivaraṇāni kuśalapravṛtterantarāyaṃ kurvantītyarthaḥ / kāmacchandaṃ pravrajyābhiraterantarāyaṃ karoti, viṣayopabhogābhilāṣamukhena tatra tatrābhiramaṇāt / vyāpādaścodanāyāṃ samyakpratipatteḥ, sabrahmacāribhiḥ śikṣāsthāneṣu codyamānasya
body.translated_text: They are called 'hindrances' (<s>nīvaraṇa</s>) because they cover the mind so that the wholesome side does not become manifest—meaning they create obstacles to the occurrence of wholesome [states]. Sensual desire (<s>kāmacchanda</s>) creates an obstacle for one who delights in renunciation (<s>pravrajyā</s>), by causing delight here and there through the longing for enjoyment of sense-objects. Ill-will (<s>vyāpāda</s>) [hinders] correct practice when one is being urged by fellow practitioners regarding the bases of training,

body.text: vyāpannacittatayāsamyakśaikṣaṇāt / styānamiddhamoddhatyakaukṛtyaṃ ca śamathapragrahayoḥ, pūrvavatsaṃkṣepavikṣepāvāhanādibhiḥ / vicikitsā upekṣāyām, niścaya mantareṇābhyupekṣitumaśakyatvāt //
body.translated_text: because of incorrect training due to having a corrupted mind. Torpor-and-drowsiness (<s>styānamiddha</s>) and restlessness-and-regret (<s>auddhatyakaukṛtya</s>) [hinder] calm-abiding (<s>śamatha</s>) and exertion (<s>pragraha</s>) respectively, by bringing about contraction and distraction as before. Doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>) [hinders] equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>), because without certainty, equanimity is impossible.

body.text: pratipakṣalāṃgarlaidurbhedārthena khilavyavasthānaṃ veditavyam, janmāntarābhyāsena khilībhūtatvāt //
body.translated_text: The establishment of <s>khila</s> (rigidity) should be understood in the sense of being difficult to break by the antidote, because through habitual practice in previous lives it has become rigid.

body.text: dauḥśīlyāśucisaṃbhāvanānimittatvānmalāḥ //
body.translated_text: They are called <s>malas</s> (stains) because they are the cause of conceiving immoral conduct and impurity.

body.text: punaḥ punaḥ saṃsāre jātijarāmaraṇayogena nidhnantīti nighāḥ //
body.translated_text: They are called <s>nighas</s> (destroyers) because they destroy again and again in <s>saṃsāra</s> through the connection with birth, aging, and death.

body.text: bhavabhogeṣu ratneṣu ca tṛṣṇāvicikatsāmukhenānupraviśya todanācchalyāḥ //
body.translated_text: They are called <s>śalyas</s> (thorns) because they penetrate through craving and doubt with respect to existence, enjoyments, and treasures, causing pain.

body.text: bahūpakaraṇaparigraheṇa sakiṃcanaṃ kṛtvā bhayādibhiryojanāt kiṃcanāḥ //
body.translated_text: They are called <s>kiñcanas</s> (encumbrances) because, having made one burdened through the possession of many requisites, they connect one with fear and the like.

body.text: prāṇātipātādyakuśalacaryāvāhanādduścaritāni / lobhadveṣamohānāmevākuśalamūlatvena vyavasthānam, ebhirmukhaiḥ sattvānāṃ duścaritacaraṇāt / tatrāmiṣakiṃcitkahetoḥ bhogārthino lobhena duścaritaṃ caranti / apakāranimittaparikalpahetoḥ parāparādhāmarṣiṇo dveṣeṇa, mithyādharmābhiniveśahetoḥ viparītadarśino mohena duścaritaṃ caranti yājñikādaya iti //
body.translated_text: They are called <s>duścaritas</s> (misconduct) because they bring about unwholesome conduct such as killing and the rest. The establishment of <s>lobha</s> (greed), <s>dveṣa</s> (hatred), and <s>moha</s> (delusion) as the unwholesome roots is because through these channels beings engage in misconduct. Among these, those who desire enjoyments engage in misconduct through greed for the sake of some material gain. Those who are intolerant of offenses by others engage in misconduct through hatred because of imagining a cause for harm. Those with distorted views engage in misconduct through delusion because of attachment to wrong doctrines — such as ritualists and the like.

body.text: cittavisāraṃ srutaṃ kurvantītyāsravāḥ //
body.translated_text: They are called <s>āsravas</s> (outflows) because they cause the mind to flow out and leak.

body.text: kāyikacaitasikavighātakaratvādvighātāḥ //
body.translated_text: They are called <s>vighātas</s> (afflictions) because they cause destruction to both body and mind.

body.text: ayoniśonimittamanuvyañjanaṃ ca grāhayitvā kāyaṃ cittaṃ ca paridahantīti paridāhāḥ //
body.translated_text: They are called <s>paridāhas</s> (burnings) because, having caused one to grasp the signs and secondary features of objects unmethodically, they burn the body and mind.

body.text: rūpādike vastuni ratyadhyavasānaṃ kārayitvā tadvipariṇāme śokādibhiḥ sattvānāyāsantītyu pāyāsāḥ //
body.translated_text: They are called <s>upāyāsas</s> (tribulations) because, having caused attachment and conviction regarding objects such as form and the rest, when those objects change, they torment beings with grief and the like.

body.text: raṇayanti śastrādānādibhiriti raṇāḥ //
body.translated_text: They are called <s>raṇas</s> (conflicts) because they cause fighting through the taking up of weapons and the like.

body.text: adharmarāgādimahāparidāhakaratvāt jvarā iva jvarā veditavyāḥ // tatrādharmarāgaḥ yo 'kuśaleṣu karmapatheṇānurāgaḥ / viṣamalobho 'nyāyenādharmeṇa viṣayaparyaṣṭiḥ / mithyādharmo durākhyāto dharmavinayo veditavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: They should be understood as <s>jvaras</s> (fevers), like fevers, because they cause the great burning of unlawful passion and the rest. Among these, <s>adharmarāga</s> (unlawful passion) is the attachment to unwholesome courses of action. <s>Viṣamalobha</s> (crooked greed) is the obsession with objects through injustice and unrighteousness. <s>Mithyādharma</s> (false doctrine) should be understood as a badly proclaimed <s>dharma</s> and <s>vinaya</s> (discipline).

body.text: jātimūlaka saṃskārataruvanaṃ saṃjānayantīti vanasāḥ //
body.translated_text: They are called <s>vanasas</s> (thickets) because they produce the forest of the tree of conditioned existence rooted in birth.

body.text: kāyasāpekṣāditayā kuśalaprayogavibandhanādvibandhāḥ / kāyasāpekṣatādīni punaḥ pañca cetovinibandhānadhikṛtya //
body.translated_text: They are called <s>vibandhas</s> (hindrances) because they obstruct wholesome practice through dependence on the body and the rest. The dependence on the body and the rest, furthermore, is with reference to the five mental hindrances.

body.text: rāgo viṣaye dṛṣṭau ca vipratipanna iti bhāvanāprahātavyo darśanaprahātavyaśca yathākramam / śubhatāmātrālaṃbanatvādrāgasya yo 'pi sattveṣu rāgaḥ so 'pi viṣayamukhenaiva vipratipanno veditavyaḥ / evaṃ pratikūlamātrālaṃbanatvāt pratighasya sattveṣvapi pravartamāno viṣayamukhenaiva vipratipanno veditavyaḥ // mānaḥ sattveṣu dṛṣṭau ca [vi]pratipannaḥ hīnādasmi śreyānityevamādyākārapravṛttatvātsatveṣu vipratipanno veditavyaḥ / satkāyāntagrāhamithyādṛṣṭayo jñeye vipratipannāḥ samāropāpavādamukhena yathāyogam / śīlavrataparāmarśādiḥ dṛṣṭau vipratipannaḥ dṛṣṭidoṣeṇaiva śīlavratasya śuddhitaḥ parāmarśanāt / vicikitsā pratipakṣe vipratipannā satyeṣu buddhirdvaghāpādanāt / te duḥkhasamudayayordaśāpi kleśā nidānaṃ bhavanti / tau ca teṣāṃ padasthānam / ataste tannidānapadasthānato vipratipannā ityucyante / nirodhe mārge cottrāsasaṃjananato vipratipannāḥ kleśavaśātsaṃsāre 'bhiratasya vyavadānataḥ prapātasaṃjñātrāsāt / viparītakalpanataśca nirodhe mārge ca vipratipannā draṣṭavyāḥ, tīrthyairanyathā parikalpya tatra [vi]pratipatteḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Rāga</s> (passion) is misdirected regarding objects and regarding views, and thus is to be abandoned through cultivation and through seeing, respectively. Because passion takes only what is attractive as its object-support, even passion toward beings should be understood as misdirected through the channel of objects. Likewise,

body.text: kāmāvacaro rāgaḥ pañcavijñānakāyikaḥ sukhena saṃprayujyate / manovijñānakāyikaḥ saumanasyena / sarva upekṣayāprabandhoparatikāle / duḥkhadaurmanasyābhyāṃ tu na saṃprayujyate, harṣākārapravṛttatvāt //
body.translated_text: <s>Rāga</s> of the <s>kāmadhātu</s> (desire realm), when belonging to the five sense-consciousness groups, is associated with pleasure. When belonging to the mental consciousness group, it is associated with mental happiness. All are associated with equanimity at the time of the cessation of their continuity. But it is not associated with pain or mental unhappiness, because it operates in the manner of delight.

body.text: pratigho duḥkhena saṃprayujyate pañcavijñānakāyikaḥ, ṣaṣṭho daurmanasyena, sarva upekṣayā pūrvavat sukhasaumanasyābhyāṃ na saṃprayujyate, dainyākārapravṛttatvāt //
body.translated_text: <s>Pratigha</s> (aversion), when belonging to the five sense-consciousness groups, is associated with pain; the sixth, with mental unhappiness; all are associated with equanimity as before. It is not associated with pleasure or mental happiness, because it operates in the manner of dejection.

body.text: mānaḥ kāmadhatau sukhena na saṃprayujyate, pañcavijñānakāyikābhāvāt / prathamadvitīyayostarhi dhyānayoḥ kathaṃ sukhena saṃprayujyate / manobhūmikena sukhena /
body.translated_text: <s>Māna</s> (pride) in the <s>kāmadhātu</s> (desire realm) is not associated with pleasure, because it does not belong to the five sense-consciousness groups. Then how is it associated with pleasure in the first and second <s>dhyānas</s>? Through the pleasure that belongs to the mental level.

body.text: kathaṃ tatra manobhūmikaṃ sukham / yattaducyate prītisukhamiti, yathoktam - "prītiḥ katamā / yā parivṛttāśrayasya parivṛttivijñānāśritā cittatuṣṭiḥ cittaudvilyaṃ cittaharṣaḥ cittakalpatā sātaṃ veditaṃ vedanāgatam / sukhaṃ katamat / yatparivṛttāśrayasyālayavijñānāśrita āśrayānugrahata āśrayahlādaḥ sātaṃ veditaṃ vedanāgatamiti /" tadetaduktaṃ bhavati / sukhā vedanā prathamadvitīyayordhyānayorutpadyamānā yena cittacaitakalāpena saṃprayujyate taṃ ca harṣākāreṇa prīṇayati, āśrayaṃ cālayavijñānasvabhāvaṃ prasrabdhisukhena hlādayati / atastadubhayakṛtyakaratvādubhayathaivāsyā vyavasthānaṃ veditavyaṃ prītiḥ sukhaṃ ceti / tasmāttayā saṃprayujyamāno mānaḥ sukhena saumanasyena ca saṃprayujyata ityucyate /
body.translated_text: How is there pleasure belonging to the mental level there? That which is called '<s>prītisukha</s>' (joy-and-bliss) — as it is said: 'What is <s>prīti</s> (joy)? That mental satisfaction, mental elation, mental delight, mental readiness, and pleasant feeling that depends on the consciousness belonging to the transformed basis —'

body.text: mithyādṛṣṭiḥ kāmadhātau daurmanasyena saumanasyena ca saṃprayujyate, sukṛtaduṣkṛtakāriṇāṃ tadvaiphalyadarśanenādhṛtiharṣotpādāt / sukhaduḥkhābhyāṃ na saṃprayujyate, manobhūmikatvāt sarvasyā dṛṣṭeḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Mithyādṛṣṭi</s> (wrong view) in the <s>kāmadhātu</s> is associated with both mental unhappiness and mental happiness, because in those who do good and those who do evil, seeing the fruitlessness of their deeds produces both discouragement and elation. It is not associated with pleasure or pain, because all views belong to the mental level.

body.text: vicikitsā kāmadhātau saumanasyena na saṃprayujyate, aniścitacittasya nairvṛttyamantareṇa saumanasyābhāvāt / rūpadhātau vicikitsottaradhyāyināmapi prītisukhaṃ samādhivalādhānenānuvartata eveti tatra sukhasaumanasyābhyāmapi saṃprayujyate //
body.translated_text: <s>Vicikitsā</s> (doubt) in the <s>kāmadhātu</s> is not associated with mental happiness, because for one whose mind is uncertain, there is no mental happiness without certainty. In the <s>rūpadhātu</s> (form realm), even for those who meditate with subsequent doubt, the joy-and-bliss continues through the force of <s>samādhi</s>, and therefore there —

body.text: āveṇikāyā apyavidyāyā eṣa eva nayo draṣṭavyaḥ sukhasaumanasyābhyāṃ saṃprayogāsaṃprayogamārabhya //
body.translated_text: This same principle should be applied to <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) that is distinctive, beginning with its association and non-association with pleasure and mental happiness.

body.text: sarvakleśā upekṣayā saṃprayujyante audāsīnyamāgamyāstagamanatāmupādāyeti kleśapravandhasya mandataratamatāgamanenoparatavegasyoparamaṇādante 'vaśyamaudāsīnyamukhenopekṣāyāḥ saṃprayogo veditavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: All defilements are associated with equanimity — in the sense that they reach indifference, adopting the character of subsidence — because when the momentum of the stream of defilements gradually weakens and ceases, at the end the association with equanimity through the channel of indifference should be understood.

body.text: rūpadhātau caturvijñānakāyikastatra ghrāṇajihvāvijñānābhāvāt / mānādayo manovijñānakāyikā eva, paritulanatāmukhapravṛttitvāt / mānasyaikadeśapravṛttitvaṃ kenacidevāṃśenonnatigamanāt //
body.translated_text: In the <s>rūpadhātu</s> (form realm), there are four consciousness-groups because smell-consciousness and taste-consciousness are absent there. <s>Māna</s> (pride) and the rest belong exclusively to the mental consciousness group, because they operate through the channel of comparison. The partial operation of pride is because one approaches elevation through only some aspect.

body.text: kāmadhatau daśa dukhadarśanaprahātavyā iti ye tatra tannidānapadasthānato vipratipannāḥ / evaṃ samudayādiṣu yathāyogaṃ vipratipannāstaddarśanaprahātavyā iti veditavyāḥ / kiṃ khalu ye yadālaṃbanāste tatra
body.translated_text: In the <s>kāmadhātu</s>, ten are to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering — those that are misdirected regarding the basis and ground of that. Likewise, those that are misdirected regarding the origin and the rest, as appropriate, should be understood as to be abandoned by seeing those. Are those that have such-and-such objects to be abandoned by seeing those same objects?

body.text: vipratipannā iti veditavyāḥ / nāvaśyam, anāsravālaṃbanānāṃ sāsrave vastunyanuśayāditi / rūpadhātau pratidhābhāvānnava eva duḥkhādidarśanaprahātavyā veditavyāḥ / evamārūpyadhātau / sahajā satkāyadṛṣṭiḥ kā bhāvanāprahātavyā / yāmadhiṣṭhāyotpannadarśanamārgasyāpyāryaśrāvakasyāsmimānaḥ samudācarati / yathoktam - "nāhamāyuṣmandāsakemān pañcopādānaskandhānātmata [ā]tmīyato vā samanupaśyāmyapi tvasti me eṣu pañcasūpādānaskandheṣvasmīti māno 'smīti chando 'smītyanuśayo 'prahīṇo 'parijñāto 'nirodhito 'vāntīkṛta iti /" yathā kliṣṭasya dhātrīcailasyoṣādibhiḥ sudhautasya nirmalasyāpi satastadadhivāsanākṛtaṃ gandhamātramanuvartate yattatsugandhadravyaparibhāvanayā bhūyo 'pyapanetavyaṃ bhavatyevameva darśanamārgeṇa prahīṇaparikalpitasatkāyadṛṣṭimalasyāpyāryaśrāvakasya pūrvābhiniveśābhyāsakṛtamaparicchinnavastukamātmadarśanamanuvartate yattatpunarmārgabhāvanayā prahātavyaṃ bhavatīti / antagrāhadṛṣṭiḥ sahajocchedadṛṣṭisaṃgṛhītā veditavyā, yayā nirvāṇāt pratyudāvartate mānasaṃ paritrasanamupādāyātha kastarhi me ātmeti / rāgādayo bhāvanāprahātavyā dṛṣṭipakṣān muktvā //
body.translated_text: They should be understood as misdirected. Not necessarily, because those having uncontaminated objects can be latent tendencies with respect to contaminated things. In the <s>rūpadhātu</s>, because of the absence of <s>pratigha</s> (aversion), only nine are to be abandoned by seeing suffering and the rest. Likewise in the <s>ārūpyadhātu</s> (formless realm). The innate <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> (view of the self-existing body) —

body.text: tannidānavastuparijñānaṃ kleśānuśayaścāprahīṇo bhavatyevamādi pūrvavat / svabhāvaparijñānaṃ kleśa eṣa utpannaḥ cittasaṃkleśātmaka iti / ādīnavaparijñānamātmāvyāvādhāya saṃvartate paravyābādhāyobhayavyā[bā]dhāya, dṛṣṭadhāmikamavadyaṃ prasavati sāṃparāyikaṃ dṛṣṭadharmasāṃparāyikamavadyaṃ prasavati tajjaṃ caitasikaṃ duḥkhadaurmanasyaṃ pratisaṃvedayata ityevaṃ tribhiḥ prakāraiḥ parijñāyotpannaḥ kleśo 'nadhivāsanayogena parivarjyate / anutpannasya tvanutpādāya mārgo bhāvyate //
body.translated_text: The full understanding of the basis and ground of that, and the latent tendency of the defilement being not yet abandoned — and so forth as before. Full understanding of the intrinsic nature is: 'this is a defilement that has arisen, having the nature of mental defilement.' Full understanding of the danger is: 'it tends toward harm to oneself, harm to others, and harm to both' —

body.text: asaṃbhinnālaṃbanena manaskāreṇeti miśrālaṃbanena sarvadharmasāmānya lakṣaṇākāreṇetyarthaḥ / yadi sarvadharmā anātmana iti nairātmyajñānenaiva kleśaprahāṇaṃ bhavatyanityādyākārāḥ kimarthamupadiśyante / na te kleśaprahāṇārthaṃ kiṃtarhyanātmākāraparikarmārtham / anityākāraṃ hi niḥsṛtyānātmākāraḥ / yathoktam - "yadanityaṃ taddukhaṃ yaddukhaṃ tadanātmeti" / ata evānātmākārasyānuttaryavyavasthānam / ānuttaryāṇyārabhya trīṇyānuttaryāṇi - jñānānuttaryaṃ
body.translated_text: 'With a mental engagement whose object is undivided' means with a mixed object-support, with the mode of the general characteristic of all <s>dharmas</s> — this is the meaning. If 'all <s>dharmas</s> are without self,' then if the abandonment of defilements occurs through the knowledge of selflessness alone, for what purpose are the modes of impermanence and the rest taught?

body.text: pratipadānuttaryaṃ vimuktyānuttaryaṃ ca / tatra jñānānuttaryaṃ nairātmyajñānam, tataḥ pareṇa jñānāntarāparyeṣaṇā[t] / pratipadānuttarya sukhā kṣiprābhijñā, tasyāḥ sarvapratipadagratvāt / vimuktyānuttarya maśaikṣākopyā ca vimuktiḥ, sarvavimuktiprativiśiṣṭatvāt / etāni ca trīṇyānuttaryāṇi yathākramaṃ darśanabhāvanāniṣṭhāmārgānadhikṛtya veditavyāni //
body.translated_text: The unsurpassed in path and the unsurpassed in liberation. Among these, the unsurpassed in knowledge is the knowledge of selflessness, because beyond that there is no seeking for another knowledge. The unsurpassed in path is the pleasant and swift path with direct knowledge, because it is the foremost of all paths. The unsurpassed in liberation —

body.text: upalabdhikarma cakṣurādīnāṃ rūpadarśanādi / kāritrakarma pṛthivyādīnāṃ dhāraṇādi yadvā yasya svalakṣaṇakṛtyam / tadyathā rūpaṇā rūpasyetyevamādi / vyavasāyakarmābhisaṃdhipūrvakaṃ kāyādikarma / pariṇatikarma suvarṇakārādīnāmalaṃkārādi / prāptikarmāryamārgādīnāṃ nirvāṇādhigamādi // asmiṃstvarthe yadbhūyasyā vyavasā karmābhipretamiti prāptikāritrakarmaṇorapi saṃbhavāt //
body.translated_text: The function of apprehension is that of the eye and the rest — seeing form and so forth. The function of activity is that of earth and the rest — supporting and so forth; or alternatively, the function that is specific to each thing's own characteristic. For example, the modification of form, and so forth. The function of determination is the bodily and other actions preceded by intention. The function of transformation —

body.text: kāyādikarma karmapathā iti sūtrānusāreṇa yathāpradhānaṃ nirdeśo veditavyaḥ, tatprayogādīnāpi kāyādikarmāntarbhāvāt / trayaścatvārastrayaśca karmapathā yathākramaṃ kāyavāṅmanaḥkarmalakṣaṇā veditavyāḥ // prāṇātipātādīnāṃ vastu sattvasaṃkhyātamasattvasaṃkhyātaṃ vā yathāyogaṃ yadadhiṣṭhāya prāṇātipātādayaḥ pravartante / āśayastatra vastuni tatsaṃjñāśayastatkarmapathakriyecchāśayaśca / prayogastatkriyāyai svayaṃ parairvā kāyavāṅmanobhirārambhaḥ / kleśaḥ lobhadveṣamohā yathāyogaṃ samastavyastāḥ / niṣṭhāgamanaṃ tena tena prayogeṇa tasya tasya karmaṇaḥ paripūraṇaṃ tatkālamūrdhvakālaṃ vā // tatra prāṇātipātasya vastu sattvaḥ / āśayastatra tatsaṃjñino vadhābhiprāyaḥ / prayogo vadho yatpraharaṇādibhiḥ / kleśo lobhādikaḥ / niṣṭhāgamanaṃ tasya prāṇinastena prayogeṇānantaraṃ praścādvā maraṇam // adattādānādonāṃ vastu ca niṣṭhāgamanaṃ ca nirdhekṣyāmaḥ / śeṣaṃ yathāyogaṃ yojayitavyam / adattādānasya vastu paraparigṛhītaṃ sattvasaṃkhyātamasattvasaṃkhyātaṃ vā / niṣṭhāgamanaṃ tatsvīkaraṇam / kāmamithyācārasya vastvagamyā strī gamyā vānaṅgādeśākāle vamātrāyuktābhyāṃ ca sarvaśca pumānnapuṃsakaṃ ca / niṣṭhāgamanaṃ dvayadvayasamāpattiḥ / mṛṣāvādasya vastu dṛṣṭaṃ śrutaṃ mataṃ vijñātamadṛṣṭamaśrutamamatamavijñātaṃ ca /
body.translated_text: That bodily and other actions are <s>karmapaths</s> (courses of action) should be understood according to the <s>sūtra</s> as a designation based on what is predominant, because the preparations and the rest of those actions are also included within bodily and other karma. The three, four, and three <s>karmapaths</s> should be understood as having the character of bodily, verbal, and mental karma, respectively.

body.text: āśayo 'nyathāvatkukāmatā / niṣṭhāgamanaṃ parṣatprativādivijñāpanam / paiśunyasya vastu samagravyagrāḥ sattvāḥ / āśayasteṣāmeva bhedāpratisaṃdhānābhiprāyaḥ / niṣṭhāgamanaṃ bhedyavijñāpanam / pāruṣyasya vastvāghātanimittabhūtāḥ sattvāḥ / niṣṭhāgamanaṃ pārūṣāṇām / saṃbhinnapralāpasya vastvanarthopasaṃgṛhītārthaḥ / niṣṭhāgamanaṃ tasya bhāṣaṇam / abhidhyāyā vastu parakīyaṃ vittopakaraṇam / āśayastatra tatsaṃjñinastathāruciḥ / prayogastatsvīkaraṇasaṃpradhāraṇam / niṣṭhāgamanaṃ tatsvīkaraṇaniścayaḥ / vyāpādasya vastvāghātanimittabhūtāḥ sattvāḥ / niṣṭhāgamanaṃ prahanananiścayaḥ / mithyādṛṣṭervastu sannarthaḥ / āśayaḥ satyatatsaṃjñinastathāruciḥ / niṣṭhāgamanamapavādaniścayaḥ //
body.translated_text: The intention [of lying] is the desire to misrepresent the actual [situation]. Its completion (<s>niṣṭhāgamana</s>) is making [the falsehood] known to the addressee or opponent. The object of slander (<s>paiśunya</s>) is beings who are either united or disunited. The intention is the aim to create division or to prevent reconciliation among them. Its completion is informing [someone] to be divided. The object of harsh speech (<s>pāruṣya</s>) is beings who have become causes of resentment. Its completion is the [utterance of] harsh words. The object of idle talk (<s>saṃbhinnapralāpa</s>) is a meaning that pertains to what is meaningless. Its completion is the speaking of that. The object of covetousness (<s>abhidhyā</s>) is the wealth and possessions belonging to others. The intention is the inclination of one who regards it with that perception. The application is the deliberation of appropriating it. Its completion is the firm resolve to appropriate it. The object of malice (<s>vyāpāda</s>) is beings who have become causes of resentment. Its completion is the firm resolve to strike [them]. The object of wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>) is an existing thing. The intention is the inclination of one who regards the true as true. Its completion is the firm resolve to deny.

body.text: parājñaptisaṃcetanīyatā yathā kaścidanicchannapi parairbalādājñāpyamano 'bhisaṃghāyākuśalamācarati / parasaṃjñaptisaṃcetanīyatā yathā kaścidanicchanniva paraiḥ saṃjñāpyamānaḥ samādāpyamāno hitametaditi grāhyamāṇo 'bhisaṃghāyā kuśalamācarati / avijñāya saṃcetanīyatā yathā kaścidguṇadoṣānabhijño 'nabhiniviṣṭaḥ yadṛcchayābhisaṃdhāyākuśalamācarati / mūlābhiniveśasaṃceta nīyatā yathā kaścidkuśalamūlaiḥ lobhādibhirabhibhūta āviṣṭacittastīvreṇābhiniveśenābhisaṃghāyākuśalamācarati / viparyāsasaṃcetanīyatā yathā kaściddharmakāmo viṣamahetudṛṣṭirāyatyāmiṣṭaphalārthamabhisaṃdhāyākuśalamācarati / tatra pūrvikābhistisṛbhiḥ saṃcetanīyatābhiḥ kṛtamapi karma naivopacīyate yato 'sya nāvaśyaṃ vipākaḥ pratisaṃvedanīyaḥ / paścimābhyāṃ tu saṃcetanīyābhyāṃ yadi kṛtaṃ bhavatyupacitaṃ cāvaśyamevāsya vipākaḥ pratisaṃvedyate / upacayo vāsanāvṛddhirityālayavijñāne vipākabīja paripoṣaṇaṃ veditavyam //
body.translated_text: Intentionality through compulsion by others (<s>parājñaptisaṃcetanīyatā</s>) is when someone, even unwilling, being compelled by force by others, perpetrates unwholesome [action] deliberately. Intentionality through persuasion by others (<s>parasaṃjñaptisaṃcetanīyatā</s>) is when someone, as if unwilling, being persuaded and induced by others — told 'this is beneficial' — perpetrates unwholesome [action] deliberately. Intentionality through ignorance (<s>avijñāyasaṃcetanīyatā</s>) is when someone, not knowing the merits and faults, not fixated, by chance perpetrates unwholesome [action] deliberately. Intentionality through fixation on root [afflictions] (<s>mūlābhiniveśasaṃcetanīyatā</s>) is when someone, overpowered by unwholesome roots such as greed and so forth, with a possessed mind, through intense fixation perpetrates unwholesome [action] deliberately. Intentionality through distortion (<s>viparyāsasaṃcetanīyatā</s>) is when someone who desires <s>dharma</s>, holding a view of uneven causation, perpetrates unwholesome [action] deliberately with the aim of obtaining a desired result in the future. Therein, by the first three types of intentionality, even <s>karma</s> that is done is not accumulated, because its maturation-result need not necessarily be experienced. But by the last two types of intentionality, if [the <s>karma</s>] is done, it becomes accumulated, and its maturation must inevitably be experienced. 'Accumulation' means the increase of habitual impregnation (<s>vāsanā</s>) — this should be understood as the nourishment of the maturation-seed in the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (storehouse consciousness).

body.text: karmakriyāniyamaḥ pūrvakarmabhireva niyamya vipākasaṃtatirāviddhā bhavati / yadasmin janmanyanenedaṃ karma karaṇīyamiti sa tamavadhimalaṃghayitvā tatkarma karoti, yasyākaraṇāya pratibandhaṃ buddhā api bhagavanto na samarthāḥ kartum yathāhetuniyamanaṃ phalasaṃtānapariṇāmāditi / vipākapratisaṃvedanāniyamaḥ saṃcetanīyasya karmaṇaḥ pūrvavat / avasthāniyame dṛṣṭadharmavedanīyādibhiravasthāpi niyamitā bhavatīti / yathānena vipākena dṛṣṭe dharme bhavitavyamanenopapadyānenāparasmin paryāya iti //
body.translated_text: The determination of karmic action: through prior <s>karmas</s> alone, the continuum of maturation is determined and set in motion — 'In this birth, this action must be performed by this [person]' — and having overstepped that limit, one performs that action, the prevention of which even <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bhagavāns</s>, are not able to accomplish, just as the determination of the cause [brings about] the transformation of the continuum of the result. The determination of experiencing the maturation: as before, for intentional <s>karma</s>. In the determination of life-stage: the life-stage too is determined by [the karmas] to be experienced in the present life and so forth — namely, 'by this maturation one must exist in the present life, by this in the [next] birth-existence, by this in a subsequent occasion.'

body.text: akuśalānāṃ karmapathānāṃ mṛdumadhyādhi mātrāṇāṃ vipākaphalaṃ tiryakpretanarakeṣu veditavyam / niṣyandaphalamapāyebhyaścyutvā manuṣyeṣūpapannānaṃ pratyekaṃ prāṇātipātādattādānādyānurūpyeṇātmabhāvaparigrahayorvipattiḥ / tadyathālpāyuṣkatā dāridrayamityevamādi yathāyogam / adhipatiphalaṃ pratyekaṃ tadānurūpyeṇaiva bāhyānāṃ bhāvānāṃ [sa]syādīnāṃ vipattiḥ / tadyathā prāṇātipātasyādhipatyenālpaujaso bhavantyevamādi //
body.translated_text: The maturation result (<s>vipākaphala</s>) of the unwholesome action-paths — mild, medium, and intense — should be understood as [rebirth] among animals, hungry ghosts, and hell-beings [respectively]. The outflow result (<s>niṣyandaphala</s>) is, for those who have departed from the lower realms and been reborn among humans, the misfortune in personal existence and possessions corresponding individually to killing, stealing, and so forth. For example, short lifespan, poverty, and so forth, as appropriate. The dominant result (<s>adhipatiphala</s>) is the deterioration of external things such as crops and so forth, corresponding individually to each [unwholesome action-path]. For example, through the dominance of killing, things become of little vitality, and so forth.

body.text: yathāsūtram - "sarvairdaśabhirakuśalaiḥ karmapathairāsevitairbhāvitairbahulīkṛtairnarakeṣūpapadyate / tadeṣāṃ vipākaphalam / sa cedicchatvamāgacchati manuṣyāṇāṃ sabhāgatām, prāṇātipātenālpāyurbhavati adattādānena bhogavyasanī bhavati / kāmamithyācāreṇa sasapatnadāraḥ / mṛṣāvādenābhyākhyānabahulaḥ / paiśūnyena mitrabhedo 'sya bhavati / pāruṣyeṇāmanojñaśabdaśravaṇaṃ bhavati / saṃbhinnapralāpenānādeyavākyaḥ / abhidhyayā tīvrarāgaḥ / vyāpādena tīvradveṣaḥ / mithyādṛṣṭyā tīvramohaḥ, tasyā mohabhūyastvāt / idameṣāṃ niṣyandaphalam / prāṇātipātenātyāsevitena bāhyābhāvā alpaujaso bhavanti / adattādānenāśanirajobahulāḥ / kāmamithyācāreṇa rajo 'vakīrṇāḥ / mṛṣāvādena dugandhāḥ / paśūnyenotkūlanikūlāḥ / pārūṣyeṇoṣarajaṅgalāḥ pratikrusṭāḥ pāpabhūmayaḥ / saṃbhinnapralāpena viṣamartupariṇāmāḥ / abhidhyayā sūkṣmaphalāḥ / vyāpādena kaṭukaphalāḥ / mithyādṛṣṭayālpaphalā aphalā vā / idameṣāmadhipatiphalam //"
body.translated_text: As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Through all ten unwholesome action-paths, when practiced, cultivated, and frequently engaged in, one is reborn in the hells. This is their maturation result. If one happens to come to the state of human class-homogeneity: through killing, one has a short lifespan; through stealing, one suffers loss of wealth; through sexual misconduct, one has a co-wife; through lying, one is subject to much false accusation; through slander, one experiences the breaking of friendships; through harsh speech, one hears unpleasant sounds; through idle talk, one's words are not heeded; through covetousness, one has intense attachment; through malice, intense hatred; through wrong view, intense delusion, because delusion predominates in it. This is their outflow result. Through killing, when excessively practiced, external things become of little vitality; through stealing, there are many hailstorms and much dust; through sexual misconduct, [the land is] covered with dust; through lying, it is foul-smelling; through slander, [the terrain is] uneven with hills and valleys; through harsh speech, [the land is] saline, barren, harsh, and of evil ground; through idle talk, there are irregularities of season; through covetousness, the fruits are small; through malice, the fruits are bitter; through wrong view, the fruits are scanty or entirely absent. This is their dominant result.'

body.text: daśānāṃ kuśalānāṃ karmapathānāṃ vipākaphalaṃ devamanuṣyeṣu / niṣyandaphalaṃ teṣveva pratyekamānurūpyeṇātmabhāvaparigrahasaṃpattiḥ /
body.translated_text: The maturation result (<s>vipākaphala</s>) of the ten wholesome action-paths is [rebirth] among gods and humans. The outflow result (<s>niṣyandaphala</s>) is the prosperity in personal existence and possessions corresponding individually to each [wholesome action-path], among those very [gods and humans].

body.text: yathākuśalānāṃ karmapathānāṃ vipākaphalādi triphalā vasthānaṃ kṛtam, evaṃ kuśalādīnāṃ karmapathānāṃ sāsravāṇāṃ devamanuṣyeṣu trīṇi phalāni yathāyogaṃ yojayitavyāni //
body.translated_text: Just as the threefold fruition — maturation result and so forth — has been established for the unwholesome action-paths, so too the three results of the wholesome and other action-paths that are contaminated (<s>sāsrava</s>) should be applied as appropriate among gods and humans.

body.text: ekena karmaṇā ekamātmabhāvamākṣipati, ekena karma[kṣa]ṇenaikajanmikasyaiva vipākasya bījapoṣaṇāt / ekenānekamākṣipati, tenaivānekajanmikavipākabījapoṣaṇāt / anekenaikamākṣipati, bahubhiḥ karmakṣaṇaiḥ tasyaivaikasya punaḥ punaḥ bījapoṣaṇāt / anekenānekamākṣipati, bahubhiranyonyāpekṣayā janmaparaṃparābījapoṣaṇāditi //
body.translated_text: By a single <s>karma</s>, a single personal existence is projected — because through a single <s>karma</s>-moment, the seed of maturation for a single birth is nourished. By a single [<s>karma</s>], many [existences are projected] — because by that very [single <s>karma</s>], the seed of maturation for multiple births is nourished. By many [<s>karmas</s>], a single [existence is projected] — because through many <s>karma</s>-moments, the seed of that very single [existence] is nourished again and again. By many [<s>karmas</s>], many [existences are projected] — because through many [<s>karmas</s>], in mutual dependence, the seeds for a succession of births are nourished.

body.text: kena kāraṇena rūpārūpyapratisaṃyuktaṃ kuśalamānijyamityucyate / yathā kāmāvacaramanyagatikamapi paripūrakaṃ kuśalamūlamanyatra vipākaṃ prayacchati, naivaṃ rūpyārūpyāvacaram, bhūminaiyamyena phaladānāt / ato vipākadānaṃ pratyakampanārthenānijyamuktaṃ samāhitabhūmikatvāccākampanārthe[ne]ti //
body.translated_text: For what reason is the wholesome associated with the form and formless realms called 'unshakeable' (<s>ānijya</s>)? Just as wholesome root-merit belonging to the desire realm, even though productive of another destiny, gives its maturation elsewhere [as a completing karma], not so for [the wholesome] belonging to the form and formless realms, because it gives its result only within its own level due to the fixed nature of the level. Therefore, it is called 'unshakeable' in the sense that it does not waver in giving its maturation, and because it belongs to the level of concentration, [it is called 'unshakeable'] also in the sense of non-wavering.

body.text: phalavipākasaṃmūḍhasyāpuṇyāḥ saṃskārāḥ saṃbhavanti, teṣāmekāntakliṣṭatvenāvidyāsāṃnidhye sati phalavipākābhisaṃpratyayākārāyāḥ samyagdṛṣṭeranavakāśāt / tattvārthasaṃmūḍhasya puṇyāniṃjyāstattvārtha ucyate catvāryāryasatyāni / tatra saṃmohaḥ kuśalacittānāmapyadṛṣṭasatyānāmanuśayato 'nubuddho bhavati yadvaśena te duḥkhatastraidhātukasya yathābhūtamaparijñānāt punarbhavahetubhūtān puṇyānijyasaṃskārānutthāpayanti / na tvevaṃ dṛṣṭasatyāstattvārthasaṃmohābhāvāt / ataste taddhetukā ityucyante //
body.translated_text: For one who is confused about the fruition and maturation, non-meritorious formations (<s>apuṇya saṃskāras</s>) arise — because when ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) is present, since those [formations] are exclusively afflicted, there is no room for the right view that has the aspect of acknowledging fruition and maturation. For one who is confused about ultimate reality, meritorious and unshakeable [formations arise]. The ultimate reality referred to is the Four Noble Truths. Therein, the confusion, even in those with wholesome minds who have not seen the truths, is followed as a latent tendency (<s>anuśaya</s>), by the power of which they, not having fully comprehended the three realms as suffering of conditioned existence (<s>saṃskāraduḥkhatā</s>) as it really is, produce meritorious and unshakeable formations that are causes of renewed existence. But those who have seen the truths do not [produce such formations], because of the absence of confusion about ultimate reality. Therefore, those [formations] are said to be caused by that [confusion].

body.text: prāṇātipātasya lobhena prayogo māṃsikādīnām / dveṣeṇaiva vairaniryātanakāmānām / mohena yājñikādīnām / dveṣeṇaiva niṣṭhā nirghṛṇatāmantareṇa parasattvavipādanāsaṃbhavāt / evaṃ pāruṣyādīnāṃ yathāyogaṃ yojayitavyam /
body.translated_text: The application (<s>prayoga</s>) of killing motivated by greed pertains to butchers and the like. Motivated by hatred, it pertains to those who wish to exact revenge. Motivated by delusion, it pertains to ritualists who perform sacrifices and the like. The completion is through hatred alone, because the destruction of another being is not possible without cruelty (<s>nirghṛṇatā</s>). Similarly, harsh speech and so forth should be applied as appropriate.

body.text: abhidhyādīnāṃ kathaṃ lobhādibhiḥ prayogaḥ / tatrābhidhyākarmapathaḥ paravittopakaraṇasvīkaraṇaniścaya ityuktam / tadyadi tenaiva vittopakaraṇenārthī bhava[ti] tatsvīkaraṇāyābhisaṃskarotyato 'sya lobhena prayogo vyavasthāpyate / atha maivāsya bhūdityevaṃ dveṣeṇa / atha parasvīkaraṇe na kaściddoṣa iti mohena prayogo veditavyaḥ / evamanyadapi yojayitavyam //
body.translated_text: How is the application of covetousness (<s>abhidhyā</s>) and so forth [explained] through greed and so forth? Therein, the action-path of covetousness has been said to be the firm resolve to appropriate others' wealth and possessions. If one desires that very wealth and possessions and fashions [the resolve] to appropriate it, then the application is established as through greed. If [one thinks] 'may this not be his!' — then through hatred. If [one thinks] 'there is no fault in appropriating what belongs to another' — the application should be understood as through delusion. Similarly, the rest should also be applied.

body.text: anyonyādhipateyamapi karma sādhāraṇaṃ veditavyaṃ yadvaśātsattvā anyonyaṃ citacaittapariṇāmanimittaṃ bhavantīti //
body.translated_text: Shared <s>karma</s> (<s>sādhāraṇa</s>) should also be understood as mutually dominant — because under its power, beings become the causes of each other's mental and mental-factor transformations.

body.text: vaipakṣikāt karmaṇaḥ prātipakṣikai karma bala[va]ddraṣṭavyam, pratipakṣabalenākṣiptasyāpi vipakṣaphalasyānyathātvāpādanāt / sarvaṃ ca kuśalaṃ karma saṃcetanīyaṃ pratipakṣabalikasyākuśalād balavaddraṣṭavyam / pratipakṣabaladurbalasya tvakuśalaṃ kuśalādbalavat / sarvaṃ cāviśeṣeṇa kuśalākuśalaṃ niyatavipākamārya mārgeṇāprahīṇaṃ balavadityucyate / kāmapratisaṃyuktamakuśalaṃ prakṛtyā balavat, kleśopakleśādibahuparivāratvāt / yadyapi pūrvābhyastaṃ tadapi balavat, saṃtatestena bhāvitatvāt / yadapi padasthaṃ paripūrṇavayasām, tīvrābhiniveśaprasādakaraṇāt / yadapyasādhyamaparinirvāṇadharmakāṇām, pratipakṣeṇānuddhāryatvāt / kṣetrato 'pi mātṛbadhādikam / cittābhisaṃskārato 'pi mahābodhipraṇidhānādikaṃ balavatkarma veditavyam / punarnavabhirākārairbalavatkarma veditavyam / tadyathā kṣetrato yadi guṇavaddakṣiṇīyaṃ kṣetraṃ bhavati / vastuno yadi praṇītaṃ prabhūtaṃ deyavastu bhavati / svabhāvato dānācchīlaṃ śīlādbhāvanetyevamādiḥ / āśrayataḥ puṇyānāṃ kartā yadi vītarāgo bhavati / manaskārato yadi tīvraprasādasahagato manaskāro bhavati / āśayato yadi nirvāṇāśayo bhavati / sahāyato yadi tadanyapuṇyakriyāvastuparigṛhītaṃ bhavati / bahulīkārataḥ yadi paunaḥ punyena kṛtaṃ bhavatyanuvitarkitaṃ vā / bāhujanyato yadi svayaṃ ca kṛtaṃ bhavatyanyaiśca kāritamiti //
body.translated_text: <s>Karma</s> that is opposed should be viewed as stronger than its counterpart, because through the power of the antidote, even the result of the opposing [unwholesome karma] that has been projected is brought to a different outcome. And all wholesome <s>karma</s> that is intentional should be viewed as stronger than the unwholesome of one whose antidote-power is strong. But the unwholesome is stronger than the wholesome of one whose antidote-power is weak. And all wholesome and unwholesome [<s>karma</s>] without distinction that has a definite maturation and has not been abandoned by the noble path is called 'strong.' Unwholesome [<s>karma</s>] associated with the desire realm is strong by nature, because of having many attendant afflictions and secondary afflictions. Even that which has been previously cultivated is strong, because the continuum has been habituated by it. Even that which is stable, belonging to those of full maturity, because of producing intense fixation or clarity. Even that which is intractable, belonging to those whose <s>dharma</s>-nature is not to attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, because it cannot be eradicated by the antidote. Also by field (<s>kṣetra</s>) — killing one's mother and the like. Also by mental construction — the aspiration for great awakening (<s>mahābodhipraṇidhāna</s>) and the like should be understood as strong <s>karma</s>. Furthermore, strong <s>karma</s> should be understood through nine aspects. Namely: through field — if the recipient-field is endowed with qualities. Through substance — if the gift-substance is excellent and abundant. Through intrinsic nature — morality is [stronger] than generosity, and meditation than morality, and so forth. Through basis — if the performer of merits is one who has become dispassionate. Through attention — if the attention is accompanied by intense clarity. Through intention — if the intention is directed toward <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Through companions — if it is accompanied by other bases of meritorious action. Through frequent performance — if it has been done repeatedly or reflected upon repeatedly. Through wide benefit — if it has been done by oneself and caused to be done by others.

body.text: ya evaṃ vadet - yathā yathāyaṃ puruṣapudgalaḥ karma karotyupacinoti tathā tathā vipākaṃ pratisaṃvedayata ityevaṃ sati brahmacaryavāso na bhavatyavakāśaśca
body.translated_text: Whoever would say thus: 'In whatever manner this person performs and accumulates <s>karma</s>, in that very manner one experiences its maturation' — if this were so, the holy life (<s>brahmacaryavāsa</s>) would not exist, and no opportunity

body.text: na prajñāyate samyagduḥkhakṣayāya duḥkhasyāntakriyāyai / kathaṃ kṛtvā brahmacaryavāso na bhavati / tīvrakleśasya pratisaṃkhyāya sahaduḥkhena sahadaurmanasyena śīlaparipālanāt / yadi tadvipākastathaiva sahaduḥkhena sahadaurmanasyenānubhūyeta vṛthā tatparipālanaṃ syāt / pāradārikaprabhṛtīnāṃ ca sahasukhena sahasaumanasyena dauḥśīlyakaraṇādyadi tadvipākastathaivānubhūyeta vṛthā tadviratiḥ syādityevaṃ kṛtvā brahmacaryavāso na bhavati // kathamavakāśaśca na prajñāyate samyagduḥkhakṣayāya duḥkhasyāntakriyāyai / ata eva tadupaniṣadbhatasya brahmacaryavāsasya duḥkhavipākatvāditi / evaṃ ca kṛtvā sukhasahagatasya karmaṇaḥ sukhasahagata eva vipāko duḥkhasahagatasya duḥkhasahagato 'duḥkhāsukhasahagatasya tatsahagata eveti niyamaḥ pratiṣiddhaḥ // atra yastvevaṃ yathāvedanīyaṃ yathāvedanīyamityevamādinā sukhasahagatasya kuśalākuśalasya yathāyogamāyatyāṃ sukhaduḥkhāduḥkhāsukhavedanīyasya sukhādiko vipāko 'nujñātaḥ / evaṃ duḥkhāduḥkhāsukhasahagatasya sukhādivedanīyasya sukhādiko vipāko 'nujñāyata iti //
body.translated_text: would be discerned for the complete destruction of suffering, for making an end of suffering. How is it that the holy life would not exist? Because one who has intense afflictions, having analyzed, guards moral conduct together with suffering and mental distress — if its maturation were experienced in exactly the same manner, together with suffering and mental distress, then the guarding of that [morality] would be futile. And since adulterers and the like perform immorality together with pleasure and mental satisfaction — if its maturation too were experienced in exactly the same manner, then abstention would be futile. In this way, the holy life would not exist. And how would no opportunity be discerned for the complete destruction of suffering, for making an end of suffering? Precisely because that holy life, which is the means thereto, would have a painful maturation. Thus, the strict correspondence — that the maturation of <s>karma</s> accompanied by pleasure is necessarily accompanied by pleasure, that of <s>karma</s> accompanied by suffering is necessarily accompanied by suffering, and that of <s>karma</s> accompanied by neither-suffering-nor-pleasure is necessarily accompanied by that — is refuted. But here, by [the statement] 'as it is to be experienced, so it is to be experienced' and so forth, the maturation of wholesome or unwholesome [<s>karma</s>] accompanied by pleasure — to be experienced in the future as pleasant, painful, or neither-pleasant-nor-painful as appropriate — is permitted as having a pleasant and so forth maturation. Similarly, the maturation of [<s>karma</s>] accompanied by suffering or neither-suffering-nor-pleasure, [which is] to be experienced as pleasant and so forth, is permitted as having a pleasant and so forth maturation.

body.text: pravrajitasya saṃvaraḥ pañcavidho bhikṣusaṃvaro yāvacchāmaṇerīsaṃvara iti / sa duścaritavivekacaritaṃ kāmavivekacaritaṃ ca pudgalamadhikṛtya vyavasthāpitaḥ / tathāhi sa tādṛśaḥ śaknoti yāvajjīvaṃ prāṇātipātāda brahmacaryācca virantumiti / upāsakopāsikāsaṃvaro duścaritaviveka caritamadhikṛtya no tu kāmavivekacaritam / ataḥ evāsya yāvajjīvaṃ kāmamithyā cāraviratirvyavasthāpyate nābrahmacaryaviratiriti / upavāsasaṃvaro naiva duścaritavivekacaritaṃ na kāmavivekacaritam / ata evāsyāhorātrika upavāsasaṃvaraḥ prajñaptaḥ, śanaistadubhayābhyasanārthamiti / yathā paṇḍapaṇḍakānāṃ bhikṣubhikṣuṇī pakṣopāsanāyogyatvādupāsakatvapratiṣedhaḥ, evamubhayavyañjanānāmapi strīpuruṣakleśasamudācāreṇobhayapakṣopāsanāyogyateti na te pṛthaguktāḥ / dhyānasaṃvaro dauḥśīlyasamutthāpakānāṃ lobhādīnāṃ kāmāvacarāṇāṃ kleśopakleśānāṃ viṣkambhaṇapratipakṣeṇa bījopaghāte sati pradeśavairāgyeṇāpi kāmebhyo vītarāgasya yā tasmādauḥśīlyādviratiḥ / yāvattṛtīyadhyānavītarāgasya dūrībhāvapratipakṣeṇa teṣāmeva dauḥśīlyasamutthāpakānāṃ sutarāṃ bījopaghāto veditavyaḥ / caturthadhyānavītarāgasya tvārūpyeṣu rūpābhāvāccholasaṃvarāvyavasthānaṃ veditavyam //
body.translated_text: The restraint of the renunciant is fivefold: the <s>bhikṣusaṃvara</s> (monk's restraint) up to the <s>śāmaṇerīsaṃvara</s> (novice nun's restraint). It is established with reference to the person who practices separation from misconduct and separation from sense pleasures. For such a person is able to refrain for life from killing and the rest, and from non-celibacy. The <s>upāsaka</s> (layman) and <s>upāsikā</s> (laywoman) restraint is established with reference to separation from misconduct but not separation from sense pleasures. Therefore, for them, lifelong abstention from sexual misconduct is established, not abstention from all non-celibacy. The <s>upavāsasaṃvara</s> (fast-day restraint) is neither for one who practices separation from misconduct nor for one who practices separation from sense pleasures. Therefore, it is designated as a one-day-and-night fast-day restraint, for the purpose of gradually practicing both. Just as <s>paṇḍakas</s> (eunuchs) are prohibited from becoming monks or nuns because they are unsuitable for service to either gender's group, and therefore from becoming lay followers, likewise those of both characteristics are also unsuitable for service to both groups because of the arising of defilements of both female and male types, and so they are not mentioned separately. The <s>dhyānasaṃvara</s> (meditative restraint) — when there is damage to the seeds of the greed and other defilements of the desire realm that give rise to immorality, through the antidote of suppression, then even through partial dispassion, for one who is dispassionate toward sense pleasures, there is abstention from that immorality. Up to one dispassionate toward the third <s>dhyāna</s>, through the antidote of distancing, the damage to the seeds of those same factors that give rise to immorality should be understood as even greater. But for one dispassionate toward the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, since there is no form in the formless realms, the establishment of this type of restraint should be understood as not applicable.

body.text: aurabhrikā ye paśūn hatvā tadvikrayeṇa jīvikāṃ kalpayanti / evaṃ kaukkuṭikādayo yathāsaṃbhavaṃ yojayitavyāḥ / nāgabandhakā araṇyāt hastino vaddhvā da[ma]yanti / nāgamaṇḍalikā ye sarpānādāya tatkrīḍanairjīvanti / mūtrakā ye parān paiśunyenopahatva jīvanti / abhijanmato vā tatkarmasamādānato veti tatkulīnasyānyakulīnasya ca yathākramam / kāyavākprayogapūrvakaḥ tatkarmādhyācāraniścayo 'saṃvara ityucyate /
body.translated_text: <s>Aurabhrikas</s> are those who kill animals and make a living by selling them. Likewise, <s>kaukkuṭikas</s> (poultry dealers) and the rest should be applied as appropriate. <s>Nāgabandhakas</s> (elephant trappers) capture elephants from the forest and tame them. <s>Nāgamaṇḍalikas</s> (snake charmers) are those who take serpents and make a living by playing with them. <s>Mūtrakas</s> (slanderers) are those who destroy others through slander and make a living thereby. 'By birth or by undertaking that occupation' refers respectively to one born in that family and one from another family. The determination to engage in that occupation, preceded by bodily and verbal action, is called non-restraint.

body.text: yathoktasaṃvarāsaṃvaravinirmuktasya dānapriyavacanādikaṃ khaṭacapeṭādikaṃ ca karma navasaṃvaronāsaṃvara ityucyate //
