body.translated_text: For one who is free from both the aforementioned restraint and non-restraint, actions such as giving, kind speech, and the rest, as well as actions such as scratching, slapping, and the rest, are called neither restraint nor non-restraint.

body.text: dṛṣṭadharmavedanīyaṃ karma yatra janmani kṛtaṃ tatraiva yadvipacyate / upapadyavedanīyaṃ yadanantare janmani, tadyathā pañcānantaryāṇi karmāṇi / yasya tāvadekamevānantarya tasya tadvipāko 'nantaraṃ yuktaḥ, yasyedānīṃ saṃbahulāni tasya kathaṃ tadvipākapratisaṃvedanā / sarveṣāṃ yugapadvipākaḥ pratisaṃvidyate, tathāhyanekānantaryakāriṇa āśrayaḥ sukumārataro nirvartate, kāraṇāśca bahutīvravicitrā yadvaśādbhūyasīṃ vedanāṃ pratyanubhavati //
body.translated_text: <s>Dṛṣṭadharmavedanīya</s> karma (karma whose result is experienced in the present life) is that which ripens in the very same life in which it was performed. <s>Upapadyavedanīya</s> (karma whose result is experienced in the next life) is that which ripens in the immediately following life — for example, the five actions of immediate retribution. For one who has committed only one such action, its retribution immediately following is appropriate. But for one who has committed many, how is the retribution of those —

body.text: ārambhaṃ ca pratyetāni dṛṣṭadharmavedanīyādīni vyavasthāpyante, na tanmātravedanīyatāmadhikṛtya / yasya tatraiva janmani vipāko vipaktumārabhate taddṛṣṭadharmavedanīyam / yasyānantare janmanyārabhate tadupapadyavedanīyam / yasyānantaraṃ janma laghayitvārabhate tadaparaparyāyavedanīyamityevaṃ ca kṛtvā hācittāvadāne - "ānantaryasya karmaṇo narake punaḥpunaścyutyupapādena vipākapratisaṃvedanam" - anulomitaṃ bhavatīti //
body.translated_text: These are established as <s>dṛṣṭadharmavedanīya</s> and the rest with reference to the commencement of ripening, not with reference to being experienced exclusively in that manner. That whose result begins to ripen in that very same life is <s>dṛṣṭadharmavedanīya</s>. That whose result begins in the immediately following life is <s>upapadyavedanīya</s>. That which skips the immediately following life —

body.text: kṛṣṇaṃ kṛṣṇavipākaṃ karmākuśalam, kliṣṭatvādaniṣṭavipākatvācca //
body.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> (dark) karma with dark result is unwholesome karma, because it is defiled and because its result is undesirable.

body.text: viparyayācchuklaṃ śuklavipākaṃ traidhātukaṃ kuśalam //
body.translated_text: By the converse, <s>śukla</s> (bright) karma with bright result is wholesome karma of all three realms.

body.text: kṛṣṇaśuklaṃ kṛṣṇaśuklavipākaṃ yatkāmapratisaṃyuktaṃ vipākaṃ vyāmiśraṃ kuśalākuśalamityarthaḥ / kathamekaṃ kuśalaṃ bhavatyakuśalaṃ ca / nātra
body.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇaśukla</s> (dark-and-bright) karma with dark-and-bright result is that which is connected with desire-realm maturation that is mixed — meaning both wholesome and unwholesome. How can one thing be both wholesome and unwholesome? Here it is not

body.text: pravṛttikṣaṇanaiyamyenocyate tadevobhayamityapi tu sahāśayaprayogeṇaikaṃ karmetyayamatrābhi saṃdhirvedivyaḥ / tayośca kṛṣṇaśuklatāṃ pratyanyonyāsādṛśye satyekaṃ karma kṛṣṇaśuklaṃ vyavasthāpyate / tatrāśayataḥ kṛṣṇaṃ prayogataḥ śuklaṃ yathāpi kaścitparān vañcayitukāmasteṣāṃ saṃpratyayananimittaṃ bhāvena dānāni dadāti yāvatpravrajatyapi / prayogataḥ kṛṣṇamāśayataḥ śuklaṃ yathāpi kaścitputraṃ vā śiṣyaṃ vāhitānnivārayitukāmo hite ca niyojayitukāmo 'nukampācittaḥ kāyena vācā vā paruṣayā tasminkāle saṃkliśyate //
body.translated_text: stated by the restriction of a single moment of occurrence that the same thing is both; rather, through the combination of intention and effort, it is one karma — this is the implicit meaning to be understood here. When there is mutual dissimilarity between the dark and bright aspects of those two, a single karma is established as dark-and-bright. In that case, dark from the standpoint of intention and bright from the standpoint of effort — for example, someone who —

body.text: akṛṣṇaśuklāvipākaṃ karma karmakṣayāya saṃvartate prayogānantaryamārgeṣvanāsravaṃ karmaprayogamārgānantaryamārgāṇāṃ prahāṇapratipakṣatvāt / tatrākṛṣṇaṃ kleśamalābhāvāt / śuklamekāntavyavadānatvāt / avipākaṃ saṃsāravirodhitvāt / karmakṣayāya saṃvartate 'syaiva kṛṣṇādikasya trividhasya sāsravasya karmaṇastenānāsraveṇa karmaṇā vipākadānavāsanāsamudghātāt //
body.translated_text: <s>Akṛṣṇāśukla</s> (neither-dark-nor-bright) karma with no maturation tends toward the exhaustion of karma — the uncontaminated karma in the paths of effort, the path of immediate preparation, and the uninterrupted path, because the paths of effort and the uninterrupted path serve as antidotes for abandonment. Among these, it is neither-dark because of the absence of the stain of defilements. It is bright because it is exclusively purifying. It is without maturation because it is opposed to <s>saṃsāra</s>. It tends toward the exhaustion of karma —

body.text: aviśeṣeṇa ca sarvasyānāsravasya karmaṇaḥ paripanthamānukūlyaṃ svabhāvamadhikṛtya vaṃkadoṣakaṣāyāṇāṃ śauceyānāṃ mauneyānāṃ ca yathākramaṃ vyavasthānaṃ veditavyam //
body.translated_text: And without distinction, with respect to the nature of all uncontaminated karma in terms of its obstructive, favorable, and intrinsic nature, the establishment of <s>vaṅka</s> (crookedness), <s>doṣa</s> (fault), <s>kaṣāya</s> (defilement), <s>śauceya</s> (purity), and <s>mauneya</s> (saintly conduct) should be understood respectively.

body.text: tatra vaṃkamṛjukamārgasyāṣṭāṅgasyotpattyāvaraṇabhūtaṃ kāyavāṅmanaḥkarma / doṣo yena kāyādikarmaṇā dūṣite saṃtāne tattādṛśamāvaraṇabhūtaṃ karmotpadyate / kaṣāyāḥ tīrthikadṛṣṭisaṃniśritaṃ kāyādi karma, buddhaśāsanaprasādavipakṣeṇāśraddhyakāluṣyaparigṛhītatvāt / aparaḥ paryāyaḥ - śāśvatocchedānupatitaṃ madhyamāpratipadvirodhārthena vaṃkam / apavādadṛṣṭiparigṛhītaṃ vyavadānavyavasthānapradveṣārthena doṣaḥ / satkāyadṛṣṭiparigṛhītaṃ nairātmyatattvadarśanaprativaddhārthena kaṣāya iti //
body.translated_text: Among these, <s>vaṅka</s> (crookedness) is bodily, verbal, and mental karma that obstructs the arising of the eightfold straight path. <s>Doṣa</s> (fault) is the karma by which, when the continuum is corrupted by bodily and other karma, such obstructive karma arises. <s>Kaṣāyas</s> (defilements) are bodily and other karma dependent on the views of non-Buddhist teachers, being grasped by the impurity of faithlessness that opposes confidence in the <s>Buddha's</s> teaching —

body.text: śauceyāni suviśuddhaśīlasaṃgṛhītamṛjudṛṣṭisaṃgṛhītaṃ ca yatkāyavāṅmanaḥkarma, śīladṛṣṭivipattimalavarjitatvāt / mauneyāni śaikṣāśaikṣāṇāṃ yadanāsravaṃ kāyavāṅmanaḥkarma munīnāṃ tatkarmeti kṛtvā / dānasaṃpadamadhikṛtya dānaṃ dātā bhaviṣyatītyanenābhīkṣṇadānatāṃ darśayati, tacchīlatayā punaḥ punardānāt / śramaṇebhyo brāhmaṇebhya ityevamādināpakṣapātadānatām, aviśeṣeṇa sarvārthibhyo dānāta /
body.translated_text: <s>Śauceyas</s> (purities) are bodily, verbal, and mental karma that is comprised in thoroughly pure morality and comprised in straight views, because it is free from the stain of failure in morality and views. <s>Mauneyyas</s> (saintly conducts) are the uncontaminated bodily, verbal, and mental karma of trainees and adepts, because that is the karma of <s>munis</s> (sages). With reference to the perfection of giving, 'giving — he will be a giver' — by this, the habitual —

body.text: annapānamityevamādinecchāparipūraṇadānatām, yathābhiprāyaṃ sarvopakaraṇavastuparityāgāt / muktatyāgaḥ pratatapāṇirvyavasargarato yāyajūkastyāgasaṃpanno dānasaṃvibhāgarata ityebhiḥ padairyathākramamaniśritadānatādayo veditavyāḥ / aniśritadānatā punarbhavabhogāpariṇāmitatvena veditavyā // deyasaṃpadamadhikṛtyotthānavīryādhigatairityanenānabhidrugdhadeyavastutāṃ darśayati / abhidrugdhaṃ hyanutthānabīryādhigataṃ bhavati, svasthāne sthitvā paranikṣepā[pa]lapanena pratilabdhatvāt / bāhubalopārjitairityanenāparāpahṛtadeyavastutām / parebhyo hyapahṛtaṃ na bāhubalopārjitaṃ bhavati, taiḥ kṛcchreṇa vividhairūpāyairarjitasyāpaharaṇāt / svedamalāpakṣiptairityanenākuthitavimaladeyavastutām, svedamalābhyāmapakṣiptatvādujjhitatvādityarthaḥ / dhārmikairityanena kalpikadeyavastutām, śastraviṣamadyādyakalpikavastuvivarjitatvāt / dharmalabdhairityanena dharmārjitadeyavastutāṃ darśayati, tulākūlādimithyājīva parivarjanenopārjitatvāt //
body.translated_text: 'food and drink' and so forth — thus the giving that fulfills desires, because of the relinquishing of all requisites and possessions as one wishes. 'Released in generosity, with hands outstretched, delighting in relinquishment, responsive to requests, endowed with generosity, delighting in sharing' — by these terms, respectively, non-attached giving and the rest should be understood. Non-attached giving furthermore —

body.text: śīlaṃ samādāyākhaṇḍanena tadyogācchīlavān bhavati / mokṣaṃ prati yaḥ saṃvaraḥ sa prātimokṣasaṃvaraḥ / sa hi saṃsārānniryāṇāya bhavati / ācārasaṃpannaḥ sadbhiragarhiteryāpathāditvāt / gocarasaṃpannaḥ pañcāgocaraparivarjanāt / pañca bhikṣoragocarāḥ - ghoṣo veśaḥ pānāgāraṃ rājakulaṃ caṇḍālakaṭhinameva pañcamam / prajñaptisāvadyeṣvapi prakṛtisāvadyeṣviva tīvreṇa gauraveṇa śikṣaṇādaṇumātreṣvavadyeṣu bhayadarśī bhavati / samantāt paripūrṇa śikṣāmādāya śikṣate śikṣāpadeṣvityucyate //
body.translated_text: Having undertaken <s>śīla</s> (morality), one becomes possessed of morality through the practice of not breaking it. The restraint that is directed toward liberation is the <s>prātimokṣasaṃvara</s> (individual liberation restraint). For it exists for the sake of escape from <s>saṃsāra</s>. 'Accomplished in conduct' — because one's deportment and the rest are not censured by the virtuous. 'Accomplished in resort' — because of avoiding the five improper resorts. The five improper resorts for a <s>bhikṣu</s> are —

body.text: ataḥ paraṃ śīlamārabhya yadbhagavatā sūtrāntareṣu nirdiṣṭaṃ kāyena saṃvṛto bhavatītyevamādi tasyārtha ucyate / tatra kāyena vācā saṃvṛto bhavati saṃprajanyaparigṛhītatayā yathanujñātamabhikramapratikramādiṣu buddhipūrvaṃ samyagvartanāt /
body.translated_text: From this point onward, regarding morality, the meaning of what the <s>Bhagavān</s> has taught in other <s>sūtras</s> — 'one is restrained in body' and so forth — is explained. Among these, one is restrained in body and speech because, being endowed with clear comprehension, one conducts oneself properly and deliberately in approaching and departing and the rest, as has been permitted.

body.text: kāyavāksaṃpattyā saṃpannaḥ āpattyanadhyāpannatayā śīlāvipādanāt / pariśuddhakāyavākasamudācāraḥ samādhisaṃniśrayatayā samādhibalena dauḥśīlyamaladūrīkaraṇāt / kuśala[kāya]vāksamudācāraḥ kliṣṭavitarkāvyavakīrṇatayaikāntaśubhatvāt / anavadyakāyavāksamudācāro bhavabhogāpariṇāmitatvena sadbhiḥ praśastatvāt / avyābadhyakāyavāksamudācāra ātmotkarṣaṇādibhiḥ pareṣāmavajñāduḥkhasaṃvāsenāghaṭṭanāt / ānulomikakāyavāksamudācāro nirvāṇānuprāptyanukūlatayāryamārgāvāhanāt / anucchavikakāyavāksamudācāraḥ svadoṣaguṇāviṣkambhaṇachādanārtham / aupayikakāyavāksamudācāraḥ sabrahmacāryupagrahaṇaśīlatayopagamanārhatvāt / pratirūpakāyavāksamudācāro guruṣu gurusthānīyeṣu ca nihitamānatayā yathārhamupacaraṇāt / pradakṣiṇakāyavāksamudācāro 'vavāde pradakṣiṇagrāhitayāsvayaṃdṛṣṭiparāmarśatvāt / ataptakāyavāksamudācāraḥ kaṣṭatapolūhādhimuktivivarjitatayānātmatapatvāt / ananutāpyakāyavāksamudācāraḥ samutsṛṣṭān bhogān karmāntāṃścārabhyāvipratisāritayā paścāttāpābhāvāt / avipratisārakāyavāksamudācāraḥ kuśalapakṣamārabhyālpamātreṇāsaṃtuṣṭasyā vipratisāritayā yāvacchakyaṃ saṃpādanāt //
body.translated_text: 'Accomplished in the purity of body and speech' — because morality is not impaired through not incurring offenses. 'Having purified bodily and verbal conduct' — because through the support of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), the stain of immorality is removed by the power of concentration. 'Having wholesome bodily and verbal conduct' — because it is exclusively pure, being unmixed with defiled thoughts. 'Having blameless bodily and verbal conduct' —

body.text: karma svakameṣāṃ ta ime karmasvakāḥ / kathaṃ punasteṣāṃ karma svakaṃ bhavati / svayaṃkṛtakarmavipākapratisaṃvedanatāmupādāya, taddhi nāma svakamityucyate yatparairasādhāraṇamiti / karmāṇi dāyāya eṣāṃ ta ime karmadāyādāḥ / kathaṃ karmaṇāṃ dāyādatvam / tasyāṃ svayaṃkṛtavipākapratisaṃvedanāyāṃ kuśalākuśalānāṃ karmaṇāmanyonyadāyādatāmupādāya yathāsvamiṣṭāniṣṭaphalasaṃvibhajanāt / te punaḥ svakṛtakarmeṣṭāniṣṭavipākapratisaṃvedinaḥ sattvāḥ kuta āditaḥ saṃbhūtāḥ kimahetukā āhosvit prakṛtīśvarādihetukā ityāha karmayonīyāḥ / karmeveṣāmahetuviṣamahetuvarjito yoniḥ sattvānāṃ saṃbhavāyetyarthaḥ / evaṃ tāvatpravṛttimārabhya nivṛttimapyārabhya karmapratisaraṇāḥ, sāsravakarmaprahāṇāyānāsravakarmasaṃśrayaṇāt karmaivaiṣāṃ pratisaraṇaṃ bhavatīti //
body.translated_text: Karma is their own — these are the owners of their karma. How then does karma become their own? By virtue of experiencing the results of karma made by oneself — for that alone is called 'one's own' which is not shared with others. They are heirs to karma — these are the heirs of karma. How is one an heir of karma?

body.text: yaduktamacintyaḥ sattvānāṃ karmavipāka iti na sarvaiḥ prakāraiḥ [a] sāvacintyo veditavyaḥ / kathaṃ tarhi cintyaḥ kathamacintyaḥ /
body.translated_text: As it is said, 'The <s>karmavipāka</s> (maturation of karma) of beings is inconceivable' — this should not be understood as inconceivable in every respect. In what way then is it conceivable, and in what way inconceivable?

body.text: kuśalākuśalasyeṣṭāniṣṭo vipākaḥ sugatidurgatyoriti cintyaḥ, śakyatvāt samyagdṛṣṭyādiguṇāvāhanācca / anena karmaṇā sattvānāmātmabhāvasya varṇasaṃsthānādiprakārabhedavaicitryamityacintyaḥ, aśakyatvāt sarvajñādanyasyonmādādidoṣābāhanācca / tadeva karmasthānādibhiracintyam / [tatra sthānaṃ] yatra pradeśe sthitvā yatkarma kṛtvā grāme vā nagare vetyādi / vastu yadadhiṣṭhānaṃ sattvasaṃkhyātamasattvasaṃkhyātaṃ vā / hetuḥ kuśalākuśalādeḥ kuśalākuśalamūlāniyathāyogam / vipākastadevātmabhāvavaicitryam / bāhyabhāvavaicitryābhinirvartakaṃ karmācintyam, kīdṛśena khalu karmaṇā kaṇṭakādīnāṃ taikṣṇādikaṃ kṛtamiti lokacintā nantarbhūtatvāt / maṇimantrauṣadhimuṣṭiyogapratisaṃyuktaṃ karmācintyam / tatra maṇi[prati]saṃyuktaṃ candrakāntādīnāmudakakṣaraṇādi / mantrapratisaṃyuktaṃ tadabhimantritānāmadāhādi / auṣadhipratisaṃyuktaṃ tayā gṛhītayānturdhātādi / muṣṭiyogapratisaṃyuktaṃ tena tena muṣṭiyogena jvarāpagamādi / sarva ca yogināṃ prabhāvakarmācintyam / katham / te cittaprabhāvena mahāpṛthivī kampayantyākāśena votpatantītyevamādi / bodhisattvānāṃ vaśitābhiryat kriyate karma tadacintyam / tadyathā āyurvaśitayā bodhisattvā āyuḥsaṃskārānadhiṣṭhā ya yāvadicchanti tiṣṭhanti / cittavaśitayā yathecchaṃ samādhīn samāpadyante pariṣkāravaśitayāprameyamanardheyamupakaraṇavarṣa sattvānāṃ varṣanti / karmavaśitayānyadhātu bhūmigatiyonyavasthāvedanīyāni karmāṇyanyathā pariṇāmayanti / upapattivaśitayā dhyānairapi vihṛtyāparihīṇā eva kāmadhātāvupapadyante / adhimuktivaśitayā pṛthavyādīnavāditvenādhimucyante / praṇidhānavaśitayā yatheṣṭaṃ svaparārthasaṃpattikarāṇyasaṃkhyeyāni mahāpraṇidhānānyabhinirha[ra]nti / ṛddhivaśitayā sattvānāmāvaja nārthamaprameyamṛddhipratihārya saṃdarśa[ya]nti / jñānavaśitayā dharmārthaniruktipratibhānānāṃ prakarṣaparyantaṃ gacchanti / dharmavaśitayā yathārhaṃ yāvat sarvasatvānāmanyānyairnāmapadavyaṃjanakāryaḥ sūtrādīn dharmān vyavasthāpya yugapaccittaparitoṣaṇe samarthā bhavantīti //
body.translated_text: That the maturation of wholesome and unwholesome karma is desirable and undesirable in the happy and miserable destinies, respectively — this is conceivable, because it is possible and because it brings about qualities such as right view and the rest. That through this karma there is the diversity of varieties such as color, shape, and so forth in the personal existence of beings — this is inconceivable, because it is impossible for anyone other than an omniscient one, and because it would bring about faults such as madness and the rest. That very karma is inconceivable with respect to place and the rest. Place is the location where, while situated, one performs a karma — in a village, a city, and so forth. Object is the basis, whether a sentient being or non-sentient being. Cause is the unwholesome and wholesome roots of the wholesome and unwholesome, as appropriate. Maturation is that very diversity of personal existence. Karma that produces the diversity of external existence is inconceivable — for the worldly reflection 'by what kind of karma was the sharpness of thorns and the rest produced?' is not included within its scope. Karma connected with gems, mantras, medicines, and magical techniques is inconceivable. Among these, that connected with gems is the flowing of water and the like from moonstones and the rest. That connected with mantras is the non-burning and the like of things consecrated by them. That connected with medicines is the becoming invisible and the like when one takes them. That connected with magical techniques is the removal of fever and the like through various techniques. And all the power-karma of <s>yogins</s> is inconceivable. How? Through the power of mind they cause the great earth to tremble, or they fly through space, and so forth. The karma accomplished through the masteries of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is inconceivable. For example, through mastery over lifespan, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> sustain the life-formations and remain as long as they wish. Through mastery over mind, they enter <s>samādhis</s> at will. Through mastery over requisites, they rain down immeasurable and priceless provisions upon beings. Through mastery over karma, they transform karmas that would ripen in other realms, levels, destinies, births, and states so that they ripen differently. Through mastery over birth, even while dwelling in the <s>dhyānas</s>, they take rebirth in the desire realm without any decline. Through mastery over aspiration, they resolve earth and the rest to be water and the rest. Through mastery over vows, they bring forth innumerable great vows that accomplish the welfare of self and others as they wish. Through mastery over miraculous powers, they display immeasurable miraculous feats for the purpose of inspiring beings. Through mastery over knowledge, they reach the ultimate perfection of <s>dharma</s>, meaning, etymology, and eloquence. Through mastery over <s>dharma</s>, they establish the <s>dharma</s> teachings such as <s>sūtras</s> and the rest through various names, words, and syllables, as appropriate for all beings —

body.text: buddhānāṃ buddhakṛtyānuṣṭhānakarmācintyam / katham / anābhogapratigatā dharmadhātvekarasatāprāptā sarve buddhā bhagavantaḥ sattvānāṃ yathā yadā yāvatkṛtyamanuṣṭhātavyaṃ tatsarvamanutiṣṭhanti evaṃ buddhānāṃ buddhaviṣayo 'cintyaḥ //
body.translated_text: The karma of <s>Buddhas</s> in accomplishing Buddha-activities is inconceivable. How? All <s>Buddhas Bhagavāns</s>, having attained the effortless functioning and the single taste of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, accomplish everything that needs to be done for beings — however, whenever, and to whatever extent. Thus the domain of <s>Buddhas</s> is inconceivable.

body.text: punarbhavasya vāsanāyā āhārakaṃ kāraṇamiti hetuḥ / upacitavāsanānāṃ sattvanāṃ devādisatvanikāye tadākṛtiprakṛtisādṛśyena samasyodayasya kāraṇamiti samudayam / pratyātmaṃsaṃtānanaiyabhyena gatiyonyādisarvaprakāraiḥ prakarṣeṇa yāvadbhavāgragatasyodbhavasya kāraṇamiti prabhavaḥ / apūrvasyānyasyātmabhāvasya prāptau pūrvātmabhāvātyayena kāraṇamiti pratyayaḥ //
body.translated_text: The cause that nourishes the imprint of future existence is the <s>hetu</s> (cause). The cause of beings with accumulated imprints arising together in a class of beings such as <s>devas</s> and the rest, through similarity in their form and nature, is the <s>samudaya</s> (origin). The cause of arising, with respect to one's own continuum in its natural course, through all the varieties of destiny, birth, and the rest, up to the peak of existence, is the <s>prabhava</s> (production). The cause of a new, different personal existence —

body.text: saṃskārāṇāmuparamātsa nirodho 'nyaḥ syāttadasaṃvadhyamāno 'rthāntarabhūtaḥ syāt / athānanyaḥ syātsaṃkleśalakṣaṇaḥ syāt / ata eva nobhayo nānubhayaśca / prapañcaḥ punarasminnarthe 'yoniśaścintyetyamārgeṇānyāyenānayena cintyetyarthaḥ, anyathā cintayitavye 'nyathācintanā[t] / kathaṃ punaścintyaḥ / śāntaḥ praṇīta ityevamādibhiḥ prakāraiḥ //
body.translated_text: If there were cessation from the ceasing of the <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) as something other, then being non-increasing it would be a different entity. But if it were not other, it would have the character of defilement. Therefore, it is neither both nor neither. Conceptual elaboration regarding this matter is 'thinking unmethodically' — meaning thinking by wrong path, by wrong method, and by wrong approach, for it is thinking otherwise about what should be thought otherwise. How then should one think about it? Peacefully —

body.text: niralaṃkāraḥ prajñāviktānāṃ vidyādivaiśeṣikaguṇālaṃkārābhāvāt //
body.translated_text: 'Without ornament' — because those who are separated from wisdom lack the ornamental qualities of learning and other distinctive virtues.

body.text: paryāyato 'śeṣaprahāṇamityuddeśaḥ, śeṣo nirdeśaḥ / ata eva tatpariśiṣṭāni padānyupādāyetyucyate, taistasya nirdeśāt / kathaṃ kṛtvāśeṣa prahāṇam / paryavasthānānuśayaprahāṇāt / tatra pratiniḥsargaḥ paryavasthānaprahāṇamadhikṛtya, utpannasya parivarjanāt / vyantībhāvo 'nuśayaprahāṇam, mūlābhāve 'tyantamanutpādāt / tatpunardarśanabhāvanāmārgapratipakṣabhedāddvidhā vyavasthāpyate - kṣayo virāga iti / tatra darśanamārgeṇa virāgatāmadhikṛtya kṣayaḥ, alpamātrāvaśiṣṭatvāt kleśarāśeḥ / bhāvanāmārgeṇa virāgaḥ, tasya bhūmivairāgyagamanapravibhāvitatvāt / tadubhayavisaṃyoge punaḥ satyāyatyāṃ ca duḥkhaṃ nirudhyate, anutpattidharmatāpādanāt / dṛṣṭe ca dharme daurmanasyaṃ vyupaśāmyati, asamudācārāt / atastatphalabhūtasya duḥkhasya prahāṇamadhikṛtyāha - nirodho vyupaśama iti / pūrvakarma kleśasamudāgatānāṃ tu sattvānāṃ svarasenaivoparama[ma]dhikṛtyāha - astaṃgama iti / evaṃ kṛtvāśeṣaprahāṇaṃ nirdiṣṭaṃ veditavyam //
body.translated_text: 'Complete abandonment by way of synonyms' — this is the summary; the rest is the exposition. Therefore it is said 'taking up the remaining terms,' because the exposition is by means of those terms. How is the abandonment complete? Through the abandonment of both manifest defilements and latent tendencies. Among these, <s>pratiniḥsarga</s> (relinquishment) pertains to the abandonment of manifest defilements, because it involves the avoidance of what has arisen. <s>Vyantībhāva</s> (disappearance) is the abandonment of latent tendencies, because in the absence of the root there is ultimate —

body.text: asaṃskṛtamutpādavyayasthityanyathātvābhāvātsaṃskṛtaviparyayeṇa / durdṛśamāryasyaivaikasya prajñā cakṣuṣo gocaratvāt / acalaṃ narakādigatyasaṃcāreṇa sthiratvāt / anataṃ kāmarūpārūpyatṛṣṇābhāvena bhaveṣvanamanāt / amṛtaṃ maraṇāśrayaskandhābhāvāt / anāsravamāsravābhāvāt / layanaṃ vimukti prītisukhasaṃniśrayatvāt / dvīpaṃ saṃsāramahārṇave sthalabhūtatvāt / trāṇaṃ tatprāptau jātyādisarvopadravāpagamanāt / śaraṇaṃ tatkṛtāśayaprayogayoravandhatvasya padasthānatayāśrayaṇī[ya]tvāt / parāyaṇaṃ paramasyāryatvasyāgamanāya padasthānatvādārhatyatvaprāptyupāyālaṃbanatvādityarthaḥ / acyutam[a]jātatvena bhraṃsāsaṃbhavāt / nirjvaraṃ sarvecchāvighātasaṃtāpābhāvāt / niṣparidāhaṃ śokādisarvaparidāhapratiprasrabdhyā śītalatvāt / kṣemaṃ vyādhijarāmaraṇabhayarahitārya vihārāśrayatvāt / śivaṃ sarvakuśaladharmāśrayatvāt / sauvarṇakaṃ lokottarasukhavastutvā[t] / svastyayanaṃ sukhena prayogeṇa tatpprāptaye ālaṃbanabhavāt / ārogyaṃ kleśādyāvaraṇarogarahitatvāt / āniñjyaṃ sarvaviṣayaprapañcavikṣeparahitatvāt / nirvāṇaṃ rūpādisaṃjñāpaga[ma]sya śāntasukhavihārasyālaṃbanatvāt //
body.translated_text: The unconditioned — because of the absence of arising, cessation, abiding, and alteration, it is the opposite of the conditioned. Difficult to see — because it is the domain only of the wisdom-eye of a single <s>Ārya</s> (noble one). Immovable — because it is stable through not transmigrating in the destinies such as the hells and the rest. Unbent — because it does not incline toward existences through the absence of craving for the desire realm, form realm, and formless realm. Deathless — because of the absence of the aggregates that are the basis of death. Without outflows — because of the absence of outflows. A place of rest — because of the experience of the bliss of liberation —

body.text: punarnirodhasatyamārabhyājātādayaḥ paryāyāḥ duḥkhalakṣaṇaviparyayārthena veditavyāḥ / dukhaṃ hi tatra tatra sattvanikāye pratisaṃdhibandhena jāyate / tata uttarakālamātmabhāvaparipūryā vardhate / tacca duḥkhaṃ pūrvakarmakleśāvedhena kṛtam / tacca vartamānaṃ duḥkhaṃ karmakleśānāṃ cānyabhavasaṃskaraṇe padasthānaṃ bhavati / tato 'vyucchedayogena punarbhavasya saṃtatyutpādo bhavati / atastadviparyayeṇa duḥkhanirodha āryasatyaṃ yathākramamajātamabhūtamakṛtamasamutpannaṃ veditavyam /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, beginning from the truth of cessation, the synonyms starting with 'unborn' and the rest should be understood in the sense of the opposite of the characteristics of suffering. For suffering is born through the bond of rebirth-connection in each class of beings. Thereafter, it grows through the full development of the personal existence. And that suffering is produced through the penetration of former karma and defilements. And that present suffering, in producing the formations of another existence through karma and defilements —

body.text: api khalu nirodhasatyamadhikṛtya / śāntalakṣaṇaṃ
body.translated_text: Moreover, with reference to the truth of cessation, the characteristic of peace

body.text: saṃskāraduḥkhatayāpraśāntalakṣaṇānāmupādānaskandhānāṃ visaṃyogamadhikṛtya / praṇītalakṣaṇaṃ kleśaduḥkhavisaṃyogāt svayaṃ śucisukhasvabhāvatāmadhikṛtya / niḥsaraṇalakṣaṇaṃ nityahitasvabhāvatāmadhikṛtya, apunarāvartanāt kṣematvācca yathākramaṃ hitaṃ kuśalamiti śakyatvāt //
body.translated_text: pertains to the separation from the aggregates of clinging whose character is unpeaceful due to <s>saṃskāraduḥkhatā</s> (the suffering of conditioned existence). The characteristic of excellence pertains to its own nature of purity and bliss through separation from the suffering of defilements. The characteristic of escape pertains to its nature of eternal welfare — respectively, because of non-return and because of security, inasmuch as 'welfare' can mean 'wholesome.'

body.text: mārgasatyaṃ yena dukhaṃ parijānīta ityevamādi, satyeṣvasya kṛtyādhikāreṇa lakṣaṇanirdeśo veditavyaḥ / pañcavidho mārga iti prabhedādhikāreṇa / pañcaprabhedaḥ saparivāramārgasatyādhikārādveditavyam //
body.translated_text: The truth of the path — 'by which suffering is fully known' and so forth — the exposition of its characteristics should be understood with reference to its function regarding the truths. 'The path is fivefold' — this is with reference to its classification. The fivefold classification should be understood with reference to the truth of the path together with its accompaniments.

body.text: tatra saṃbhāramārgaḥ śīlādiko yasya paripūrṇatvāduṣmagatādyānupūrvyā satyadarśanāya tadāvaraṇaprahāṇāya ca saṃtānasya yogyatāṃ pratilabhata iti / yadvā punaranyadaupaniṣadaṃ kuśalamityavipratisārādikaṃ veditavyam //
body.translated_text: Among these, the <s>saṃbhāramārga</s> (path of accumulation) is morality and the rest, by the completion of which, through the sequence of the heat stage and the rest, the continuum attains the capacity for seeing the truths and for abandoning their obscurations. Or alternatively, the other preparatory wholesome, namely freedom from remorse and the rest, should be understood.

body.text: uṣmagataṃ pratyātmaṃ satyeṣvālokalabdhaḥ samādhiḥ prajñā sasaṃyoga iti samāhitena cittena satyādhipateyasya sūtrādikasya dharmasya manojalpasya mukhairarthasaṃprakhyāne sati śamathaśca vipaśyanā coṣmagatamiti veditavyam // tadvṛddhirmūrdhānastadupari vyavasthāpanārthena / kṣāntirekadeśapraviṣṭānusṛtaḥ samādhiriti / kathamekadeśapraviṣṭo bhavati / ekāntena grāhyabhāvalakṣaṇāt / kathamekadeśānumṛtaḥ grāhakābhāvaprativedhānukūlyāvasthānāt / laukiko 'gradharmo yadantaramādito lokottaro mārgaḥ //
body.translated_text: The <s>uṣmagata</s> (heat stage) should be understood as the <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) and <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) together with their associates, through which one obtains a glimpse of the truths within oneself — that is, when there is the discernment of meaning through the channels of the <s>sūtra</s> and other <s>dharma</s> teachings that are governed by the truths, through mental discourse, with a concentrated mind, then both <s>śamatha</s> (calm) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) constitute the heat stage. Its increase is the <s>mūrdhānas</s> (summit), for the purpose of establishing what is above that. <s>Kṣānti</s> (patience) — having partially entered and followed —

body.text: darśanamārgo laukikāgradharmānantaraṃ nirvikalpaśamathavipaśyanālakṣaṇo veditavyaḥ / samasamālaṃbyālaṃbanajñānamapi taditi tena grāhya grāhakābhāvatathatāprativeghāt / pratyātmamapanīta sattvasaṃketadharmasaṃketa sarvato 'panītobhayasaṃketālaṃbanadharmajñānamapi taditi / kathaṃ pratyātmamapanītasattvasaṃketālaṃbanadharmajñānam / tena sva[sa]ntāne ātmanimittāvikalpanāt / kathaṃ pratyātmamapanītadharmasaṃketālaṃbanadharmajñānam / tena svasaṃtāna eva rūpādidharmanimittāvikalpanāt / kathaṃ sarvato 'panītobhayasaṃketālaṃbanadharmajñānam / sarvatrāviśeṣeṇātma dharmanimittāvikalpa[nā]diti //
body.translated_text: The <s>darśanamārga</s> (path of seeing) should be understood as having the character of non-conceptual <s>śamatha</s> and <s>vipaśyanā</s>, immediately following the supreme mundane <s>dharmas</s>. The knowledge that apprehends its object in equal and even manner is also that, because it penetrates the <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) of the absence of apprehender and apprehended. The knowledge of <s>dharmas</s> whose object-support has removed the conventions of beings within oneself, and has completely removed both conventions from all directions — is also that. How does one remove the convention of beings within oneself?

body.text: prabhedaśaḥ punardarśanamārgaḥ satyeṣu ṣoḍaśadharmānvayakṣāntijñānāni / tatra duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣāntiḥ prayogamārge duḥkhasatyādhikārikasūtrādidharmavicāraṇājñānaṃ yoniśo manaskārasaṃgṛhītamadhipati kṛtvā svasaṃtānikaduḥkhasatye tattathatāpratyakṣānubhāvino lokottarā prajñā samyagdṛṣṭisvabhāvotpadyate yayā duḥkhadarśanaprahātavyāṃstraidhātukānaṣṭāviṃśatimanuśayān prajahāti / tasmāducyate duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣāntiriti / tayā kṣāntyā duḥkhadarśanaprahātavyakleśaprahāṇāt parivartita āśraye tadanantaraṃ yena jñānena tāmāśrayaparivṛtti pratyanubhavati tadduḥkhe dharmajñānamityucyate / etaccobhayamādyaṃ kṣāntijñānamanvayaḥ sarveṣāṃ śaikṣāśaikṣāṇāmāryadharmāṇām, tatasteṣāṃ samudāgamāt / atastadālaṃbyānvaya eṣa āryadharmāṇāmiti pratyātmaṃ pratyakṣānubhāvinyanāsravā prajñā duḥkhe anvayajñānakṣānti / tāmanvayajñānakṣāntiṃ yena jñānena pratyanubhavati tadanvayajñānamityucyate / lokottarasya hi mārgasya dvayaṃ viṣayaḥ - tathatā samyagjñānaṃ ca / tatra dharmajñānapakṣasya mārgasya tathatā viṣayaḥ / anvayajñānapakṣasya samyagjñānam / ata idamucyate - dharmajñānakṣāntijñānairgrāhyāvabodhaḥ, anvayakṣāntijñānairgrāhakāvabodha iti / yo bhagavatā ṣaṣṭho '[ni]mittavihārī pudgala ākhyātaḥ sa eteṣu kṣāntijñāneṣu vartamāno veditavyaḥ, sarvanimittānupalaṃbhāt / ta ete kṣānti[jñāna]saṃgṛhītāḥ ṣoḍaśa cittakṣaṇā darśanamārgaḥ, tairadṛṣṭapūrvāṇāmāryasa tyānāṃ pratyekaṃ caturbhirdarśanāt / na cātra bhāvasyābhatvā prādurbhāvamātraṃ cittakṣaṇo veditavyaḥ / kiṃ tarhi yāvatā jñeye jñānātpatteḥ parisamāptirbhavati / tadyathā duḥkhaṃ parijñeyamityekaścittalakṣaṇaḥ / evaṃ samudayaḥ prahātavya ityevamādiḥ / yaccaitaddarśanamārgamārabhya vistareṇa vipaṃcittaṃ vyavasthānamātraṃ tatsarvaṃ veditavyam, pratyātmameva vedanīyatvāt lokottarāyā avasthāyāḥ //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the path of seeing in its classifications consists of sixteen <s>dharma</s>-patience-knowledges and <s>anvaya</s>-patience-knowledges regarding the truths. Among these, the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge-patience regarding suffering — when in the preparatory path, the investigation of <s>sūtra</s> and other <s>dharma</s> teachings pertaining to the truth of suffering, being comprised in methodical attention and taken as dominant, gives rise to the supramundane <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) having the nature of right view, which directly experiences the <s>tathatā</s> of the truth of suffering within one's own continuum —

body.text: sarvaṃ hi mārgasatyaṃ caturbhiḥ prakārairanugantavyam - vyavasthānato vikalpanato 'nubhavataḥ paripūritaśca / tatra vyavasthānata, yathāsvamadhigamaniṣṭhāprāptā śrāvakādayastatpṛṣṭhalabdhena jñānena pareṣāṃ prāpaṇanimittaṃ nāmapadavyañjanakāyaiḥ mārgasatyaṃ vyavasthāpayanti, ityapi satyeṣu kṣāntayo jñānānī tyevamādi / vikalpanataḥ, abhisamayaprayuktā laukikena yathāvyavasthānaṃ vikalpayato yadabhyasya nti / anubhavataḥ, tathābhyasyanto yāmādito
body.translated_text: For indeed, the entire truth of the path (<s>mārgasatya</s>) is to be pursued in four ways — through establishment, through conceptualization, through experience, and through completion. Therein, through establishment: <s>Śrāvakas</s> and others who have reached the culmination of their respective attainments, by means of the knowledge subsequently obtained, establish the truth of the path through collections of names, sentences, and syllables for the purpose of leading others to attainment — such as 'in the truths there are acceptances (<s>kṣānti</s>) and knowledges (<s>jñāna</s>)' and so forth. Through conceptualization: those engaged in penetration (<s>abhisamaya</s>) conceptualize in accordance with the established [teaching] through worldly [understanding], which they practice. Through experience: thus practicing, from the first watch onward

body.text: darśanamārgākhyāṃ lokottarāṃ niṣprapañcāvasthāṃ pratyātmamanubhavanti paripūritaḥ tadūrdhva yāmāśrayaparivṛttiṃ paripūrya [yā]vadadhigamaniṣṭhāṃ prāpnuvanti / te punaradhigamaniṣṭhāprāptāstatpṛṣṭhalabdhena jñānena mārgasatyaṃ vyavasthāpayanti / ityevamādi tacca[tu]rākāraṃ mārgacakraṃ punaḥ punaranyonyāśrayeṇa pravartata iti veditavyam //
body.translated_text: they personally experience the supramundane state free from conceptual elaboration called the path of seeing (<s>darśanamārga</s>). Through completion: thereafter, having completed the transformation of the basis through the watches [of the night], they reach the culmination of attainment. Those again, having reached the culmination of attainment, establish the truth of the path by means of the knowledge subsequently obtained. And so forth — this four-aspected wheel of the path should be understood as turning again and again in mutual dependence.

body.text: yaduktaṃ virajo vigatamalaṃ dharmeṣu dharmacakṣurutpadyata iti taddarśanamārgamadhikṛtyoktam, tatprathamataḥ satyeṣvāryaprajñācakṣuḥsvabhāvatvāt / tatra dharmakṣāntibhirvirajaḥ, tābhiḥ kleśarajaḥprahāṇāt / dharmajñānairvigatamalam, teṣāṃ prahāṇatadāvaraṇamalāśrayotpādāt / punaranayoreva kṣāntijñānāvasthayoryathākramaṃ parijñayā prahāṇena ca mārgasya viśuddhatāmadhikṛtya virajo vigatamalaṃ veditavyam //
body.translated_text: The statement 'the <s>dharmacakṣus</s> (eye of dharma) arises in regard to <s>dharmas</s>, free from dust and free from stain' was said with reference to the path of seeing (<s>darśanamārga</s>), because it is first among the truths and has the nature of the noble wisdom-eye (<s>āryaprajñācakṣus</s>). Therein, 'free from dust' is through the <s>dharmakṣāntis</s> (dharma-acceptances), because through them the dust of afflictions is abandoned. 'Free from stain' is through the <s>dharmajñānas</s> (dharma-knowledges), because through them there arises the basis that removes the stain of the obstruction of what has been abandoned. Furthermore, with reference to these very two states of acceptance and knowledge, 'free from dust' and 'free from stain' should be understood as the purity of the path through full understanding (<s>parijñā</s>) and abandonment (<s>prahāṇa</s>), respectively.

body.text: dṛṣṭetyevamādyāpi darśanamārgamevādhikṛtya veditavyam, vineyānāṃ satyābhisamayānantaraṃ vacanāt / tatra dharmakṣāntibhirdṛṣṭadharmāḥ, tābhistattvaprativedhāt / dharmajñānaiḥ prāptadharmāḥ, tairāśrayaparivṛttisākṣātkaraṇāt / anvayakṣāntibhirviditadharmāḥ, tābhirāryadharmānvaya eṣa iti tadubhayasaṃvedanāt / anvayajñānaiḥ paryavagāḍhadharmāḥ, tairyāvajjñeyaṃ parisamāpanāt / sarvaistīrṇakāṃkṣaḥ sarvaiḥ kṣāntijñānaiḥ, lokottareṇa mārgeṇa phalādhigame sati dīrgharātramabhikāṃkṣite svādhigame 'saṃdehāt / tīrṇavicikitsaḥ paridhigame sarvairiti vartate, parādhigame tadavasthasyānyeṣāmapi viśeṣādhigamaṃ prati vimatyabhāvāt / aparapratyayo mārgabhāvanāyāṃ paropadeśamantareṇāpi svayaṃkuśalatvāt / ananyaneyo 'vetya prasādapratilabhena śāstuḥ śāsane 'nyatīrthyairjanmāntare 'pyahāryatvāt / dharmeṣu vaiśāradyaprāpto 'dhigamamārabhya paripraśnadharmeṣu pāpecchābhimānikavadavalīnacittatābhāvāt //
body.translated_text: 'Having seen [the <s>dharmas</s>]' and so forth should also be understood with reference to the path of seeing alone, being the statement immediately following the penetration of the truths by those to be trained. Therein, through the <s>dharmakṣāntis</s> (dharma-acceptances), they have 'seen the <s>dharmas</s>,' because through them reality is penetrated. Through the <s>dharmajñānas</s> (dharma-knowledges), they have 'attained the <s>dharmas</s>,' because through them the transformation of the basis is directly realized. Through the <s>anvayakṣāntis</s> (subsequent acceptances), they have 'understood the <s>dharmas</s>,' because through them they recognize that 'this is the conformity with the noble <s>dharmas</s>' — sensing both [acceptance and knowledge]. Through the <s>anvayajñānas</s> (subsequent knowledges), they have 'penetrated deeply into the <s>dharmas</s>,' because through them what is to be known is completed. 'One whose doubts have been crossed' — through all acceptances and knowledges, because when the fruit is attained through the supramundane path, there is no doubt regarding one's own attainment that has been longed for over a long time. 'One whose hesitation has been crossed' applies to the attainment of others — because in knowing others' attainment, for one in that state there is no uncertainty about the superior attainment of others as well. 'Not dependent on another' — because in the cultivation of the path, even without the instruction of others, one is capable by oneself. 'Not to be led by another' — because, having gained the clarity of understanding based on evidence regarding the <s>Śāstā</s>'s (Teacher's) teaching, one cannot be led astray even in another birth by other sectarians. 'One who has attained confidence in <s>dharmas</s>' — because from the time of attainment onward, regarding <s>dharmas</s> pertaining to inquiry, there is no cowering of mind like that of the wishing-for-evil and the conceited.

body.text: bhāvanāmārgo laukiko mārgaḥ / tatra laukiko mārgo dhyānā[nyā]rūpyāśca /
body.translated_text: The cultivation path (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>) is the mundane path. Therein, the mundane path consists of the <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations) and the formless attainments (<s>ārūpyas</s>).

body.text: te punardhyānārūpyāḥ saṃkleśato vyavadānato vyavasthānato viśuddhitaśca veditavyāḥ //
body.translated_text: Those <s>dhyānas</s> and formless attainments should be understood from the standpoint of defilement, purification, arrangement, and purity.

body.text: kathaṃ saṃkleśataḥ / catvāryavyākṛtamūlāni tṛṣṇā dṛṣṭirmāno 'vidyā ca, taiḥ saṃkliṣṭacittānāṃ kliṣṭadhyānamukhena rūpārūpyāvacarasarvanivṛtāvyākṛtakleśopakleśāvartanāt / tatra tṛṣṇayāsvādasaṃkleśena saṃkliśyate, prasrabdhisukhāsvādāt / dṛṣṭyā dṛṣṭyuttaradhyāyitayā saṃkliśyate, dhyānaṃ niścitya pūrvāntakalpādidṛṣṭisamutthāpanāt / mānena mānottara dhyāyitayā saṃkliśyate, tena viśeṣādhigamenonnatigamanāt / avidyayā vicikitsottaradhyāyitayā saṃkliśyate, tattvā prativedhena mokṣakāmasya tasminviśeṣādhigame mokṣo na mokṣa iti vicikitsotpādanāt //
body.translated_text: How from the standpoint of defilement? The four indeterminate roots are craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>), views (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>), pride (<s>māna</s>), and ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>). Through these, for those with defiled minds, all the obstructed-indeterminate afflictions and secondary afflictions of the form and formless realms revolve through the gateway of defiled meditation. Therein, through craving, one becomes defiled by the defilement of savoring (<s>āsvāda</s>) — from savoring the bliss of tranquility (<s>prasrabdhisukha</s>). Through views, one becomes defiled by meditating based on [wrong] views — because having relied on meditation, one generates views such as those about the past and so forth. Through pride, one becomes defiled by meditating based on pride — because through that superior attainment, one becomes elevated. Through ignorance, one becomes defiled by meditating based on doubt — because for one who desires liberation, without penetrating reality, doubt arises regarding that superior attainment: 'Is this liberation or not?'

body.text: kathaṃ vyavadānataḥ / śuddhakā dhyānārūpyā laukikā api kuśalatvātparyavasthānamalāpagatatvena vyavadātā ityucyante //
body.translated_text: How from the standpoint of purification? The pure <s>dhyānas</s> and formless attainments, even though mundane, are called 'purified' because they are wholesome and free from the stain of manifest afflictions (<s>paryavasthāna</s>).

body.text: kathaṃ vyavasthānataḥ / dhyānānāṃ tāvaccaturdhā vyavasthānam, aṅgasamāpattimātrāsaṃjñākaraṇabhedāt / ārūpyāṇāṃ tridhāṅgavarjaiḥ //
body.translated_text: How from the standpoint of arrangement? The arrangement of the <s>dhyānas</s> is fourfold — due to the distinction of limbs, attainment, mere [perception], and the making of non-perception. That of the formless attainments is threefold — by the same factors excluding limbs.

body.text: kiṃ punaradhikṛtya dhyāneṣu / vitarkādaya evāṅgatvena vyavasthāpitāḥ satsvanyeṣu dharmeṣu / tāvadbhiḥ pratipakṣānuśaṃsatadubhayāśrayāṅgaparisamāpteḥ / prathame tāvaddhyāne vitarko vicāraśca pratipakṣāṅgam, tābhyāṃ kāmavyāpādavihiṃsāvitarkādiprahāṇāt / prītiḥ sukhaṃ cānuśaṃsāṅgam, vitarkavicārābhyāṃ pratipakṣite vipakṣe tadvivekajaprītisukhalābhāt / cittaikāgratā tadubhayaniśrayāṅgam, samādhisaṃniśrayabalena vitarkādipravṛtteriti / tathā dvitīye dhyāne 'dhyātmasaṃprasādaḥ pratipakṣāṅgam, tena vitarkavicārapratipakṣaṇāt / prītisukhe cittaikāgratā ca śeṣe aṅge pūrvavat / tṛtīye dhyāne upekṣā smṛtiḥ saṃprajanyaśca pratipakṣāṅgam, taiḥ prītipratipakṣaṇāt / sukhaṃ cittaikāgratā ca śeṣe aṅge
body.translated_text: For what purpose, moreover, are investigation (<s>vitarka</s>) and the rest established as limbs in the <s>dhyānas</s>, when other <s>dharmas</s> also exist? Because the completion of limbs — as antidote-limbs, benefit-limbs, and basis-of-both-limbs — is accomplished by just that many. In the first <s>dhyāna</s>, <s>vitarka</s> (investigation) and <s>vicāra</s> (examination) are the antidote-limbs, because through them the investigation of desire, malice, harm, and so forth is abandoned. Joy (<s>prīti</s>) and bliss (<s>sukha</s>) are the benefit-limbs, because when the opposing [factors] have been counteracted by <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s>, one obtains the joy and bliss born of seclusion. One-pointedness of mind (<s>cittaikāgratā</s>) is the basis-of-both-limb, because it is through the power of the support of <s>samādhi</s> that the functioning of investigation and so forth occurs. Likewise, in the second <s>dhyāna</s>, inner clarity (<s>adhyātmasaṃprasāda</s>) is the antidote-limb, because it counteracts <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s>. Joy, bliss, and one-pointedness of mind are the remaining limbs as before. In the third <s>dhyāna</s>, equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>), mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>), and clear comprehension (<s>saṃprajanya</s>) are the antidote-limbs, because they counteract joy (<s>prīti</s>). Bliss and one-pointedness of mind are the remaining limbs

body.text: yathākramam / caturthe dhyāne upekṣāpariśuddhiḥ smṛtipariśuddhiśca pratipakṣāṅgam, tābhyāṃ sukhapratipakṣaṇāt / aduḥkhāsukhā vedanānuśaṃsāṅgam / cittaikāgratā tadubhayāṅgamiti //
body.translated_text: respectively. In the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, purity of equanimity (<s>upekṣāpariśuddhi</s>) and purity of mindfulness (<s>smṛtipariśuddhi</s>) are the antidote-limbs, because through them bliss is counteracted. Neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling is the benefit-limb. One-pointedness of mind is the basis-of-both-limb.

body.text: kathaṃ punaḥ prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ samāpadyamānasya sapta manaskārā bhavanti / yena samāhitabhūmikena manaskāreṇa kameṣvādīnavādidarśanenaudārikalakṣaṇaṃ pratisavedayate / tadabhāvācca prathamadhyāne śāntalakṣaṇam / ayamucyate lakṣaṇapratisaṃvedanīya manaskāraḥ, sa ca śrutacintāvyavakīrṇo veditavyaḥ / tadūrdhva śrutaṃ cintāṃ cātikramyaikāntena bhāvanākāreṇa tadaudārikaśāntalakṣaṇanimittālaṃbanāṃ śamathavipaśyanāṃ bhāvayan punaḥ punaryathāparyeṣitāmaudārikaśāntatāmadhimucyate ityayamadhimokṣikaḥ / tadabhyāsāttatprathamataḥ prahāṇamārgasahagato manaskāraḥ prāvivekyaḥ, tenādhimātrakleśaprakāraprahāṇāttatpakṣadauṣṭhulyāpagamācca / sa yogī tadūrdhva prahāṇārāmo bhavati prahāṇe 'nuśaṃsadarśī parīttapravivekaprītisukhasaṃspṛṣṭaḥ kālena kālaṃ prasadanīyena manaskāreṇa saṃpraharṣayati yāvadeva styānamiddhauddhatyopaśamāya / ayaṃ ratisaṃgrāhakaḥ / tasyaivaṃ samyakprayuktasya kuśalapakṣaprayogopastabdhatvāt kāmāvacarakleśaparyavasthānāsamudācāre sati tatprahīṇāprahīṇatāvagamārtha tadutpattyanukūlaśubhanimittamanaskāreṇa pratyavekṣaṇaṃ mīmāṃsāmanaskāraḥ / tasyaivaṃ mīmāṃsāpratipakṣaṃ bhāvayataḥ tāvatkālikayogena sarvakāmāvacarakleśavisaṃyogāya prathamadhyānaprayogaparyavasānagataḥ pratipakṣamanaskāraḥ prayoganiṣṭhaḥ / tadanantaraṃ maulaprathamadhyānasahagataḥ prayoganiṣṭhāphala iti / tatra lakṣaṇapratisavedinā prahātavyaṃ prāptavyaṃ ca samyakparijñāya prahāṇāya prāptaye ca cittaṃ praṇighatte / ādhimokṣikena tadartha samyakprayogamārabhate / prāvivekyenādhimātrān kleśān jahāti / ratisaṃgrāhakeṇa madhyaṃ kleśaprakāraṃ jahāti / mīmāṃsakena prāptinirabhimānatāyāṃ cittamavasthāpayati / prayoganiṣṭhena mṛduṃ kleśaprakāraṃ jahāti / prayoganiṣṭhāphalena eṣāṃ manaskārāṇāṃ subhāvitānāṃ bhāvanāphalaṃ pratyanubhavati / yathā prathamadhyānasamāpattaye sapta manaskārā evaṃ yāvannaivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanasamāpattaye yathāyogaṃ yojayitavyāḥ / audārikalakṣaṇaṃ punaḥ sarvāsvadhobhūmiṣu yāvadākiṃcanyāyatanāt samāsena dvividhaṃ veditavyam - duḥkhataravihāritāpraśāntavihāritayā, alpāyuskataratā ca tadviparyayeṇordhvabhūmeḥ śāntalakṣaṇaṃ veditavyam //
body.translated_text: How, then, do the seven mental engagements (<s>manaskāra</s>) occur for one entering the first <s>dhyāna</s>? With a mental engagement belonging to the concentrated level, by seeing the defects and so forth in sensual pleasures, one experiences the coarse characteristic. And because of the absence of that [coarseness] in the first <s>dhyāna</s>, [one experiences] the peaceful characteristic. This is called the mental engagement of experiencing the characteristics (<s>lakṣaṇapratisaṃvedanīya manaskāra</s>), and it should be understood as mixed with learning and reflection. Thereafter, having transcended learning and reflection, by exclusively cultivating <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) with the sign of those coarse and peaceful characteristics as object-support, one repeatedly resolves upon the coarseness and peacefulness as investigated — this is the mental engagement of conviction (<s>ādhimokṣika</s>). Through practice of that, the mental engagement that first accompanies the path of abandonment is the mental engagement of seclusion (<s>prāvivekya</s>), because through it the intense types of afflictions are abandoned and the unsuitability pertaining to that side departs. The <s>yogin</s>, thereafter delighting in abandonment, seeing the benefits in abandonment, touched by the limited joy and bliss of seclusion, from time to time gladdening [the mind] with the mental engagement of delight — this is the mental engagement that gathers joy (<s>ratisaṃgrāhaka</s>), [used] only for the purpose of suppressing torpor, drowsiness, and excitation. When for this one who is thus properly engaged, because of the steadfastness of the engagement in the wholesome side, the manifest afflictions of the desire realm do not occur, in order to ascertain whether they have been abandoned or not, the examination with a mental engagement of the attractive sign conducive to their arising is the mental engagement of investigation (<s>mīmāṃsā manaskāra</s>). When for this one who thus cultivates the antidote through investigation, through temporary practice, the mental engagement at the conclusion of the preparatory practice for complete dispassion from all desire-realm afflictions through the first <s>dhyāna</s> preparatory [stage] is the mental engagement of the final preparatory [practice] (<s>prayoganiṣṭha</s>). Immediately thereafter, [the mental engagement] accompanying the fundamental first <s>dhyāna</s> is the fruit of the final preparatory [practice] (<s>prayoganiṣṭhāphala</s>). Therein, through the mental engagement of experiencing the characteristics, having fully comprehended what is to be abandoned and what is to be attained, one directs the mind toward abandonment and attainment. Through the mental engagement of conviction, one undertakes the proper practice for that purpose. Through the mental engagement of seclusion, one abandons the intense afflictions. Through the mental engagement that gathers joy, one abandons the medium type of afflictions. Through the mental engagement of investigation, one establishes the mind in freedom from conceit regarding attainment. Through the final preparatory mental engagement, one abandons the mild type of afflictions. Through the fruit of the final preparatory practice, one experiences the fruit of cultivation of these well-cultivated mental engagements. Just as [there are] seven mental engagements for the attainment of the first <s>dhyāna</s>, so too up to the attainment of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception should they be applied as appropriate. The coarse characteristic in all lower levels up to the base of nothingness should be understood in summary as twofold — through more painful abiding and more unsettled abiding, and through shorter lifespan; the peaceful characteristic of the higher level should be understood as the opposite of those.

body.text: mātrāvyavasthānaṃ dhyānānāṃ tāvanmṛdumadhyādhimātraparibhāvitatvāt / pratyekaṃ tridhā dhyānopapattiḥ phalaṃ bhavati / tadyathā brahmakāyikā brahmapurohitā mahābrahmāṇaṃ ityevamādi yathāpūrvamuktam / ārūpyeṣu tu vimānasthānāntarasaṃniveśāsaṃbhavādevamupapatti bhedo na vyavasthāpyate / api tu teṣāmapyasti mṛdvādiparibhāvitānāmupapattāvuccanīcatā āyurādiviśeṣeṇa, hīnapraṇītatā ca kliṣṭākliṣṭatābāhulyaviśeṣeṇeti //
body.translated_text: The arrangement by degree of the <s>dhyānas</s> is because each is cultivated as mild, medium, and intense. In each case, the threefold rebirth in the <s>dhyāna</s> [levels] becomes its fruit. For example, the <s>Brahmakāyika</s>, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, and <s>Mahābrahmā</s> [gods] — and so forth as previously stated. In the formless attainments, however, because the occurrence of distinct celestial-mansion locations is not possible, such a distinction of rebirth is not established. But even among them, for those cultivated as mild and so forth, there is a high and low [distinction] in rebirth according to the differences in lifespan and the like, and inferiority and excellence according to the preponderance of afflicted and unafflicted [states].

body.text: saṃjñākaraṇavyavasthānaṃ caturthadhyānaprabhedānāṃ samādhīnāmasaṃkhyeyānyacintyāni ca nāmāni / tathāhi yāvataḥ prathamadhyānasaṃgṛhītān samādhīn buddhā bhagavanto bodhisattvāśca mahāprabhāvaprāptāḥ samāpadyante, teṣāṃ samādhīnāṃ śrāvakāḥ pratyekabuddhāśca nāmānyapi na jānanti / kutaścaiṣāṃ saṃkhyāṃ jñāsyanti samāpatsyante vā / yathā nirdiṣṭaṃ prajñāpāramitāyām - "sādhitaṃ samādhiśatam" / evamanyeṣvapi teṣu teṣu mahāyānasūtreṣviti //
body.translated_text: The arrangement by designation of the subdivisions of the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> — the names of the <s>samādhis</s> are innumerable and inconceivable. For indeed, however many <s>samādhis</s> included in the first <s>dhyāna</s> the <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bhagavāns</s>, and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have attained great power enter, the <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> do not even know the names of those <s>samādhis</s> — how then would they know their number or enter them? As stated in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>: 'a hundred <s>samādhis</s> are accomplished.' Similarly in those various other <s>Mahāyāna sūtras</s>.

body.text: kathaṃ viśuddhitaḥ / prāntakoṭikā dhyānārūpyā viśuddhirityucyate, vaiśeṣikaguṇābhinirhārāya nikāmalā[bhā]dibhiḥ karmaṇyatāprakarṣanayanāt //
body.translated_text: How from the standpoint of purity? The <s>dhyānas</s> and formless attainments at the highest limit are called 'purity,' because through [practices such as] effortless attainment and so forth, the peak of workability (<s>karmaṇyatā</s>) is brought about for the production of superior qualities.

body.text: lokottaramārgo bhāvanāmārge 'ṣṭau duḥkhā[didharmā]nvayajñānāni yathā darśanamārge nirdiṣṭāni / tatsaṃprayuktaśca samādhiranāgamyasaṃgṛhītaḥ prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ yāvadākiṃcanyāyatanam / naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanamaparisphuṭaṃ saṃjñāpracāratayā paramapaṭupracārasyāryamārgasyāsaṃniḥśrayatvādekāntena laukikaṃ veditavyam / ata eva ca tatsaṃjñāmāndyādālambanānimittīkaraṇārthenānimittamityucyate / kutaḥ punaretat jñāyate naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatane āryamārgo nāstīti / yasmāduktaṃ bhagavatā "yāvadeva saṃjñāsamāpattistāvadājñāprativedha" iti / nirodhasamāpattirlokottarā, āryamārgapṛṣṭhalabhyatvāt / manuṣyeṣvabhi[ni]rhriyate utpādyata ādita ityarthaḥ, pūrvotpāditāyāḥ paścātsaṃmukhobhāvo manuṣyeṣu vā tasminneva janmani rūpadhātau vā upapadya / kathamārūpyalābhino rūpadhātuvītarāgasyāryaśrāvakasya rūpadhātāvupapatiḥ / nāvaśyaṃ rūpadhātuvītarāga evārūpyaṃ samāpadyate / ata evātra catuṣkoṭikaṃ bhavati - yo rūpavītarāgaḥ sarvaḥ sa ārūpyaśāntavimokṣasamāpattā, yo
body.translated_text: The supramundane path in the cultivation path (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>) consists of the eight knowledges — <s>dharma</s>-knowledges and subsequent knowledges of suffering and so forth — as indicated in the path of seeing. And the <s>samādhi</s> associated with them includes the preliminary stage (<s>anāgamya</s>), the first <s>dhyāna</s> up to the base of nothingness (<s>ākiṃcanyāyatana</s>). The base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (<s>naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana</s>), because the operation of perception there is unclear, cannot serve as a support for the noble path which operates with utmost acuity — it should be understood as exclusively mundane. And precisely because of the dullness of perception there, it is called 'signless' (<s>ānimitta</s>), for the purpose of preventing the sign-making of the object-support. How then is it known that the noble path does not exist in the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception? Because the <s>Bhagavān</s> stated: 'Only up to the attainment of perception is there penetration to full knowledge.' The attainment of cessation (<s>nirodhasamāpatti</s>) is supramundane, because it is obtained subsequently to the noble path. 'It is produced among humans' means it is generated for the first time — that is the meaning; the subsequent manifestation of what was previously generated [occurs] either among humans in that very birth, or having been reborn in the form realm. How is rebirth in the form realm possible for a noble <s>Śrāvaka</s> who has attained the formless [realm] and is dispassionate toward the form realm? It is not necessarily the case that only one who is dispassionate toward the form realm enters the formless attainment. Therefore, here a fourfold classification (<s>catuṣkoṭika</s>) applies: whoever is dispassionate toward form, all of those [are in] the formless peaceful liberation attainment; and whoever

body.text: vā ārūpyaśāntavimokṣasamāpattā sarvaḥ sa rūpavītarāga iti / prathamā koṭiḥ - anāgamyaṃ niśritya rūpavītarāgaḥ / dvitīyā koṭiḥ - caturthadhyānalābhī ārya āryopapattyānarthī prahāṇamārgaṃ nirākṛtya viśeṣamārgaṃ niśrityārūpyaśāntavimokṣasamāpattā / tṛtīyā koṭiḥ - sa eva vairāgyārthī prahāṇamārgaṃ niśrityārūpyaśāntavimokṣasamāpattā / caturthī - etānākārān sthāpayitvā / ārūpye ṣūpapannānāṃ kasmānna saṃmukhībhavati / śāntena vihāreṇa vihartukāmā āryā manuṣyeṣvenāmabhinirhṛtya saṃmukhīkurvanti / ārūpyeṣu tūpapannāste 'prayatnenaiva vaipākikaiḥ paramaśāntaiḥ vimokṣavihārairviharantītyatastatsaṃmukhīkaraṇārthaṃ na punaḥ prayatnamārabhanta iti //
body.translated_text: is in the formless peaceful liberation attainment, all of those are dispassionate toward form — [this is not the case]. The first alternative: one who is dispassionate toward form based on the preliminary stage (<s>anāgamya</s>) [but has not entered the formless peaceful liberation attainment]. The second alternative: one who has obtained the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, who is a noble one, not desiring noble rebirth, having set aside the path of abandonment and relying on the path of distinction, is in the formless peaceful liberation attainment [but is not dispassionate toward form]. The third alternative: that very one, desiring dispassion, relying on the path of abandonment, is in the formless peaceful liberation attainment [and is also dispassionate toward form]. The fourth: setting aside these configurations. Why does [the attainment of cessation] not become manifest for those reborn in the formless [realm]? Noble ones who wish to abide in the peaceful abiding produce it first among humans and then make it manifest. But those reborn in the formless realms, without any effort, already abide in the supreme peaceful liberation-abiding that is their maturational [result] — therefore, they do not again undertake effort for the purpose of making it manifest.

body.text: mṛdumadhyādhimātro mārgaḥ pratyekaṃ punaḥ mṛdvādibhistribhiḥ prakārairbhittvā navaprakāro vyavasthāpyate, bhāvanā heyānāṃ krameṇa prahāṇajñāpanārtham / kiṃ punaḥ kāraṇaṃ mṛdumṛdunā mārgeṇādhimātraḥ kleśaḥ prahīyate / sa hyatyarthaḥ vipannahrīvyapannāpyālajjinaḥ saṃtāne samudācarati sūpalakṣaścāsau suparicchedastasmādasau sthūlamalavadalpenāpi pratipakṣeṇāpanīyate / yastvayaṃ duṣparicchedasamudācāraḥ sūkṣmalīnaḥ saṃtāne mṛdumṛdukleśaḥ sūkṣmamalavanmahatā pratipakṣabalenāpanīyata ityado vipakṣaprakāraviparyayeṇa pratipakṣaprakāravyavasthānaṃ veditavyam //
body.translated_text: The path is mild, medium, and intense; each again divided by three modes of mild etc., making nine varieties—for the purpose of indicating the sequential abandonment of what is to be abandoned through cultivation (<s>bhāvanāheya</s>). Why is the intense defilement abandoned by the mild-mild path? Because that [intense defilement], being extreme, manifests in the continuum of one whose sense of shame and moral dread have deteriorated; and being easy to discern and easy to define, it is removed like coarse dirt by even a small antidote. But that which is difficult to define in its manifestation, subtle and hidden in the continuum—the mild-mild defilement (<s>kleśa</s>)—is removed like fine dirt only by great antidotal power. Thus the arrangement of antidote-types should be understood as the reverse of the adversary-types.

body.text: prayogamārgo yena mārgeṇa bhāvyamānena pratyekamadhimātrādhimātrādikleśaprakārādijātipakṣasya dauṣṭhulyāṅgasyāpagamātkrameṇāśrayaḥ parivartate sa bhāvanāmārge prayogamārge ityucyate //
body.translated_text: The preparatory path (<s>prayogamārga</s>): that path through the cultivation of which, by the departure of the bad-disposition component belonging to each class of defilement beginning with the intense-intense etc., the basis (<s>āśraya</s>) is gradually transformed—that is called the preparatory path within the path of cultivation (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>).

body.text: yasya tvanantaraṃ tatprakārakleśajātitatpakṣadauṣṭhulyāvaśeṣāpagamāttena dauṣṭhulyena nirdauṭhulya āśrayaḥ parivartate sa ānantaryamārgaḥ //
body.translated_text: The uninterrupted path (<s>ānantaryamārga</s>): that immediately after which, through the departure of the remainder of the bad-disposition belonging to the class of that type of defilement, the basis is transformed as free from bad-disposition (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>) with respect to that [particular] bad-disposition.

body.text: vimuktimārgo yena nāmāśrayaparivṛtti pratyātma[ma]nubhavati /
body.translated_text: The liberation path (<s>vimuktimārga</s>): that by which one personally experiences the transformation of the basis.

body.text: viśeṣamārgastadūrdhvāvaśeṣakleśaprahāṇaṃ kurvato ye prayogānantaryavimuktimārgāḥ / aparaḥ paryāya 'viśeṣamārgastasya kleśaprahāṇaprayogamadhyupekṣya sūtrādīn dharmāścintayataḥ, pūrvacintitādhigatadharmapratyavekṣaṇāvihāreṇa vā viharataḥ samāpattyantaraṃ vā samāpadyamānasya yo mārgaḥ / punarabhijñādīn vaiśeṣikān guṇānabhinirharatastairvā viharato yo mārgaḥ //
body.translated_text: The special path (<s>viśeṣamārga</s>): the preparatory, uninterrupted, and liberation paths of one who is working on the abandonment of the remaining defilements above that. Another interpretation: the special path is the path of one who, setting aside the effort for abandoning defilements, reflects on the <s>Dharma</s> of <s>sūtras</s> etc., or who abides in the dwelling of reviewing previously reflected-upon and realized <s>dharmas</s>, or who is attaining another meditative attainment (<s>samāpatti</s>). Furthermore, the path of one who accomplishes special qualities such as the superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>) etc. or abides with those.

body.text: ityevaṃ bhāvanāmārga vistareṇa nirdiśya tadanuṣaṃgeṇa mārgabhāvanā varṇyate /
body.translated_text: Having thus taught the path of cultivation (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>) in detail, in connection with that, the cultivation of the path (<s>mārgabhāvanā</s>) is described.

body.text: caturvidhā mārgabhāvanā samyak prahāṇānadhikṛtya yathāyogam / tatra pratilambhāya bhāvanā pratilambhabhāvanā, tayālabdhakuśaladharmapratilambhāt / niṣevaṇameva bhāvanā niṣevaṇabhāvanā, labdhakuśaladharmābhyasanāt / nirdhāvanāya bhāvanā nirdhāvanabhāvanā, samudācārāvasthākuśaladharmanirvāsanāt / pratipakṣasya bhāvanā pratipakṣabhāvanā, anāgatākuśaladharmānutpattidharmatāpādanāt //
body.translated_text: The fourfold cultivation of the path, with reference to the four right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>), as applicable: (1) Cultivation for attainment (<s>pratilambhabhāvanā</s>)—through it, unobtained wholesome <s>dharmas</s> are obtained. (2) Cultivation as practice (<s>niṣevaṇabhāvanā</s>)—through practicing already-obtained wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. (3) Cultivation for removal (<s>nirdhāvanabhāvanā</s>)—through driving away unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> in the state of active occurrence. (4) Cultivation as antidote (<s>pratipakṣabhāvanā</s>)—through bringing about the nature of non-arising for future unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: aparaḥ paryāyaḥ - mārga utpadyamānaḥ svāṃ vāsanāṃ sthāpayati[sā]dhāsanā pratilambhabhāvanā, tatastadanvayānāmuttaptatarāpatteḥ / asyaiva mārgasya saṃmukhībhāvo 'bhiniṣevaṇabhāvanā / tena svavipakṣadauṣṭhulyanirodhanānnirdhāvanabhāvanā / āśrayasya parivṛttatvādāyatyāmanutpattidharmatāyāmavasthāpanaṃ pratipakṣabhāvanā / punaḥ pratipakṣasya vidūṣaṇādikaḥ caturvidhaḥ prabhedo veditavyaḥ / tatra vidūṣaṇāpratipakṣaḥ sāsraveṣu saṃskāreṣvādīnavadarśanam, tena rogagaṇḍādibhirākārairupādānaskandhadūṣaṇāt / prahāṇapratipakṣaḥ prayogānantaryamārgāḥ, taiḥ kleśaprahāṇāt / ādhārapratipakṣo vimuktimārgāḥ, taiḥ prahāṇaprāptisaṃdhāraṇāt / dūrībhāvapratipakṣastaduparimo mārgaḥ, tena pūrvaprahīṇakleśadūrīkaraṇāt //
body.translated_text: Another interpretation: the path, when arising, establishes its own imprint (<s>vāsanā</s>)—that is the cultivation of attainment of the imprint, because from that, more intense states of the same type arise. The coming into presence of this very path is the cultivation as practice. Through it, the bad-disposition of its own adversary being gradually attenuated...

body.text: punarbodhipakṣyādibhedenaikādaśavidho mārgo vyavasthāpyate / tadyathā vastuparīkṣāmārgaḥ smṛtyupasthānāni, āditastenāśubhādibhirākāraiḥ kāyavedanācittadharmavastuparīkṣaṇāt /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the path is established as eleven-fold through the division of the factors of awakening (<s>bodhipakṣya</s>) and so forth. Namely: the path of examining objects (<s>vastuparīkṣāmārga</s>) consists of the foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>)—because from the beginning, through aspects such as the impure etc., one examines the objects of body, feeling, mind, and <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: vyāvasāyiko mārgaḥ samyakprahāṇāni, tathā sarvāṇi vastūni parīkṣyānenāvaraṇaprahāṇāya vīryārambhāt / samādhiparikarmamārga ṛddhipādāḥ, tathāpariśodhitāvaraṇasyānena chandavīryacittamīmāṃsāmukhaiḥ samādheḥ karmaṇyatāpādanāt / abhisamayaprayogiko mārga indriyāṇi, tathākṛtasamādhiparikarmaṇo 'nenāryamārgasamudāgamāyādhipatibhūtoṣmagatordhvaprayogāt / abhisamayaśliṣṭo mārgo balāni, tathādhipatyaprāptasyānenā[na]ntaraṃ satyaprativedhāyāśraddhādivipakṣānabhibhūtakṣāntyagradharmaprayogāt / abhisamayamārgo bodhyaṅgāni, tenāditaḥ pratyātmaṃ tattvābhisaṃbodhāt / viśuddhinairyāṇiko mārga āryāṣṭāṅgo mārgaḥ, tadūrdhvaṃ tena bhāvanāprahātavyakleśaprahāṇāya viśuddhaye niryāṇāditi / ata evaiṣāṃ bodhipakṣāṇāmevānupūrvī veditavyā / niśrayendriyabhinno mārgaḥ catasraḥ pratipadaḥ / tatra duḥkhā pratipadanāgamyārūpyaniśritā yathākramaṃ śamathavipaśyanāmāndyāt / sukhā dhyānaniśritā yuganaddhavāhitvāt / dhandhābhijñā dvayorapyanayorduḥkhasukhaniśrayayormṛdvindriyāṇām / kṣiprābhijñā tayoreva tīkṣṇendriyāṇāmiti / śikṣā trayapariśodhano mārgaḥ catvāri dharmapadāni / tatrānabhidhyāvyāpādamadhiśīlaṃ śikṣāyāḥ pariśodhanam, ananunayāpratighamukhena śikṣāpadākhaṇḍanāt / samyaksmṛtyādhicittaṃ śikṣāyāḥ pariśodhanam, ālaṃbanāsaṃmoṣe sati cittasamādhānāt / samyaksamādhinādhiprajñaṃ śikṣāyāḥ pariśodhanam, samāhitacittasya yathābhūtajñānāditi // sarvaguṇābhinirhārako yo mārgaḥ śamathavipaśyanā, tataḥ sarvalaukikalokottaraguṇābhiniṣpatteḥ / mārgasaṃgrahamārgastrīṇīndriyāṇī, tatrānājñātamājñāsyāmīndriyeṇa prayogadarśanamārgayoḥ saṃgrahaḥ, ājñendriyeṇa bhāvanāmārgasya, ājñātāvīndriyeṇa niṣṭhāmārgasyeti //
body.translated_text: The path of determination (<s>vyāvasāyikamārga</s>) consists of the right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>)—because, having thus examined all objects, one initiates energy for the abandonment of obstructions. The path of preparatory concentration (<s>samādhiparikarmamārga</s>) consists of the bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>)—because, for one whose obstructions have thus been purified, concentration is prepared through the doors of intention (<s>chanda</s>), energy (<s>vīrya</s>), mind (<s>citta</s>), and investigation (<s>mīmāṃsā</s>).

body.text: punarbodhipakṣyāṇāṃ dharmāṇāṃ pañcabhiḥ prakāraiḥ vyavasthānaṃ veditavyam - ālambanataḥ svabhāvataḥ sahāyato bhāvanāto bhāvanāphalataśca //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the establishment of the factors of awakening (<s>bodhipakṣya dharma</s>) should be understood through five aspects: through their object (<s>ālambana</s>), their intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāva</s>), their companions (<s>sahāya</s>), their cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>), and the fruit of their cultivation (<s>bhāvanāphala</s>).

body.text: tatra smṛtyupasthānānāmālaṃbanaṃ yathākramaṃ kāyo vedanā cittaṃ dharmāḥ / kimartha punaretadevamālaṃbanaṃ vyavasthāpyate / yasmādviparyastabuddhayo
body.translated_text: The object of the foundations of mindfulness is, in due order: body, feeling, mind, and <s>dharmas</s>. Why is the object established thus? Because beings with distorted understanding,

body.text: bālāḥ prāyeṇa sendriyaṃ kāyamāśritya sukhādimupabhuñjānā upalabdhalakṣaṇā ātmarāgādibhiḥ śraddhādibhiśca saṃkliśyante vyavadāyante ceti vikalpayantyata āditaḥ samyaktadvastulakṣaṇaparīkṣārthamevaṃ caturdhālambanavyavasthānaṃ veditavyam //
body.translated_text: who are mostly foolish, relying on the body endowed with sense faculties, enjoying pleasant [feeling] and so forth, with the characteristic of perception, become defiled through self-attachment (<s>ātmarāga</s>) and so forth, and become purified through faith (<s>śraddhā</s>) and so forth—thus discriminating, the correct examination of the characteristics of those very objects [is undertaken] from the beginning.

body.text: svabhāvataḥ prajñā smṛtiśca, kāyādyanupaśyanāvacanāt smṛtyupasthānavacanācca yathākramam //
body.translated_text: As to their intrinsic nature: wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) and mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>), from the expressions 'contemplation of the body etc.' and 'foundation of mindfulness' respectively.

body.text: sahāyatastābhyāṃ saṃprayuktāścitacaitasikāḥ //
body.translated_text: As to their companions: the mind and mental factors (<s>citta-caitasika</s>) associated with those two.

body.text: bhāvanādhyātmaṃ bahirdhādhyātmabahirdhā ca kāyādiṣu kāyādyanupaśyanā //
body.translated_text: As to cultivation: contemplation of body etc. in the internal body etc., external, and both internal and external.

body.text: tatrādhyātmaṃ kāyaścakṣuśrotraghrāṇajihvākāyendriyāṇi, ādhyātmikāyatanasaṃgṛhītatvātsattvasaṃkhyātatvācca / bahirdhā kāyo bahirdhārūpaśabdagandharasaspraṣṭavyāni, bāhyāyatanasaṃgṛhītatvādasattvasaṃkhyātatvācca / adhyātmabahirdhā kāyaścakṣurādyāyatanasaṃbaddhāni rūpādīnyāyatanānīndriyādhiṣṭhānabhūtāni, sattvasaṃkhyātatvādvāhyāyatanasaṃgṛhītatvācca / pārasaṃtānikāni cādhyātmikāni rūpīṇyāyatanānyadhyātmabahirdhā kāyaḥ, āyatanavyavasthāṃ saṃtānavyavasthāṃ ca pramāṇayitvā //
body.translated_text: The internal body (<s>adhyātma</s>) [consists of]: the eye, ear, nose, tongue, and body faculties—because they are included in the internal sense bases (<s>ādhyātmikāyatana</s>) and because they are counted as beings. The external body (<s>bahirdhā</s>): external form, sound, odor, taste, and tactile objects—because they are included in the external sense bases and are not counted as beings.

body.text: kāye kāyasya sādṛśyena paśyanā kāye kāyānupaśyanā, vikalpapratibimbakāyadarśanānusāreṇa prakṛtibimbakāyāvadhāraṇāt //
body.translated_text: 'Contemplation of the body in the body' (<s>kāye kāyānupaśyanā</s>): seeing through similarity with the body—because by following the seeing of the body as a conceptual reflection, one ascertains the body as the original image.

body.text: adhyātmaṃ vedanādayo 'dhyātmaṃ kāyamupādāyotpannāḥ cakṣurādyālaṃbanatayā svāśrayotpannanatayā vā / bahirdhā vedanādayo bahirdhā kāyamupādāyotpannāḥ, rūpādyālambanatayā parāśrayotpannatayā vā / adhyātmabahirdhā vedanādayo dhyātmabahirdhākāyamupādāyotpannāḥ, svasantānikabāhyā[yatanā]lambanatayā pārasaṃtānikādhyātmikāyatanālaṃbanatayā vā //
body.translated_text: Internal feelings etc.: those arisen dependent on the internal body, through having objects such as the eye etc. or through arising from one's own basis. External feelings etc.: those arisen dependent on the external body, through having objects such as form etc. or through arising from another's basis. Both internal and external...

body.text: cetaso līnatvaṃ viśeṣādhigamapratyātmaparibhavamukhaiḥ viṣādaḥ / parisravaparikhedo daṃśamaśakādyupadravotpīḍanāsahanam / alpamātrasaṃtuṣṭiḥ alaṃ me tāvatā kuśalapakṣeṇeti prativāraṇam / āpattivipratisāro
body.translated_text: Depression of the mind [arises] through despair by way of self-disparagement regarding the attainment of distinction. Fatigue from outflows: inability to endure afflictions from mosquitoes, gadflies, and so forth. Contentment with little: the mental barrier [thinking] 'that much of the wholesome side is enough for me.' Regret for transgressions...

body.text: 'bhikramapratikramādiṣvasaṃprajñānacāriṇaḥ śikṣāvyatikramapūrvaḥ paścāttāpaḥ / nikṣiptadhuratā pramādadoṣeṇa yathārambhaṃ kuśalapakṣaprayogāntānirvāha iti //
body.translated_text: One who acts without clear comprehension (<s>asaṃprajñānacārin</s>) in coming, going, and so forth—remorse following violation of the training rules. Giving up effort (<s>nikṣiptadhuratā</s>): through the fault of heedlessness (<s>pramāda</s>), not carrying through to completion the practice of the wholesome side as begun.

body.text: phalaṃ yathākramaṃ smṛtyupasthānānāṃ śucisukhanityātmaviparyāsapraharaṇam, aśu[bha]bhāvanā[taḥ], yatkiṃcit veditamidamatra duḥkhasyeti jñānāt, āśrayālaṃbanādibhedaiḥ pratikṣaṇaṃ vijñānasyānyathāvagamāt, nirvyāpārasaṃkleśabyavadānadharmamātraparīkṣaṇācceti //
body.translated_text: The fruit, in due order, of the foundations of mindfulness is the destruction of the four distortions (<s>viparyāsa</s>) of pure, pleasant, permanent, and self—through the cultivation of the impure (<s>aśubhabhāvanā</s>), through the knowledge 'whatever is felt, that is suffering here,' through understanding consciousness as changing at every moment through the divisions of basis, object, and so forth...

body.text: punareṣāṃ yathākramaṃ catuḥsatyāvatāraḥ phalam / kāyasmṛtyupasthānena duḥkhasatyamavatarati, saṃskāraduḥkhatālakṣaṇena dauṣṭhulyena prabhāvitatvāt kāyasya / tathāhi tatpratipakṣabhūtā prasrabdhiḥ kāya eva viśeṣeṇotpadyata iti / vedanāsmṛtyupasthānena samudayasatyamavatarati, sukhādivedanādhiṣṭhānatvāt saṃyogāditṛṣṇāyāḥ / cittasmṛtyupasthānena nirodhasatyamavatarati, nirātmakaṃ vijñānamātraṃ na bhaviṣyatīti paśyata ātmocchedāśaṅkāmukhena nirvāṇottrāsābhāvāt / dharmasmṛtyupasthānena mārgasatyamavatarati, vipakṣadharmaprahāṇāya pratipakṣadharmabhāvanāditi / punareṣāṃ kāyavedanācittadharmavisaṃyogaḥ phalaṃ yathākramaṃ veditavyam, tadbhāvanayā kāyādipakṣadauṣṭhulyāpagamāditi //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, their fruit in due order is entry into the four truths (<s>catuḥsatya</s>). Through the foundation of mindfulness of the body, one enters the truth of suffering (<s>duḥkhasatya</s>), because the body is brought about by the bad-disposition (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>) characterized by the suffering of conditioned existence (<s>saṃskāraduḥkhatā</s>). For the antidote to that is pliancy (<s>prasrabdhi</s>)...

body.text: samyakprahāṇānāṃ prathamasyānutpanno vipakṣa ālaṃbanam, tenānutpannapāpakākuśaladharmānutpādāya chandajananāt / dvitīyasyotpanno vipakṣaḥ / tṛtīyasyānutpannaḥ pratipakṣaḥ / caturthasyotpanna ālaṃbanamiti yathāsūtraṃ yojayitavyam /
body.translated_text: The object of the first right effort: the unarisen adversary—because it generates aspiration for the non-arising of unarisen evil unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>. Of the second: the arisen adversary. Of the third: the unarisen antidote. Of the fourth: the arisen [antidote] as the object...

body.text: chandaṃ janayatītyevamādibhiḥ sāśrayā vīryabhāvanā paridīpitā / atrāśrayaśchandaḥ, tatpūrvakatvādudyogasya / yadā śamathādinimittamanaskāreṇa nirapekṣālaṃbanaṃ kevalaṃ pratipakṣaṃ bhāvayati tadā vyāyaccjhata ityucyate / yadā tulayopakleśe utpanne tadapakarṣaṇārtha prasadanīyādimanaskāraiḥ cittamunnāmayati,
body.translated_text: 'Generates aspiration' and so forth—by these expressions, the cultivation of energy (<s>vīrya</s>) together with its basis is illustrated. The basis here is aspiration (<s>chanda</s>), because effort is preceded by it. When through mental engagement with signs of calm-abiding (<s>śamatha</s>) etc., one cultivates the antidote alone with an independent object, then one is said to 'strive' (<s>vyāyacchate</s>)...

body.text: auddhatyopakleśe cotpanne pratyāsaṃkṣepamukhena cittaṃ dhārayati tadā vīryamārabhata ityucyate / ata eva layauddhatyāpakarṣaṇopāyasaṃdarśanārthamanantaramāha cittaṃ pragṛhṇāti pradadhātīti /
body.translated_text: And when restlessness (<s>auddhatya</s>) as a secondary defilement has arisen, one holds the mind through the door of re-contracting—then one is said to 'initiate energy.' For this very reason, to show the means of removing torpor (<s>laya</s>) and restlessness (<s>auddhatya</s>), immediately [the text] says 'one uplifts the mind, one establishes it.'

body.text: phalaṃ prathamadvitīyayoḥ samyakprahāṇayoraśeṣavipakṣahāniḥ, tābhyāṃ yathāyogamutpannānutpannapāpakākuśaladharmaprahāṇāt / tṛtīyasya pratipakṣapratilambhaḥ, tenānutpannakuśaladharmotpādanāt / caturthasya pratipakṣavṛddhiḥ, tenotpannakuśaladharmavipulatāpādanāditi //
body.translated_text: The fruit of the first and second right efforts: the complete elimination of all adversaries, because through them, arisen and unarisen evil unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> are respectively abandoned. Of the third: the attainment of the antidote, because through it, unarisen wholesome <s>dharmas</s> are produced. Of the fourth...

body.text: ṛddhipādālaṃbanaṃ niṣpannena samādhinā yatkaraṇīyamṛddhayādikaṃ kṛtyam //
body.translated_text: The object of the bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>): the tasks to be accomplished with the perfected concentration (<s>samādhi</s>), such as the activity of supernatural power and so forth.

body.text: chandasamādhiryat satkṛtyaprayogamāgamya spṛśati cittasyaikāgratāṃ tīvreṇa chandena tīvreṇādareṇa prayogaḥ satkṛtyaprayoga iti kṛtvā / vīryasamādhiryatsātatyaprayogamāgamya spṛśati cittasyaikāgratām / tadvīryamityucyate yannityaṃ prayujyata eva na kadācinna prayujyate / cittasamādhiryatpūrvajanmāntare samādhibhāvanāmāgamyatatparipuṣṭabījatvāccittasya svarasena samādhyanukūlapariṇāme sati spṛśati cittasyaikāgratām / api khalu ṛddhipādābhinirhārayornidarśanārthameva samyakprahāṇabhāvanāyāṃ chandaṃ janayatītyevamādinirdeśo veditavyaḥ / cittaṃ pradadhāti pragṛhṇātītyeṣā cātra pāṭhānupūrvī veditavyā / tatra cittasamādhiryaccitaṃ pradadhat spṛśatīti pratyātmaṃ cittameva cittaṃ dhārayan śamayannabhisaṃkṣipannadhigacchatītyarthaḥ / mīmāṃsāsamādhiryaccitaṃ pragṛhṇanniti dharmavipaśyanāmukhena cittamuttāpayatītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: The <s>chandasamādhi</s> (concentration through aspiration) — that which, through earnest effort, touches one-pointedness of mind; intense aspiration with intense diligence constitutes earnest effort. The <s>vīryasamādhi</s> (concentration through vigor) — that which, through continuous effort, touches one-pointedness of mind; that is called vigor which is constantly applied and never not applied. The <s>cittasamādhi</s> (concentration through mind) — that which, through the cultivation of <s>samādhi</s> in a previous life, having well-nourished seeds, when the mind naturally turns favorably toward concentration, touches one-pointedness of mind. Moreover, the indication for the production of the <s>ṛddhipādas</s> (bases of miraculous power) — 'one generates aspiration in the cultivation of right effort' and so forth — should be understood as merely illustrative. 'He settles the mind, he takes hold of it' — this is the sequential reading to be understood here. Among these, the <s>cittasamādhi</s> — 'settling the mind, he touches' — means that within oneself, sustaining the mind itself, calming it, collecting it, one attains it. The <s>mīmāṃsāsamādhi</s> (concentration through investigation) — 'taking hold of the mind' — means raising up the mind through the channel of <s>dharma</s>-insight.
