body.text: bhāvanā chandādīnāmaṣṭānāṃ prahāṇasaṃskārāṇāmabhyāsaḥ / te punaraṣṭau prahāṇasaṃskārāścaturdhā kriyante / tadyathā vyāvasāyikaśchandavyāyāmaśraddhāḥ // tatra chando vyāyāmasyāśrayaḥ / chandasya punaḥ śraddhā nimittam / tathāhi yo yenārthī bhavati tatprāptyartha vyāyacchate / arthitvaṃ ca nāntareṇa tadasti tvādyabhisaṃpratyamiti / anugrāhikaḥ prasrabdhiḥ, tayā kāyacittānugrahakaraṇāt / aupanibandhikaḥ smṛtisaṃprajanye, ālaṃbanāsaṃpramoṣeṇa cittasyaikāgrāvasthānāt, tatpramāde ca sati paricchedāt yathākramam / prātipakṣikaścetanopekṣe, cittapragrahapradhānābhisaṃskārābhyāmutpannalayauddhatyaparivarjanānnirupakleśaśamathādinimittānukaraṇācceti //
body.translated_text: <s>Bhāvanā</s> (cultivation) is the practice of the eight <s>prahāṇasaṃskāras</s> (factors of abandonment) beginning with aspiration. These eight factors of abandonment are classified fourfold. Namely: the factors of determination are aspiration, effort, and faith. Among these, aspiration is the basis of effort. Faith, in turn, is the cause of aspiration. For one who desires something exerts effort to obtain it, and the desiring does not exist without the belief that 'this is so.' The supportive factor is <s>prasrabdhi</s> (pliancy), because through it the body and mind are supported. The binding factors are <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) and <s>saṃprajanya</s> (clear comprehension) — because through non-forgetfulness of the object there is one-pointed abiding of the mind, and because when there is heedlessness regarding that, there is discernment, respectively. The antidote factors are <s>cetanā</s> (volition) and <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity) — because through the two formations of taking hold and predominance of the mind, arisen sinking and agitation are avoided, and the signs of calm and the rest that are free from affliction are followed.

body.text: saṃkṣepanidānaṃ vipaśyanārahitasya kausīdyamukhena layaḥ / vikṣepanidānamaśubhasaṃjñārahitasyauddhatyamukhena saṃpragrahaḥ / saṃkṣepaḥ styānanimittamukhe nāntaḥsaṃkocaḥ / vikṣepaḥ śubhanimittānusāramukhena viṣayeṣu visāraḥ / ālīnatvānukūlā bhāvanā pratyavekṣaṇānimittaṃ niśritya dharmavipaśyanā / avikṣepānukūlāśubhataḥ keśādidravyapratyavekṣā / tadubhayānukūlālokasaṃjñā / etacca yathā kramamadhikṛtyoktaṃ bhagavatā - naca me chando 'tilīno bhaviṣyati, nātipragṛhītaḥ, nādhyātmaṃ saṃkṣiptaḥ na bahirdhā vikṣiptaḥ, paścātpūrvasaṃjñī bhaviṣyati ūrdhvamadhaḥsaṃjñī ca, vivṛtena cetasāparyavanaddhena saprabhāsasahagataṃ cittaṃ bhāvayiṣyāmi na ca me 'ndhakārāyattatvaṃ bhaviṣyati cetasa iti /
body.translated_text: The cause of sinking — for one lacking <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight), sinking through the channel of laziness is contraction. The cause of distraction — for one lacking the perception of the unattractive, agitation through the channel of restlessness is excessive grasping. Contraction is an internal shrinking through the channel of the sign of <s>styāna</s> (torpor). Distraction is a spreading out toward objects through the channel of pursuing the sign of the attractive. The cultivation favorable to a withdrawn state —

body.text: phalaṃ yatheṣṭamṛddhayādiguṇaniṣpādanāt //
body.translated_text: The result is the accomplishment of qualities such as <s>ṛddhi</s> (miraculous powers) and the rest as desired.

body.text: indriyāṇāṃ catvāryāryasatyānyālaṃbanam, satyābhisamayaprayogasaṃgṛhītatvena tadākāratvāt // phalaṃ tadādhipatyādacireṇa kālena darśanamārgasyotpādaḥ tasminneva ca kāle nirvedhabhāgīyabhajanaṃ ca saṃtānasya //
body.translated_text: The object of the <s>indriyas</s> (faculties) is the four noble truths, because they are included in the practice of realizing the truths and have those as their mode. The result — through their dominance, the arising of the <s>darśanamārga</s> (path of seeing) in a short time, and the suitability of the continuum for sharing in the <s>nirvedhabhāgīyas</s> (factors conducive to penetration) at that very time.

body.text: balānāmālaṃbanādikamindriyaiḥ samānam // phale tu viśeṣaḥ / tathāhyeṣāṃ tacca yathoktam - āśradvyādivipakṣanirlekhaścādhika ityata evaiṣāṃ tulyānāmālaṃbanasvabhāvādikānāmapyanavamṛdyatārthaviśeṣeṇa bodhipakṣāntaratvam //
body.translated_text: The object and the rest of the <s>balas</s> (powers) are the same as those of the faculties. But there is a distinction regarding the result. For these, there is also that which has been stated — the additional removal of the opposition of unfaith and the rest — and therefore, although their object, intrinsic nature, and the rest are the same, their distinctive meaning of invincibility establishes them as a separate set of factors conducive to enlightenment.

body.text: bodhyaṅgānāmālaṃbanaṃ caturṇāmāryasatyānāṃ yathābhūtateti paramārtho viśuddhayālaṃbanamityarthaḥ / svabhāvaḥ smṛtyādayaḥ sapta dharmāḥ / tatra smṛtiḥ
body.translated_text: The object of the <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (factors of awakening) is the four noble truths as they truly are — meaning that the ultimate is the object of purity. Their intrinsic nature consists of seven <s>dharmas</s> beginning with <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness). Among these, <s>smṛti</s>

body.text: saṃniśrayāṅgam, upasthitasmṛteḥ sarvakuśaladharmābhilapanāt / dharmavicayaḥ svabhāvāṅgam, saṃbodhilakṣaṇatvāt / vīryaṃ niryāṇāṅgam, tena yāvadgamyaṃ gamanāt / prītiranuśaṃsāṅgam, tayā saṃtānaprīṇanāt / prasrabdhiḥ samādhirupekṣā cāsaṃkleśāṅgam / tatra prasrabdhyā na saṃkliśyate, tayā dauṣṭhulyasrāvaṇāt / samādhau na saṃkliśyate, tatra sthitasyāśrayaparivartanāt / upekṣāsaṃkleśaḥ, abhidhyādaurmanasyāpagatākliṣṭāvasthāsvabhāvatvāt / bhāvanā smṛtisaṃbodhyaṅgaṃ bhāvayati vivekaniśritamityevamādirebhiḥ caturbhiḥ padairyathākramaṃ catuḥsatyālaṃbanā bodhyaṅgabhāvanā paridīpitā / tathāhi duḥkhaṃ duḥkhata ālaṃbamānasya tadvivekānveṣaṇādduḥkhālaṃbanaṃ vivekaniśritamityucyate / tṛṣṇālakṣaṇaṃ duḥkhasamudayaṃ duḥkhasamudayata ālaṃbamānasya tadvirāgānveṣaṇāttadālaṃbanaṃ virāganiśritam / duḥkhanirodhaṃ duḥkhanirodhata ālaṃbamānasya tatsākṣātkaraṇānveṣaṇāttadālaṃbanaṃ nirodhaniśritam / duḥkhanirodhagāminī pratipad vyavasarga ityucyate, tayā duḥkhavisarjanāt / tāṃ tathālaṃbamānasya tadbhāvanānveṣaṇāttadālaṃbanaṃ vyavasargapariṇatamityucyate / phalaṃ darśanaheyānāṃ kleśānāṃ prahāṇam, bodhyaṅgānāṃ darśanamārgasvabhāvatvāt //
body.translated_text: is the factor of support, because with established mindfulness there is the undertaking of all wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. <s>Dharmavicaya</s> (investigation of dharmas) is the factor of intrinsic nature, because it has the character of awakening. <s>Vīrya</s> (vigor) is the factor of going forth, because through it one goes as far as can be gone. <s>Prīti</s> (joy) is the factor of benefit, because through it the continuum is gladdened. <s>Prasrabdhi</s> (pliancy), <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), and <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity) are the factors of non-defilement —

body.text: mārgāṅgānāmālaṃbanaṃ darśanamārgāduttarakālaṃ saiva yathādṛṣṭānāṃ satyānāṃ yathābhūtatā / svabhāvaḥ samyagdṛṣṭayādayo 'ṣṭau dharmāḥ / tatra samyagdṛṣṭiḥ paricchedāṅgam, tayā yathānubhavaṃ tattvāvadhāraṇāt / samyaksaṃkalpaḥ parasaṃprāpaṇāṅgam, tena yathādhigamaṃ vyavasthāpya vāksamutthāpanāt / samyagvākkarmāntājīvāḥ parasaṃpratyayāṅgam, tairyathākramamadhigantuḥ paraidṛṣṭayādiviśuddhiniścayanāt / tatra samyagvācādhigamānurūpapraśnavyākaraṇasāṃkathyaviniścayenāsya darśanaviśuddhirvijñāyate / samyakkarmāntenābhikramapratikramādiṣu saṃpannacāritratayā śīlaviśuddhiḥ samyagājīvena yathānujñaṃ dharmeṇa cīvarādiparyeṣaṇādājīvaviśuddhiriti / samyagvyāyāmaḥ kleśāvaraṇaviśodhanāṅgam, tenāśeṣa saṃyojanaprahāṇāt / samyaksmṛtirupakleśāvaraṇaviśodhanāṅgam,
body.translated_text: The object of the <s>mārgāṅgas</s> (factors of the path) is, from the <s>darśanamārga</s> onward, that very suchness of the truths as they have been seen. Their intrinsic nature consists of eight <s>dharmas</s> beginning with <s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s> (right view). Among these, <s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s> is the factor of discernment, because through it there is the ascertainment of reality as experienced. <s>Samyaksaṃkalpa</s> (right intention) is the factor of communicating to others, because through it what —

body.text: tayā samyakśamathādinimittāsaṃpramoṣeṇa layādyupakleśānavakāśāt / samyaksamādhirvaiśeṣikaguṇāvaraṇaviśodhanāṅgam, tenābhijñādiguṇābhinirharaṇāt / bhāvanā bodhyaṅgavat, tadyathā samyagdṛṣṭiṃ bhāvayati vivekaniśritāmiti vistaraḥ / teṣāṃ ca padānāmarthaḥ yathānirdiṣṭaṃ purastāttathānugantavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: through it, by not forgetting the signs of right calm and the rest, there is no opportunity for sinking and other minor defilements. <s>Samyaksamādhi</s> (right concentration) is the factor of purifying the obstruction to distinctive qualities, because through it there is the accomplishment of qualities such as the <s>abhijñās</s> (higher knowledges) and the rest. The cultivation is like that of the <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> — for example, 'one cultivates right view, which is based on seclusion' and so forth in detail. And the meaning of those terms —

body.text: pratipadāṃ dharmapadānāṃ ca pūrvavadarthanirdeśo veditavyaḥ dukhā pratipadanāgamyārūpyaniśritā yathākramaṃ śamathavipaśyanāmāndhāt / sukhā dhyānaniśritā yuganaddhavāhitvāt dhandhābhijñā dvayorapyanayorduḥkhasukhaniśrayayormṛdvindriyāṇām / kṣiprābhijñā tayoreva tīkṣṇendriyāṇāmiti //
body.translated_text: The exposition of the meaning of the types of practice and the <s>dharma</s>-terms should be understood as before. The painful practice is based on the preliminary stage and the formless realms, because, respectively, it is one-sided toward <s>śamatha</s> (calm) or <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight). The pleasant practice is based on the <s>dhyānas</s> because it proceeds with both yoked together. The slow-in-direct-knowledge practice belongs to those with weak faculties in both of these, whether based on pain or pleasure. The swift-in-direct-knowledge practice —

body.text: śamathaḥ navakāracittasthitiḥ / tatra bāhyālaṃbanebhyaḥ pratisaṃhṛtyā dhyātmamavikṣepāpāditaścittasyopanibandhaḥ sthāpanā / tasya cittasyaivamādita upanibaddhasya calasyaudārikasya tasminnevālaṃbane saṃtatiyogena sūkṣmīkaraṇena cābhisaṃkṣepaḥ saṃsthāpanā / tasya smṛtisaṃpramoṣādvahirdhā vikṣiptasya punaḥ pratisaṃharaṇamavasthāpanā / ādita eva tasya cittasya bahiravisārāyopasthitasmṛtitopasthāpanā / pūrvameva vikṣepanimitteṣu rūpādiṣvādīnavasaṃjñāmadhipati kṛtvā cittasya prasarādānaṃ damanam / cetaḥsaṃkṣobhakareṣu vitarkopakleśeṣvādīnavadarśanena prasarādānaṃ śamanam / smṛtisaṃpramoṣādvitarkādisamudācāre sati tadanadhivāsanā vyupaśamanam / abhisaṃskāreṇa niśchidranirantarasamādhipravāhāvasthāpanā ekotīkaraṇam / svabhyastatvādanabhisaṃskāreṇānābhogena cittasamādhipravāhasyāvikṣepeṇa pravṛttiḥ samādhānamiti //
body.translated_text: <s>Śamatha</s> (calm) is the ninefold settling of the mind. Among these, the settling is the binding of the mind inwardly without distraction, having withdrawn it from external objects. The condensation of that very mind, thus bound from the beginning, which is restless and gross — through continuous application to that very object, making it subtle —

body.text: vipaśyanā yathāpi taddharmānvicinotītyevamādiḥ / tatra caritaviśodhanamālaṃbanaṃ kauśalyālaṃbanaṃ vā kleśaviśodhanaṃ vā yāvadbhāvikatayā
body.translated_text: <s>Vipaśyanā</s> (insight) is as follows: 'one investigates those <s>dharmas</s>' and so forth. Among these, the object is the purification of conduct, or the skillful means of objects, or the purification of defilements — insofar as it investigates in terms of future possibility,

body.text: vicinoti, yathāvadbhāvikatayā pravicinoti, savikalpenamanaskāreṇa prajñāsahagatena nimittīkurvan parivitarkayati, saṃntīrayan parimīmāṃsāmāpadyata iti //
body.translated_text: and investigates in terms of how things truly are; with conceptual attention accompanied by wisdom, making into a sign, one reflects, examines, and enters into thorough investigation.

body.text: api khalu [śamatha]vipaśyanāmāgamya catvāro mārgā iti catvāro mārgopadeśanāmadhikṛtya / tatra prathamaḥ śamathasya lābhitvādabhiniṣīdanneva cittaṃ sthāpayati yāvatsamādhatte, vipaśyānāyā alābhitvāttu samādhiṃ niśritya paścāttathāniṣaṇṇastān dharmānvicinoti yāvatparimīmāṃsāmāpadyate / dvitīyo viparyayeṇa veditavyaḥ / tṛtīyā ubhayasyālābhyubhayatra yogaṃ karoti / kathaṃ kṛtvā, śrutodgrahaṇamukhena vivaśyanāyāṃ yogaṃ karoti tatpūrvakaṃ ca śamathe / caturtha ubhayasya lābhāt //
body.translated_text: Moreover, 'with reference to <s>śamatha</s> and <s>vipaśyanā</s>, the four paths' — this is with reference to the four designations of paths of instruction. Among these, the first — because of having attained <s>śamatha</s>, one settles the mind while deeply absorbed, up to entering <s>samādhi</s>; but because of not having attained <s>vipaśyanā</s>, relying on concentration, afterward while thus absorbed one investigates those <s>dharmas</s> —

body.text: ajñātamājñāsyāmīndriyaṃ prayogamārge nirvedhabhāgīyasaṃgṛhīte pañcadaśasu ca darśanamārgacittakṣaṇeṣu yadindriyam, tadyathā manaindriyam, pañca śraddhādīni, anāgamyādiniśrayabhedena yathāsaṃbhavaṃ sukhasaumanasya daurmanasyopekṣendriyāṇāṃ cānyatamam / daurmanasyendriyaṃ punaḥ prayogakāle nirvedhabhāgīyapṛṣṭhenottaravimokṣaspṛhāsaṃgṛhītaṃ veditavyam / tadetatsaṃbhavato daśavidhamindriyamanājñātapūrvasya tattvasyājñāyai pravṛttatvādanājñātamājñāsyāmīndriyamityucyate / etadeva daśavidhamindriyaṃ ṣoḍaśāddarśanamārgacittakṣaṇādyāvadvajropamaḥ samādhirityetasminśaikṣamārge ājñendriyamityucyate, apūrvajñeyābhāvāt / etadeva punarnavavidhamindriyaṃ daurmanasyendriyavarjamaśaikṣamārge ājñātāvīndriyamityucyate, ājñātāvino 'rhat indriyamiti kṛtvā //
body.translated_text: The <s>ajñātamājñāsyāmīndriya</s> (faculty of 'I shall come to know what is not yet known') is the faculty present in the preparatory path included in the <s>nirvedhabhāgīyas</s> (factors conducive to penetration) and in the fifteen mind-moments of the path of seeing — namely, faculties such as the mental faculty, the five beginning with faith, and depending on the distinction of basis such as the preliminary stage and the rest, whichever among the faculties of pleasure, mental happiness, mental unhappiness, and equanimity is applicable —

body.text: bhāvanā mārgādhikāreṇedamapi vakṣyate / ūrdhvabhūmike mārge saṃmukhībhāvena bhāvyamāne 'saṃmukhībhūtānyapyadhobhūmikāni kuśalamūlakāni
body.translated_text: Cultivation with reference to the path — this too will be stated. When a path of a higher level is being cultivated by being brought into presence, even the wholesome roots of the lower levels that have not been brought into presence

body.text: bhāvanāṃ gacchanti, teṣu vibhutvalābhāt / vibhutvaṃ punaruttaptasaṃmukhībhāvena taśitā veditavyā //
body.translated_text: also undergo cultivation, because mastery is obtained over them. Mastery, moreover, should be understood as the sharpening through being heated by being brought into presence.

body.text: niṣṭhāmārgaḥ sarvadauṣṭhulyānāṃ pratiprasrabdheriti vistaraḥ //
body.translated_text: The <s>niṣṭhāmārga</s> (path of completion) is because of the complete subsiding of all unwholesome dispositions — and so forth in detail.

body.text: tatra sarvadauṣṭhulyāni caturvitirbhavanti / tadyathā sarvatragamabhilāpadauṣṭhulyaṃ yā cakṣurādisarvadharmanāmābhiniveśavāsanālayavijñāne saṃniviṣṭānādikālānusṛtā, yāsāvucyate prapañcavāsaneti, yataścakṣurādayo dharmāḥ sanāmābhiniveśāḥ punaḥ punaḥ pravartanta iti / veditadauṣṭhulyaṃ sāsravāṇāṃ vedanānāṃ vāsanā / kleśadauṣṭhulyaṃ kleśānāmanuśayaḥ / karmadauṣṭhulyaṃ sāsravāṇāṃ karmaṇāṃ vāsanā / vipākadauṣṭhulyaṃ vipākasyā karmaṇyatā / kleśāvaraṇadauṣṭhulyaṃ tīvrāyatakleśatā / karmāvaraṇadauṣṭhalyaṃ mārgāntarāyikānantaryādikakarmāvṛtatā / vipākāvaraṇadauṣṭhulyaṃ satyābhisamayavidhuranārakādyātma bhāvapratilambhaḥ / nivaraṇadauṣṭhulyaṃ kuśalapakṣaprayogāntarāyikakāmachandādyabhibhūtatā / vitarkadauṣṭhulyaṃ pravrajyābhirati vibandhakāmavitarkādyabhibhūtatā / āhāradauṣṭhulyamatyalpabahubhojananena prayogāyogyatā / maithunadauṣṭhulyaṃ dvayadvayasamāpattikṛtā kāyacittavyathā / svapnadauṣṭhulyaṃ middhakṛtamāśrayajāḍyam / vyādhidauṣṭhulyaṃ dhātuvaiṣamyakṛtāsvasthatā / jarādauṣṭhulyaṃ bhūtavipariṇāmakṛtāvidheyatā / maraṇadauṣṭhulyaṃ mriyamāṇasya sarvendriyākulatā / pariśramadauṣṭhulyamatigamanādikṛto 'ṅgamardaḥ / dṛḍhadauṣṭhulyaṃ yathāsaṃbhavameta devābhilāpadauṣṭhulyādikamaparinirvāṇavatām / audārikamadhyasūkṣmadauṣṭhulyāni
body.translated_text: There, all the bad-dispositions (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>) are of four times twenty [types]. Namely: (1) the all-pervasive designation-bad-disposition (<s>sarvatraga-abhilāpa-dauṣṭhulya</s>)—the imprint (<s>vāsanā</s>) of clinging to names for all <s>dharmas</s> such as the eye etc., deposited in the <s>ālaya-vijñāna</s> (store consciousness), followed from beginningless time, which is called the 'imprint of proliferation' (<s>prapañcavāsanā</s>), because of which <s>dharmas</s> such as the eye etc. continue to manifest again and again with the clinging to names. (2) The feeling-bad-disposition (<s>vedita-dauṣṭhulya</s>): the imprint of contaminated feelings. (3) The defilement-bad-disposition (<s>kleśa-dauṣṭhulya</s>): the latent tendency (<s>anuśaya</s>) of the defilements. (4) The karma-bad-disposition (<s>karma-dauṣṭhulya</s>): the imprint of contaminated karmas. (5) The maturation-bad-disposition (<s>vipāka-dauṣṭhulya</s>): the non-workability of the maturation. (6) The defilement-obstruction-bad-disposition (<s>kleśāvaraṇa-dauṣṭhulya</s>): having intense and extensive defilements. (7) The karma-obstruction-bad-disposition (<s>karmāvaraṇa-dauṣṭhulya</s>): being obstructed by immediately effective karma etc. that is an obstacle to the path. (8) The maturation-obstruction-bad-disposition (<s>vipākāvaraṇa-dauṣṭhulya</s>): obtaining an existence such as a hell-being etc. that is far from the realization of the truths (<s>satyābhisamaya</s>). (9) The hindrance-bad-disposition (<s>nivaraṇa-dauṣṭhulya</s>): being overcome by sensual desire etc. that obstructs the practice of the wholesome side. (10) The discursive thought-bad-disposition (<s>vitarka-dauṣṭhulya</s>): being overcome by thoughts of sensuality etc. that bind delight in renunciation. (11) The food-bad-disposition (<s>āhāra-dauṣṭhulya</s>): unsuitability for practice due to eating too little or too much. (12) The sexual-bad-disposition (<s>maithuna-dauṣṭhulya</s>): physical and mental distress caused by the union of two. (13) The sleep-bad-disposition (<s>svapna-dauṣṭhulya</s>): heaviness of the basis caused by torpor (<s>middha</s>). (14) The illness-bad-disposition (<s>vyādhi-dauṣṭhulya</s>): unwellness caused by imbalance of the elements. (15) The aging-bad-disposition (<s>jarā-dauṣṭhulya</s>): unmanageability caused by the transformation of the elements. (16) The death-bad-disposition (<s>maraṇa-dauṣṭhulya</s>): the agitation of all the sense faculties of one who is dying. (17) The fatigue-bad-disposition (<s>pariśrama-dauṣṭhulya</s>): bodily aching caused by excessive walking and so forth. (18) The firm-bad-disposition (<s>dṛḍha-dauṣṭhulya</s>): these [bad-dispositions] beginning with the designation-bad-disposition, as applicable, for those who have not attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. The coarse, medium, and subtle bad-dispositions

body.text: yathākramaṃ kāmarūpārūpyāvacarāṇi veditavyāni / kleśāvaraṇadauṣṭhulyaṃ śrāvakapratyekabuddhabodhi[vi]pakṣaḥ / samāpattyāvaraṇadauṣṭhulyaṃ navā[nu]pūrvasamāpattyabhinirhāra[vi]pakṣaḥ / jñeyāvaraṇadauṣṭhulyaṃ sarvajñatāvipakṣaḥ / ityevameṣāṃ yathāyogaṃ sarvadauṣṭhulyānāṃ pratiprasravdheniṣṭhāmārgaḥ / yathoktaṃ - "tasya cetovimukteḥ pāripūryā prajñāvimukteḥ pāripūryā kāyadauṣṭhulyānāṃ pratiprasrabdheḥ / smṛtyā samanvāgamahetorevamasya prathamaṃ dvāraṃ sudāntaṃ bhavati suguptaṃ surakṣitaṃ susaṃvṛtaṃ subhāṣitam, yaduta cakṣurvijñeyeṣu rūpeṣvevaṃ yāvanmano vijñeyeṣu dharmeṣvi"ti //
body.translated_text: should be understood, in due order, as belonging to the desire, form, and formless realms. The defilement-obstruction-bad-disposition is the adversary of the awakening of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. The attainment-obstruction-bad-disposition (<s>samāpattyāvaraṇa-dauṣṭhulya</s>) is the adversary of accomplishing the nine successive attainments (<s>navānupūrvasamāpatti</s>).

body.text: vajropamaḥ samādhirbhāvanāmārgasyāntyā prahāṇamārgāvasthā veditavyā / sa ca samādhirnirantarastatpravāharaya laukikena mārge ṇāntarākhaṇḍanāt / dṛḍhaḥ sarvāvaraṇairacchidraṇāt sarvāvaraṇabheditayā ca sāratvāt / ekarasa iti nirvikalpaikarasatvāt / vyāpī sarvajñeyasāmānyatathatālaṃbanatvāt / etadarthapratibimbanārtha bhagavatoktam - tadyathā mahāśailaḥ parvato 'khaṇḍo 'cchidro 'śuṣira ekadhanaḥ susaṃvṛta iti //
body.translated_text: The vajra-like <s>samādhi</s> (<s>vajropamaḥ samādhiḥ</s>) should be understood as the final stage of the abandonment-path within the path of cultivation. That <s>samādhi</s> is uninterrupted, because it is not broken by the mundane path in its continuous flow. It is firm, because it is not pierced by any obstructions. It is impenetrable by all...

body.text: nirantarāśrayaparivṛttividhārśakṣamārgalābhinaḥ / cittāśrayaparivṛttirdharmatā, cittasya prakṛtiprabhāsvarasyāśeṣāgantukopakleśāpagamādyā parivṛttiḥ, tathatāparivṛttirityarthaḥ / mārgāśrayaparivṛtiḥ pūrvaṃ laukiko mārgo 'bhisamayakāle lokottaratvena parivṛtaḥ śaikṣaścocyate sāvaśeṣakaraṇīyatvāt / yadā tu nirhatāśeṣavipakṣo bhavati traidhātukavairāgyāttadāsya mārgasvabhāvasyāśrayasya paripūrṇā parivṛttirvyavasthāpyate / dauṣṭhulyāśrayaparivṛttirālayavijñānasya sarvakleśānuśayāpagamena parivṛttirveditavyā //
body.translated_text: [One who has attained] the uninterrupted path capable of disclosing the transformation of the basis (<s>āśrayaparivṛtti</s>). The transformation of the basis of mind is the <s>dharmatā</s> (nature of reality): the transformation through the complete departure of all adventitious secondary defilements from the mind that is naturally luminous (<s>prakṛtiprabhāsvara</s>)—meaning the transformation of suchness (<s>tathatā</s>). The transformation of the basis of the mind...

body.text: kṣaye sati, viṣaye vā tasmin yajjñānaṃ kṣayajñānametaduktaṃ bhavati / niravaśeṣaṃ prakṣīṇe samudaye yajjñānaṃ tadavasthasya hetunirodhālaṃbanaṃ vā kṣayajñānamiti //
body.translated_text: When there is extinction [of suffering], or regarding that object, the knowledge that arises is called 'extinction-knowledge' (<s>kṣayajñāna</s>). When the origination [of suffering] has been utterly and completely extinguished, the knowledge of that state—or [the knowledge] having the cessation of causes as its object—is extinction-knowledge.

body.text: tathānutpāde sati viṣaye vā tasmin yajjñānamanutpādajñānam āyatyāṃ sarvasya duḥkhasyātyantamanutpattidharmatāyāṃ satyāṃ yajjñānamanyasatyālaṃbanamiti / yadvā duḥkhasatyānutpādālaṃbanaṃ tadanutpādajñānamityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Likewise, when there is non-arising, or regarding that object, the knowledge that arises is 'non-arising-knowledge' (<s>anutpādajñāna</s>)—when in the future the nature of absolute non-arising of all suffering is the case, the knowledge [that arises] has another truth as its object. Or alternatively, the knowledge having the non-arising of the truth of suffering as its object...

body.text: daśāśaikṣā dharmā aśaikṣāñchīlādīn pañca skandhānadhikṛtya / tatra aśaikṣā samyagvākkarmāntājīvā aśaikṣaśīlaskandhaḥ /
body.translated_text: The ten qualities of a non-learner (<s>aśaikṣa dharma</s>) are with reference to the five aggregates of the non-learner's morality (<s>śīla</s>) etc. Among these, the non-learner's right speech, right action, and right livelihood constitute the non-learner's aggregate of morality (<s>śīlaskandha</s>).

body.text: samyaksmṛtisamādhiḥ samādhiskandhaḥ / samyagdṛṣṭisaṃkalpavyāyāmāḥ prajñāskandhaḥ / samyagvimuktirvimuktiskandhaḥ / samyagjñānaṃ vimuktirjñānadarśanaskandha iti //
body.translated_text: Right mindfulness and right concentration constitute the aggregate of concentration (<s>samādhiskandha</s>). Right view, right intention, and right effort constitute the aggregate of wisdom (<s>prajñāskandha</s>). Right liberation constitutes the aggregate of liberation (<s>vimuktiskandha</s>). Right knowledge constitutes the aggregate of the knowledge-and-vision of liberation (<s>vimuktijñānadarśanaskandha</s>).

body.text: punarmārgasatyasya catvāra ākārāścatvāri lakṣaṇāni / tatra tattvārtha mārgayatyaneti mārgaḥ / aya[thā]bhūtānāṃ kleśānāṃ pratipakṣatvāt nyāyaḥ / tattvānavabodhadoṣeṇānityādiviparyāsairviparyastasya cittasyāviparyāse tattvāvabodhe pratipādanātpratipat / nitya ātyantike niḥsaraṇapade yānānnairyāṇika iti //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the truth of the path (<s>mārgasatya</s>) has four aspects and four characteristics. Among these: it is 'the path' (<s>mārga</s>) because it seeks and reaches the true meaning. It is 'correct' (<s>nyāya</s>) because it is the antidote to the defilements that are contrary to reality. [It overcomes] the distortions (<s>viparyāsa</s>) of permanence etc. due to the fault of not understanding reality...

body.text: duḥkhādisatyeṣvanityādayaḥ ṣoḍaśākārā laukikā lokottarāśca santi / tatra laukikā jñeye 'praviṣṭāḥ sāvaraṇāḥ savikalpāśca, tathatāyā aprativedhāt kleśānuśayitvādabhilāpamukhena prapañcanācca yathākramam / viparyayeṇa lokottarāḥ supraviṣṭā nirāvaraṇāśca santo nirvikalpatayā laukikebhyo viśiṣyante / kathaṃ punarete 'vikalpayanto jñeyeṣu praviṣṭā bhavanti / yasmādeteṣu vartamāno 'nityārtha paśyati sākṣādanubhavati, na tvanityamiti paśyatyabhilāpaprapañcamukheneti / evaṃ duḥkhādiṣvākāreṣu yojayitavyam //
body.translated_text: Regarding the truths of suffering etc., the sixteen aspects beginning with impermanence are both mundane (<s>laukika</s>) and supramundane (<s>lokottara</s>). Among these, the mundane [aspects] have not penetrated the knowable, are with obstructions (<s>sāvaraṇa</s>), and are with conceptualization (<s>savikalpa</s>)—because of not penetrating suchness (<s>tathatā</s>), because of being accompanied by the latent tendencies of defilements, and because of operating through designation...

body.text: dharmaviniścayo nāma tṛtīyaḥ samuccayaḥ
dharmaviniścaye dharmo dvādaśāṅgaṃ vacogatam //
body.translated_text: In the determination of <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmaviniścaya</s>): the <s>Dharma</s> is the twelve-fold spoken word (<s>dvādaśāṅga vacogata</s>).

body.text: tatra sūtraṃ yadabhipretārthasūcanākāreṇa gadyabhāṣitam / kiṃ punaḥ kāraṇaṃ tathāgatastamabhipretamartha vivṛtyaiva na deśayatītyāha daśānuśaṃsān saṃpaśyaṃstathāgataḥ sūcanākāreṇa dharmaṃ deśayati / sukhaṃ vyavasthāpayati, daiśikairhi, bahudhā vyavasthāpya prāpaṇīyasyārthasya, saṃkṣipyākṛcchreṇa vyavasthāpanāt / sukhaṃ deśayati, alpena mahato 'rthavistarasya pratyāyanāt, tadyathā sthāpayati saṃsthāpayatītyevamādi / śrotāpi sukhamudgṛhṇāti / dharmagauravatayā kṣipraṃ saṃbhārān paripūrayati, bhāvagamyo 'yaṃ dharma ityavagamya jātāsthasya tasmin dharme ādaramukhena śraddhādisaṃbhāraparipūraṇāt / āśu dharmatāṃ pratividhyati, tathādaraprayogiṇaḥ prajñāyāḥ taikṣṇībhāvāt / ratneṣvavetya prasādaṃ pratilabhate, deśanāyāḥ suvyavasthitabhāvagamena daiśikādiṣvabhiprasādotpādāt / paramadṛṣṭadharmasukhavihāraṃ spṛśati, abhiprāyārtha tīvreṇa yogena cintayitvā labdhavataḥ prāmodyaviśeṣādhigamāt / sāṃkathyaviniścayena satāṃ cittamārādhayati, gūḍhārthavivaraṇāt, ata eva paṇḍitaḥ paṇḍita iti saṃkhyāṃ gacchati, yaśo 'sya samantānniścaratītyarthaḥ / ubhayaṃ caitatpaścimasabhisamayaiko 'nuśaṃso draṣṭavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Among these, a <s>sūtra</s> is what is spoken in prose in the manner of indicating the intended meaning. Why does the <s>Tathāgata</s> not teach by simply revealing the intended meaning? He does so perceiving ten benefits—[therefore he teaches] in the manner of indication...

body.text: nītārtha sūtraṃ vyākaraṇam tena vivṛtyābhisaṃdhivyākaraṇāt //
body.translated_text: A <s>sūtra</s> of definitive meaning (<s>nītārtha</s>) is an 'explanation' (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>)—because through it, the hidden intention is revealed and explained.

body.text: udānaṃ yadāttamanaskenodāhṛtam tadyathā yadā ime prādurbhavanti dharmā ityevamādi //
body.translated_text: An 'inspired utterance' (<s>udāna</s>) is what is uttered by one with an uplifted mind—such as 'When these <s>dharmas</s> manifest...' and so forth.

body.text: nidānaṃ yatkiṃcideva pudgalamuddiśya bhāṣitaṃ sotpattikaśikṣā prajñaptikabhāṣitaṃ vā, tadyathāsminnidāne 'smin prakaraṇa iti vistaraḥ //
body.translated_text: A 'narrative occasion' (<s>nidāna</s>) is whatever is spoken with reference to a particular person, whether a spoken teaching with a specific originating occasion or a designation of training—as in 'on this occasion, on this topic' and so forth in detail.

body.text: avadānaṃ sadṛṣṭāntakaṃ bhāṣitam, tenārthavyavadānādabhivyañjanādityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: An 'illustration' (<s>avadāna</s>) is a spoken teaching with examples—because through it, the meaning is clarified through illustration; that is the meaning.

body.text: vaipulyaṃ vaidalyaṃ vaitulyamityete mahāyānasya paryāyāḥ, tadetatsaptavidhamahattvayogānmahattvayānamityucyate / saptavidhaṃ mahatvam - ālaṃbanamahattvaṃ śatasāhasrikādisūtrāparimitadeśanādharmā laṃbanādbodhisattvamārgasya / pratipattimahattvaṃ sakalasvaparārthapratipatteḥ / jñānamahatvaṃ pudgaladharmanairātmyajñānāt / vīryamahattvaṃ triṣu mahākalpāsaṃkhyeyeṣvanekaduṣkaraśatasahasraprayogāt / upāyakauśalyamahattvaṃ saṃsāranirvāṇāpratiṣṭhānāt / prāptimahattvaṃ valavaiśāradyāveṇikabuddhadharmādyaprameyāsaṃkhyeyaguṇādhigamāt / karmamahattvaṃ yāvatsaṃsārabodhyādisandarśanena buddhakāryānuṣṭhānāditi //
body.translated_text: <s>Vaipulya</s>, <s>vaidalya</s>, and <s>vaitulya</s> are synonyms for the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. This is called the 'great vehicle' (<s>mahāyāna</s>) because of its connection with sevenfold greatness. The sevenfold greatness is: greatness of object (<s>ālambana-mahattva</s>), [as in] the immeasurable <s>sūtras</s> of a hundred thousand [verses] and so forth...

body.text: upadeśo yatrāviparītena dharmalakṣaṇena sūtrādīnāmarthanirdeśaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Instruction' (<s>upadeśa</s>) is where the meaning of <s>sūtras</s> etc. is taught through the correct characteristic of <s>dharma</s>.

body.text: nidānaṃ sotpattikaśikṣāprajñaptibhāṣitasaṃgṛhītaṃ vinayapiṭakam, avadānādikaṃ tasya parivāro veditavyaḥ / adbhutadharmāṇāṃ bodhisattvasūtrapiṭake saṃgrahaṇam, teṣāṃ viśeṣeṇācintyodāraprabhāvaviśeṣayogāt / upadeśa ubhayatra śrāvakayāne mahāyāne cābhidharmapiṭakam //
body.translated_text: The <s>nidāna</s> [category] includes the <s>Vinaya Piṭaka</s>, which comprises spoken teachings with originating occasions and designations of training; and <s>avadāna</s> and the like should be understood as its supplement. The inclusion of 'marvelous <s>dharmas</s>' (<s>adbhutadharma</s>) in the <s>Bodhisattva Sūtra Piṭaka</s> is because they especially [contain] inconceivable and wondrous [events]...

body.text: sūtrapiṭakavyavasthānaṃ vicikitsopakleśapratipakṣeṇa vineyānāmutpannānutpannasaṃśayacchedādhikāreṇa sūtrageyādi deśanāt / vinayapiṭakavyavasthānamantadvayānuyogopakleśapratipakṣeṇa, saṃnidhikāraparibhogādipratikṣepāt śatasāhasrakavastrānujñānācca / antadvayaṃ punaḥ kāmasukhallikānta ātmaklemathāntaśca / abhidharmavyavasthānaṃ svayaṃdṛṣṭiparāmarśopakleśapratipakṣeṇa, tatra vistareṇa dharmalakṣaṇasthāpanāt //
body.translated_text: The establishment of the <s>Sūtra Piṭaka</s> is through the teaching of <s>sūtra</s>, verse (<s>geya</s>), etc. as the antidote to the secondary defilement of doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>), for the purpose of cutting the arisen and unarisen doubts of those to be trained. The establishment of the <s>Vinaya Piṭaka</s> is as the antidote to the secondary defilement of pursuing the two extremes...

body.text: punaḥ sūtrapiṭakaṃ niśritya vineyāḥ śikṣātraye vyutpadyante, tatra tasya vistareṇodbhāvitatvāt / vinayaṃ niśrityādhiśīlamadhicittaṃ śikṣāṃ niṣpādayanti, tatra prātimokṣasaṃvaraśikṣāmārgopadeśaniśrayeṇa śīlapariśodhanāttatpariśuddhikṛtāvipratisārādyānupūrvyā ca cittasamādhānāt / abhidharmaniśrityādhiprajñaṃ śikṣāṃ niṣpādayanti, tatra vistareṇa dharmapravicayopāyopadeśāditi ato 'pi piṭakatrayavyavasthānam //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, relying on the <s>Sūtra Piṭaka</s>, those to be trained gain understanding in the threefold training (<s>śikṣātraya</s>), because it is set forth therein in detail. Relying on the <s>Vinaya</s>, they accomplish the training in higher morality (<s>adhiśīla</s>) and the training in higher mind (<s>adhicitta</s>)—because the training in the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> discipline...

body.text: punaḥ sūtrapiṭakaṃ niśritya granthārthavyutpattiḥ / vinayaṃ niśritya tadubhayasākṣātkriyā, śikṣāpratipattiprabhāvi[ta]tvādvinayasya / tato dharmārthayoḥ sākṣātkriyāyāḥ padasthānamityucyate āśrayārthena / abhidharmaṃ niśritya parasparaṃ sāṃkathyaviniścayakṛtena dharmasaṃbhogena sparśavihāro bhavati, tatra bahuprakāraṃ dharmāṇāṃ svalakṣaṇādidharmatāyā vyutpādanāt //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, relying on the <s>Sūtra Piṭaka</s>, there is understanding of the meaning of texts. Relying on the <s>Vinaya</s>, there is direct realization of both [text and meaning]—because the <s>Vinaya</s> is brought about through the practice of training. Therefore, the standing-ground for direct realization of <s>Dharma</s> and meaning...

body.text: etānyeva trīṇi piṭakāni caturaśītidharmaskandhasahasrāṇi bhavanti, śrāvakayānādhikāreṇa yāni sthavirānandenodgṛhītāni // kiṃ punarekasya dharmaskandha[sya] parimāṇam / daśaśatasaṃkhyo dharmaskandhaḥ sahasrasaṃkhya ityarthaḥ / yadyevaṃ sahasrasaṃkhya ityevaṃ ki nocyate / sāhasrikaikaskandhavyavasthāne prayojanajñāpanārtham / tathāhyekādivṛddhayā daśasaṃkhyā śatasaṃkhyā sahasrādisaṃkhyāḥ / taddaśaśatasaṃkhyā upaniṣado draṣṭavyāḥ / tadyathā daśa śatāni sahasram, śataṃ sahasrāṇāṃ śatasahasram, śataṃ śatasahasrāṇāṃ koṭirityevaṃ sarvāsūttarāsu saṃkhyāsvavaśyamanayoḥ daśaśatasaṃkhyayoranyataropaniṣadbhavati / ata ete eva samasya daśaśatānyeko dharmaskandho vyavasthāpyate / anayā ca gaṇanayā caturaśītidharmaskandhasahasrāṇyaṣṭau koṭyaḥ catvāriśacca lakṣā bhavanti //
body.translated_text: These very three <s>piṭakas</s> (baskets) constitute eighty-four thousand aggregates of <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmaskandha</s>), with reference to the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s>, which were taken up by the elder <s>Ānanda</s>. What then is the measure of one <s>dharmaskandha</s>? A composition of a thousand syllables...

body.text: sa eṣa piṭakatrayasaṃgṛhīto dharmaḥ kasya gocaraḥ / śrutamayādīnāṃ cittacaitasikānāṃ gocara ālaṃbanamityarthaḥ /
body.translated_text: This <s>Dharma</s> included in the three <s>piṭakas</s>—whose domain is it? It is the domain, i.e., the object-support (<s>ālambana</s>), of the mind and mental factors (<s>citta-caitasika</s>) [arising from wisdom] born of learning (<s>śrutamaya</s>) and so forth.

body.text: etatprasaṃgena sālaṃbanādilakṣaṇānāṃ cittacaitasikānāṃ dharmamārabhyālaṃbanādikaṃ vyavasthāpyate / tatra dharme teṣāṃ kimālaṃbanam / sūtrādi nāmapadavyañjanakāyasaṃgṛhītā
body.translated_text: In this connection, the object-support etc. of the mind and mental factors whose characteristic is having an object-support (<s>sālambana</s>) etc. is established with respect to <s>Dharma</s>. Among these, what is their object-support with respect to <s>Dharma</s>? [It is] the <s>sūtra</s> etc. included in the collection of name-words, words, and syllables (<s>nāmapadavyañjanakāya</s>).

body.text: sūtrādideśanetyarthaḥ / ākāraḥ, yān skandhādīnartha prakārānārabhya sā deśanā, tadākārāste cittacaitasikā veditavyāḥ / āśrayaḥ paravijñaptismṛtirvāsanā ca / tatra deśanākāle paravijñaptirāśrayo yo 'sāvucyate parato ghoṣata iti tata uttarakālaṃ smṛtirāśrayo yathāśrutamanusmṛtyābhyasanāt / tata uttarakālaṃ vāsanāśrayastadanusmṛtimantareṇāpi paścādabhyāsabhāvanābalena pratibhāsanāditi / saṃprayogaḥ cittacaitasikānāmanyonyasahāyabhāvena sūtrādyālaṃbane skandhādipratisaṃyuktārthākāraiḥ saṃpratipattiḥ //
body.translated_text: meaning: the teaching of <s>sūtras</s> and so forth. The aspect (<s>ākāra</s>) refers to the modes of meaning such as <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) and so forth with reference to which that teaching is given — those aspects of <s>citta</s> (mind) and <s>caitasikas</s> (mental factors) should be understood. The basis (<s>āśraya</s>) is the communication of others (<s>paravijñapti</s>), memory (<s>smṛti</s>), and habitual impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>). Among these, at the time of teaching, the communication of others is the basis — this is what is called 'from others, from sound'; then at a subsequent time, memory is the basis, due to recollecting and practicing what was heard; then at a still later time, habitual impression is the basis, since even without that recollection, appearances arise later through the force of repeated cultivation. The conjunction (<s>saṃprayoga</s>) is the mutual engagement of <s>citta</s> and <s>caitasikas</s> with one another as companions, through aspects of meaning connected with <s>skandhas</s> and so forth, with respect to the objects such as <s>sūtras</s> and so on.

body.text: qharme ālaṃbana prabhedo vyāpyālaṃbanādikaścaturvidhaḥ /
body.translated_text: The classification of objects (<s>ālambana</s>) in <s>dharmas</s> is fourfold, beginning with the pervaded object (<s>vyāpyālambana</s>).

body.text: vyāpyālaṃbanaṃ punaḥ savikalpapratibimbādibhedena caturbidham / tatra adhimuktimanaskāra ekāntalaukiko yo manaskāraḥ / tattvamanaskāro lokottarastatpṛṣṭhalabdhaśca / yāvadbhāvikatayā dharmāṇāmetāvanti sarvadharmavastuni yajjñeyavyavasthānam tadyathā skandhadhātvāyatanāni / yathāvadbhāvikatayā ebhiḥ prakāraiḥ sujñeyamiti / tadyathā satyamukhena tānyeva skandhadhātvāyatanāni yathāsaṃbhavaṃ duḥkhatojñeyāni yāvanmārgataḥ / ākāramukhenaikaikaṃ satyaṃ caturbhirākārairjñeyam, aviśeṣataśca sarvāṇi tathatākāreṇa / dharmoddānādhikāreṇa vānityataḥ sarvasaṃskārā jñeyā yāvacchāntato nirvāṇam / vimokṣādhikāreṇa vā śūnyato yāvadanimitta[ta] iti // kāryapariniṣpattirāśrayapariniṣpattiḥ, parinivṛttāśrayasyāviparītālaṃbanasaṃprakhyānāt / yathāvadbhāvikatāyā nirdaśe ṣoḍaśaprakārā uktāstrayaśca vimokṣākārāḥ teṣāṃ cānyonyasaṃgrahaḥ / katha kṛtvā / ṣoḍaśānāmākārāṇāṃ dvau śūnyatākārau - śūnyākārānātmākāraśca / ṣaḍapraṇihitākārāḥ - anityākārā duḥkhākāro hetusamudayaprabhavapratyayākārāśca, taistraidhātuke 'praṇidhānāt / aṣṭāvinimittākārāḥ śeṣāḥ nirodhamārgayornimittīkartumaśakyatvāt //
body.translated_text: The pervaded object (<s>vyāpyālambana</s>) is again fourfold, through the distinction of conceptual reflection-images (<s>savikalpapratibimba</s>) and so forth. Among these, the mental engagement of conviction (<s>adhimuktimanaskāra</s>) is exclusively mundane. The mental engagement of reality (<s>tattvamanaskāra</s>) is supramundane and that obtained subsequently. As regards the extent of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>yāvadbhāvikatā</s>), the determination of the knowable with respect to all <s>dharma</s>-objects is of such-and-such extent — namely, the <s>skandhas</s>, <s>dhātus</s>, and <s>āyatanas</s>. As regards their nature as they truly are (<s>yathāvadbhāvikatā</s>), they are easily known through these modes — namely, through the approach of the truths, those very <s>skandhas</s>, <s>dhātus</s>, and <s>āyatanas</s> are to be known as suffering and so forth up to the path, as applicable. Through the approach of aspects, each truth is to be known through four aspects, and without distinction, all are to be known through the aspect of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness). Or through the topic of the <s>dharma</s>-summary (<s>dharmoddāna</s>), all conditioned things are to be known as impermanent, and so forth up to <s>nirvāṇa</s> as peace. Or through the topic of liberation, as emptiness and so forth up to signlessness. The accomplishment of the result is the accomplishment of the basis, because one whose basis has been transformed has an undistorted apprehension of objects. In the exposition of <s>yathāvadbhāvikatā</s>, sixteen modes and three liberation-aspects (<s>vimokṣākāra</s>) have been stated, along with their mutual inclusion. How so? Of the sixteen aspects, two are emptiness-aspects — the aspect of emptiness and the aspect of non-self. Six are the non-aspiration aspects (<s>apraṇihitākāra</s>) — the aspects of impermanence, suffering, cause, origination, arising, and condition, since through these one does not aspire toward the three realms. The remaining eight are signlessness-aspects, since cessation and the path cannot be made into signs.

body.text: caritaviśodhanamālaṃbanaṃ rāgacaritādīnāmaśubhādi, tenotsadarāgādyupaśamanāt //
body.translated_text: The object for purifying conduct (<s>caritaviśodhana</s>) is the meditation on the impure (<s>aśubha</s>) and so forth for those of lustful temperament (<s>rāgacarita</s>) and others, since thereby the prominent lust and other afflictions are pacified.

body.text: avidyādayo dharmāḥ saṃskārādīndharmānabhiṣyandayanti, na hyeṣāṃ nirhetuka utpādo nāpīśvarādiviṣamahetuka iti yajjñānamidaṃ pratītyasamutpādakauśalyam /
body.translated_text: Ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) and other <s>dharmas</s> cause the flowing forth of <s>dharmas</s> such as formations (<s>saṃskāras</s>) and so forth — for their arising is neither without cause nor from an unequal cause such as <s>Īśvara</s> (God) and the like. The knowledge of this is skill in dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpādakauśalya</s>).

body.text: dharmamātrahetukatve 'pi satyanurūpāddhetoranurūpasyaiva phalasyotpattiḥ, tadyathā sucaritasyeṣṭo vipāko duścaritasyāniṣṭa ityevamādi yajjñānamidaṃ sthānāsthānakauśalyaṃ veditavyam //
body.translated_text: Even though causation is solely by <s>dharmas</s>, from a cause conforming to reality, only a conforming result arises — for example, the <s>vipāka</s> (fruition) of good conduct is pleasant, and of bad conduct is unpleasant, and so forth. The knowledge of this should be understood as skill in the tenable and untenable (<s>sthānāsthānakauśalya</s>).

body.text: kleśaviśodhanamālaṃbanaṃ laukikamārgādhikāreṇādhaūrdhvabhūmīnāmaudārikaśāntatā, tena paryavasthānaviṣkambhaṇāt / lokottaramārgādhikāreṇa samāsatastathatā, vyāsena catvāryāryasatyāni, tenānuśayasamudghātāt //
body.translated_text: The object for purifying afflictions (<s>kleśaviśodhana</s>): in the domain of the mundane path, it is the coarseness and peacefulness of the lower and higher levels, since thereby the manifest afflictions (<s>paryavasthāna</s>) are suppressed. In the domain of the supramundane path, in brief it is <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), and in detail, the four noble truths, since thereby the latent afflictions (<s>anuśaya</s>) are eradicated.

body.text: sūtrādidharmavicārāṇāṃ saṃbnadhena catasro yuktayo varṇyante, tābhistadvicāraṇāt // tatra apekṣāyuktiryā saṃskārāṇāmutpattau pratyayāpekṣā, tadyathāṅkurasyotpattau bījodakakṣetrāṇyapekṣyante, vijñānasyendriyārthamanaskārā ityevamādi / kāryakāraṇayuktistadyathā cakṣurādīnāṃ cakṣurvijñānādyāśrayabhāvaḥ rūpādīnāmālaṃbanabhāvaḥ, cakṣurvijñānādīnāṃ rūpādiprativijñāpanam, suvarṇakārādīnāṃ ca śilpināṃ suvarṇādighaṭanamityevamādi / upapattisādhanayuktisvabhāvaviśeṣasaṃgṛhītasya sādhyasyārthasya pratyakṣādipramāṇāviruddhaḥ pratijñādyupadeśaḥ / dharmatāyuktistadyathāgninā dāhaḥ, udakena kleda ityevamādikā prasiddhā dharmāṇāṃ dharmatā / yathoktaṃ cakṣuḥ samṛddhaṃ śūnyaṃ nityena yāvadātmīyena / tatkasya hetoḥ / prakṛtirasyaiṣeti //
body.translated_text: In connection with the investigation of <s>dharmas</s> in <s>sūtras</s> and so forth, four types of reasoning (<s>yukti</s>) are described, since investigation is conducted through them. Among these, the reasoning of dependence (<s>apekṣāyukti</s>) is the dependence on conditions for the arising of conditioned things — for example, for the arising of a sprout, seed, water, and soil are required; for consciousness, sense-faculty, object, and mental engagement, and so forth. The reasoning of cause and effect (<s>kāryakāraṇayukti</s>) is, for example: the eye and other faculties serve as the basis for eye-consciousness and so forth; forms and other objects serve as the objective support; eye-consciousness and so forth cognize forms and so forth; and goldsmiths and other craftsmen fashion gold and other materials, and so forth. The reasoning of proof by establishment (<s>upapattisādhanayukti</s>) is the instruction through propositions and so forth, not contradicted by means of valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>) such as direct perception and so forth, regarding a subject to be established that is included in a particular nature. The reasoning of the nature of things (<s>dharmatāyukti</s>) is, for example: burning by fire, moistening by water — such is the well-known nature of <s>dharmas</s>. As it is said: 'The eye, being complete, is empty of permanence, and so forth up to empty of selfhood. For what reason? Because this is its nature.'

body.text: nāmaparyeṣaṇā nāmakāyādīnāṃ prajñaptisattvādapariniṣpannameṣāṃ svalakṣaṇamiti yā vicāraṇā / vastuparyeṣaṇā skandhādīnāṃ tathāpariniṣpattiryathā nāmakāyādibhirabhilapyanta iti yā saṃtīraṇā parīkṣaṇetyarthaḥ / svabhāvaprajñaptiparyeṣaṇā yābhidhānābhidheyasaṃbandhe svabhāvaprajñaptimātrasya vyavahāranimittatvena saṃtīraṇā / abhidhānābhidheyasaṃbandhaḥ / punaranyonyasaṃpratyayanimittatvam / tathāhi vyutpannavyavahārasyābhidhānamātraṃ śrutvā tadabhidheye saṃpratyaya utpadyate smṛtimukhena, abhidheyaṃ vā punarupalabhya tadabhidhāne / ityevaṃvidhe saṃbandhe prasiddhe cakṣurityevamādisvalakṣaṇaprajñaptimātraṃ tadākhyāmāsapiṇḍādivyavahārasya nimittaṃ bhavatīti yā parīkṣeyamucyate svabhāvaprajñaptiparyeṣaṇā / viśeṣaprajñaptiparyeṣaṇā yā tathaivābhidhānābhidheyasaṃbandhe
body.translated_text: The investigation of names (<s>nāmaparyeṣaṇā</s>) is the examination that, since name-groups (<s>nāmakāya</s>) and so forth are merely designations (<s>prajñapti</s>), their intrinsic characteristics are not ultimately established. The investigation of things (<s>vastuparyeṣaṇā</s>) is the scrutiny and examination that <s>skandhas</s> and so forth are not ultimately established in the way they are expressed by name-groups and so forth. The investigation of the designation of intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāvaprajñaptiparyeṣaṇā</s>) is the scrutiny that, in the relation between expression (<s>abhidhāna</s>) and the expressed (<s>abhidheya</s>), the mere designation of intrinsic nature serves as the basis for conventional usage. The relation between expression and expressed is further this: it serves as the basis for mutual understanding. For indeed, when one versed in convention hears merely an expression, understanding of the expressed object arises through memory; or conversely, upon perceiving the expressed object, understanding of its expression arises. When such a relation is established, the mere designation of intrinsic characteristics such as 'eye' and so forth becomes the basis for conventions such as naming, compounding, and so forth — the examination of this is called the investigation of the designation of intrinsic nature. The investigation of the designation of distinctions (<s>viśeṣaprajñaptiparyeṣaṇā</s>) is that which, likewise in the relation between expression and expressed,

body.text: nityānityottarānuttararūpyasanidarśanānidarśanatādiviśeṣalakṣaṇaprajñaptimātrasya vyavahāranimittatā saṃtīraṇā //
body.translated_text: examines the fact that the mere designation of distinguishing characteristics such as permanent and impermanent, higher and lower, material and immaterial, with-obstruction and without-obstruction, and so forth, serves as the basis for conventional usage.

body.text: catvāri yathābhūtaparijñānāni yathāparyeṣitāni nāmādyanupalabdhijñānāni //
body.translated_text: The four knowledges of things as they truly are (<s>yathābhūtaparijñāna</s>) are the knowledges of the non-apprehension of names and so forth, corresponding to the investigations.

body.text: samādhiprayuktasya yogabhūmiḥ pañcākārādhārādiḥ / tatra ādhāro yādṛśaṃ bāhuśrutyaṃ śamathavipaśyanayoḥ pratiṣṭhā bhavatyālaṃbanayogena tadādhāra ityucyate / tatpunaḥ saṃbhṛtasaṃbhārasya satyābhisamayamadhikṛtyodgṛhītaṃ yatsūtrādikaṃ śrutam / ādhānaṃ tadālaṃbano yoniśomanaskāraḥ, tena tasmin bāhuśrutye 'viparītārthacittākāreṇa cittākaraṇāt / ādarśastadbāhuśrutyālaṃbanaḥ sahanimittena samādhiḥ, jñeyavastusabhāgapratibimbākāra ityarthaḥ / ādarśatvaṃ punarasya tena jñeyabimbaparīkṣaṇādveditavyam / āloko grāhyagrāhakānupalabdhijñānaṃ darśanamārgasaṃgṛhītaṃ pratyakṣavṛttitvāditi / kathaṃ ca punaḥ bodhisattva ekasyāṃ yaugabhūmau prayukto nopalambhaṃ spṛśati saṃbhṛtapuṇyajñāna saṃbhāro bodhisattvaḥ kalpāsaṃkhyeyaniryātastathāprativedhānukūlaṃ śrutaṃ yoniśomanasikurvan samādhiṃ niṣpādayati / sa evaṃ samāhite citte yajjñeyapratibimbaṃ, niśritya dhyāyati tattasmātsamāhitāccittādananyaditi saṃpaśyaṃstasmin pratibimbe viṣayasaṃjñāṃ vyāvartya tadākāraṃ svasaṃjñāmātramavadhārayati / tadā cāsau svacittamātrāvasthānādadhyātma sthitacitto bhavan sarvathā grāhyabhāvaṃ prativedayate / tataśca grāhyābhāvādgrāhakamapi na pariniṣpannamiti tasyāpyabhāvaṃ parivedayate / tataḥ pratyātmaṃ tadubhayasvabhāvopalambhāpagatamanupalambhamadhigacchati / etadeva cādhikṛtyoktaṃ bhagavatā pratibimbaṃ manaḥ paśyanniti vistaraḥ / āśrayaḥ āśrayaparivṛttiḥ, dauṣṭhulyāpagamātpariśuddha āśraya ityarthaḥ / sā ceyaṃ yogabhūmirhetutaḥ phalataśca nirdiṣṭā veditavyā / tatrādhārādibhiścaturbhirhetunirdeśaḥ paścimenaikena phalanirdeśa iti //
body.translated_text: The ground of yoga (<s>yogabhūmi</s>) for one engaged in <s>samādhi</s> has five aspects beginning with the foundation (<s>ādhāra</s>). Among these, the foundation is whatever extensive learning (<s>bāhuśrutya</s>) becomes the basis for <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) through connection with the object — that is called the foundation. Furthermore, it is the <s>sūtras</s> and other scriptures that have been learned and taken up with respect to the realization of the truths by one who has accumulated the requisites. The placing (<s>ādhāna</s>) is the proper mental engagement (<s>yoniśomanaskāra</s>) directed toward that object, since through it the mind is directed toward that extensive learning with an undistorted mental aspect regarding the meaning. The mirror (<s>ādarśa</s>) is the <s>samādhi</s> directed toward that extensive learning together with its signs — meaning an image-aspect resembling the knowable object. Its mirror-nature should be understood from the fact that through it one examines the reflected image of the knowable. The light (<s>āloka</s>) is the knowledge of the non-apprehension of grasped and grasper, included in the path of seeing, since it functions as direct perception. And how does a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, engaged in a single ground of yoga, touch non-apprehension? A <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has accumulated the requisites of merit and knowledge, having emerged from incalculable <s>kalpas</s>, properly attending to what has been learned in conformity with such penetration, brings <s>samādhi</s> to completion. When his mind is thus concentrated, relying on whatever reflected image of the knowable arises, he meditates, and seeing that it is not different from that concentrated mind, he turns away from the perception of an external object with respect to that reflection, and ascertains its aspect as merely his own cognition (<s>svasaṃjñāmātra</s>). Then, abiding in the state of his own mind alone (<s>svacittamātra</s>), being one whose mind is established inwardly, he realizes the complete absence of the grasped (<s>grāhya</s>). Then, since the grasped does not exist, the grasper (<s>grāhaka</s>) too is not established, and he realizes its absence as well. Thereupon, he attains non-apprehension (<s>anupalambha</s>), free from the perception of both natures as they pertain to oneself. With reference to this very point, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Seeing the reflection, the mind...' and so forth in detail. The basis (<s>āśraya</s>) is the transformation of the basis (<s>āśrayaparivṛtti</s>) — meaning the basis is purified through the removal of afflictive obstructions (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>). This ground of yoga should be understood as taught from the standpoint of both cause and result. Among these, the teaching of cause is through the first four beginning with the foundation, and the teaching of result is through the last one.

body.text: yaduktaṃ sthavirānandena - pañcabhirāyuṣmañchāriputradharmaiḥ samanvāgato bhikṣurlaghu ca gṛhṇātītyatra sūtre taireva pañcabhirdharmairlaghugrahaṇādīni catvāri yathāyogaṃ veditavyāni / catvāri kathaṃ kṛtvā / dharmakuśalo laghu gṛhṇāti bāhuśrutyātprāyeṇa bhinnapadavyañjanatayā / arthakuśalo bahu gṛhṇāti, abhidharmādilakṣaṇajñatvāt, skandhadhātvādikathāvastvadhikāreṇa prabhūtagranthasaṃkalanataḥ / vyañjanakuśalo niruktikulaśca sūdgṛhītaṃ gṛhṇāti, suniruktavyañjanajñatvādātmātmeti janapadaniruktimanabhiniviśyānuvyavahārajñatvācca granthārthayoraviparotagrahaṇataḥ / pūrvāntāparāntānusaṃdhikuśala udgṛhītaṃ na nāśayati, pūrvamudgahītāndharmānniśritya paścānniḥsartavyamiti buddhābhisaṃdhijñatvādadhigamena tatsārādānataḥ //
body.translated_text: Regarding what the elder <s>Ānanda</s> stated — 'Endowed with five qualities, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bhikṣu</s> grasps quickly' — in this <s>sūtra</s>, the four qualities beginning with quick grasping should be understood as corresponding to those very five qualities. How are there four? One skilled in <s>dharmas</s> grasps quickly, since through extensive learning the words and syllables are mostly distinct. One skilled in meaning grasps much, since knowing the characteristics of <s>Abhidharma</s> and so forth, he compiles extensive texts organized by the topics of <s>skandhas</s>, <s>dhātus</s>, and other categories. One skilled in expression and proficient in etymology (<s>nirukti</s>) grasps what has been learned well, since knowing well-analyzed expressions, and knowing conventional usage without being attached to regional etymologies as 'self, self' — thereby grasping text and meaning without distortion. One skilled in connecting the earlier and later portions does not lose what has been learned, since knowing the <s>Buddha</s>'s intention that one should proceed further based on <s>dharmas</s> previously learned — thereby extracting the essence through realization.

body.text: dharmavihārī bhikṣurdharmavihāri bhikṣuriti bhadantocyata ityatra sūtre bhagavatā samastena śrutacintābhāvanāvihāreṇa dharmavihāro bhavati, nānyataraprayogamātreṇeti saṃdarśitam / tatra paryāptisvādhyāyadeśanābahulā vitarkaṇā bahulāścetyanena kevalaṃ śrutacintāprayuktā na bhāvanāprayuktā yogādiriñcanādato [na] dharmavihāriṇo vyavasthāpyante / yo 'pi kaścicchrutacintāmanāgamya kevalaṃ bhāvanāprayuktaḥ syātso 'pi na dharmavihārī vyavasthāpyate / tata eva tāvaddharmavihāriṇaṃ bhikṣumārabhya iha tu bhikṣurddharmaṃ paryāpnoti sūtraṃ geyamiti vistareṇoktvā paścādāha na riñcati yogamityevamādi, yathā vijñāyeta śrutaṃ cintāṃ bhāvanāṃ cāgamya tadubhayavihāreṇa dharmavihārīti / na riñcati yogamityevamādinā samādhiprayogāsaṃtuṣṭibhyāṃ bhāvanāmayaṃ saṃdarśitam / samādhiprayogaḥ
body.translated_text: Regarding the <s>sūtra</s> where it is said, 'A <s>bhikṣu</s> who dwells in the <s>Dharma</s>, a <s>bhikṣu</s> who dwells in the <s>Dharma</s>, venerable one' — the <s>Bhagavān</s> has shown that one becomes a <s>Dharma</s>-dweller through the complete practice of dwelling in hearing (<s>śruta</s>), reflection (<s>cintā</s>), and meditation (<s>bhāvanā</s>), not merely through the practice of one alone. There, by the statement 'one who is devoted to thorough study, teaching, and discursive thinking' — those who are engaged only in hearing and reflection but not in meditation practice, who abandon the yoga and so forth, are not established as <s>Dharma</s>-dwellers. And one who, without relying on hearing and reflection, is engaged solely in meditation practice — he too is not established as a <s>Dharma</s>-dweller. Therefore, beginning with the <s>Dharma</s>-dwelling <s>bhikṣu</s>, it is said in detail: 'Here a <s>bhikṣu</s> learns the <s>Dharma</s> — <s>sūtra</s>, <s>geya</s>,' and so forth, and then afterwards it says, 'He does not abandon the yoga,' and so on — so that it may be understood that one is a <s>Dharma</s>-dweller through dwelling in both hearing-and-reflection and meditation. By 'he does not abandon the yoga' and so forth, the meditation-born practice is shown through the practice of <s>samādhi</s>

body.text: punardvividhaḥ saṃdarśitaḥ sātatyasatkṛtyaprayogasaṃgṛhītaśca na riñcati yogamityanena, aviparīta[pra]yogasaṃgṛhītaśca na riñcati manaskāramityanena / asaṃtuṣṭirna riñcatyadhyātmacetaḥ śamathamityanena saṃdarśitā, tadanāsvādanāduttaraśamathaprayogāccāsyāriñcanaṃ veditavyam //
body.translated_text: and non-complacency. [The <s>samādhi</s> practice] is shown as twofold: that included in continuous and earnest practice, shown by 'he does not abandon the yoga'; and that included in correct practice, shown by 'he does not abandon mental engagement (<s>manaskāra</s>).' Non-complacency is shown by 'he does not abandon the inner calming of the mind' — this non-abandonment should be understood as arising from not savoring that attainment and from the practice of higher calm abiding.

body.text: kena kāraṇena vaipulyaṃ sūtrāntare bodhisattvapāramitāpiṭakamityucyate / tatra pāramitānāṃ saṃkhyānirdeśādyāvadanyonyaviniścayanācca //
body.translated_text: For what reason is the <s>Vaipulya</s> (extensive) scripture called the <s>Bodhisattva-pāramitā-piṭaka</s> (Collection of the Bodhisattva Perfections)? Because therein the enumeration of the <s>pāramitās</s> is taught, and so forth up to their mutual determination.

body.text: tatra saṃkhyā dvividhā, gaṇanāsaṃkhyā tanmātrasaṃkhyā ca / ṣaṭpāramitā iti gaṇanāsaṃkhyā / sarvākārayorvodhisattvābhyudayaniḥśreyasamārgayostisṛbhistisṛbhiśca saṃgrahāt ṣaḍevapāramitā na bhūyasyo nālpoyasya itīyaṃ tanmātrasaṃkhyā //
body.translated_text: There the enumeration is twofold: the enumeration by counting and the enumeration of just that measure. 'Six <s>pāramitās</s>' — this is the enumeration by counting. Because the two paths of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> — worldly prosperity (<s>abhyudaya</s>) and the supreme good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>) — are encompassed in all their aspects by three and three respectively, there are exactly six <s>pāramitās</s>, neither more nor fewer — this is the enumeration of just that measure.

body.text: trividho 'bhyudayo mahābhogatā mahātmatā mahāpakṣatā ca / tatra dānapāramitāyā mahābhogatā phalam / śīlapāramitāyā mahātmatā phalam, śīlena sugatātmabhāvasaṃpattipratilambhāt / kṣāntipāramitāyā mahāpakṣatā phalam, kṣāntyā sarvajanābhigamanoyatāpratilambhāditi //
body.translated_text: Worldly prosperity (<s>abhyudaya</s>) is threefold: great wealth (<s>mahābhogatā</s>), greatness of self (<s>mahātmatā</s>), and a great retinue (<s>mahāpakṣatā</s>). Among these, the fruit of the perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>) is great wealth. The fruit of the perfection of moral discipline (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>) is greatness of self, since through moral discipline one obtains an excellent personal existence. The fruit of the perfection of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>) is a great retinue, since through patience one obtains the quality of being approachable by all people.

body.text: trividho niḥśreyasamārgaḥ - kleśamabhibhūya kuśalapakṣaprayogopāyaḥ, sattvaparipācanopāyaḥ, buddhadharmasamudānayanopāyaśca, eṣāmanyatareṇāpi vinā bodhisattvasya niḥśreyasānupapatteḥ / tatra sattvaparipācanopāyo dhyānapāramitā, tatsaṃniśrayeṇābhijñābhiḥ sattvaparipācanāt //
body.translated_text: The path to the supreme good (<s>niḥśreyasamārga</s>) is threefold: the means of overcoming afflictions and applying oneself to the wholesome, the means of maturing beings (<s>sattvaparipācana</s>), and the means of bringing about the qualities of a <s>Buddha</s> — since without any one of these, the supreme good of a <s>Bodhisattva</s> is impossible. Among these, the means of maturing beings is the perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>), since through reliance on it, beings are matured through the superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>).

body.text: punarapratiṣṭhitanirvāṇopāyataḥ ṣaḍeva pāramitāḥ / bodhisattvena hi nirvāṇapratiṣṭhāviparyayeṇa saṃsāre 'bhyudayaḥ parigrahītavyaḥ / saṃsārapratiṣṭhāviparyayeṇa tasminnasaṃkleṣṭavyam / atastisro 'bhyudayalābhopāyāstisrastadasaṃkleśopāyā yathāyogaṃ pūrvānusāreṇaiva veditavyāḥ / asaṃkleśopāye tu vīryeṇa pratipakṣabhāvanā, dhyānena kleśaviṣkambhaṇam, prajñayā kleśānuśayasamudghāta iti //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, from the standpoint of the means to non-abiding <s>nirvāṇa</s> (<s>apratiṣṭhitanirvāṇa</s>), there are exactly six <s>pāramitās</s>. For a <s>Bodhisattva</s> must embrace worldly prosperity in <s>saṃsāra</s> by way of the reverse of abiding in <s>nirvāṇa</s>, and must not be defiled in it by way of the reverse of abiding in <s>saṃsāra</s>. Therefore, the three means of obtaining worldly prosperity and the three means of non-defilement therein should be understood in the same order as before. With regard to the means of non-defilement: through vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), the cultivation of the antidote; through meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), the suppression of afflictions; through wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), the eradication of latent afflictions (<s>kleśānuśaya</s>).

body.text: sarvānugrahatāṃ kleśapratipakṣatāṃ copā[dā]yetyaparaḥ paryāyaḥ / tatra dānena bodhisattvaḥ sattvānupakaraṇopasaṃhārānugraheṇānugṛhṇāti / śīlena vighātotpīḍāviheṭhākaraṇenānugṛhṇāti, yathākramaṃ bhogakāyacittopaghātānupasaṃhārāt / kṣāntyā vighātotpīḍāviheṭhāmarṣaṇenānugṛhṇāti, parebhya ātmano bhogādyupaghātasahanāt / ābhistisṛbhiranugṛhṇāti // vīryeṇāviṣkambhitakleśo 'pi kuśalapakṣe
body.translated_text: Another explanation is based on benefiting all beings and counteracting afflictions. There, through giving (<s>dāna</s>), a <s>Bodhisattva</s> benefits beings by providing them with material support and assistance. Through moral discipline (<s>śīla</s>), he benefits them by not causing harm, oppression, or injury — since he refrains from damaging their possessions, bodies, and minds, respectively. Through patience (<s>kṣānti</s>), he benefits them by forbearing harm, oppression, and injury — since he endures damage to his own possessions and so forth from others. Through these three, he provides benefit. Through vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), even though afflictions have not yet been suppressed, in the wholesome domain

body.text: prayujyate / dhyānena kleśaṃ viṣkambhayati / prajñayānuśayaṃ samudghātayati / imāstisraḥ kleśapratipakṣā veditavyā //
body.translated_text: one applies oneself. Through <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), one suppresses the defilements. Through <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), one eradicates the latent tendencies. These three should be understood as antidotes to defilements.

body.text: tatra pāramitālakṣaṇam / bodhisattvasya dānapāramitā katamā / yadbodhisattvasya bodhisattvadharmatāyāṃ vyavasthitasya bodhicittaṃ niśritya karuṇāpuraḥsareṇa cetasā sarvāstiparityāge kāyavāṅmanaskarma / evaṃ ca kṛtvā dānapāramitāyāḥ lakṣaṇaṃ gotrataḥ praṇidhānata āśayato vastutaḥ svabhāvataśca nirdiṣṭaṃ veditavyam / tadyathā bodhisattvadharmatā gotram, bodhicittaṃ praṇidhānam, karuṇāpuraḥsaraṃ ceta āśayaḥ, sarvāstiparityāgo vastu, kāyavāṅmanaskarmasvabhāva ityevaṃ yāvat prajñāpāramitā vistareṇa veditavyāḥ / ayaṃ tu viśeṣaḥ / śīlakṣāntivīryapāramitāsu yathākramaṃ sarvasaṃvarasamādānānurakṣāyāṃ sarvāpakāraduḥkhamarṣaṇādhivāsanāyāṃ sarvakuśaladharmasamudānayanatāyāṃ yatkāyavāṅmanaskarmeti veditavyam / dhyānapāramitāyāṃ sarvākārakāyavāṅmanaskarmavibhutve sarvākārā cetasaḥ sthitiriti / prajñāpāramitā[yāṃ] sarvākārakāyavāṅmanaskarmavibhutve yaḥ sarvākāro dharmapravicaya iti vaktavyam / śeṣaṃ dānavadeva sarvaṃ veditavyam //
body.translated_text: Regarding the characteristics of the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections): What is the <s>dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of giving) of a <s>Bodhisattva</s>? It is the bodily, verbal, and mental karma of a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who is established in the <s>Bodhisattva</s> nature, relying on <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening), with a mind preceded by compassion, in the complete relinquishing of all possessions. And thus, the characteristic of the <s>dānapāramitā</s> should be understood as indicated through lineage, aspiration, disposition, substance, and intrinsic nature. Namely: the <s>Bodhisattva</s> nature is the lineage; <s>bodhicitta</s> is the aspiration; the mind preceded by compassion is the disposition; the complete relinquishing of all possessions is the substance; and bodily, verbal, and mental karma is the intrinsic nature. In this way, up to the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom), they should be understood in detail. But here is the distinction: in the <s>śīlapāramitā</s> (perfection of morality), <s>kṣāntipāramitā</s> (perfection of patience), and <s>vīryapāramitā</s> (perfection of vigor) respectively, the bodily, verbal, and mental karma should be understood as being in the undertaking and guarding of all restraints, in the enduring and tolerating of all harm and suffering, and in the gathering of all wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. In the <s>dhyānapāramitā</s> (perfection of meditation), it is the mastery of bodily, verbal, and mental karma of all types, and the settling of the mind in all modes. In the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, it should be said that in the mastery of bodily, verbal, and mental karma of all types, there is the investigation of <s>dharmas</s> in all modes. The remainder should be understood just as for giving.

body.text: punaryaddānaṃ sarvajñatāmārabhya sarvajñatāyai saṃvartate sarvajñatāṃ parigṛhṇāti sarvajñatākṛtyaṃ ca karoti taddānapārimitetyucyate / etāni punaścatvāri padāni yathākramamārambhato vāsanātaḥ kāyato nisyandataśca veditavyāni / tatrārambhataḥ sarvajñatāmārabhyotpannotpannasya tatra pariṇāmanāt / tadeva punardānaṃ saṃtati vāsayate, yata āyatyāṃ sarvajñatāyai saṃvartate / tadeva yadā paripūrṇaṃ bhavati tadā dharmakāyapariniṣpādanayogena sarvajñatāṃ parigṛhṇāti / tata uttarakālaṃ sāṃbhogikarnarmāṇikakāyanisyandamukhena sarvajñatākṛtyaṃ karoti / evaṃ yāvatprajñāpāramitā veditavyāḥ //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, giving that is undertaken toward omniscience, that conduces to omniscience, that comprehends omniscience, and that performs the function of omniscience — that is called <s>dānapāramitā</s>. These four terms should be understood respectively through undertaking, imprinting, embodiment, and outflow. Among these, 'undertaken toward omniscience' — because there is dedication thereto of each and every instance of giving as it arises. That very giving, moreover, perfumes the continuum, whereby in the future it conduces to omniscience. When that same giving is fully complete, it comprehends omniscience through the perfection of the <s>dharmakāya</s> (truth-body). Thereafter, it performs the function of omniscience through the outflow channel of the <s>saṃbhogikakāya</s> (enjoyment-body) and <s>nairmāṇikakāya</s> (emanation-body). Thus, up to the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, they should be understood.

body.text: anukramaḥ / uttarottarasaṃniśrayatāmupādāya dānapāramitayādhyātmikabāhyasarvavastuparityāgābhyāsātkāyajīvitanirapekṣo bodhisattvo mahāntamapi bhogaskandhaṃ prahāya śīlasamādānaṃ karoti / śīlānurakṣī - ākruṣṭena mayā na pratyākroṣṭavyam - ityevamādibhiḥ prakāraiḥ kṣamo bhavati / kṣamaḥ śītādīnām, tannidānaṃ prayogāsrasanādārabdhavīryā bhavati /
body.translated_text: The sequential order: by virtue of each being the support of the next, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, through the practice of relinquishing all internal and external possessions through the <s>dānapāramitā</s>, becomes indifferent to body and life, and having abandoned even a great mass of wealth, undertakes the observance of <s>śīla</s> (morality). Guarding morality, one becomes patient in various ways such as 'when reviled, I should not revile in return' and the rest. Being patient with cold and the like, and because of that cause, one initiates vigorous effort without slackening.

body.text: ārabdhavīryaḥ prayoganiṣṭhāphalādhigamādadhyānaṃ saṃpādayati / saṃpannadhyānaśca samāhitacitto yathābhūtajñānāllokottarāṃ prajñāṃ pratilabhata iti //
body.translated_text: Having initiated vigor, through attaining the fruit of effort and completion, one accomplishes <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation). And having perfected meditation, with a concentrated mind, through knowledge as it truly is, one attains supramundane <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom).

body.text: punaruttarottarādhārataḥ, śīlaṃ dānasyādhāra evaṃ yāvatprajñā dhyānasya / tathāhi śīlavato dānaṃ viśuddhaṃ bhavati, dānenānugṛhītasya śīlena paghātākaraṇataḥ / evamasya pratigrāhakasya bodhisattvena viheṭhāvirahitopakaraṇasukhopasaṃhārācchīlabalena dānapāramitā viśuddhirveditavyā / evaṃ kṣamiṇaḥ śīlaviśuddhiḥ, parāpakāraiḥ śikṣāpadākhaṇḍanāt / ārabdhavīryasya kṣāntiviśuddhiḥ, utsāhabalenotpatya saṃsāramabhyupagatavato 'kṛcchreṇa sattvavipratipattiduḥkhasa[ha]nāt / dhyāyinī vīryaviśuddhiḥ, saha sukhena saumanasyena sarvakuśaladharmaprayogāt / prajñāvato dhyānaviśuddhiḥ, bahuprakārāndharmānvipaśyatyadhyātmaṃ śamathataḥ samādhyabhivṛddheḥ, nāsti dhyānamaprajñasyeti gāthāyāṃ vacanāditi //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, from the standpoint of each subsequent being the support of the preceding: <s>śīla</s> is the support of <s>dāna</s>, and so forth up to <s>prajñā</s> being the support of <s>dhyāna</s>. For the giving of one who is moral becomes purified, because one endowed with giving does not cause harm through morality. Thus, because through the power of morality the <s>Bodhisattva</s> brings about the well-being of the recipient through provision free from harm, the purification of the <s>dānapāramitā</s> through the power of <s>śīla</s> should be understood. Likewise, the purification of morality for one who is patient — because one does not break the training rules through the harm done by others. The purification of patience for one with initiated vigor — because through the power of enthusiasm, having voluntarily entered <s>saṃsāra</s>, one effortlessly bears the suffering of beings' hostility. The purification of vigor for one who meditates — because all wholesome <s>dharma</s> practice is accompanied by bliss and mental happiness. The purification of meditation for one with wisdom — because seeing <s>dharmas</s> in many ways, from inner calm there is the enhancement of <s>samādhi</s>, as the verse says 'there is no meditation for one without wisdom.'

body.text: yathaudārikaścāparo 'nukramo veditavyaḥ / sarvaudārikaṃ hi dānamataḥ prathamato vyavasthāpyate / tadanantaraṃ kṣāntyādibhyaḥ śīlamaudārikamevaṃ yāvatprajñāyā dhyānamaudārikam / sarvasūkṣmā tu prajñā, ataḥ sarvapaścādvyavasthāpyata iti //
body.translated_text: Thus the sequential order from coarse to fine should also be understood. For giving is the coarsest of all, therefore it is established first. After that, morality is coarser than patience and the rest, and so on up to meditation being coarser than wisdom. But wisdom is the subtlest of all, therefore it is established last.

body.text: nirvacanam / kena kāraṇena dānaṃ dānapāramitetyucyate / mahaddānaṃ nirdoṣaṃ nirmalaṃ dānapāramitetyucyate / tatra mahaddānaṃ sarvaprakārādhyātmikabāhyavastu dānato dīrghakāladānataśca / nirdoṣaṃ viṣamaparyeṣṭayādivivarjitatvāt nirmalaṃ mātsaryavipakṣaprahāṇāt / yathoktaṃ dānapāramitāmārabhyāryākṣayamatinirdeśasūtre nirmalaṃ savāsanavipakṣaprahāṇāt / tadanayā trividhayā paramatayā dānapāramitetyabhidyotitaṃ bhavati / trividhā paramatā - svabhāvaparamatā sahaparicayena, upāyaparamatā, phalaparamatā ca / paricayaḥ punardīrghakāladānato veditavyaḥ / evaṃ yāvatprajñāpāramitā veditavyā / śīlādīnāṃ punarnirdoṣatvamā tmasamāropavarjitatvādibhiryathāyogam, tadakṣayamatisūtreṣu draṣṭavyam //
body.translated_text: Etymology: For what reason is giving called <s>dānapāramitā</s>? Great giving that is faultless and stainless is called <s>dānapāramitā</s>. Among these, great giving — because of giving all types of internal and external possessions and because of giving over a long period. Faultless — because of being free from wrongful acquisition and the like. Stainless — because of the abandonment of the opposing force of miserliness. As stated regarding the <s>dānapāramitā</s> in the <s>Āryākṣayamatinirdeśasūtra</s>, stainless because of the abandonment of the opposing force together with its imprints. Thus, through this threefold supremacy the <s>dānapāramitā</s> is illuminated. The threefold supremacy consists of: supremacy of intrinsic nature together with familiarity, supremacy of means, and supremacy of fruit. Familiarity, moreover, should be understood through giving over a long period. Thus, up to the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, they should be understood. The faultlessness of morality and the rest, however, should be understood through being free from self-glorification and the like, as appropriate — this should be examined in the <s>Akṣayamatisūtra</s>.

body.text: punardvādaśavidhena paramatvena yogātpāramitetyucyate / dvādaśavidhaṃ punaḥ paramatvam - audāryaparamatvaṃ sarvalokasampattyanarthitvādutkṛ[ṣṭa]tvācca / āyatatvaparamatvaṃ trikalpāsaṃkhyeyaparibhāvanāt / adhikāraparamatvaṃ sarvasattvārthakriyādhikārapravṛttatvāt / akṣayatvaparamatvaṃ mahābodhipariṇāmanayātyantamaparyādānāt / nairantaryaparamatvamātmaparasamatādhimokṣātsarvasattvadānādibhiḥ
body.translated_text: Furthermore, it is called <s>pāramitā</s> because of the yoga of twelvefold supremacy. The twelvefold supremacy is: supremacy of magnificence — because of not desiring the prosperity of all worlds and because of excellence. Supremacy of extent — because of cultivation through three incalculable <s>kalpas</s> (aeons). Supremacy of purpose — because of operating for the purpose of accomplishing the welfare of all beings. Supremacy of inexhaustibility — because of utter non-diminishment through dedication to great awakening. Supremacy of uninterruptedness — through the resolution of equality of self and others, through the giving and the rest for all beings,

body.text: pāramitāparipūraṇāt / akṛcchratvaparamatvamanumodanāmātreṇa paradānādīnāṃ pāramitāparipūraṇāt / vibhutvaparamatvaṃ gaganagañjasamādhyādibhirdānādiparipūraṇāt / parigrahaparamatvaṃ nirvikalpajñātaparigṛhītatvāt / ārambhaparamatvamadhimukticaryābhūmāvadhimātrāyāṃ kṣāntau / pratilambhaparamatvaṃ prathamāyāṃ bhūmau / nisyandaparamatvaṃ tadanyāsvaṣṭāsu / niṣpattiparamatvaṃ daśamyāṃ bhūmau tāthāgatyāṃ ca bodhisattvapariniṣpattyā buddhapariniṣpattyā ceti //
body.translated_text: the fulfillment of the <s>pāramitās</s>. Supremacy of effortlessness — because of the fulfillment of the <s>pāramitās</s> through mere rejoicing in the giving and the rest of others. Supremacy of mastery — because of the fulfillment of giving and the rest through the <s>gaganagañjasamādhi</s> and the like. Supremacy of comprehension — because of being grasped by non-conceptual knowledge. Supremacy of inception — in the stage of aspiration-conduct, at the highest level of patience. Supremacy of attainment — at the first <s>bhūmi</s> (stage). Supremacy of outflow — in the other eight stages. Supremacy of completion — at the tenth <s>bhūmi</s> and in the state of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, through the completion of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> and the completion of the <s>Buddha</s>.

body.text: punaḥ paramairīhitā itāśceti pāramitāḥ, buddhabodhisattvaiśceṣṭitā gatāścetyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>pāramitās</s> because they are sought and practiced by the supreme ones — meaning they are performed and followed by <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>.

body.text: punarjñeyapāraṃgatāḥ pāramitāḥ, buddhatve pratiṣṭhitā ityarthaḥ /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the <s>pāramitās</s> are those that have gone to the far shore of the knowable — meaning they are established in <s>Buddhahood</s>.

body.text: punaḥ parānātmānaṃ ca paramāmīti tārayantoti pāramitāḥ, parānātmānaṃ ca duḥkhārṇavamatikrāmantītyarthaḥ // idaṃ tāvatsādhāraṇaṃ nirvacanam //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>pāramitās</s> because they ferry others and oneself to the supreme — meaning they cross over the ocean of suffering for others and oneself. This is the general etymology.

body.text: pratyekaṃ punardāyakadāridrayāpanayatāddānam, dāhāpanayanādvā pratigrāhakānām // śāntendriyālambhanācchubhagatilīyanācchaityālayācca śīlaṃ yathākramamindriyeṣu guptadvāratāvāhanāt sugatigamanahetubhāvanādavipratisārādyānupūrvyā yāvannirvāṇāśrayatvāditi / krodhakṣāratiraskaraṇāt kṣaticittāgatitiraskaraṇāt kṣemāviṣkaraṇācca kṣatināṃ kṣāntiḥ / kṣaticittaṃ punaryenāpa kāriṇāṃ pratyapakāraḥ kriyate tasyāgatasyānayā vilopanaṃ tiraskaraṇaṃ veditavyam / kṣatameṣāṃ vairaṃ vidyata iti kṣatinasteṣāmabhayaprakāśanaṃ kṣemasyāviṣkaraṇaṃ veditavyam / vadhavṛddhohāyogādvoryam / tatra vadhāyehākuśaladharmavigamāya dvābhyāṃ samyakprahāṇābhyām, vṛddhaye īhā kuśaladharmasamudāgamāya dvābhyāṃ samyakprahāṇābhyāṃ ca / dhāraṇayamanasaṃyamanavinayananayanāddhyānam / tatra dhāraṇāmālaṃbane cittasya, yamanaṃ vikṣepataḥ, saṃyamanaṃ cittasya, vinayanaṃ paryavasthānānāṃ viṣkambhaṇam, nayanaṃ vibhutvasya prāpaṇaṃ veditavyam / parapraṇītajñānāt
body.translated_text: Individually: <s>dāna</s> (giving) — because of removing the poverty of the giver, or because of removing the burning of the recipients. <s>Śīla</s> (morality) — because of calming the sense faculties, because of resting in happy destinies, and because of being a temple of coolness — respectively, because of bringing about restraint of the doors of the senses, because of cultivating the cause of going to happy destinies, and because through freedom from remorse and the rest in succession, up to being the support of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. <s>Kṣānti</s> (patience) — because of removing the caustic quality of anger, because of concealing the hostile mind, and because of revealing safety for those who are harmed. The hostile mind is that by which retaliation is made against those who have caused harm — the concealment and covering of its arising by patience should be understood. 'Their enmity is healed' — those who are harmed — the revealing of safety for them should be understood as making fearlessness manifest. <s>Vīrya</s> (vigor) — because of the combination of destroying and increasing. Among these, the effort of destroying is directed here toward the elimination of unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>, through two of the right efforts; the effort of increasing is directed toward the acquisition of wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, through the other two right efforts. <s>Dhyāna</s> (meditation) — because of holding, restraining, controlling, disciplining, and guiding. Among these, holding is of the mind on the object; restraining is from distraction; controlling is of the mind; disciplining is the suppression of the manifest defilements; and guiding should be understood as the attainment of mastery. <s>Prajñā</s> (wisdom) — because of knowledge from another that is superior,

body.text: pratyātmajñānāt prakārajñānāt śamaprāptiguṇaprakarṣajñānācca prajñā / tatra parapraṇītajñānaṃ parato ghoṣānvayā yoniśomanaskārasaṃprayuktā prajñā, pratyātmajñānaṃ lokottarā, prakārajñānaṃ lokottarapṛṣṭhalabdhā, śamaprāptaye jñānaṃ bhāvanāmārge kleśapratipakṣabhūtā, guṇaprakarṣāya jñānaṃ vaiśeṣikaguṇābhinirhārāya prajñā veditavyā //
body.translated_text: because of knowledge within oneself, because of knowledge of varieties, and because of knowledge for the attainment of calm and the excellence of qualities. Among these, knowledge from another that is superior is the wisdom connected with methodical attention following the voice of another. Knowledge within oneself is the supramundane.
