Knowledge of varieties is that obtained subsequently to the supramundane. Knowledge for the attainment of calm is the wisdom that serves as the antidote to defilements in the path of cultivation. Knowledge for the excellence of qualities should be understood as the wisdom for the accomplishment of distinctive qualities.

body.text: bhāvanā pañcavidhā, upadhisaṃniśritā yāvadvibhutvasaṃniśritā //
body.translated_text: Cultivation is fivefold — based on the substrates, up to based on mastery.

body.text: tatropadhisaṃniśritā caturākārā / hetusaṃniśritā yo gotrabalena pāramitāsu pratipattyabhyāsaḥ vipākasaṃniśritā ya ātmabhāvasaṃpattibalena / prāṇidhānasaṃniśritā yaḥ pūrvapraṇidhānabalena / pratisaṃkhyānabalasaṃniśritā yaḥ prajñābalena pāramitāsu pratipattyabhyāsaḥ //
body.translated_text: Among these, cultivation based on the substrates is fourfold. Based on the cause — the practice and cultivation of the <s>pāramitās</s> through the power of the spiritual lineage. Based on maturation — through the power of the excellence of personal existence. Based on aspiration — through the power of former vows. Based on the power of analytical reflection — the practice and cultivation of the <s>pāramitās</s> through the power of wisdom.

body.text: manaskārasaṃniśritā pāramitābhāvanā caturākārā / adhimuktimanaskāreṇa sarvapāramitāpratisaṃyukta sūtrāntamadhimucyamānasya / āsvādanāmanaskāreṇa labdhāḥ pāramitāḥ, āsvādayato guṇadarśanayogena / anumodanāmanaskāreṇa sarvalokadhātuṣu sarvasattvānāṃ dānādikamanumodamānasya / abhinandanāmanaskāreṇātmanaḥ sattvānāṃ cānāgataṃ pāramitāviśeṣamabhinandamānasya //
body.translated_text: Cultivation of the <s>pāramitās</s> based on mental engagement is fourfold. Through the mental engagement of aspiration — for one who has faith in all the <s>sūtras</s> connected with the <s>pāramitās</s>. Through the mental engagement of savoring — for one who savors the <s>pāramitās</s> already attained, through seeing their qualities. Through the mental engagement of rejoicing — for one who rejoices in the giving and the rest of all beings in all world-realms. Through the mental engagement of delight — for one who delights in the future distinction of the <s>pāramitās</s> for oneself and for beings.

body.text: āśayasaṃniśritā pāramitābhāvanā ṣaḍākārā - atṛptāśayena vaipulyāśayena muditāśayenopakarāśayena nirlepāśayena kalyāṇāśayena ca / tatra bodhisattvasya dāne 'tṛptāśayo yadbodhisattvasyaikakṣaṇe gaṅgānadīvālikāsamānlokadhātūn saptaratnaparipūrṇān pratipādayato gaṅgānadīvālikāsamāṃścātmabhāvanevaṃ pratikṣaṇaṃ gaṅgānadīvālikāsamān kalpān pratipādayataḥ / yathā caikasattvasyaivaṃ yāvān sattvadhāturanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau paripācitavyaḥ / tamanena paryāyeṇa pratipādayedatṛpta eva bodhisattvasya dānāśaya iti / ya evaṃrūpaṃ āśayo 'yaṃ bodhisattvasya dāne 'tṛptāśayaḥ / na ca bodhisattva evaṃrūpāṃ dānaparaṃparāṃ kṣaṇamātramapi hāpayati vicchinattyābodhimaṇḍaniṣadanāditi / ya evaṃrūpa āśayo 'yaṃ bodhisattvasya dāne vipulāśayaḥ / muditataraśca bodhisattvo
body.translated_text: Cultivation of the <s>pāramitās</s> based on disposition is sixfold — through an insatiable disposition, an expansive disposition, a joyful disposition, a helpful disposition, an untainted disposition, and a benevolent disposition. Among these, the <s>Bodhisattva's</s> insatiable disposition in giving is: even if the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, at a single moment, were to bestow world-realms equal in number to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, filled with the seven treasures, and personal existences equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, and were to continue giving in this way, moment after moment, for <s>kalpas</s> equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>; and just as for one being, so for all the beings in the entire realm of beings who are to be matured toward unsurpassed perfect awakening; even if one were to provide for them in this manner — the <s>Bodhisattva's</s> disposition of giving would still be insatiable. The disposition of such a character is the <s>Bodhisattva's</s> insatiable disposition in giving. And the <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not let fall or interrupt such a succession of giving even for a single moment until sitting at the seat of awakening. The disposition of such a character is the <s>Bodhisattva's</s> expansive disposition in giving. And the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is most joyful

body.text: bhavati tānsattvāṃstathā dānenānugṛhṇan, na ca te sattvāstena dānenānugṛhyamāṇā iti / ya evaṃrūpa āśayo 'yaṃ bodhisattvasya dāne muditāśayaḥ / upakaratarāṃśca bodhisattvastān sattvānātmanaḥ samanupaśyati yeṣāṃ tathā dānenopakaroti nātmānam, teṣāmanuttarasamyaksaṃbodhyupastambhatāmuṣā[dā]ya iti / ya evaṃrūpa āśayo 'yaṃ bodhisattvasya dāne upakarāśayaḥ / na ca bodhisattvaḥ sattveṣu tathā vipulamapi dānamayaṃ puṇyamabhisaṃskṛtya pratikāreṇa vārthī bhavati vipākena veti / ya evaṃrūpa āśayo 'yaṃ bodhisattvasya dānapāramitābhāvanāyāṃ nirlepāśayaḥ / yadbodhisattvastathā vipulasyāpi dānaskandhasya vipākaṃ sattveṣvevābhinandati nātmanaḥ, sarvasattvasādhāraṇaṃ ca kṛtvānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayatīti / ya evaṃrūpa āśayo 'yaṃ bodhisattvasya dānapāramitābhāvanāyāṃ kalyāṇāśayaḥ /
body.translated_text: in thus benefiting those beings through giving, and yet those beings are not truly being benefited by that giving. The disposition of such a character is the <s>Bodhisattva's</s> joyful disposition in giving. And the <s>Bodhisattva</s> regards those beings to whom he thus gives as being more helpful to himself than he is to them, taking it as their support for unsurpassed perfect awakening, not himself. The disposition of such a character is the <s>Bodhisattva's</s> helpful disposition in giving. And the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, even having generated such vast merit through giving toward beings, does not desire either requital or maturation in return. The disposition of such a character is the <s>Bodhisattva's</s> untainted disposition in the cultivation of the <s>dānapāramitā</s>. When the <s>Bodhisattva</s> delights in the maturation of even such a vast aggregate of giving as belonging to beings alone and not to himself, and making it common to all beings, dedicates it to unsurpassed perfect awakening — the disposition of such a character is the <s>Bodhisattva's</s> benevolent disposition in the cultivation of the <s>dānapāramitā</s>.

body.text: tatra bodhisattvasya śīlapāramitābhāvanāyāṃ yāvatprajñāpāramitābhāvanāyāmatṛptāśayaḥ, yadbodhisattvo gaṅgānadīvālikāsameṣvātmabhāveṣu gaṅgānadīvālikāsamakalpāyuḥpramāṇeṣu sarvopakaraṇanirantaravighātī trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātāvāgniparipūrṇe caturvidhamīryāpathaṃ kalpayannekaṃ śīlapāramitākṣaṇaṃ yāvatprajñāpāramitākṣaṇaṃ bhāvayet, etena paryāyeṇa yāvacchīlaskandho yāvatprajñāskandho yenānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate, śīlaskandhaṃ yāvatprajñāskandhaṃ bhāvayet, atṛpta evaṃ bodhisattvasya śīlapāramitābhāvanāyāmāśayo yāvatprajñāpāramitābhāvanā[yā]māśaya iti / ya evaṃrūpa āśayo 'yaṃ bodhisattva[sya] śīlapāramitābhāvanāyāmatṛptāśayo yāvatprajñāpāramitāyāṃ bhāvanāyām / yadbodhisattvastāṃ śīlapāramitābhāvanāparaṃparāṃ yāvatprajñāpāramitābhāvanāparaṃparamā bodhimaṇḍaniṣadanānna bhraṃśayati na vicchinattīti / ya evaṃrūpa āśāyo 'yaṃ bodhisattvasya śīlapāramitābhāvanāyāṃ yāvatprajñāpāramitābhāvanāyāṃ vipulāśayaḥ / muditataraśca bodhisattvo bhavati tayā śīlapāramitābhāvanayā yāvatprajñāpāramitābhāvanayā sattvānanugṛhṇan, na tveva te sattvā anugṛhyamāṇā iti / ya evaṃrūpaāśayo 'yaṃ bodhisattvasya śīlapāramitābhāvanāyāṃ yāvatprajñāpāramitābhāvanāyāṃ muditāśayaḥ / upakaratarāṃśca sa bodhisattvastān sattvānātmanaḥ samanupaśyati yeṣāṃ tathā śīlapāramitābhāvanayā yāvatprajñāpāramitābhāvanayā upakarāti nātmānam, teṣāmanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhyupastambhatāsu pādāyeti / ya evarūpa āśayo 'yaṃ bodhisattvasya śīlapāramitābhāvanāyāṃ yāvatprajñāpāramitābhāvanāyāmupakarāśayaḥ / na ca bodhisattvastathā vipulamapi śīlapāramitāmayaṃ yāvatprajñāpāramitāmayaṃ puṇyamabhisaṃskṛtya tasya pratikāreṇa
body.translated_text: Among these, the insatiable aspiration (<s>atṛpta-āśaya</s>) of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in the cultivation of the perfection of morality (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>) through to the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>) [is as follows]: even if the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, in as many existences as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, with lifespans as many as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> in kalpas, continuously afflicted with the loss of all possessions in a triple-thousand great-thousand world-system filled with fire, maintaining the four postures, were to cultivate a single moment of the perfection of morality through to the perfection of wisdom—by this method, he should cultivate the aggregate of morality through to the aggregate of wisdom by which one fully awakens to unsurpassed perfect awakening. Such is the insatiable aspiration of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. This aspiration is [also called] the vast aspiration (<s>vipulāśaya</s>)—because the <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not let fall or interrupt the continuity of cultivating the perfection of morality through to the perfection of wisdom until sitting at the seat of awakening (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>). The joyful aspiration (<s>muditāśaya</s>)—because the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is most delighted in benefiting beings through the cultivation of the perfection of morality through to the perfection of wisdom, more so than those very beings who are being benefited. The beneficent aspiration (<s>upakarāśaya</s>)—because that <s>Bodhisattva</s> sees those very beings as more beneficial to himself than himself, for they serve as the foundation for his support of their unsurpassed perfect awakening. And the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, even having generated such vast merit consisting of the perfection of morality through to the perfection of wisdom, [does not seek] in return for that

body.text: vārthī bhavati vipākena veti / ya evaṃrūpa āśayo 'yaṃ bodhisattvasya śīlapāramitāyāṃ yāvatprajñāpāramitāyāṃ nirlepāśayaḥ / tatra yadbodhisattva evaṃ śīlapāramitābhāvanāmayasya yāvatprajñāpāramitābhāvanāmayasya puṇyaskandhasya vipākaṃ sattveṣvevābhinandati nātmanaḥ, sarvasattvasādhāraṇaṃ ca kṛtvānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayatīti / ya evaṃrūpa āśayo 'yaṃ bodhisattvasya śīlapāramitāyāṃ bhāvanāyāṃ yāvatprajñāpāramitābhāvanāyāṃ kalyāṇāśayaḥ //
body.translated_text: any maturation-result. Such is the unstained aspiration (<s>nirlepāśaya</s>) of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in the perfection of morality through to the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> thus cultivates the perfection of morality through to the perfection of wisdom...

body.text: upāyasaṃniśritā pāramitābhāvanā trayākārā nirvikalpena jñānena trimaṇḍalapariśuddhipratyavekṣaṇatāmupādāya / tathāhi sa [u]pāyaḥ sarvamanaskārāṇāmabhiniṣpattaye //
body.translated_text: The cultivation of the <s>pāramitās</s> based on skillful means (<s>upāya</s>) is of three aspects, through the review of the purity of the three spheres (<s>trimaṇḍalapariśuddhi</s>) by means of non-conceptual knowledge (<s>nirvikalpajñāna</s>). For that skill in means is for the accomplishment of all mental engagements...

body.text: vibhutvasaṃniśritā pāramitābhāvanā trayākārā kāyavibhutvataḥ, caryāvibhutvataḥ deśanāvibhutvaśca / tatra kāyavibhutvaṃ tāthāgatau dvau kāyau draṣṭavyau svābhāvikaḥ sāṃbhogikaśca / tatra caryāvibhutvaṃ nairmāṇikaḥ kāyo draṣṭavyo yena sarvākārāṃ sarvasattvānāṃ sahadhārmikacaryāṃ darśayati / deśanā vibhutvaṃ ṣaṭpāramitāsarvākāradeśanāyāmavyāghātataḥ //
body.translated_text: The cultivation of the <s>pāramitās</s> based on sovereign power (<s>vibhutva</s>) is of three aspects: through sovereignty of body (<s>kāyavibhutva</s>), sovereignty of conduct (<s>caryāvibhutva</s>), and sovereignty of teaching (<s>deśanāvibhutva</s>). Among these, sovereignty of body: the two bodies of a <s>Tathāgata</s> should be seen—the essential body (<s>svābhāvika</s>)...

body.text: prabhedato 'ṣṭādaśabhirupastambhaiḥ ṣaṇṇāṃ pāramitānāṃ prabhedo veditavyaḥ / aṣṭādaśopastambhāḥ - kāyopastambhaḥ, cittopastambhaḥ, kuśalopastambhaḥ, sugatyupastambhaḥ, bodhyupastambhaḥ, karuṇopastambhaḥ, sattvāparityāgopastambhaḥ, hīnacittaparityāgopastambhaḥ / anutpattikadharmakṣāntyupastambhaḥ kuśalamūlaprayogopastambhaḥ, kuśalamūlasamudāgamopastambhaḥ, kuśalamūlākṣayatopastambhaḥ, aparikhedopastambhaḥ, sarvacintitārthasamṛddhayupastambhaḥ, gaṇaparikarṣaṇopastambhaḥ, bhūmipraveśopastambhaḥ, buddhadharmasamudānayanopastambhaḥ, buddhakṛtyānuṣṭhānopastambhaśca //
body.translated_text: As to classification, the sixfold distinction of the six <s>pāramitās</s> should be understood through eighteen supports (<s>upastambha</s>). The eighteen supports are: the support of body (<s>kāyopastambha</s>), the support of mind (<s>cittopastambha</s>), the support of the wholesome (<s>kuśalopastambha</s>), the support of happy destiny (<s>sugatyupastambha</s>)...

body.text: pratyekaṃ dānādīnāṃ traivighyāt tribhistribhirupastambhairyathākramaṃ saṃgraho veditavyaḥ / tatra trividhaṃ dānam - abhayadānaṃ dharmadānamāmiṣadānaṃ ca / trividhaṃ śīlam - saṃvaraśīlaṃ kuśaladharmasaṃgrāhakaṃ śīlaṃ sattvārthakriyāśīlaṃ ca / trividhā
body.translated_text: The inclusion [of supports] with three each should be understood for each of giving etc., from the threefold [nature] of each, in due order. Among these, the threefold giving (<s>dāna</s>): giving of fearlessness (<s>abhayadāna</s>), giving of <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmadāna</s>), and giving of material goods (<s>āmiṣadāna</s>). Threefold morality (<s>śīla</s>)...

body.text: kṣāntiḥ - apakāramarṣaṇakṣāntirduḥkhādhivāsanākṣāntirdharmanidhyānakṣāntiśca / trividhaṃ vīryam - saṃnāhavīryaṃ prayogavīryaṃ sattvārthakriyāvīryaṃ ca / trividhaṃ dhyānam - dṛṣṭadharmasukhāvihārāya dhyānamabhijñānirhārāya dhyānaṃ sattvārthakriyāyai ca dhyānam / trividhā prajñā - saṃvṛtyālaṃbanā paramārthālaṃbanā sattvārthālambanā ca //
body.translated_text: patience (<s>kṣānti</s>): patience of forbearance toward harm (<s>apakāramarṣaṇakṣānti</s>), patience of endurance of suffering (<s>duḥkhādhivāsanākṣānti</s>), and patience of investigation of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmanidhyānakṣānti</s>). Threefold energy (<s>vīrya</s>): the energy of armor (<s>saṃnāhavīrya</s>), the energy of application (<s>prayogavīrya</s>), and the energy of accomplishing the welfare of beings (<s>sattvārthakriyāvīrya</s>). Threefold...

body.text: tatrāmiṣadānaṃ kāyopastambhaḥ, annapānādyupakaraṇaiḥ pratigrāhakāśrayānugrahaṇāt / abhayadānaṃ cittopastambhaḥ daurmanasyaviśeṣā[pa]gamāya cetasa āśvāsāya saṃhārāt / ityevamanyadapi yojyam //
body.translated_text: Among these, the giving of material goods (<s>āmiṣadāna</s>) is the support of body, because it benefits the basis of the recipient through provisions such as food, drink, etc. The giving of fearlessness (<s>abhayadāna</s>) is the support of mind, because it consoles the mind for the removal of particular forms of mental anguish...

body.text: hīnacittaṃ punarbodhisattvasya saṃsāraduḥkhaparikheditayā śrāvakapratyekabuddhacittam, tatparityāgopastambho duḥkhādhivāsanakṣāntirveditavyā //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the inferior mind (<s>hīnacitta</s>) of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is the mind [inclined toward] <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> through weariness with the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s>. The support of abandoning that should be understood as the patience of endurance of suffering (<s>duḥkhādhivāsanākṣānti</s>).

body.text: kuśalamūlākṣayatā sarvasattveṣu kriyārthādhikāritayā yāvatsāraṃ nirupadhiśeṣe 'pi nirvāṇadhātāvaparityāgaḥ, tadupastambhaḥ sattvārthakriyāyaṃ vīryaṃ veditavyam //
body.translated_text: The inexhaustibility of roots of merit (<s>kuśalamūlākṣayatā</s>): because of being authorized to act for the welfare of all beings—non-abandonment even in the <s>nirvāṇa</s>-realm without remainder, as long as [beings] need [help]. The support of that should be understood as the energy of accomplishing the welfare of beings (<s>sattvārthakriyāvīrya</s>)...

body.text: gaṇaparikarṣaṇaṃ karmaṃ adhigamaṃ niśritya vineyānāmasamāhitasya cittasya samādhānāya samāhitasya vā cittasya vimokṣāyāvavādānuśāsanopradānam, tadupastambhaḥ sattvārthakriyāyai dhyānam //
body.translated_text: The work of guiding an assembly (<s>gaṇaparikarṣaṇa</s>): based on realization, the giving of instruction and admonition for the concentration of the unconcentrated mind of those to be trained, or for the liberation of the already-concentrated mind. The support of that should be understood as the <s>samādhi</s> of...

body.text: bhūmipraveśo yayā deśanayā dharmādhimuktipūrvikayāsaṃbhāraparipūryāpramuditāṃ bhūmiṃ praviśati, tadupastambhaḥ saṃvṛtisatyālaṃbanā prajñā //
body.translated_text: Entry into the stages (<s>bhūmipraveśa</s>): the teaching through which, preceded by aspiration toward the <s>Dharma</s>, one enters the first stage (<s>Pramuditā bhūmi</s>, the Joyful) through the completion of the accumulations. The support of that should be understood as the wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) having conventional truth (<s>saṃvṛtisatya</s>) as its object.

body.text: śeṣaṃ suyojyatvānna yojitam //
body.translated_text: The remainder is not construed because of its easy applicability.

body.text: punaḥ prabhedaḥ sapta dānāmi - mūladānaṃ gotrāvasthasya bodhisattvasya dānapāramitā, gotramātraṃ niśritya dānāt / ādhānadānaṃ cittotpādāvasthasya, praṇidhānasamādānaṃ niśritya dānāt / anugrahadānaṃ svaparārthapratyavasthasya / anavagrahadānaṃ tattvārthaparīkṣāvasthasya, dāyakādivikalpābhiniveśāvagrāhābhāvāt / niṣparigrahadānaṃ prabhāvāvasthasya, vinā vāhyenopakaraṇaparigraheṇa gaganagañjādisamādhibhirākāśe pāṇiṃ saṃcārya yatheṣṭaṃ ratnādivarṣaṇāt / pratyarhadānaṃ paripākāvasthasya, yathāvineyānurūpaṃ dānāt / mahādānaṃ paramabodhyavasthasya, niruttaratvāt / evaṃ yāvatprajñā yathāyogaṃ veditavyam //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, as to classification, there are seven types of giving: (1) Root-giving (<s>mūladāna</s>): the perfection of giving of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in the stage of the spiritual lineage (<s>gotra</s>), since it is giving based merely on the lineage. (2) Foundation-giving (<s>ādhānadāna</s>): [that] of the stage of generating the thought [of awakening], together with aspiration...

body.text: saṃgrahaḥ dānādabhirbodhisattvabhūmisaṃgrahārthena, tatredamudāharaṇamātraṃ pāramitādibhiḥ / gotrasaṃgraho dānapāramitādigotraṃ liṅgato 'nugantavyam / cittotpādasaṃgraho viśiṣṭacittotpādasaṃ[gra]haṇāt / dvividho hi cittotpādaḥ - aviśiṣṭo viśiṣṭaśca / tatrāviśiṣṭo 'ho vatāhamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyeti / viśiṣṭa evaṃ dānapāramitāṃ paripūrayeyaṃ yāvatprajñāpāramitāmiti / tadanena viśiṣṭena cittotpādena pāramitānāṃ saṃgraho veditavyaḥ, tāsāṃ kāraṇabhāvāt / svaparārthasaṃgraho yaddānenaiśvarya parigṛhaṇātyayaṃ svārthaḥ, yatpunaḥ parānupakaraṇopasaṃhāreṇānugṛhṇātyayaṃ svārthaḥ evamavaśiṣṭābhiḥ saṃgraho veditavyaḥ / paramārthasaṃgrahaḥ - dharmadhātumārabhya, tathatāyā dānādisāmānyalakṣa[ṇa]tvāt / jñānasaṃbhāramārabhya, sarvajñatābhājanatāpādanāt / jñānaparigrahamārabhya sarvajñatāpariniṣpādanāt / jñānānuparivartatāmārabhya, pañcānāṃ prajñāpāramitānuparivartanāt / jñānalakṣaṇamārabhya, prajñāpāramitāḥ samyagjñānasvabhāvatvāt / ityevaṃ tathatāsamyajjñānasvabhāvataḥ paramārtho dānādibhiḥ saṃgṛhīto veditavyaḥ / etenodāharaṇamātreṇa śeṣaḥ saṃgraho veditavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: The inclusion [of stages is to be understood]: through giving etc., for the purpose of including the <s>Bodhisattva</s> stages—and this is merely an illustration through the <s>pāramitās</s> etc. The inclusion of the lineage (<s>gotra</s>): the lineage of the perfection of giving etc. should be traced through its marks. The inclusion of generating the thought of awakening (<s>cittotpāda</s>)...

body.text: vipakṣo dānādīnāṃ yathākramaṃ mātsaryadauḥśīlye krodhakauśīdye vikṣepadauḥprajñe / api khalu yāvantaḥ kuśalā dharmāḥ pāramitābhiḥ saṃgṛhītāsteṣāṃ yo vipakṣo jñeyāvaraṇaṃ ca sa tāsāṃ vipakṣo veditavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: The adversaries (<s>vipakṣa</s>) of giving etc. are, in due order: miserliness (<s>mātsarya</s>), immorality (<s>dauḥśīlya</s>), anger (<s>krodha</s>), laziness (<s>kauśīdya</s>), distraction (<s>vikṣepa</s>), and wrong understanding (<s>dauḥprajñya</s>). Moreover, the adversary of all the wholesome <s>dharmas</s> included in the <s>pāramitās</s> should be known...

body.text: anuśaṃsaḥ pañcavidhaphalādhikāreṇāprameyo veditavyaḥ / tadyathā yathāsvamāsāṃ vipakṣaprahāṇaṃ visaṃyogaphalam / dṛṣṭe dharme svaparānugrahaṇaṃ puruṣakāraphalam / āyatyāmuttarāttaraviśiṣṭattaratamotpattirniṣyandaphalam / mahābodhiradhipatiphalam / mahābhogatā sugatigamanamavarābhedasukhasaumanasya bahulatā sattvādhipapatyamavyābādhyātmabhāvatā maheśākhyatā ca yathākramaṃ dānādīnāṃ vipākaphalaṃ veditavyam //
body.translated_text: The benefit (<s>anuśaṃsa</s>) should be understood as immeasurable, with reference to five types of fruit. Namely: for each [<s>pāramitā</s>] respectively, the abandonment of its adversary is the fruit of separation (<s>visaṃyogaphala</s>). In the present life, the benefiting of self and others is the fruit of personal effort (<s>puruṣakāraphala</s>)...

body.text: anyonyaviniścayastrividhaḥ - prāyogikaḥ, prābhedikaḥ, prabhidyasāṃdarśikaśca //
body.translated_text: The mutual determination (<s>anyonyaviniścaya</s>) [of the <s>pāramitās</s>] is threefold: practical (<s>prāyogika</s>), analytical (<s>prābhedika</s>), and demonstrative (<s>prabhidyasāṃdarśika</s>).

body.text: tatra prāyogikaḥ dānaprayoge sarvāsāṃ vṛttirūpalabhyate / tadyathādhyātmikaṃ bāhyaṃ vastuparityajanataḥ dānaprayogaḥ / tatra yaḥ parityāgaḥ sa dānapāramitā / tatraiva yā maitracittasya paratravighātotpīḍāviheṭhasaṃvaraṇatā sā śīlapāramitā / tatraiva yoparodhavighātakhedamarṣaṇatā sā kṣāntipāramitā / tatraiva yā bhūyo bhūyaścittasyotsahanatā sā vīryapāramitā / tatraiva yā cittasyaikāgratā kuśalādbahiravisaraṇatā sā dhyānapāramitā / tatraiva yā yathāvaddhetu phalasugṛhītatā dṛṣṭyaparāmarṣaṇatā sā prajñāpāramitā / evaṃ yāvatprajñāpāramitāyāṃ yathāyogaṃ yojayitavyamubhayadānaṃ sarvajñajñānamiti kṛtvā //
body.translated_text: Among these, the practical [determination]: in the practice of giving, the activity of all [<s>pāramitās</s>] is found. For example, the practice of giving through the relinquishing of internal and external things. Among these, the relinquishing itself is the perfection of giving. And that...

body.text: tatra prābhedikaḥ svabhāvaprabhedena, anukāraprabhedena ca / tatra dānādīnāṃ svabhāvo yathākramaṃ visargaḥ saṃvaro marṣaṇābhyutsāhaścitasthitiḥ pravicayaśca / tatra dānādiprayogeṣu tadanyapāramitānāmanuvṛttiḥ pūrvavat / tatra dānādīnāmupayogaḥ samādāpanā varṇavāditā sumanojñatā ca / tatra dānādīnāṃ ropaṇā yā parasaṃtāne pratiṣṭhāpanā / tadatra dānapāramitāmiṣadānam, tadanyāḥ pañcābhayadānam, sarvāḥ saddharmadānaṃ parasaṃtāne ropaṇāt //
body.translated_text: Among these, the analytical [determination] is through the distinction of intrinsic nature and through the distinction of analogy. The intrinsic nature of giving etc. is, in due order: relinquishing (<s>visarga</s>), restraint (<s>saṃvara</s>), forbearance (<s>marṣaṇa</s>), exertion (<s>abhyutsāha</s>), mental stability (<s>cittasthiti</s>), and discernment (<s>pravicaya</s>). And...

body.text: tatra prabhidyasāṃdarśika ekāvacārakādibhiḥ / tadyathā yā dānapāramitā śīlapāramitāpi sā, yā vā śīlapāramitā dānapāramitāpi sā, paścātpādakaḥ - yā yāvacchīlapāramitā dānapāramitāpi sā, syāddānapāramitā na śīlapāramitā śīlapāramitayāsaṃgṛhītā yā dānapāramitā / evaṃ yāvatyajñāpāramitayāsaṃgṛhītā dānapāramitā paścātpādakairyojayitavyā / yaddānaṃ sarvā sā pāramitā, yā dānapāramitā sarvaṃ taddānamiti catuṣkoṭikam / syāddānaṃ na pāramitā yanna mahobodhipariṇāmitam / syāt pāramitā na dānaṃ śīlādayo mahābodhipariṇāmitāḥ / syāddānaṃ ca pāramitā ca
body.translated_text: Among these, the demonstrative [determination] is through the principle of single occasion etc. For example: that which is the perfection of giving is also the perfection of morality; that which is the perfection of morality is also the perfection of giving. The qualification: whatever is the perfection of morality...

body.text: bodhipariṇāmitāni dānādīni / syānna dānaṃ na pāramitā uktavinirmuktā dharmāḥ / evaṃ yāvatprajñāpāramitāmārabhya catuṣkoṭikaṃ pratyekaṃ yojayitavyam / yo dānaṃ samācarati sarvo 'sau dānapāramitānvayaṃ puṇyaṃ prasavatīti catuṣkoṭikam / prathamā koṭiḥ - mahābodhyapariṇāmitaṃ dānaṃ samācarati / dvitīyā koṭiḥ - dānapāramitāṃ yāṃ samādāpanavarṇabhāṣaṇasumanojñatābhiḥ / tṛtīyā koṭiḥ - mahābodhipariṇāmitena dānena / caturthī koṭiḥ - etānākārān sthāpayitvā / evaṃ yāvatprajñāpāramitāmārabhya pratyekaṃ catuṣkoṭikaṃ yojayitavyam //
body.translated_text: giving and the rest that are dedicated to awakening. There may be what is giving but not <s>pāramitā</s> — <s>dharmas</s> that are excluded from what has been stated. Thus, up to the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, the tetralemma should be applied to each individually. 'Does everyone who practices giving generate merit that accords with the <s>dānapāramitā</s>?' — this is the tetralemma. The first alternative: one practices giving that is not dedicated to great awakening. The second alternative: the <s>dānapāramitā</s>, which is through inducing others, praising, speaking pleasantly. The third alternative: through giving that is dedicated to great awakening. The fourth alternative: <s>dharmas</s> other than these modes. Thus, up to the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, the tetralemma should be applied to each individually.

body.text: viśeṣato vaipulye audāryagāmbhīryadeśanā tatphalasya sarvajñatvasya paramodāragambhīratvātphalānurūpyeṇa hetunirdeśo draṣṭavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Especially regarding the extensive teaching of magnificence and profundity — because the fruit, omniscience, is supremely magnificent and profound, the exposition of the cause should be seen as corresponding to the fruit.

body.text: ekatyānāṃ tadanadhimokṣe trāsaḥ bodhisattvagotravaikalyaṃ prakṛtyā hīnacittatayā gāmbhīryaudāryadeśanāṃ nādhimoktuṃ śaknuvanti / satyapi tadgotratve mahābodhimārabhya praṇidhānādīnāṃ kuśalamūlādīnāmanavaropaṇāt, satyapi tadavaropaṇe mahāyānapratikṣepakasattvaparigṛhītatvāditi / adhimucyamānānāmapyekatyānāmaniryāṇaṃ nītārtha sūtrama[na]nviṣya svayaṃ dṛṣṭiparāmarṣasthāyitayā yathārutamarthābhiniveśāta / tadyathā sarvadharmaniḥsvabhāvatāvacanāt sarvalakṣaṇena sarvabhāvāpavādinaḥ / evamanye 'pi yathārutārthābhiniveśino mahāyāne na niryāntotiveditavyaṃ nānābhiprāyabhāṣitatvāt mahāyānasyeti / idaṃ ca saṃdhāyoktaṃ bhagavatā mahādharmādarśe dharmaparyāye - bodhisattvasya yathārutamayoniśo dharmān vicinvato 'ṣṭāviṃśatirasaddṛṣṭaya utpadyante //
body.translated_text: The fright of certain persons at not having faith in that — some lack the <s>Bodhisattva</s> lineage and are unable to have faith in the teaching of profundity and magnificence because their minds are naturally inferior. Even if they have that lineage, because they have not planted the wholesome roots such as aspirations and the rest directed toward great awakening. Even if they have planted those, because they are under the influence of beings who reject the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. Among those who do have faith, certain ones still do not attain liberation — because they do not seek <s>sūtras</s> of definitive meaning, and through their own adherence to clinging to views, they grasp the meaning literally. For example, from the statement that all <s>dharmas</s> are without intrinsic nature, they deny all entities in every aspect. Thus, others also who grasp the literal meaning should be understood as not attaining liberation in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, because the <s>Mahāyāna</s> is spoken with various implicit intentions. And with this in mind, the <s>Bhagavān</s> stated in the <s>Mahādharmadarśa</s> scripture: 'For a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who investigates <s>dharmas</s> literally and unmethodically, twenty-eight false views arise.'

body.text: aṣṭāviṃśatirasaddṛṣṭayaḥ katamāḥ / nimittadṛṣṭiryāvadabhimānadṛṣṭiśca / tatra nisvabhāvāḥ sarvadharmā anutpannā ityevamādikaṃ mahāyāne rutamupalabhya tadabhisaṃdhyakuśalāḥ yathārutamevāsyārthamadhimucyamānā abhāva evāyaṃ bhagavatā deśitaḥ sarvadharmāṇāmanutpāda evetyabhāvādinimittamabhiniviśante saiṣāṃ bhavati nimittadṛṣṭiḥ / ta evamabhāvādinimittamabhiniviśamānāstrīnsvabhāvānavadante parikalpitaṃ svabhāvaṃ paratantraṃ pariniṣpannaṃ ca / tatrāyaṃ parikalpitaḥ svabhāvo yadrūpamiti vā yāvannirvāṇāmiti vābhilāpaprajñaptimātrabhabhūto niḥśarīrārtho yadbālā rūpādilakṣaṇaṃ samāropattaḥ parikalpayanti / tatrāyaṃ paratantraḥ svabhāvā yattadevābhūtaparikalpamātram / tatrāyaṃ pariniṣpannaḥ svabhāvo yatsarvadharmāṇāṃ tattvaṃ
body.translated_text: What are the twenty-eight false views? The view of signs, up to the view of conceit. Among these, those who are unskilled in the implicit meaning, upon encountering in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> the statement 'all <s>dharmas</s> are without intrinsic nature, unproduced' and so forth, and grasping the meaning literally, conclude that non-existence alone is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> has taught, all <s>dharmas</s> —

body.text: tathatā / tadapavādākārāstisro dṛṣṭayo bhavanti - prajñaptyapavādadṛṣṭiḥ parikalpāpavādadṛṣṭistattvāpavādadṛṣṭiśca / ta evaṃ sarvathā sarvadharmānapavadamānāstasyā apavādadṛṣṭeḥ pratiṣṭhāpanārthaṃ kāṃcideva yuktiṃ parigṛhṇanti, ye 'pi nītārthāḥ sūtrāntā nirabhilāpadharmatādyotakāstānapi sarvān svadṛṣṭayānulomyena pariṇāmayanti / te eva dve dṛṣṭo bhavataḥ parigrahadṛṣṭiḥ pariṇatidṛṣṭiśca / te punarevaṃdṛṣṭayo bhavanti - ya etāmīdṛśīṃ dṛṣṭiṃ niśritya kuśalamakuśalaṃ vā samācarati sa niravadya eva bhavati nirdoṣaḥ sarvamevāsya tatkalyāṇatāṃ yāti, pūrvopacitāccāvaraṇātsa niḥsaratotyevameṣāṃ dve dṛṣṭī anavadyatādṛṣṭirniḥsaraṇadṛṣṭiśca / te caivaṃ svadṛṣṭāvabhiniviṣṭāstad dṛṣṭiviparyayeṇa skandhādidharmavyavasthāpakaṃ śrāvakapiṭakamavajānanti, ye ca tāmapavādadṛṣṭimanadhimuktāḥ śrāvakayānīyāstān pradviṣanti / te ete dve dṛṣṭī bhavato 'vajñādṛṣṭiḥ prakopadṛṣṭiśca / svadṛṣṭyanusāreṇa caite yathāvacchūnyatānimittāpraṇihitāni vyavasthāpayamānā atallakṣaṇe tallakṣaṇasaṃjñino viparītameṣāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ vyavasthāpayanti, evaṃcittāśca bhavanti - yasyāmīdṛśyāṃ dharmatāyāmavatarantyavatārayanti vā sarve te 'prameyaṃ puṇyaṃ prasavantītyevamete dṛṣṭī viparītadṛṣṭiḥ prasavadṛṣṭiśca / yadā punaste tāṃ dṛṣṭimārabhya paraṃranuyujyante tadā na kiṃcitsvayamicchantyabhyupagantum, chalajātibhyāṃ ca parānanuyuñjante / te ete anabhyupagamadṛṣṭiḥ kusṛtidṛṣṭiśca / te caivamabhimānino bhavanti - ya evaṃ pratipadyante [te] samyagbuddhān bhagavataḥ pūjayanti satkurvantītyeṣāṃ satkāradṛṣṭiḥ / aviparītadharmatākuśalaiśca tatā dṛṣṭervivecyamānāḥ sūpapannayā prasiddhayā yuktayā pratyāyamānā api tāṃ dṛṣṭiṃ na kathaṃcit parityajanti, etadeva tathyaṃ mithyānyadityeṣā dṛḍhamūḍhatādṛṣṭiḥ / etāsāṃ ca yathānirdiṣṭānāṃ dṛṣṭīnāṃ yadvāsanādauṣṭhulyaṃ sā mūladṛṣṭiḥ / eta eva ca saptadaśadṛṣṭayo doṣodbhāvanāmukhenāvaśiṣṭābhiḥ dṛṣṭibhiḥ punarnidiśyante / tadyathā dṛṣṭāvadṛṣṭadṛṣṭi nimittadṛṣṭirityucyate, abhāvādinimittābhiniveśina eva sataḥ sarvanimittānabhiniveśasajñitvāt / prajñaptyapavādadṛṣṭiḥ parikalpāpavādadṛṣṭistattvāpavādadṛṣṭiśca prayoganirākaraṇadṛṣṭiḥ, sarvāpavādino vyāyāmaniḥ sāmarthyasaṃjñitvāt / parigrahadṛṣṭiḥ pariṇatidṛṣṭiścānairyāṇikadṛṣṭiḥ,
body.translated_text: <s>tathatā</s> (suchness). The three views that negate that take the form: the view negating designations, the view negating conceptual construction, and the view negating reality. Those who thus negate all <s>dharmas</s> in every way, in order to establish their nihilistic view, seize upon some reasoning — even those <s>sūtras</s> that are of definitive meaning —

body.text: anupāyaprayuktasya tatphalānavāpteḥ / anavadyatādṛṣṭiniḥsaraṇadṛṣṭiścāvaraṇopacayadṛṣṭiḥ, mithyāpratipadyamānasyāvaraṇakṣayāsaṃbhavāt / avajñādṛṣṭiḥ prakopadṛṣṭiścāpuṇyaprasavadṛṣṭiḥ, saddharmasabrahmacārivipratipattimukhena mahākṣatisamāsādanāt / viparītadṛṣṭiḥ prasavadṛṣṭiśca vaiphalyadṛṣṭiḥ, [a]samyagdharmatāvyavasthāpanagrahaṇagrāhaṇairviśeṣā nadhigamāt, anabhyupagamadṛṣṭiḥ kusṛtidṛṣṭiśca nigrāhyadṛṣṭiḥ, [a]nyāyena vādaṃ kurvato jayāsaṃbhavāt / satkāradṛṣṭirabhyākhyānadṛṣṭiḥ, atadākhyāyini tatsamārāpaṇāt / dṛḍhamūḍhatādṛṣṭirakathyadṛṣṭiḥ, mithyābhiniveśinā saha sāṃ kathyapratiṣedhānnirathakatāmupādāya / mūladṛṣṭirmahādṛṣṭiḥ, tata āyatyāṃ puṣṭatarasarvadṛṣṭigatapratāpanāt / sarvā etāḥ saptaviṃśatidṛṣṭayo 'bhimānadṛṣṭiḥ, abhūtābhimānasamutthitatvāt / ata evānantaraṃ tatraiva sūtra uktamitīmāḥ saptadaśa samānāḥ daśa bhavanti, daśa samānāḥ saptadaśa bhavanti, saptaviṃśatiḥ samānā ekā bhavati, ekā samānā saptaviṃśatirbhavantīti //
body.translated_text: because one who applies wrong means does not attain the fruit of that. The view of blamelessness and the view of escape are actually views of the accumulation of obscurations, because for one who practices wrongly the exhaustion of obscurations is impossible. The view of contempt and the view of anger are views of the production of demerit, because through hostility toward the true <s>dharma</s> and fellow practitioners one incurs great harm.

body.text: niḥsvabhāvāḥ sarvadharmāḥ yasmātsvayameṣāṃ bhāvo nāsti, pratyayāṃstvapekṣya bhāvo na pratiṣidhyate / yena vā svabhāvenaite pūrvamabhūvanna tena svena bhāvena bhūyaḥ śakyamebhirbhavitumiti niḥsvabhāvāḥ / prāptābhraṣṭalakṣaṇānāmapi pratyutpannānāṃ sve bhāve 'vasthānābhāvānniḥsvabhāvāḥ / yādṛśo vādṛṣṭasatyairdharmāṇāṃ svabhāvo lakṣaṇamabhilāpaprapañcavāsanāmukhena gṛhyate tena bālagrāhānurūpeṇa svabhāvena vi[ra]hitatvānniḥ svabhāvāḥ //
body.translated_text: All <s>dharmas</s> are without intrinsic nature because they do not have existence by themselves; but existence depending on conditions is not denied. Or, because with whatever intrinsic nature they did not formerly exist, they cannot exist again with that very nature — therefore they are without intrinsic nature. Even for present things that have the character of having been attained and not lost, in their own —

body.text: api khalu sarvadharmā ucyante trayaḥ svabhāvāḥ / tatra parikalpitasya svalakṣaṇameva nāstyataḥ svalakṣaṇaniḥsvabhāvatayā niḥsvabhāvaḥ / paratantrasya svayamutpattirnāsti pratyayāpekṣaṇādato nāsya svena bhāvena bhāva ityutpattiniḥ svabhāvatayā niḥsvabhāvaḥ / pariniṣpanno viśuddhyālaṃbanatvāt paratantraparikalpitalakṣaṇābhāvasvabhāvatvācca paramārthaścaiṣa niḥsvabhāvatāprabhāvitaśceti paramārthaniḥsvabhāvatayā niḥsvabhāvaḥ / ityevaṃ ca kṛtvā niḥsvabhāvāḥ sarvadharmā draṣṭavyāḥ, na tu sarvathālakṣaṇābhāvamadhikṛtyeti //
body.translated_text: Moreover, all <s>dharmas</s> are said to be the three natures. Among these, the <s>parikalpita</s> (imagined) — its own characteristic simply does not exist, therefore it is without intrinsic nature through the absence of own-characteristic. The <s>paratantra</s> (dependent) — it does not arise by itself because it depends on conditions, therefore its existence is not by its own nature — it is without intrinsic nature through the absence of self-arising. —

body.text: api khalu mahāyāne tathāgatasya sarve 'bhiprāyāḥ saṃkṣepeṇa catvāro bhavanti / tadyathā samatābhiprāyo yadāha - ahameva tasmin samaye vipaśyī
body.translated_text: Moreover, in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, all the implicit intentions of the <s>Tathāgata</s> are, in summary, four. Namely: the intention of equality — when he says 'I myself at that time was <s>Vipaśyin</s>

body.text: samyaksaṃbuddho 'bhūvamiti, avaśiṣṭadharmakāyatvāt / kālāntarābhiprāyoyadāha - ye sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātau praṇidhānaṃ kariṣyanti te tatropa patsyanta iti, vimalacandraprabhavasya ca nāmadheyagrahaṇamātreṇa niyato bhavatyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhāviti, kālāntareṇetyabhiprāyaḥ / arthāntarābhiprāyo yadāha - niḥsvabhāvāḥ sarvadharmā anutpannā ityevamādi, ayathārutārthatvāt / pudgalāśayābhiprāyo yattadeva kuśalamūlaṃ kasyacitpraśaṃsanti kasyacidvigarha te 'lpamātrasaṃtuṣṭasya / tathā rāgacaritasya buddhakṣetravibhūti darśayati, mānacaritasya keṣāṃcideva buddhānāmadhikāṃ saṃpattiṃ varṇayanti / kaukṛtyenāvṛtasya ye buddhabodhisattveṣvapakāramapi kariṣyanti te sarve svargopagā bhaviṣyantītyāha / aniyatagotrasya mahāśrāvakā[n] buddhatve vyākaroti, ekaṃ ca yānaṃ na dvitīyamastīti deśayati śrāvakatvāśayatyājanārtham //
body.translated_text: the perfectly awakened one,' because of the remaining <s>dharmakāya</s>. The intention of another time — when he says 'those who make aspirations toward the world-realm <s>Sukhāvatī</s> will be reborn there,' and that by merely grasping the name of <s>Vimalacandraprabha</s> one becomes determined toward unsurpassed perfect awakening —

body.text: punaḥ sarve 'bhisaṃghayo 'bhisamasya catvāro bhavantya vatāraṇābhisaṃdhyādayaḥ / tatra avatāraṇābhisaṃdhiḥ śrāvakeṣu draṣṭavyaḥ, śāsanā vatāraṇārthamanutrāsāya rūpādyastitvadeśanāt / lakṣaṇābhisaṃdhistriṣu parikalpitādisvabhāveṣu draṣṭavyaḥ, niḥsvabhāvānutpannādisarvadharmadeśanāt / pratipakṣābhisaṃdhiḥ doṣāṇāṃ vinaye draṣṭavyo yathāṣṭāvaraṇapratipakṣatāgrayānasaṃbhāṣā / aṣṭāvaraṇāni buddhadharmāvajñeti vistaraḥ / tadudāharaṇāni ca yathāyogaṃ caturabhiprāryānirdeśāni draṣṭavyāni / pariṇāmanābhisaṃdhirabhidhānagāmbhīrye draṣṭavyaḥ, yadāha -
body.translated_text: Furthermore, all implicit meanings are also four, beginning with the implicit meaning of introduction. Among these, the implicit meaning of introduction should be seen with respect to <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers) — because of teaching the existence of form and the rest, in order to introduce them into the teaching without frightening them. The implicit meaning of characteristics should be seen with respect to the three natures — the imagined and the rest — because the lack of intrinsic nature —

body.text:
asāre sārama[ta]yo viparyāse ca susthitāḥ /
kleśena ca susaṃkliṣṭā labhante bodhimuttamām // iti /
body.translated_text:
Those who regard the essenceless as having essence, who are well-established in distortion,
and who are thoroughly defiled by defilements — they attain the supreme awakening.

body.text: atrāyamabhisaṃdhiḥ - avikṣepe yeṣāṃ sārabuddhiḥ pradhānabuddhiḥ, vikṣepo hi visāraścetasaḥ viparyāse ca susthitāḥ iti nityasukhaśucyātmaviparyayeṇānityādike viparyāse ca susthitā aparihāṇitaḥ kleśena ca susaṃkliṣṭāḥ iti dīrghaduṣkara vyāyāmaśrameṇātyartha parikliṣṭāḥ //
body.translated_text: Here the implicit meaning is as follows: 'who regard the essenceless as having essence' means those for whom the notion of essence is the notion of what is primary, regarding non-distraction — for distraction is the spreading out of the mind. 'Well-established in distortion' means well-established from the standpoint of non-decline in the distortion of the impermanent and the rest as permanent, pleasant, pure, and self. 'Thoroughly defiled by defilement' means through the exertion of long and difficult effort —

body.text: vaipulye dharmasamādhikuśalabodhisattvanirdeśaḥ śamathānuśaṃsaṃ vipaśyanānuśaṃsaṃ tadubhayānuśaṃsaṃ cādhikṛtya veditavyaḥ / tatra śamathānuśaṃso dvividhaḥ / kṣaṇe kṣaṇe prakarṣagāminyā prasrabdhyā nirantaramāśrayaspharaṇāt pratikṣaṇaṃ sarvadauṣṭhulyāśraya drāvaṇam, aviśeṣeṇa sarvadeśanādharme karasatādhimokṣasamādhānādvividhaskandhādyarthākārasaṃjñāvigatāyāḥ sūtrādidharmārāmarateḥ
body.translated_text: In the extensive scriptures, the instruction on <s>Bodhisattvas</s> skilled in <s>dharma-samādhi</s> should be understood with reference to the benefits of <s>śamatha</s> (calm), the benefits of <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight), and the benefits of both together. Among these, the benefit of <s>śamatha</s> is twofold: because of the uninterrupted pervasion of the basis by progressively intensifying <s>prasrabdhi</s> (pliancy) moment after moment, there is the elimination of all unwholesome dispositions at every moment —

body.text: pratilambhaśca / vipaśyanānuśaṃso 'pi dvividhaḥ / yathāpravicittadharmanirantarāsaṃpramoṣātpratismṛtimātramukhenāparicchinnākāro 'pramāṇaḥ sūtrādidharmeṣu prajñāvabhāsaḥ, āśrayaparivṛttipūrvarūpabhūtānāṃ cāvikalpitānāmanabhisaṃskṛtānāṃ nimittānāṃ samudācāraśca / tadubhayānuśaṃso dharmakāyasya jñeyāvaraṇa prahāṇāśrayaparivṛttisaṃgṛhītasya paripūraye daśamyāṃ bhūmau pariniṣpattaye vā tāthāgatyāṃ bhūmāvuttarāduttaratara niṣyandavāsanādhānayogena hetuparigraha iti //
body.translated_text: and attainment. The benefit of <s>vipaśyanā</s> is also twofold: through the uninterrupted non-forgetfulness of the <s>dharmas</s> that have been investigated, merely through the channel of recollection, the light of wisdom in the <s>dharma</s> teachings such as <s>sūtras</s> and the rest becomes unlimited in scope, without defined boundaries; and the arising of unconstructed and non-conceptualized signs that are the preliminary form of the transformation of the basis —

body.text: tadetatpañcavidhāyā bhāvanāyāḥ phalaṃ pañcavidhaṃ nirvartata iti saṃdarśitam / pañcavidhā bhāvanā katamā / prasrabdhinimittabhāvanāsaṃbhinnabhāvanānimittabhāvanānābhogabhāvanā parinirvṛtinimittabhāvanā ca //
body.translated_text: Thus it has been shown that the fruit of the fivefold cultivation is fivefold. What is the fivefold cultivation? Cultivation with the sign of pliancy (<s>prasrabdhinimittabhāvanā</s>), cultivation that is unimpaired (<s>asaṃbhinnabhāvanā</s>), cultivation without signs (<s>animittabhāvanā</s>), cultivation without effort (<s>anābhogabhāvanā</s>), and cultivation with the sign of complete cessation (<s>parinirvṛtinimittabhāvanā</s>).

body.text: kena kāraṇena tulye dharmakāyaniṣyandatve vaipulyadharmo dhūpamālyādibhiḥ pūjyo na tathā śrāvakayānadharmaḥ / vaipulyadharmasya sarvasattvahitasukhādhiṣṭhānatāmupādāya mahārthatayā niruttarāprameyapuṇyaprasavāyatanatvāt //
body.translated_text: For what reason, when both [the Mahāyāna and Śrāvakayāna dharmas] equally have the <s>dharmakāya</s> as their outflow-nature, is the <s>Vaipulya</s> (Mahāyāna) <s>Dharma</s> worthy of worship with incense, garlands, etc., but not equally the <s>Śrāvakayāna Dharma</s>? Because the <s>Vaipulya Dharma</s>, being established as the basis for the welfare and happiness of all beings, is of great purpose and is the source of unsurpassed and immeasurable merit.

body.text: prāptiviniścayo nāma caturthaḥ samuccayaḥ
prāptiviniścayo 'dhigantṛpudgalavyavasthānato 'dhigamavyavasthānataśca draṣṭavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: The determination of attainment (<s>prāptiviniścaya</s>) should be viewed from the standpoint of the establishment of the attaining persons and from the standpoint of the establishment of the attainments.

body.text: asatyapi pudgaladravye pudgalavyavasthānaṃ caturbhiḥ kāraṇaiḥ / tadyathā sukhasaṃvyavahārārtham, rūpādīnāṃ bahūnāṃ bahudhābhinnalakṣaṇasaṃjñānāmekayā sāmudāyikyā sattvaprajñaptyākṛcchreṇa ehi yāhi ityevamādisaṃvyavaharaṇāt / lokānuvṛttyartham, na hi loke dharmamātrasaṃjñābhiḥ sarvaḥ saṃvyavahāro nirūḍhaḥ kiṃtarhi prāyeṇa sattvasaṃjñayā / tasmāllokena saha saṃvyavaharadbhirāryairavaśyaṃ so 'nuvartitavya iti / anutrāsārtham, pratītyasamutpādadharmatāyāma kovidāḥ sahasāditaḥ sarvathā sattvābhāvaṃ śrutvottrasyeyuriti / ātmanaḥ pareṣāṃ ca doṣavattvaguṇavattvodbhāvanārthaṃ ca, itarathā hi sattvaprajñaptimantareṇa saṃkleśavyavadānalakṣaṇamātradeśanāyāṃ satyāmamuṣmin saṃtāne 'mī doṣāḥ prahīṇā amī vā guṇā utpannā iti na śakyate vijñātumiti //
body.translated_text: Even though there is no real substance of a person (<s>pudgaladravya</s>), the establishment of the person-designation is for four reasons: (1) For the purpose of easy communication—because through one collective designation of 'being' (<s>sattva</s>) for the many [phenomena] of form etc. that have diverse and manifold characteristics and names, one communicates without difficulty, saying 'come, go,' and so forth. (2) For the purpose of conforming to the world—because in the world, not all communication is established through designations of <s>dharmas</s> alone, but rather mostly through the designation of 'being'; therefore, noble ones communicating with the world must necessarily follow that [convention]. (3) For the purpose of not causing fear—because those unskilled in the <s>dharmatā</s> (nature of reality) of dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>) might become frightened upon suddenly hearing from the very beginning that beings are entirely non-existent. (4) For the purpose of revealing the faults and virtues of self and others—because otherwise, without the designation of 'being,' when only the characteristics of defilement and purification are taught, it would be impossible to know that 'in this continuum these faults have been abandoned' or 'these virtues have arisen.'

body.text: pudgalavyavasthānaṃ punaścaritādiprabhedena saptavidham //
body.translated_text: The establishment of the person-designation is further sevenfold, through the distinction of conduct (<s>carita</s>) and so forth.

body.text: tatra rāgādicaritastīvrāyatarāgaḥ, hīne 'pi rañjanīye vastunyadhimātrarāgotpādādutpannasya ca ciramanubandhāt / ityevaṃ yāvadvitarkacarito yathāsvaṃ vastuni yojayitavyaḥ / samabhāgacaritaḥprakṛti[stha]ḥ saṃkleśaḥ autkaṭayamāndyavivarjitasamāvasthe kleśa ityarthaḥ, yathāvastvanurūpaṃ kleśasamudācārāt / mandarajaskaḥ prakṛtisthaḥ tanutarakleśaḥ, prakṛtisthebhya uktalakṣaṇebhyastanutarāḥ kleśā asya, so 'yaṃ prakṛtisthaḥ, utkaṭe 'pi vastuni pūrvapratipakṣābhyāsavaśena prakṛtyā mṛdukleśasamudācārāditi //
body.translated_text: Among these, one of desire-conduct (<s>rāgacarita</s>) has intense and extensive desire—because even in regard to an inferior object of attraction, intense desire arises, and once arisen, it persists for a long time. Likewise, up to one of discursive-thought-conduct (<s>vitarkacarita</s>), [each] should be applied to its own respective object...

body.text: śrāvakayāniko gotrendriyapraṇidhānāśayālaṃbanapratipattiphalaprabhedairnidiṣṭo veditavyaḥ / prakṛtyā mṛdvindriyatvaṃ punarasya pratyekabuddhabodhisattvendriyā pekṣayā, itarathā hi dharmānusāryādayastīkṣṇendriyā ityetadvirudhyeta /
body.translated_text: One of the <s>Śrāvaka</s> vehicle (<s>śrāvakayānika</s>) should be understood as taught through the distinctions of lineage (<s>gotra</s>), faculties (<s>indriya</s>), aspiration (<s>praṇidhāna</s>), resolve (<s>āśaya</s>), object (<s>ālambana</s>), practice (<s>pratipatti</s>), and fruit (<s>phala</s>). Having by nature weak faculties; compared to the faculties of <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>...

body.text: tatrānutpāditapūrvanirvedhabhāgīyo 'prāptapūrvakaphalaśca khaḍgaviṣāṇakalpo bhavatyeka vihārī, tadanyaḥ pratyekajino vargacārī draṣṭavyaḥ / vyākaraṇaṃ ca pratyalabhata ityaṣṭābhyāṃ bhūmāvanutpattikeṣu dharmeṣu kṣāntiṃ pratilabhata ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Among these, one who has not previously produced the penetrative portions (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>) and has not previously attained a [noble] fruit is like a rhinoceros horn (<s>khaḍgaviṣāṇakalpa</s>), dwelling alone. The other, the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> who travels in a group (<s>vargacārī</s>), should be seen [as different]. And the prediction (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>) of <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>...

body.text: asaṃbhṛtasaṃbhārādayo mokṣabhāgīyānāṃ ca mṛdumadhyādhi mātratayā nirvedhabhāgīyotpādanaṃ satyābhisamayaṃ ca pratiniyatāniyatatajjanmakālikatvādyathākramaṃ veditavyāḥ / tatra satyādhipateye dharme 'dhimuktiprasādalakṣaṇāni mokṣabhāgīyāni, tatraiva dharmanidhyānakṣāntilakṣaṇāni nirvedhabhāgīyāni, śraddhāpradhānatvātprajñāpradhānatvācca yathākramam / laukikā gradharmaprakṛtyaiva kṣaṇika ityaprāvandhika ityarthaḥ / no tu vāsanāparihāṇita iti nirvāṇādhikārikasya kuśalamūlasyotpāditapūrvasyāpunarutpādyatvāt //
body.translated_text: From one who has not accumulated the accumulations and so forth—through the mild, medium, and intense [grades] of the portions leading to liberation (<s>mokṣabhāgīya</s>)—the production of the penetrative portions and realization of the truths (<s>satyābhisamaya</s>) should be understood as determined and undetermined, and as occurring in that very lifetime, in due order...

body.text: mṛdu mokṣabhāgī yamadhikṛtyoktaṃ bhagavatā -
body.translated_text: With reference to the mild portion leading to liberation, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

body.text:
samyagdṛṣṭiradhimātraṃ laukikī yasya vidyate /
api jātisahasrāṇi nāsau gacchati durgatim // iti //
body.translated_text: 'One who possesses intense mundane right view— / even through a thousand births, that one does not go to an unfortunate destiny.'

body.text: api khalu caturvidhaṃ mokṣabhāgīyam - ādhikārikamādhimokṣikamādhikāmikamābhigāmikaṃ ca / kuśaladharmacchandamupādāya yāvanmokṣārthaṃ kriyate tadādhikārikam / tatpratisaṃyuktadeśanādhimokṣasahagataṃ yattadādhimokṣikam / prītiprasādasahagatamokṣālaṃbanamanaskārabahulaṃ yattadādhikāmikam / nirvedhabhāyīyotpāda niyataṃ tatraiva janmani yattadābhigāmikam //
body.translated_text: Moreover, the portion leading to liberation (<s>mokṣabhāgīya</s>) is fourfold: based on authority (<s>ādhikārika</s>), based on conviction (<s>ādhimokṣika</s>), based on desire (<s>ādhikāmika</s>), and approaching [liberation] (<s>ābhigāmika</s>). Whatever is done for the sake of liberation beginning with the aspiration for wholesome <s>dharmas</s>—that is based on authority...

body.text: nirvedhamāgīyaṃ ṣaḍvidham - ānulomikaṃ prākarṣikaṃ prātivedhikamanyapāriṇāmikamaikajanmikamekāsanikaṃ ca / tatra yatsatyālambanakāramādito mṛdukaṃ kuśalamūlamutpadyate tadānulomikam / yanmadhyaṃ tatprākarṣikam, tataḥ tatprakṛṣṭataratvāt / yadadhimātraṃ satyaprativedhāya tatraiva janmani saṃvartate tatprātivedhikam / tatpunaryadaniyatagotrāṇāṃ bodhiviśeṣāya
body.translated_text: The penetrative portion (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>) is sixfold: conforming (<s>ānulomika</s>), intensive (<s>prākarṣika</s>), penetrative (<s>prātivedhika</s>), transferable to another [vehicle] (<s>anyapāriṇāmika</s>), occurring in a single lifetime (<s>aikajanmika</s>), and occurring in a single session (<s>ekāsanika</s>). Among these, that wholesome root which initially arises in a mild form having the truths as its object...

body.text: pariṇāmyate tacca pratyekabuddhānāmanācāryakābhisaṃbodhāya janmāntare pariṇamati tadanyapāriṇāmikam / yattatraiva janmani satyaprativedhāya saṃvartate tadaikajanmikam / yattatraivāsane tadekāsanikamiti //
body.translated_text: is transferred—and that which is transferred for the self-awakening of <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> without a teacher, maturing in another lifetime, is the transferable [type]. That which conduces to the penetration of the truths in that very lifetime is the single-lifetime [type]...

body.text: kāyasākṣī vimokṣalābhyanāgāmī, aṣṭau vimokṣān kāyena sākṣātkṛtvopasaṃpadya viharaṇāt / aṣṭau vimokṣā rūpī rūpāṇi paśyatītyevamādayaḥ paścānnirdekṣyante / prajñāvimuktaḥ prajñāvipakṣakleśāvaraṇamātrāśeṣaprahāṇāt / ubhayato bhāgavimuktaḥ sarvakleśasamāpattyāvaraṇābhyāṃ yo vimuktaḥ / srotāpattiphalapratipannaka ekāsanikaṃ nirvedhabhāgīyamārabhya yāvadādyaṃ phalaṃ na prāpnoti //
body.translated_text: The body-witness (<s>kāyasākṣin</s>) is a non-returner who has attained the liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>)—because having directly realized and attained the eight liberations with the body. The eight liberations such as 'one who has form sees forms' and so forth will be taught later. The wisdom-...

body.text: kaḥ punardarśanamārgāvasāne ādyaṃ phalaṃ prāpnoti / yaḥ pradeśavairāgyeṇāpi kāmebhyo 'vītarāgaḥ samyaktvaṃ niyāmamavakrāmati / yastu pūrvaṃ laukikena mārgeṇa kāmāvacarān bhāvanāprahātavyān ṣaṭprakārān prahāya yatra yo vītarāgo bhavan paścātsamyaktvaṃ niyāmamavakrāmati sa ṣoḍaśe cittakṣaṇe sakṛdāgāmyeva bhavati / navāpi prakārān prahāya kāmavītarāgo bhavan yo niyāmamavakrāmati so 'nāgāmyeva bhavati //
body.translated_text: Who then attains the first fruit at the end of the path of seeing (<s>darśanamārga</s>)? One who enters the correct certainty (<s>samyaktvaniyāma</s>) without being free from passion for sense-pleasures even through partial dispassion. But one who has previously become free from passion for sense-pleasures through the mundane path...

body.text: sarvadarśanaprahātavyaprahāṇe 'pi trayāṇāmeva saṃyojanānāṃ prahāṇāt srotāpannavacanam, eṣāṃ mokṣaprāptibibandhanatvena prādhānyāt / tathāhi satkāyadṛṣṭayā pañcopādānaskandhānātmata ātmīyataścābhiniveśyālayārāmatayā duḥkhānnoccalati / uccalito 'pi kathaṃcinmokṣaṃ prati śīlavrataparāmarśena vicikitsayā cāsanmārgābhiniveśātsanmārgasaṃśayanācca mithyā niryāti samyaktvamaniryāti // punaḥ satkāyadṛṣṭayā jñeye vipratipadyate, duḥkhamātra [ā]tmātmīyalakṣaṇa samāropaṇāt / śīlavrataparāmarśena dṛṣṭau, tayā śuddhipratyayanāt / vicikitsayā pratipakṣe, ratnatrayāniścayanāditi //
body.translated_text: Even though all that is to be abandoned by seeing is abandoned, the statement 'stream-enterer' (<s>srotāpanna</s>) is made with reference to the abandonment of only three fetters (<s>saṃyojana</s>), because of their predominance in binding one from attaining liberation. For through the view of the real self (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), one clings to the five...

body.text: sakṛdā[gā]miphalapratipannakaḥ darśanamārgādūrdhvaṃ kāmāvacarasya yāvanmadhyamadhyasya kleśaprakārasya prahāṇamārge yaḥ pudgalaḥ / sakṛdāgāmī madhyamṛdoḥ kleśaprakārasya prahāṇa mārga parisamāptau yaḥ pudgalaḥ / anāgāmiphalapratipannakaḥ sakṛdāgāmiphalādūrdhvaṃ kāmāvacarāṇāṃ mṛdvadhimātramṛdumadhyayoḥ
body.translated_text: The one practicing toward the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmiphala</s>): the person who is on the abandonment-path above the path of seeing, up to the abandonment-path of the medium-medium defilement-type of the desire realm. The once-returner (<s>sakṛdāgāmin</s>): the person on the abandonment-path of the medium-mild defilement-type...

body.text: kleśaprakārayoḥ prahāṇamārge yaḥ pudgalaḥ / anāgāmī navamasya mṛdumṛdoḥ kleśaprakārasya prahāṇāya mārgaparisamāptau yaḥ pudgalaḥ //
body.translated_text: defilement-types. The non-returner (<s>anāgāmin</s>): the person at the completion of the path for the abandonment of the ninth, mild-mild defilement-type.

body.text: sarvakāmāvacarabhāvanāprahātavyaprahāṇe 'pi pañcānāmavarabhāgīyānāṃ saṃyojanānāṃ prahāṇādanāgāmivacanaṃ sūtre eṣāṃ gatidhātvavarakāraṇatvena prādhānyāt / gatyavaraṃ punaḥ narakatiryakpretagatayaḥ / dhātvavaraṃ kāmadhātuḥ / tatra satkāyadṛṣṭiśīlavrataparāmarśavicikitsābhiḥ gatya varāsamatikrāntatvātkāraṇatvam / kāmacchandavyāpādābhyāṃ dhātvavarāsamatikramāditi //
body.translated_text: Even though all that is to be abandoned through cultivation in the desire realm is abandoned, the statement 'non-returner' in the <s>sūtra</s> is made with reference to the abandonment of only five lower fetters (<s>avarabhāgīya saṃyojana</s>), because of their predominance as the cause of the lower realm and destiny...

body.text: traidhātukasarvakleśaprahāṇe 'pi pañcānāmūrdhvabhāgīyānāṃ prahāṇādarhadvacanam, ūrdhvopādānāparityāgakāraṇatvena prādhānyam / tatra rūpārūpyarāgābhyāṃ kāmadhātau ūrdhvopādānaṃ rūpārūpyadhātūpapattirityarthaḥ / auddhatyamānāvidyābhirurdhvāparityāgaḥ, tṛṣṇāmānavicikitsottaradhyāyitvena satra saṃkleśāditi //
body.translated_text: Even though all defilements of the three realms are abandoned, the statement '<s>Arhat</s>' is made with reference to the abandonment of only five upper fetters (<s>ūrdhvabhāgīya</s>), because of their predominance as the cause of not relinquishing upper clinging. Among these, through desire-realm attachment and form-and-formless-realm attachment...

body.text: kulaṃ kulaḥ kulaḥ srotāpanna eva sakṛdāgāmiphalapratipannako deveṣu vā manuṣyeṣu vā niyamena dvau bhavau saṃsṛtya parinirvāti / ekavīcikaḥ sakṛdāgāmyevānāgāmiphalapratipannako deveṣvevaikaṃ bhavaṃ saṃsṛtyaṃ parinirvāti / ekā vīcirantaraṃ janmāvakāśo 'sya so 'yamekavīcikaḥ / antarāparinirvāyī yena kleśāvedhenopapattideśaṃ gatvā pratisandadhyāttatparikṣaye sati yenānuśayamātreṇa maraṇādūrdhva skandhānabhinirvartayan tadavaśeṣe satyantarābhavamabhinirvartya pūrvābhyastamārgasaṃmukhībhāvādeva sa viśiṣṭānuśayaprahāṇe parinirvāti / sa punarupapattideśaṃ pratyanuccalitoccalitamātradūragabhāvasthatayā trividho veditavyaḥ satpuruṣagatisūtrānusāreṇa / anabhisaṃskāreṇa yo mārgaṃ saṃmukhīkṛtyeti pūrvaṃ svabhyastatvātsvarasavāhitayāprayatne[ne]tyarthaḥ / viparyayādabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī / ūrdhvasrotā dvividhaḥ - akaniṣṭhago bhavāgragaśca / tatra akaniṣṭhaga āsvādanābahulatayotpannotpannamṛdvādidhyānaprakārāsvādanāt brahmakāyikānārabhya nirantaraṃ
body.translated_text: A 'clan-to-clan' (<s>kulakula</s>) is a stream-enterer who is practicing toward the fruit of once-returning and who, having wandered through exactly two existences among gods or among humans, attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. A 'one-seed' (<s>ekavīcika</s>) is a once-returner who is practicing toward the fruit of non-return...

body.text: sarveṣu sthānāntareṣu sakṛtsakṛdupapadyamāno yāvadakaniṣṭhānpraviśya parinirvāti / bhavāgragaścaturthasya dhyānasyāvyavakīrṇabhāvitvāt kevalaṃ śuddhāvāsān parihṛtya tathaiva yāvadbhavāgraṃ gatvā parinirvāti / vyavakīrṇabhāvitasya caturthasya dhyānasya mṛdvādipañcaprakārabhāvitatvādyathākramaṃ pañcasu śuddhāvāseṣūpapattirveditavyā / cetayitvācetayitveti svayamātmānamupakramamāṇo 'nu[pa]kramamāṇo vetyarthaḥ / dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihārātparihāṇameti laukikebhyo dhyānebhya ityarthaḥ / indriyottāpanaṃ punaradhimātratānayanaṃ tīkṣṇakaraṇamityarthaḥ / ata evākopyadharmā bhavyaścendriyāṇyuttāpayitumiti noktam, prakṛtyā tīkṣṇendriyatvāt //
body.translated_text: being reborn once in each successive abode up to the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> [heaven], attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. [The one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s>] at the peak of existence—because of the uninterrupted nature of the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, passes through only the Pure Abodes (<s>Śuddhāvāsa</s>)...

body.text: kāmāvacararūpāvacara eva bodhisattvo nārūpyāvacaraḥ, prabhāvaprāptasya sattvaparipācanānāyatanatāmupādāya tatrānupapattitaḥ / ārūpyadhātuvyavakarṣitena dhyāneneti paryudastārūpyopapattikena samādhinetyarthaḥ / dhyānasukhaviharatyaparihīṇa eva dhyānebhyaḥ, dhyānavyāvartanakuśalatvāt / sattvaparipācanārthaṃ kāmadhātāvapi bodhisattva upapadyata iti veditavyam //
body.translated_text: A <s>Bodhisattva</s> is only in the desire realm and form realm, not in the formless realm—because, given that one who has attained sovereign power has no basis for maturing beings in the formless realm, one is not reborn there. Through the <s>dhyāna</s> that has been withdrawn from the formless realm...

body.text: sarvāṃ bodhisattvacaryāmiti tuṣitabhavanavāsamupādāya yāvanmāraparājayam / buddhacaryāṃ ca darśayatītyabhisaṃbodhimupādāya yāvanmahāparinirvāṇam //
body.translated_text: 'All <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct': from dwelling in the <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven up to the defeat of <s>Māra</s>. 'And he displays <s>Buddha</s>-conduct': from full awakening (<s>abhisaṃbodhi</s>) up to the great <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.

body.text: adhimukticārī bodhisattvagotre vyavasthita ādito mahābodhiprasthānamupādāya yāvatpramuditāṃ bhūmiṃ na praviśati, pratyātmaṃ lokottarābhigamābhāvāt / adhyāśayacāro daśasu bhūmiṣu, lokottareṇādhigamena viśuddhāśayatvāt / nimittacārī ṣaṭsu bhūmiṣu, anicchato 'pi nimittavyavakiraṇāt / animittacārī saptamyām, yatnaṃ kurvato yāvadicchaṃ nimittāsamudācārāt / anabhisaṃskāracārī śeṣāsu bhūmiṣu, vaipākikanirvikalpajñānapratilambhāditi //
body.translated_text: An aspiration-conduct <s>Bodhisattva</s> (<s>adhimukticārī</s>) is one established in the <s>Bodhisattva</s> lineage, from the initial setting forth toward great awakening until not yet entering the first stage (<s>Pramuditā bhūmi</s>)—because of the absence of personal supramundane realization. A resolution-conduct <s>Bodhisattva</s> (<s>adhyāśayacārī</s>)...

body.text: sakṛnnairyāṇikaḥ sakṛttraidhātukāvacarānkleśān prajahāti / prakāraśa ityadhimātrādhimātrānkāmarūpārūpyāvacarānbhāvanāprahātavyānanuśayān prajahāti, evaṃ yāvan mṛdumṛdūn darśanaprahātavyān na tu laukikamārgavadbhūmiprakārabhedena pṛthakpṛthagityarthaḥ / tatredaṃ jñāpakaṃ yathoktamaṃgulyagrasūtre - "yatkiṃcidrūpaṃ yāvadvijñānamatītānāgatapratyutpannamiti vistareṇa yāvaddūre yadvāntike tatsarvamekadhyamasaṃkṣipyaikaṃ
body.translated_text: The <s>sakṛnnairyāṇika</s> (one bound for liberation in a single return) abandons the defilements of all three realms at once. 'In various types' means one abandons the latent tendencies to be abandoned through cultivation belonging to the desire, form, and formless realms, beginning with the strongest of the strong, and so on down to the weakest of the weak, and those to be abandoned through seeing — but not separately according to the distinctions of level and type as in the mundane path. Here is the evidence for this, as stated in the <s>Aṅgulyagrasūtra</s>: 'Whatever form, up to consciousness, past, future, or present,' and so on in detail, 'whether far or near — having condensed all of that into one

body.text: bhāgaṃ karotyekaṃ piṇḍamekaṃ puñjamekaṃ rāśiṃ karotyekaṃ kṛtvātaḥ pratisaṃśikṣate sarvametadanityaṃ sarvaṃ duḥkhamiti vistaraḥ / dvayorevādyantayoḥ phalayoḥ prajñāpyate / tayostraidhātukasarvadarśanabhāvanāprahātavyāśeṣaprahāṇaprabhāvitatvādyathākramam / madhyayostu na prajñāpyate, tayordṛṣṭasatyasya kāmavacarāṇāmeva bhāvanāprahātavyānāṃ sāvaśeṣaniravaśeṣaprahāṇaprabhāvitatvāt / sakṛnnairyāṇikaṃ cādhikṛtya vibhaṅgasūtre srotāpannānantaramarhadvyavasthānaṃ veditavyam / sa dṛṣṭe dharme yadyājñāṃ tārāgayati sarvato niḥśeṣamavītarāgatvātpraṇidhānavaśena kāmadhātāvupapadyate kṣipraparinirvāṇārtham //
body.translated_text: portion, one makes it one mass, one heap, one aggregate, one collection; having made it one, one then trains thus: all this is impermanent, all is suffering' and so forth in detail. Only two, the first and last, of the fruits are designated. Because those two are empowered respectively by the complete and exhaustive abandonment of all defilements to be abandoned through seeing and cultivation in all three realms. But the two intermediate ones are not designated, because those two are empowered by the partial and complete abandonment of only the defilements of the desire realm to be abandoned through cultivation, for one who has seen the truths. And with reference to the <s>sakṛnnairyāṇika</s>, the establishment of the <s>arhat</s> immediately after the <s>srotāpanna</s> (stream-enterer) in the <s>Vibhaṅgasūtra</s> should be understood. If in this very life one does not attain final knowledge, because one is not completely free from desire for all, through the power of aspiration one is reborn in the <s>kāmadhātu</s> (desire realm) for the purpose of swift <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.

body.text: abhisamayavyavasthānaṃ daśavidham / tatra dharmābhisamayaḥ satyādhipateyeṣu sūtrādiṣu dharmeṣu paratoghoṣamadhipatiṃ kṛtvā dhimātrasyādhimuktiprasādasya paścimamokṣabhāgīyasaṃgṛhītasya pratilambhaḥ / tathāhi tadadhimuktiprasādapratilambhāttāni satyāni dharmābhisamayenābhisamitānītyucyante / arthābhisamayasteṣveva dharmeṣu yoniśomanaskāramadhipatikṛtvādhimātrāyāḥ satyeṣu dharmanidhyānakṣānte[:] paścimanirvedhabhāgīya saṃgṛhī[tā]yāḥ pratilambhaḥ / sā punardharmanidhyānakṣāntistrividhena yoniśomanaskāreṇa prabhāvitā adhimātramṛdunā tajjanmakāleṣūṣmagateṣu, adhimātramadhyena mūrdhvasu kṣāntiṣu ca, adhimātrādhimātreṇa laukikeṣvagradharmeṣviti / tattvābhisamayo darśanamārgaḥ / tatra punaḥ satyavyavasthāpanānyabhisamayāntikāni saṃvṛtijñānāni pratilambhato lokottarajñānādhipatyena tadabījapoṣaṇānna tu sammukhīkaroti ṣoḍaśānāṃ darśanamārgacittakṣaṇānāṃ nirantaratvena laukikacittānavakāśāt / pṛṣṭhābhisamayo darśanamārgādūrdhvasarvabhāvanāmārgo laukiko lokottaro vā / ratnābhisamayaḥ samyaksaṃbuddho vata bhagavān, svākhyāto 'sya dharmavinayaḥ, supratipannaḥ śrāvakasaṃgha ityevamavetya niścityāryaśrāvakasya buddhādiṣu prasādaḥ / asamudācārābhisamayo yasyākaraṇasaṃvarasyāyaṃkāntaśīla saṃgṛhītasya lābhāttadvipakṣanarakādyasamudācāraṃ pratyevaṃ niścayaḥ pravarttate kṣoṇā me narakāḥ ityevamādiḥ so 'samudācārābhisamayaḥ / niṣṭhābhisamayaḥ sarvadauṣṭhulyānāṃ pratiprasrabdhirityevamādiryathā mārgasatye niṣṭhāmārgo nirdiṣṭaḥ / eta eva saptābhisamayāḥ śrāvakāṇāṃ paratoghoṣamāgamya pratilambhataḥ śrāvakābhisamaya ityucyate / paratoghoṣamanāgamya pratilambhataḥ pratyeka[buddha]bhisamaya iti / bodhisattvābhisamaya eṣu saptasvabhisamayeṣu bodhisattvasya yā samudāgamakṣāntiḥ śrāvakapratyekabuddhavinayopāyakauśalyārthaṃ
body.translated_text: The establishment of <s>abhisamaya</s> (realization) is tenfold. Among these, <s>dharmābhisamaya</s> (realization of the <s>dharma</s>) is the attainment, for one with supreme aspiration and faith, taking as dominant the voice of another regarding the <s>dharma</s> teachings such as <s>sūtras</s> and the rest that are governed by the truths — the attainment included in the final portion conducive to liberation, of supreme conviction and faith. For through that attainment of conviction and faith, those truths —

body.text: no tu sākṣātkriyā sattvāpekṣayā hīnayānāniryāṇāt / api khalu tatprathamato bodhisattvasya bhūmipraveśābhisamaya ityucyate //
body.translated_text: but not direct realization — because with respect to beings, there is still the possibility of departure through the inferior vehicle. Moreover, this is what is called the <s>Bodhisattva's</s> realization of entering the stages for the first time.

body.text: etaṃ cābhisamaya niśrityocyate - śrāvakābhisamayādbodhisattvābhisamasya kaḥ prativiśeṣaḥ ālaṃbanaviśeṣato vaipulyālaṃbanatvāt / upastambhaviśeṣataḥ paripūrṇamahākalpāsakhyeyamahāpuṇyajñānasaṃbhāraparipūraṇāt / prativedhaviśeṣataḥ pudgaladharmanairātmyādhipateyadharmaprayogavedhato lokottareṇa jñānena tadubhayaprativedhāt abhyupagamaviśeṣataḥ svātmasamatayā sarvasattvābhyupagamāt / niryāṇaviśeṣato daśabhirbhūmibhirniryāṇāt / parigrahaviśeṣato 'pratiṣṭhitanirvāṇaparigrahaṇāt / pratiṣṭhāparivāraviśeṣato buddhakṣatrapariśīdhanādvineyajanopagrahaṇācca / abhijanmaviśeṣataḥ pitṛvaṃśasaṃdhārakaurasaputralakṣaṇatvāt / janmaviśeṣataḥ pariṣanmaṇḍaleṣūpapannaḥ / phalaviśeṣaśca punaḥ [āśraya]parivṛttiviśeṣataḥ kliṣṭākliṣṭasarvaprakāradauṣṭhulyaprahāṇātsarvaniruttaraguṇāśrayatvenāśrayaparivartanāt / guṇasamṛddhiviśeṣato balavaṃśāradyāveṇikabuddhadharmādyaparimitaguṇaniṣpatteḥ / pañcākāraviśeṣato viśuddhyādiviśeṣāt / tatra viśuddhiviśeṣaḥ savāsanakleśaprahāṇāt / pariśuddhiviśeṣo buddhakṣetrapariśodhanāt / kāyaviśeṣo dharmakāyapariniṣpādanāt / bhogaviśeṣaḥ sadā bodhisattveḥ saha parṣanmaṇḍaleṣu vicitradharmasaṃbhogāt / kamaviśeṣo yathārhaṃ nirmāṇeḥ samantādanantāparyanteṣu lokadhātuṣu buddhakṛtyānuṣṭhānāditi / kāyatrayaviśeṣataḥ svabhāvikasāmbhāgikanairmāṇikāyapariniṣpattilābhāt / nirvāṇaviśeṣato nirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau sarvasattvahitāya sarvaguṇāsamucchedāt / miśropamiśrajñānaśaktilābhaviśeṣataḥ suviśuddhadharmadhātvekarasatayā tadāśritāsu sarvākāravarajñatāsu pratyekaṃ sarvabuddhānāṃ sāmarthyāt / āvaraṇaviśuddhiviśeṣataḥ sarvakleśajñeyāvaraṇaprahāṇāt / miśropamiśrakarmakriyāviśeṣata ekaikasattvavinayanaṃ prati sarvabuddhādhipatyāt / abhisaṃbodhinirvāṇasaṃdarśanopāyaviśeṣato daśasu dikṣu yathāyogaṃ sarvalokadhātuṣu yāvadaparāntaṃ punaḥpunarbuddhotpādādi saṃdarśanena sarvavineyajanaparipācanavimocanāt / pañcākāraparitrāṇaviśeṣataśca
body.translated_text: And based on this realization it is said: 'What is the distinction of the <s>Bodhisattva's</s> realization compared to that of the <s>śrāvaka</s>?' From the distinction of the object — because it takes the extensive as its object. From the distinction of support — because of the complete fulfillment of the great accumulations of merit and knowledge over a full great incalculable <s>kalpa</s>. From the distinction of penetration — the selflessness of both persons and <s>dharmas</s> —

body.text: veditavya upadravādiparitrāṇāt / tatra upadravaparitrāṇaṃ nagarapraveśādibhi randhādīnāṃ cakṣurādipratilambhāt / anupāyaparitrāṇaṃ laukika samyagdṛṣṭipratilambhena sarvakudṛṣṭivivecanāt / apāyaparitrāṇaṃ darśanamārgotpādanena durgatisamatikramaṇāt satkāyaparitrāṇamarhattvasākṣātkaraṇena traidhātukavi mokṣāṇāt / yānaparitrāṇaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ hīnayānavicchandanāditi //
body.translated_text: should be understood as protection from dangers and the rest. Among these, protection from danger — through entering a city and the rest, the obtaining of the eye and the rest by the blind and the rest. Protection from wrong means — through the attainment of mundane right view, the discrimination from all wrong views. Protection from miserable destinies — through the production of the path of seeing, the transcending of the miserable destinies —

body.text: vaiśaṃṣikaguṇā āryaśrāvakairbhāvanāmārge vābhinirhriyante 'śaikṣamārge vetyata eṣāṃ pṛṣṭhaniṣṭhābhisamayābhyāṃ saṃgraho veditavyaḥ / te punarmaitryādayo yathāsūtrāntareṣu nirdiṣṭāḥ śrāvakayāne mahāyāne ca tathaiva veditavyāḥ / teṣāṃ cāya samāsena pañcabhirākārairyathāyogaṃ lakṣaṇanirdeśo veditavyaḥ - niśrayata ālaṃbanata ākārataḥ svabhāvataḥ sahāyataśca //
body.translated_text: The distinctive qualities are accomplished by noble <s>śrāvakas</s> either on the path of cultivation or on the path of the adept — therefore their inclusion under the subsequent realization and the final realization should be understood. Those, namely <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) and the rest, should be understood just as they are taught in other <s>sūtras</s>, both in the <s>śrāvakayāna</s> and the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. And of those, in summary, there are five —

body.text: tatra tāvat maitryā dhyānaṃ niśrayaḥ, sattvā ālaṃbanam, sukhena saṃprayujyerannityākāraḥ, samādhiḥ prajñā ca svabhāvaḥ śamathavipaśyanāsaṃgṛhītatvātsarvaguṇānām, cittacaitasikāḥ sahāyā ityevaṃ karuṇādiṣu yathāyogaṃ yojayitavyam / upekṣayā sukhādiṣu sattveṣvanunayādyabhyupekṣaṇamaho vata saṃkleśādvimucyerannityayamākāro veditavyaḥ / sa ca hitāśayavihāra ityucyate //
body.translated_text: Among these, for <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness): <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) is the support; beings are the object; 'may they be endowed with happiness' is the mode; <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) and <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) are the intrinsic nature, because all qualities are included in <s>śamatha</s> and <s>vipaśyanā</s>; mind and mental factors are the companions. Thus for <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion) and the rest, one should apply as appropriate. For <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity), regarding pleasure and the rest —

body.text: aṣṭau vimokṣāḥ / rūpī rūpāṇi paśyatyayaṃ prathamo vimokṣa iti vistaraḥ / tatra kathaṃ rūpītyucyate / svātmanyā rūpyasamāpattisaṃniśrayeṇa rūpasaṃjñāyā abhibhāvanādrūpasaṃjñāsaṃniveśanādvā draṣṭavyāni rūpasaṃjñāsaṃmukhī karaṇādityarthaḥ / kathaṃ rūpāṇi paśyatītyucyate / suvarṇadurvarṇādīni rūpāṇyadhimucyadarśanāt / kathaṃ vimokṣa ityucyate / vimucyate 'nena nirmāṇāvaraṇāditi kṛtvā / adhyātmamarūpasaṃjñārūpyasamāpattisaṃniśrayeṇa draṣṭari svātmani rūpasaṃjñāvibhāvanādarūpasaṃjñāsaṃniveśanādvādraṣṭari nāmasaṃjñāsaṃmukhīkaraṇādityarthaḥ / śeṣaṃ pūrvavat / śubhaṃ vimokṣaṃ kāyena sākṣātkṛtvopasaṃpadya viharata, śubhāśubheṣu rūpeṣvanyonyāpekṣāsaṃjñāmanyonyānugamasaṃjñāṃ ca niśrityā[nyo]nyaikarasasaṃjñālābhāt /
body.translated_text: The eight <s>vimokṣas</s> (liberations). 'Having form, one sees forms' — this is the first liberation, and so forth in detail. Among these, how is one said to 'have form'? Because, relying on the attainment of a formless meditation within oneself, one overcomes the perception of form, or because one establishes the perception of form — the meaning is that one brings the perception of form into presence.

body.text: tathāhi śubhāni rūpāṇyapekṣya tadanyeṣvaśubhānīti bhavatyaśubhāni vāpekṣya śubhānīti nānapekṣyaikajātīyānāmeva darśane śubhāśubhatābuddhyabhāvāt / tathāhi śubheṣvapyaśūbhatānugatāśubheṣvapi śubhatā, śubhasaṃmatasyāpi tvaṅmātrasya keśādiṣaṭtriśadaśucidravyāntarabhāvādityevamanyonyaṃ sarvarūpāṇi miśrayitvā śubhataikarasākārayā saṃjñayā vimucyate / tasyaivaṃ rūpādivimokṣavibhutvalābhinaḥ śubhāśubhanirmāṇāvaraṇaṃ ca prahīyate tatra ca saṃkleśotpattyāvaraṇam / kaḥ punarnirmāṇe saṃkleśaḥ / śubharūpanirmāṇe ābhogaḥ, aśubharūpanirmāṇe prātikūlyamiti / ākāśānantyāyatanādīni catvāryāryaśrāvakasya yānyanāśravānukūlāni śuddhāni tāni vimokṣakākhyāṃ labhante, tadāsvādanavimokṣaṇāt / ye te śāntā vimokṣā atikramya rūpāṇyārūpyāsteṣvasaktiḥ pariśuddhiḥ / tasyā āvaraṇamārūpyāsvādanamiti / saṃjñāvedayitanirodhasya niśrayo naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanam, ālaṃbanākārasahāyā na santi cittacaitasikānāmabhāvāt / svabhāvastasya cittacaitasikānāṃ nirodhaḥ / sa ca mokṣānusadṛśo vihāraḥ, lokottareṇa mārgeṇa parivṛtyāśrayasyāryaśrāvakasya punaścitacaitasikānāmapyapravṛttyavasthāyāḥ paramaśāntatvāt kliṣṭamano 'samudācārācca / ete cāṣṭau vimokṣā vihārā ityucyante, ebhirāryāṇāṃ viharaṇāt / tatrāpi bahulamābhyāṃ vimokṣābhyāṃ viharanti, tṛtīyenāṣṭamena ca pradhānatvāt / ata eva cānayoḥ kāyena sākṣātkṛtyopasaṃpadya viharatīti vacanaṃ nānyeṣu rūpyarūpivimokṣāvaraṇāśeṣaprahāṇādyathākramam / tayoḥ saṃpūrṇāśrayaparivṛttisākṣātkaraṇamupādāyetyaparaḥ paryāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: For with reference to attractive forms, other forms are considered unattractive, and with reference to unattractive forms, others are considered attractive; but without reference to either, in the seeing of things of a single type alone, there is no cognition of attractiveness or unattractiveness. For even in what is attractive there is the presence of unattractiveness, and even in what is unattractive there is attractiveness; even what is conventionally considered attractive — the mere skin, hair, and the thirty-six and so forth —

body.text: aṣṭāvabhibhvāyatanāni tatra adhyātmaṃ rūpasaṃjñī bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyati parīttāni suvarṇadurvarṇāni hīnapraṇī tāni, tāni khalu
body.translated_text: The eight <s>abhibhvāyatanas</s> (bases of mastery). Among these, 'perceiving form internally, one sees forms externally — limited ones, of good and bad color, of inferior quality' — those indeed

body.text: rūpāṇyabhibhūya jānātyabhibhūya paśyati tathā ca saṃjñī bhavati / idaṃ prathamamabhibhvāyatanam / adhyātmaṃ rūpasaṃjñī bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyatyadhimātrāṇi suvarṇadurvarṇāni vistareṇa yāvattayā ca saṃjñī bhavati / idaṃ dvitīyamabhibhvāyatanam / ityete dve abhibhvāyatane rūpī rūpāṇi paśyatītyetasmādvimokṣādabhinirhriyete / adhyātmamarūpasaṃjñī bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyati parīttāni vistareṇa yāvattathāsaṃjñī ca bhavati / idaṃ tṛtīyamabhibhvāyatanam / adhyātmamarūpasaṃjñī bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyatyadhimātrāṇi yathā tathāsaṃjñī ca bhavati / idaṃ caturthamabhibhvāyatanam / ityete dve abhibhvāyatane adhyātmamarūpasaṃjñī bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyatītyeta smādvimokṣādabhinirhriyete / evaṃ kṛtvā dvābhyāṃ vimokṣābhyāṃ catvāryabhibhvāyatanāni veditavyāni / adhyātma[ma]rūpasaṃjñī bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyati nīlāni nīlavarṇāni nīlanidarśanāni nīlanirbhāsāni / tadyathā umakāpuṣpaṃ saṃpannaṃ vā vārāṇasīyakaṃ vastraṃ nīlaṃ nīlavarṇa nīlanidarśanaṃ nīlanirbhāsamevamevādhyātmamarūpasaṃjñī bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyati nīlāni yāvannīlanirbhāsāni tāni khalu rūpāṇyabhibhūya jānātyābhibhūya paśyati tathāsaṃjñī ca bhavati / idaṃ pañcamamabhibhvāyatanam / adhyātmamarūpasaṃjñī bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyati pītāni yāvatpītanirbhāsāni / tadyathā karṇikārapuṣpaṃ saṃpannaṃ vā vārāṇasīyakaṃ vastraṃ pītaṃ pītavarṇamiti vistaraḥ / idaṃ ṣaṣṭhamabhibhvāyatanam / adhyātmamarūpasaṃjñī bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyati lohitāni yāvallohitanirbhāsāni / tadyathā bandhujīvakapuṣpaṃ saṃpannaṃ vā vārāṇasīyaṃ vastraṃ lohitaṃ lohita[varṇa]miti vistaraḥ / idaṃ saptamamabhibhvāyatanam / adhyātmamarūpasaṃjñī bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyatyavadātānyavadātavarṇānyavadātanidarśanānyavadātanirbhāsāni / tadyathā uṣasi tārakāyā varṇaṃ saṃpannaṃ vā vārāṇasīyakaṃ vastramavadātamavadātavarṇamavadātanidarśanamavadātanirbhāsamevamevādhyātmamarūpasaṃjñī bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyatya vadātānyavadātavarṇānyavadātanidarśanānyavadātanirbhāsāni tāni khalu rūpāṇyabhibhūya jānātyabhibhūya paśyati tathāsaṃjñī ca bhavati / idamaṣṭamamabhibhvāyatanam / etāni catvāri śubhaṃ vimokṣaṃ kāyena sākṣātkṛtvopasaṃpadya viharatītyetasmādvimokṣādabhinirhriyate //
body.translated_text: having mastered forms, one knows and sees—and one has that perception. This is the first sphere of mastery (<s>abhibhvāyatana</s>). Perceiving form internally, one sees external forms that are superior, of good or bad color, in detail—and one has that perception. This is the second sphere of mastery. These two spheres of mastery are derived from the liberation 'one who has form sees forms.' Not perceiving form internally, one sees external forms that are limited, in detail—and one has that perception. This is the third sphere of mastery. Not perceiving form internally, one sees external forms that are superior, as described—and one has that perception. This is the fourth sphere of mastery. These two spheres of mastery are derived from the liberation 'not perceiving form internally, one sees forms externally.' Thus, from the two liberations, four spheres of mastery should be understood. Not perceiving form internally, one sees external forms that are blue, blue in color, blue in appearance, blue in radiance—just as the <s>umā</s> flower, or a fine Vārāṇasī cloth that is blue, blue in color, blue in appearance, blue in radiance. Likewise, not perceiving form internally, one sees external forms that are blue, up to blue in radiance; having mastered those forms, one knows and sees, and one has that perception. This is the fifth sphere of mastery. Not perceiving form internally, one sees external forms that are yellow, up to yellow in radiance—just as the <s>karṇikāra</s> flower, or a fine Vārāṇasī cloth that is yellow, in detail. This is the sixth sphere of mastery. Not perceiving form internally, one sees external forms that are red, up to red in radiance—just as the <s>bandhujīvaka</s> flower, or a fine Vārāṇasī cloth that is red, in detail. This is the seventh sphere of mastery. Not perceiving form internally, one sees external forms that are white, white in color, white in appearance, white in radiance—just as the color of the morning star, or a fine Vārāṇasī cloth that is white, white in color, white in appearance, white in radiance. Likewise, not perceiving form internally, one sees external forms that are white, in detail; having mastered those forms, one knows and sees, and one has that perception. This is the eighth sphere of mastery. These four are derived from the liberation 'having directly realized the beautiful (<s>śubha</s>), one attains and dwells in it with the body.'

body.text: tatra vimokṣairālaṃbanamadhimucyate parīttādikam, abhibhvāyatanaistvabhibhavati, tadantardhānādyatheṣṭaṃ vā karaṇādvaśavartamānatāmupādāya / tatra parīttāni rūpāṇi sattvasaṃkhyātānyalpapramāṇatvāt / adhimātrāṇyasattvasaṃkhyātāni gṛhavimānaparvatādīni
body.translated_text: Among these, through the liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>), one gains conviction regarding the object—limited and so forth; but through the spheres of mastery (<s>abhibhvāyatana</s>), one masters [it]—through the ability to make it disappear or to do with it as one wishes, attaining control. Among these, 'limited forms' are those counted as beings, because of their small measure. 'Superior [forms]' are those not counted as beings—houses, mansions, mountains, etc.—

body.text: mahāpramāṇatvāt / suvarṇadurvarṇāni śubhāśubhavarṇasaṃgṛhītāni / hīnapraṇītāni mānuṣyakadivyāni yathākramam / tāni khalu rūpāṇyabhibhūyeti vaśe vartayitvā / jānātīti śamathamārgeṇa / paśyatīti vipaśyanāmārgeṇa / tathāsaṃjñī ca bhavatītyabhibhūte nābhibhūte vā tannirabhimānasaṃjñitāmupādāya / nīlānītyuddeśapadam / nīlavarṇāni sahajāṃ nīlatāmupādāya / nīlanidarśanāni saṃyoganīlatāmupādāya / nīlanirbhāsāni tadubhayoḥ prabhānirmokṣabhāsvaratāmupādāya / yathā nīlānyevaṃ pītalohitāvadātāni vistareṇa veditavyāni / dṛṣṭāntadvayaṃ caikaikasmin sahajasāṃyogikavarṇodbhāvanatāmupādāya / aparaḥ paryāyastadyathā nīlamiti puṣpavastrayoḥ samānamuddeśapadam / nīlavarṇamiti puṣpamevādhikṛtya, tasya sāṃyogikanīlatvasaṃbhavāt / nīlanirbhāsamityucyate puṣpavastre adhikṛtya, dvayorapi bhāsvaratvasaṃbhavāt / ityevaṃ kṛtvā dṛṣṭānte 'pi tadyathomakāpuṣpaṃ saṃpannaṃ vā vārāṇasīyakaṃ vastraṃ nīlaṃ nīlavarṇamityevamādinirdeśa upapanno bhavati / evaṃ pītādikaṃ yojayitavyam / śiṣṭaṃ yathādhimokṣeṣu / kiṃ śiṣṭam / adhyātmaṃ rūpasaṃjñī bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyatītyevamādi / tatpunaryathā rūpī rūpāṇi paśyatītyevamādi nirdeśānusāreṇa draṣṭavyam //
