body.translated_text: because of their great measure. 'Of good and bad color' means included in beautiful and ugly colors. 'Inferior and excellent' means human and divine, respectively. 'Having mastered those forms' means having brought them under control. 'Knows' means through the path of calm-abiding (<s>śamatha</s>). 'Sees' means through the path of insight (<s>vipaśyanā</s>). 'And one has that perception' means having the perception of being without conceit toward what is mastered or unmastered. 'Blue' is the heading word. 'Blue in color' means with respect to natural blueness. 'Blue in appearance' means with respect to adventitious blueness [through contact]. 'Blue in radiance' means with respect to the luminous brilliance of both. As with blue, so yellow, red, and white should be understood in detail. The pair of examples in each case is for the purpose of showing the natural and adventitious colors. Another interpretation: 'blue' is the common heading for the flower and the cloth. 'Blue in color' refers to the flower specifically, because adventitious blueness is possible for it. 'Blue in radiance' refers to both the flower and the cloth, because luminous brilliance is possible for both. Thus, in the example also, the teaching 'just as the <s>umā</s> flower, or a fine Vārāṇasī cloth that is blue, blue in color' and so forth is proper. Likewise, the yellow and the rest should be applied. The remainder is as in the [section on] convictions (<s>adhimokṣa</s>). What remainder? 'Perceiving form internally, one sees forms externally' and so forth. That again should be seen following the teaching 'one who has form sees forms' and so forth.

body.text: evamabhibhvāyatanairālaṃbanaṃ vaśe vartayitvā kṛtsnāyatanaiḥ kṛtsnaṃ spharati samantānantā paryantaṃ vistārayatītyarthaḥ / tāni punaḥ kṛtsnāyatanāni daśa bhavanti / tadyathā pṛthivīkṛtsnamapkṛtsnaṃ tejaḥkṛtsnaṃ vāyukṛtsnaṃ pītakṛtsnaṃ lohitakṛtsnamavadātakṛtsnamākāśānantyāyatanakṛtsnaṃ vijñānānantyāyatanakṛtsnaṃ ca / kṛtsnāyataneṣu pṛthivyādīni yadi na vyavasthāpyeran tenāśrayamahābhūtairvinā tadupādāyarūpaṃ nīlādiakaṃ spharituṃ na śakyeta / tasyāśrayasya rūpasya spharaṇasamṛddhimupādāyaiṣāṃ kṛtsneṣu vyavasthānaṃ veditavyam / śeṣaṃ yathāsaṃbhavaṃ vimokṣavadākāśānantyāyatanakṛtsnādi //
body.translated_text: Thus, having brought the object under control through the spheres of mastery, through the totality-spheres (<s>kṛtsnāyatana</s>) one pervades the totality—meaning one extends [the perception] without limit in all directions. Those totality-spheres are ten: the earth-totality (<s>pṛthivīkṛtsna</s>), the water-totality (<s>apkṛtsna</s>), the fire-totality (<s>tejaskṛtsna</s>), the wind-totality (<s>vāyukṛtsna</s>), the blue-totality (<s>pītakṛtsna</s>), the yellow-totality, the red-totality (<s>lohitakṛtsna</s>), the white-totality (<s>avadātakṛtsna</s>), the totality of the base of infinite space (<s>ākāśānantyāyatanakṛtsna</s>), and the totality of the base of infinite consciousness (<s>vijñānānantyāyatanakṛtsna</s>). If earth and the other [great elements] were not established in the totality-spheres, then without the supporting great elements, their derived form of blue etc. could not be pervaded. The establishment of these in the totalities should be understood through the abundance of pervading the supporting form. The remainder, such as the totality of the base of infinite space and so forth, [should be understood] as possible, like the liberations.

body.text: tatra vimokṣairārambhaḥ, abhibhvāyataneḥ prayogaḥ, kṛtsnāyatanaiḥ pariniṣpattirvimokṣāṇāṃ veditavyāḥ //
body.translated_text: Among these, through the liberations there is the commencement; through the spheres of mastery, the application; through the totality-spheres, the consummation of the liberations should be understood.

body.text: araṇā vihārī yeṣāṃ sattvānāmābhāsaṃ gantukāmo bhavati teṣāmātmani
body.translated_text: The dweller in non-conflict (<s>araṇāvihārin</s>): one who wishes to approach the presence of certain beings,

body.text: kleśasamudācāramadhikṛtyānāgatavṛttāntaṃ vihāragata eva praṇidhijñāna balenāvalokya tathā tatsamīpamupasaṃkrāmati na vā yathā te tatrānunayapratidherṣyāmātsaryādikaṃ kleśopakleśasaraṇaṃ notpādayanti / ata idamucyate 'raṇā dhyānaṃ niśritya kleśotpattyanurakṣāvihārasamṛddhāviti vistaraḥ /
body.translated_text: examines by the power of aspiration-knowledge (<s>praṇidhijñāna</s>), while remaining in one's dwelling, the future course of events regarding the arising of defilements in those [beings] with respect to oneself, and accordingly approaches or does not approach their presence, such that they do not produce the strife of defilements and secondary defilements such as attraction, aversion, jealousy, and so forth. Therefore it is said: 'the non-conflict [dwelling], relying on <s>dhyāna</s>, [is] the accomplishment of dwelling in safeguarding against the arising of defilements' and so forth in detail.

body.text: praṇidhijñānaṃ tallābhī yadyadeva traiyadhvikādikajñeyavṛttāntaṃ jñātukāmobhavati, tatra tatra mānasaṃ praṇidhāyedaṃ jānīyāmiti dhyānaṃ samāpadyate, tato vyutthitasya tatpraṇidhānaṃ samṛdhyati, tajjñeyaṃ jānātītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Aspiration-knowledge (<s>praṇidhijñāna</s>): one who has attained it, wishing to know whatever matter of the knowable pertaining to the three times and so forth, directing the mind there and there [thinking] 'I shall know this,' enters <s>dhyāna</s>; then, upon emerging, that aspiration succeeds—meaning one knows the knowable.

body.text: dharmapratisaṃvit paryāyeṣu, tadyathāvidyādīnārabhyājñānamadarśanamanabhisamaya ityevamādiṣvavyāghātasamṛddhau yaḥ samādhiriti vistaraḥ / arthapratisaṃvitsvasāmānyalakṣaṇe dharmāṇām, arthāntarādyabhiprāye cāvyāghātasamṛddhāviti vistaraḥ / niruktipratisaṃvijjanapadabhāṣāyāmiti prativiṣayaṃ yathāsvamanyonyasaṃjñāntarānuvyavahāre, dharmanirvacane ceti tadyathā lujyate pralujyate tasmāllokaḥ, rūpyate tasmādrūpa ityevamādike / pratibhānapratisaṃviddharmaprabhedeṣviti dravyasantaḥ prajñaptisantaḥ saṃvṛtisantaḥ paramārthasanta ityevamādiṣu //
body.translated_text: The analytical knowledge of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmapratisaṃvid</s>) [pertains to] synonyms—such as regarding ignorance and the rest: 'unknowing,' 'not-seeing,' 'non-realization' and so forth—the <s>samādhi</s> and so forth that accomplish the unimpeded success [in understanding these]. The analytical knowledge of meaning (<s>arthapratisaṃvid</s>) [pertains to] the particular and general characteristics of <s>dharmas</s>, and the unimpeded success in [understanding] the intention of different meanings and so forth, in detail. The analytical knowledge of etymology (<s>niruktipratisaṃvid</s>) [pertains to] regional languages—the communication through different mutual designations for each respective object, and the etymological derivation of <s>dharma</s> [terms], such as '<s>loka</s> (world) because it perishes (<s>lujyate</s>),' '<s>rūpa</s> (form) because it is formed (<s>rūpyate</s>),' and so forth. The analytical knowledge of eloquence (<s>pratibhānapratisaṃvid</s>) [pertains to] the classifications of <s>dharmas</s>—such as 'existing as substance,' 'existing as designation,' 'existing conventionally,' 'existing ultimately,' and so forth.

body.text: ṛddhayabhijñā vicitraddhivikuvitasamṛddhāviti tadyathā eko bhūtvā bahudhā bhavatītyevamādau / vicitrāṇāṃ śabdānāmanuśravasamṛddhāviti divyamānuṣyakādīnām / parasattveṣu cittacaritapraveśasamṛddhāviti sarāgādicittapracārayathābhūtajñānasamṛddhāvityarthaḥ / pūrvāntacaryāyā anusmaraṇasamṛddhāvityatītaṃ janmaparaṃparāmārabhya nāmajātigotrādiprakāravṛttāyā ityarthaḥ / cyutyutpādābhijñā divyena cakṣuṣā sattvānāṃ cyavamānānāmupapadyamānānāṃ suvarṇānāṃ durvarṇānāṃ sugatimapi gacchatāṃ durgatimapyaparāntamārabhya cyutyupapādasaṃdarśanasamṛddhau samādhyādayaḥ / āsravakṣayajñāna samṛddhāviti yenopāyenāsravāḥ parikṣoyante, yaścaiṣāṃ parikṣayastajjñānaniṣpattinimittamityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: The superknowledge of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhyabhijñā</s>): the accomplishment of manifold supernatural power and transformation—such as 'having been one, one becomes many' and so forth. The accomplishment of hearing diverse sounds—divine, human, and so forth. The accomplishment of penetrating the mental conduct of other beings—meaning the accomplishment of knowledge of things as they truly are regarding the workings of minds with desire and so forth. The accomplishment of recollecting the conduct of former lives—meaning the course of events, beginning from the succession of past births, regarding name, caste, clan, and so forth. The superknowledge of divine sight (<s>cyutyutpādābhijñā</s>): with the divine eye, seeing beings dying and being reborn, of good and bad color, going to happy or unfortunate destinies—the accomplishment of displaying death-and-rebirth regarding the future; the <s>samādhi</s> and so forth [serve this]. The accomplishment of the knowledge of the destruction of outflows (<s>āsravakṣayajñāna</s>): the means by which outflows are exhausted, and the complete destruction of those—meaning the accomplishment of that knowledge.

body.text: lakṣaṇānuvyañjanāni yatsamādhiprajñādhipatyena buddhā bhagavanto dvātriṃśatā lakṣaṇairaśītyānuvyañjanaiḥ vibhrājamānaṃ rūpakāyaṃ saṃdarśayanti vineyānām /
body.translated_text: The marks and minor marks (<s>lakṣaṇānuvyañjana</s>): that <s>samādhi</s> and wisdom through whose mastery the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> display to those to be trained the form-body (<s>rūpakāya</s>) resplendent with thirty-two marks and eighty minor marks.

body.text: tatsvabhāvāni tāni teṣāṃ veditavyāni, dharmakāyaprabhāvitatvādbuddhānāṃ bhagavatāmiti / bodhisattvānāṃ tu tathāsaṃdarśanasamarthānāṃ samādhiprajñāsvabhāvāni / tadanyeṣāṃ parṣanmaṇḍaleṣūpapannānāṃ tatsamutthitavipākasvabhāvāni veditavyāni //
body.translated_text: Those [marks and minor marks] should be understood as having the nature of those [<s>samādhi</s> and wisdom] for the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s>, because they are brought about by the <s>dharmakāya</s>. But for <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who are capable of such display, they have the nature of <s>samādhi</s> and wisdom. For others who are born into their retinue assemblies, they should be understood as having the nature of maturation-results arising from those [merits].

body.text: catasraḥ sarvakārāḥ pariśuddhayo buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ mahābhijñāprāptānāṃ ca bodhisattvānām / tatra yathākāmamāśrayasyopādānasthānaparityāgānāṃ samṛddhāviti yatrecchati tatropapattigrahaṇataḥ, tasyāṃ copapattāvāyuḥsaṃskārānadhiṣṭhāya yāvadicchamavasthānataḥ, yadecchati tadāyuḥsaṃskārotsarjanataśca yathākramam / yathākāmamālaṃbanamadhikṛtya nirmāṇapariṇāmanajñānānāṃ samṛddhāvityapūrvarūpādinirmāṇataḥ, pūrvotpannānāṃ rūpādīnāṃ suvarṇāditvena pariṇāmataḥ, sarvaprakārāvagamanataśca yathākramam / yathākāmaṃ samādhimukhavaśavartisamṛddhāviti pratikṣaṇaṃ yatheṣṭamaparimitasamādhyantarasamāpattaye / yathākāmaṃ dhāraṇīmukhasaṃdhāraṇasamṛddhāviti dvācatvāriṃśato 'kṣarāṇāmanyatamākṣaramanasikāre tadādisarvadharmaparyāyābhilapanasāmarthyapratilambhāyetyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: The four complete purifications (<s>sarvākārapariśuddhi</s>) belong to the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> and to <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have attained the great superknowledges. Among these: the accomplishment of relinquishing the basis of clinging at will—meaning grasping rebirth wherever one wishes, and having taken rebirth, sustaining the life-forces for as long as one wishes, and releasing the life-forces whenever one wishes, respectively. The accomplishment of knowledge of creation, transformation, and [direct] cognition with respect to objects at will—meaning the creation of previously non-existent forms etc., the transformation of already-arisen forms etc. into gold etc., and the comprehension of all varieties, respectively. The accomplishment of controlling the doorways of <s>samādhi</s> at will—meaning entering into unlimited different <s>samādhis</s> as desired at every moment. The accomplishment of retaining the doorways of <s>dhāraṇī</s> at will—meaning through the mental engagement with any one of the forty-two syllables, attaining the capacity to articulate all the <s>dharma</s>-discourses beginning with that [syllable].

body.text: daśa balāni - sthānāsthānajñānabalaṃ karmasvakajñānabalaṃ dhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattijñānabalamindriyaparāparajñānabalaṃ nānādhimuktijñānabalaṃ nānādhātujñānabalaṃ sarvatragāminīpratipajjñānabalaṃ pūrvanivāsānusmṛtijñānabalaṃ cyutyupapādajñānabalamāsravakṣayajñānabalaṃ ca / tatra sthānāsthānajñānabalaṃ dhyānaṃ niśritya sarvaprakārahetvahetujñānāsaṃgāpratihatasaṃmukhībhāve samādhyādayaḥ / evaṃ karmasvakajñānabalādiṣu sarvākārakarmasvakatājñānāsaṃgāpratihatasaṃmukhībhāva iti yojayitavyam //
body.translated_text: The ten powers (<s>daśabala</s>): the power of knowing what is possible and impossible (<s>sthānāsthānajñānabala</s>), the power of knowing the results of one's own karma (<s>karmasvakajñānabala</s>), the power of knowing <s>dhyāna</s>, liberations, <s>samādhi</s>, and attainments, the power of knowing the higher and lower faculties, the power of knowing the diverse aspirations, the power of knowing the diverse elements, the power of knowing the paths leading everywhere, the power of recollecting former lives, the power of knowing death-and-rebirth, and the power of knowing the destruction of outflows. Among these, the power of knowing what is possible and impossible: relying on <s>dhyāna</s>, the <s>samādhi</s> and so forth for the unobstructed and unimpeded coming into presence of the knowledge of all varieties of cause and non-cause. Likewise, in the power of knowing the results of karma and so forth, [one should construe:] 'the unobstructed and unimpeded coming into presence of the knowledge of all aspects of one's own karma-results' and so forth.

body.text: catvāri vaiśāradyāni - samyaksaṃbuddhasya vata me sata ime te dharmā anabhisaṃbuddhā ityatra māṃ kaścicchramaṇo vā devo vā māro vā brahmā vā sahadharmeṇa codayedvā smārayedvā nimittamapi na samanupaśyāmyetacca nimitta[ma]samanupaśyan kṣemaprāptaśca vaiśāradyaprāptaścodāramārṣabhaṃ sthānaṃ prajānāmi, brahmacaryaṃ pravartayāmi, pariṣadi samyak siṃhanādaṃ nadāmi / kṣīṇāsravasya vata me sata ime āsravā aparikṣīṇā iti / ye vā punarme śrāvakā[ṇā]mantarāyikā dharmā ākhyātāḥ tān pratiṣevamānasya nālamantarāyāteti
body.translated_text: The four fearlessnesses (<s>catvāri vaiśāradyāni</s>): 'Being one who is perfectly and fully awakened (<s>samyaksaṃbuddha</s>), that there are any <s>dharmas</s> not fully awakened to by me—in this regard, no ascetic, <s>deva</s>, <s>Māra</s>, or <s>Brahmā</s> could rightly challenge or remind me. Not seeing even a sign [of such a challenge], and having attained security and fearlessness, I know the supreme, bull-like station; I set the holy life in motion; I rightly roar the lion's roar in the assembly.' 'Being one whose outflows are destroyed, that there are any outflows not destroyed by me...' 'That the obstructing <s>dharmas</s> that I have declared for my disciples—that one who practices them would not [actually encounter] an obstruction...'

body.text: yo vā punarme śrāvakāṇāṃ niryāṇāya mārga ākhyāta āryonairyāṇiko nairvedhikaḥ sa vata na samyaṅniryāti tatkarasya samyagduḥ[kha]kṣayāya duḥkhasyāntakriyāyai ityatra māṃ kaścit śramaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā yāvatsiṃhanādaṃ nadāmīti vistareṇaikaikasmin vaktavyam / tānyetāni vaiśāradyāni svārthaṃ parārthaṃ cārabhya veditavyāni / tatra dvividhaḥ svārthaḥ - jñānaviśeṣaḥ prahāṇaviśeṣaśca / dvividhaḥ parārthaḥ - vipakṣadharmavivarjanaṃ pratipakṣadharmaniṣevaṇaṃ ca / tatrābhisaṃbodhivaiśāradyaṃ jñānātmakaṃ svārthamevārabhya sarvākāraṃ mayā saprabhedaparyantaṃ jñeyamabhisaṃbuddhamityetasyāḥ pratijñāyāḥ samyaṅniranuyojyatvena sarvasmin loke pratiṣṭhāpanasamṛddhau yaḥ samādhiriti pūrvavat / evaṃ śeṣāṇyapi vaiśāradyāni yojayitavyāni / sarvākārāḥ punarāsravāḥ savāsanāḥ kleśā draṣṭavyāḥ / sarvākārā antarāyikā dharmāḥ sarve sāṃkleśikāḥ vipakṣadharmā draṣṭavyāḥ / sarvākāro nairyāṇiko mārgaḥ prayogamārgamārabhya yāvanniṣṭhāmārgo draṣṭavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Or whatever path I have declared for the liberation of <s>śrāvakas</s>, the noble path of liberation and penetration — one who practices it truly attains liberation, for the proper exhaustion and ending of suffering.' Regarding this, 'no <s>śramaṇa</s> or <s>brāhmaṇa</s>,' and so forth up to 'I roar the lion's roar' — this should be explained in detail for each one. These <s>vaiśāradyas</s> (fearlessnesses) should be understood with reference to both one's own welfare and the welfare of others. Among these, the twofold welfare of self consists of: the distinction of knowledge and the distinction of abandonment. The twofold welfare of others consists of: the avoidance of opposing <s>dharmas</s> and the practice of antidote <s>dharmas</s>. Among these, the fearlessness regarding perfect awakening pertains to one's own welfare in the nature of knowledge — 'all that is to be known has been perfectly realized by me in all its aspects, including its divisions and limits' — the <s>samādhi</s> that achieves the successful establishment of this declaration as irrefutable in the entire world, as before. Thus the remaining fearlessnesses should also be applied. All the outflows with their imprints should be seen as defilements in all aspects. All obstructive <s>dharmas</s> in all aspects should be seen as all the opposing <s>dharmas</s> pertaining to defilement. The path of liberation in all aspects should be seen from the preparatory path up to the path of completion.

body.text: trīṇyāveṇikāni smṛtyupasthānāni / iha śāstā śrāvakāṇāṃ dharmaṃ deśayatyanukampakaḥ kāruṇiko 'rthakāmo hitaiṣī karuṇāyamānaḥ - idaṃ vo bhikṣavo hitāya idaṃ sukhāya idaṃ hitasukhāyeti / tasya te śrāvakāḥ śuśrūṣante śrotramavadadhatyājñācittamupasthāpayanti pratipadyante dharmasyānudharmam / tatra tathāgatasya na nāndī bhavati na saumanasyaṃ na cetasa utplāvitatvamupekṣakastatra tathāgato viharati smṛtaḥ saṃprajānan / idaṃ prathamāveṇikaṃ smṛtyupasthānam / yadāryaḥ sevate yadāryaḥ sevamāno 'rhati gaṇamanuśāsitum / punaraparaṃ śāstā śrāvakāṇāṃ dharmaṃ deśayati yāvadidaṃ hitasukhāya / tasya te śrāvakā na śuśrūṣante yāvanna pratipadyante dharmasyānudharmam / tatra tathāgatasya nāghāto bhavati nākṣāntirnāpratyayo na cetaso 'nabhirāddhirupekṣakastatreti vistaraḥ / idaṃ dvitīyam / tṛtīye 'yaṃ viśeṣaḥ - asyaike śrāvakāḥ śuśrūṣante yāvatpratipadyante dharmasyānudharmameke na śuśrūṣante yāvanna pratipadyante dharmasyānudharmam / tatra tathāgatasya na nāndo bhavati yāvaccetaso nābhirāddhiriti / etā[ni] trīṇi smṛtyupasthānāni
body.translated_text: The three unique <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness). Here the Teacher teaches the <s>dharma</s> to the <s>śrāvakas</s>, being compassionate, sympathetic, desiring their welfare, wishing their benefit, showing mercy: 'This, <s>bhikṣus</s>, is for your welfare; this is for your happiness; this is for your welfare and happiness.' Those <s>śrāvakas</s> of his listen attentively, lend their ears, bring forth the mind of understanding —

body.text: śāsturgaṇaparikarṣaṇe yathākramaṃ sarvākārānunayapratighatadubhayasaṃkleśavāsanāyā asamudācārasamṛddhau samādhyādayaḥ //
body.translated_text: In the Teacher's guiding of the assembly, respectively, the <s>samādhis</s> and the rest are for the successful non-arising of the imprints of defilement through attachment, aversion, and both, in all their aspects.

body.text: trīṇyarakṣāṇi / pariśuddhakāyasamudācārastathāgataḥ / nāsti tathāgatasyāpariśuddhakāyasamudācāratā yāṃ tathāgataḥ praticchādayitavyāṃ manyeta kaccinme pare vi[jā]nīyuriti / evaṃ vāṅmanaḥsamudācārate veditavye / ebhirnirvaktavyatayā nirāśaṅkatvātsvayaṃ śāstuvineyajanaparikarṣaṇamārabhya yatheṣṭaṃ nigṛhya prasajyāvavādānuśāsanīprayogaḥ samṛddhayatīti veditavyam //
body.translated_text: The three <s>ārakṣāṇi</s> (protections). The <s>Tathāgata</s> has purified bodily conduct. There is no impure bodily conduct of the <s>Tathāgata</s> that the <s>Tathāgata</s> would think should be concealed, thinking 'lest others come to know this of me.' Likewise, verbal and mental conduct should be understood. Because of having nothing to be reproached for in these, there is fearlessness; and of their own accord —

body.text: asaṃmoṣadharmatā sarvavineyakāryamārabhya yathāvatkṛtasya bhāṣitasya cābhilapanasamṛddhau samādhyādayaḥ //
body.translated_text: The nature of non-forgetfulness — with reference to all that needs to be done for those to be trained, the <s>samādhis</s> and the rest are for the successful recollection of what has been appropriately done and spoken.

body.text: vāsanāsamudghātaḥ sarvajñasya sataḥ kleśajñeyāvaraṇaśeṣasūcakānāṃ kāyavākceṣṭitānāmasamudācārasamṛddhau samādhyādayaḥ //
body.translated_text: The destruction of <s>vāsanā</s> (imprints) — for the omniscient one, the <s>samādhis</s> and the rest are for the successful non-arising of the bodily and verbal behaviors that indicate the residue of the obscurations of defilements and the knowable.

body.text: mahākaruṇā traidhātukāvacareṣu sarvasattveṣu nirantarasarvaprakāraduḥkhālaṃbana karuṇāvihārasamṛddhau samādhyādayaḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Mahākaruṇā</s> (great compassion) — the <s>samādhis</s> and the rest are for the successful abiding in the compassionate dwelling that takes as its object the suffering of all beings in all three realms, continuously and in all its aspects.

body.text: aṣṭādaśāveṇikā buddhadharmāstadyathā nāsti tathāgatasya skhalitam, nāsti ravitam, nāsti muṣitā smṛtiḥ, nāstyasamāhitaṃ cittam, nāsti nānātvasaṃjñā, nāstya pratisaṃkhyāyopekṣā, nāsti chandaparihāṇiḥ, nāsti vīryaparihāṇiḥ, nāsti smṛtiparihāṇiḥ, nāsti samādhiparihāṇiḥ, nāsti prajñārihāṇiḥ, nāsti vimuktiparihāṇiḥ, sarvaṃ tathāgatasya kāyakarma jñānapūrvagamaṃ jñānānuparivarti, sarvaṃ vākkarma jñānapūrvagamaṃ jñānānuparivarti, sarvaṃ manaskarma jñānapūrvagamaṃ jñānānuparivarti, atīte 'dhvanyasaṅgamapratihataṃ jñānam, anāgate 'dhvanyasaṅgamapratihataṃ jñānam, pratyutpanne 'dhvanyasaṅgamapratihataṃ jñānamiti //
body.translated_text: The eighteen unique <s>buddhadharmas</s> (qualities of a <s>Buddha</s>): the <s>Tathāgata</s> has no stumbling; no incoherent speech; no lapse of mindfulness; no unconcentrated mind; no perception of diversity; no equanimity without consideration; no decline of aspiration; no decline of vigor; no decline of mindfulness; no decline of <s>samādhi</s> —

body.text: eṣāṃ punarvyavasthānam, tadyathā arhan bhikṣuḥ kṣīṇāsravaḥ grāmaṃ piṇḍāya carannekadā caṇḍena hastinā sārgha samāgacchati / yathā caṇḍena hastinevaṃ caṇḍanāśvena,
body.translated_text: The establishment of these is as follows. An <s>Arhat</s> <s>bhikṣu</s> whose outflows are destroyed, going to a village for alms, at one time encounters a fierce elephant. Just as with a fierce elephant, so with a fierce horse,

body.text: caṇḍayā gavā, caṇḍena kukkureṇa / gahanaṃ vā kaṇṭakabāṭaṃ vā mṛdnāti / alagardaṃ vā padābhyāṃ samākrāmati / tadrūpaṃ vāgāraṃ praviśati yatrainaṃ mātṛgrāmo 'yogavihitenopanimantrayati / araṇye vā punamārgaṃ hitvā kumārgeṇa gacchati / corairvā taskarairvā sārdhaṃ samāgacchati siṃhairvyāghrairvāparavṛkairvā ityevaṃbhāgīyaṃ skhalitamarhatastathāgatasya sarveṇa sarva nāsti / punarayamarhannekadāraṇye pravaṇe 'nvāhiṇḍanmārgādapanaśya śūnyāgāraṃ praviśya śabdamudīrayati, ghoṣamanuśrāvayati, mahārutaṃ ravati / vāsanādoṣaṃ vāgamya kliṣṭaṃ mahāhāsaṃ hasati, dantavidarśakaṃ saṃcagdhitamupadarśayati / ityevaṃbhāgīyamarhato ravitaṃ tathāgatasya sarveṇa sarvaṃ nāsti / nāsti tathāgatasya muṣitā smṛtirakliṣṭacirakṛtacirabhāṣitānusmaraṇatāmuṣādāya / punaraparamarhan samāpannaḥ samāhito bhavati vyutthito 'samāhitaḥ / tathāgatasya tu sarvāvasthaṃ nāstyasamāhitaṃ cittam / punaraparamarhannekāntenopadhā ca pratikramaṇasaṃjñī bhavati nirupadhike ca nirvāṇe śāntasaṃjñī / tathāgatasya upadhau nirvāṇe ca nānātvasaṃjñā nāsti, paramopekṣāvihāritāmupādāya / punaraparamarhannapratisaṃkhyāya sattvārthakriyāmadhyupekṣate / tathāgatasya tviyamevaṃbhāgīyāpratisaṃkhyāyopekṣā nāsti / punaraparamarhan jñeyāvaraṇaviśuddhimārabhyāprāptaparihāṇyā chandenāpi parihīyate vīrye ṇāpismṛtyā samādhinā prajñayā vimuktyā vimuktijñānadarśanenāpi parihīyate / itīyaṃ saptākārā parihāṇistathāgatasya nāsti / punaraparamarhannekadā kuśale kāyakarmaṇi pravartate, ekadāvyākṛte / yathā kāyakarmaṇyevaṃ vākkarmaṇi manaskarmaṇi ca / tathāgatasya trayāṇāmapi karmaṇāṃ jñānapūrvagamatvājjñānānuparivartitvācca nāstyavyākṛtaṃ karma tatra jñānasamutthāpanatāmupādāya jñānapūrvagamam / jñānasahacaratāmupādāya jñānānuparivarti / punaraparamarhan traiyadhvikaṃ jñeyavastu na cābhogamātrātpratipadyate yenāsya saktaṃ jñānadarśanaṃ bhavati / na ca sarvaṃ pratipadyate yenāsya pratihataṃ jñānadarśanaṃ bhavati / tathāgatastraiyadhvikamābhogamātrāt sarvaṃ vastu pratipadyate / tasmādete aṣṭādaśāveṇikā buddhadharmā ityucyante / tatraiṣāmādyāḥ ṣaṭ asādhāraṇakāyavāṅmanaskarmapariśuddhisamṛddhau samādhyādayaḥ /
body.translated_text: a fierce cow, a fierce dog. Or one treads upon a dense thicket of thorns. Or one steps upon a viper with both feet. Or one enters such a dwelling where a woman invites one to improper conduct. Or in the forest, having left the path, one goes by a wrong route. Or robbers and thieves —

body.text: tatra nāsti skhalitamityayaṃ kāyakarmapariśuddhimārabhya / nāsti ravitamityayaṃ vākkarmaparaśuddhimārabhya / tatra nāsti muṣitasmṛtiḥ nāstyasamānitaṃ cittaṃ nāsti nānātvasaṃjñā nāstyapratisaṃkhyāyopekṣetyetaccatuṣṭayaṃ manaskarmapariśuddhimadhikṛtya veditavyam / nāsti chandaparihāṇiryāvannāsti vimuktijñānadarśanaparihāṇiriti sāśrayāṇāṃ saphalānāṃ tathāgatendriyāṇāmaprāptyaparihāṇisamṛddhau samādhyādayaḥ / tatrāśrayaśchandaḥ / phalaṃ vimuktirvimuktijñānadarśanaṃ ca / indriyāṇi vīryādīni veditavyāni / sarvaṃ kāyakarma vākkarma manaskarma jñānapūrvagamaṃ jñānānuvartītyete trayo 'sādhāraṇakarmacārasamṛddhau samādhyādayaḥ / atīte 'dhvanyasaṅgamapratihataṃ jñānaṃ yāvatpratyutpanne 'dhvanītyete trayo 'sādhāraṇajñānavihārasamṛddhau samādhyādayaḥ //
body.translated_text: Among these, 'there is no stumbling' — this pertains to the purity of bodily karma. 'There is no incoherent speech' — this pertains to the purity of verbal karma. Among these, 'there is no lapse of mindfulness,' 'no unconcentrated mind,' 'no perception of diversity,' 'no equanimity without consideration' — this quartet pertains to the purity of mental karma —

body.text: skandhadhātvāyataneṣu sarvākārajñatāsamṛddhāviti skandhādīnāṃ svabhāvaviśeṣalakṣaṇaprabhedaparyantajñānaniṣpattāvityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'In the accomplishment of omniscient knowledge regarding the <s>skandhas</s>, <s>dhātus</s>, and <s>āyatanas</s>' means the accomplishment of knowledge reaching to the limit of the intrinsic nature, distinctive characteristics, and classifications of the aggregates and the rest.

body.text: teṣāṃ punarabhinirhāro niśrayato 'bhinirhārakapudgalato 'bhinirhāropāyataśca paridīpitaḥ / abhinirhāropāyaḥ punaryathāvyavasthānaṃ manaskārabahulīkāratā yathādeśanaṃ samāhitasya cittasya punaḥpunastatra dhāraṇamityarthaḥ / tadyathāpramāṇānyabhinirhartukāmo maṃtrīsahagatena cittenāvaireṇāsapatnenetyevamādikāṃ deśanāṃ dhyānasaṃniśrayeṇa bhāvayan manasikurvan bahulīkaroti, evamabhijñādīnabhi nirhartukāma eko bhūtvā bahudhā bhavatītyevamādikaṃ vyavasthānaṃ manasikurvan bahulīkarotīti yojayitavyam //
body.translated_text: The accomplishment of these is illuminated through the support, the person who accomplishes, and the means of accomplishment. The means of accomplishment is the repeated mental engagement as established — meaning the repeated settling of the concentrated mind therein as taught. For example, in accomplishing the immeasurables —

body.text: ta ete 'pramāṇādayo guṇā dviprakārāḥ / svakāritrapratyupasthānāśca yairāryo yathāyogaṃ vipakṣaprahāṇādikaṃ karma karoti, vaihārikāśca yaiḥ paramapraśāntanirvikalpajñānasaṃgṛhītairanālaṃbanāpramāṇādibhirdṛṣṭe dharme sukhaṃ viharati //
body.translated_text: These qualities such as the immeasurables and the rest are of two kinds: those that function through their own activity, by which the noble one performs the task of abandoning the opposing factors and the rest as appropriate; and those that are for dwelling, by which one dwells happily in the present life through the immeasurables and the rest that have no object-support, being comprised in the supremely peaceful non-conceptual knowledge.

body.text: tatrāpramāṇaivipakṣaṃ prajahātīti yathākramaṃ vyāpādaṃ vihiṃsāmaratimanunayapratighau ca / etāni ca catvāryapramāṇānyanukampetyucyate, ebhiḥ sattvārthaṃ pratyanuguṇaṃ pravartanāt / atastairviharamāṇaḥ sarvasattveṣvanukampāvihāritayā puṇyasaṃbhāraṃ paripūrayati / ata eva sattvaparipāke ca na parikhidyate, sarvasattvānukampitvena svātmanirapekṣatvāt //
body.translated_text: Among these, the <s>apramāṇas</s> (immeasurables) abandon the opposing factors, namely: ill-will, harmfulness, displeasure, and attachment-and-aversion, respectively. And these four immeasurables are called 'compassionate' because through them one engages in accordance with the welfare of beings. Therefore, one who dwells in them, through dwelling with compassion toward all beings, fulfills the accumulation of merit —

body.text: vimokṣeṣu dvābhyāṃ vimokṣābhyāṃ nirmāṇakarmābhinirharati / tṛtīyena śubhe nirmāṇe na saṃkliśyate / catubhirāryavimokṣaiḥ śānteṣu mokṣeṣu na sajjate / praścimena paramapraśāntenāryavihāreṇa viharati / tathā tathādhimokṣārthaśca vimokṣo veditavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Among the <s>vimokṣas</s> (liberations), through two liberations one accomplishes the activity of magical creation. Through the third, one is not defiled in pleasant magical creation. Through the four noble liberations, one is not attached to peaceful liberations. Through the last one, one dwells in the supremely peaceful noble abiding. Likewise, the liberation should be understood as being for the purpose of such-and-such resolution.

body.text: abhibhvāyatanādīnāṃ karma pūrvavat tannirdeśānusāreṇaiva yojayitavyam //
body.translated_text: The function of the <s>abhibhvāyatanas</s> (bases of mastery) and the rest should be applied as before, following the exposition thereof.

body.text: araṇāyā ādeyavacano bhavati, paracittānurakṣaṇapradhānatayā yathānurūpaṃ vacanāt //
body.translated_text: Through <s>araṇā</s> (non-contentiousness), one's words are to be heeded, because one speaks appropriately with the primary aim of protecting the minds of others.

body.text: praṇidhijñānena bahumataśca bhavati lokasya, sarvaṃ jānātīti gauravitatvāt //
body.translated_text: Through <s>praṇidhijñāna</s> (knowledge from aspiration), one becomes highly regarded by the world, because of being revered through the knowledge that 'he knows everything.'

body.text: pratisaṃvidbhirdeśanayā sattvacittāni saṃtoṣayati, bahuvicitraiḥ prakāraiḥ saṃśayacchedanāt //
body.translated_text: Through the <s>pratisaṃvids</s> (analytical knowledges), one satisfies the minds of beings through teaching, because of resolving doubts through many and diverse methods.

body.text: ṛddhidivyaśrotraparacittajñānapūrvenivāsacyutyupapādāsravakṣayābhijñābhiryathākramaṃ kāyakarmādinā śāsane āvarjayati / divyaśrotrābhijñayā sarvarutaprakārābhyupapattito vākkarmaṇāvarjanaṃ veditavyam //
body.translated_text: Through the <s>abhijñās</s> (higher knowledges) — <s>ṛddhi</s> (miraculous powers), divine hearing, knowledge of others' minds, recollection of former lives, knowledge of death-and-rebirth, and knowledge of the destruction of the outflows — one, respectively, attracts beings to the teaching through bodily karma and the rest. Through the <s>abhijñā</s> of divine hearing, attraction through verbal karma should be understood through comprehension of all types of speech.

body.text: āśrayapariśuddhayā yathākāmamāśrayasyopādānasthānaparityāgānadhikṛtya saṃcintya bhavopapattiparigrahaṇādīni trīṇi veditavyāni / ālaṃbanapariśuddhayā dharmavaśavartī bhavati, cittapariśuddhayā samādhivaśavartī, jñānapariśuddhyā saddharmaṃ dhārayati //
body.translated_text: Through the purity of the basis, with reference to the abandonment of the locus of clinging to the basis at will, the three beginning with the deliberate taking up of rebirth in existence should be understood. Through the purity of objects, one has mastery over <s>dharmas</s>. Through the purity of mind, one has mastery over <s>samādhi</s>. Through the purity of knowledge, one upholds the true <s>dharma</s>.

body.text: baleṣu dvābhyāṃ balābhyāmabhyudayamārga deśayati śeṣairniḥśreyasamārgame tāvacca buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ karaṇīyam / tatra sthānāsthānajñānabalena bhagavannirhetuko 'bhyudayaḥ prakṛtīśvarādihetuko vetyevamahetuviṣamahetuvādaṃ pratikṣipati / karmasvakatājñānabalena svayamakṛtamapi karmāgacchatītyevamakṛtābhyāgamavādaṃ pratikṣipati, yataḥ samyagaviparītaṃ sugatimārga deśayati / dhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattijñānabalena sattvānāṃ cittacaritāni cetaḥ pracarānanupraviśati / indriyaparāparajñānabalena deśanābhājanatāṃ śraddhādīndriyaparipākamanupraviśati / nānādhimuktijñānabalenāśayaṃ hīnapraṇītādhimuktikatāmanupraviśati / nānādhātujñānabalenānuśayasamudghātanaśakyakleśatāmanupraviśati / sarvatragāminīpratipajjñānabalenālaṃbanaṃ śrāvakayānaṃ mahāyānaṃ vā deśanādharmasaṃgṛhītadharmamanupraviśati /
body.translated_text: Among the powers (<s>bala</s>), with two powers [the <s>Buddha</s>] teaches the path of worldly prosperity (<s>abhyudaya</s>); with the rest, the path to the highest good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>). And this is the task of the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s>. Among these, with the power of knowing what is possible and impossible (<s>sthānāsthānajñānabala</s>), the <s>Bhagavān</s> rejects the views of 'worldly prosperity is causeless' and 'it has a wrong cause such as a primordial lord (<s>prakṛtīśvara</s>) etc.' With the power of knowing the results of one's own karma, he rejects the view that 'karma comes about even though not done by oneself'—[the view of] consequence from what was not done. From this, he correctly teaches without distortion the path to happy destiny. With the power of knowing <s>dhyāna</s>, liberations, <s>samādhi</s>, and attainments, he penetrates the mental conduct and mental processes of beings. With the power of knowing the higher and lower faculties, he penetrates [beings'] receptivity to teaching and the maturity of the faculties of faith etc. With the power of knowing the diverse aspirations, he penetrates their dispositions and their convictions in inferior and superior [teachings]. With the power of knowing the diverse elements, he penetrates the defilements that can be uprooted through the removal of latent tendencies. With the power of knowing the paths leading everywhere, he penetrates the object—the <s>dharma</s> included in the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> or <s>Mahāyāna</s> teaching.

body.text: pūrvenivāsānusmṛtijñānabalena saṃbhāraṃ pūrvajanmasamudāyagatamāryamārgahetumanupraviśati // cyutyupapādajñānabalena bhavyatā māyatyāmanupraviśati / āsravakṣayajñānabalena niḥsaraṇaṃ ca sarvasmāttraidhātukādanupraviśati yato yathāvanmokṣamārga deśayati //
body.translated_text: With the power of recollecting former lives, he penetrates the accumulations—the cause of the noble path that has come about through the collection of previous births. With the power of knowing death and rebirth (<s>cyutyupapādajñānabala</s>), he penetrates the potentiality [of beings] in the future. With the power of knowing the destruction of outflows (<s>āsravakṣayajñānabala</s>), he penetrates the escape from the entirety of the three realms; from this he teaches the path of liberation as it truly is.

body.text: balatvaṃ punareṣāmebhiḥ skandhakleśadevaputramaraṇamāranigrahaṇaviśeṣāt / viśeṣaḥ punarjñeyāvaraṇaprahāṇe 'pyanantarāyakṛtatvāt, sthānāsthāne yāvadāsravakṣaya iti sarvatra praśnaṃ pṛṣṭasya praśnavyākaraṇavyāghātācca //
body.translated_text: The 'power-nature' of these is due to their special capacity for suppressing the <s>Māras</s> of the aggregates (<s>skandha</s>), the defilements (<s>kleśa</s>), the son of the gods (<s>devaputra</s>), and death (<s>maraṇa</s>). The special [nature] is further because even in the abandonment of the knowledge-obstruction (<s>jñeyāvaraṇa</s>), [the powers] function without hindrance; and because when questioned with any question whatsoever—regarding what is possible and impossible, up to the destruction of outflows—there is no failure in answering.

body.text: vaiśāradyaiḥ pariṣadi samyagātmanaḥ śāstṛtvamātmaparahitapratipannatvaṃ vyavasthāpayati / codakāṃścābhisaṃbodhau yāvanmārge tīrthyān sahadharmeṇa nigṛhṇāti //
body.translated_text: Through the fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), [the <s>Buddha</s>] establishes in the assembly his own proper status as teacher and as one who has practiced for the benefit of self and others. He also subdues challengers—non-Buddhist teachers who challenge him regarding his awakening and up to his path—through legitimate reasoning (<s>sahadharma</s>).

body.text: smṛtyupasthānairasaṃkliṣṭo gaṇaṃ parikarṣati, śūśrūṣamāṇādiṣvanunayādisaṃkleśābhāvāt //
body.translated_text: Through the foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), he guides the assembly without being defiled—because of the absence of defilements such as attraction etc. toward those who are obedient and so forth.

body.text: arakṣyairnirantaraṃ gaṇamavavadati samanuśāsti, svadoṣāvirbhāvanā śaṃkayānurakṣyābhāvāt //
body.translated_text: Through the [three] things not requiring guarding (<s>arakṣya</s>), he continuously instructs and admonishes the assembly—because of the absence of needing to guard [his conduct], since there is no apprehension of the manifestation of one's own faults.

body.text: asaṃmoṣadharmatayā buddhakṛtyaṃ na hāpayati, upasthite sattvārthakṛtye pramādena kṣaṇamapyalaṃghanāt //
body.translated_text: Through the nature of non-forgetfulness (<s>asaṃmoṣadharmatā</s>), he does not neglect the <s>Buddha</s>'s task—because when the task of benefiting beings presents itself, he does not let even a moment pass through heedlessness.

body.text: vāsanāsamudghātena niḥkleśaḥ kleśapratirūpāṃ ceṣṭāṃ na darśayati yathārhan bhikṣuḥ skhalitādikaṃ darśayati //
body.translated_text: Through the eradication of residual impressions (<s>vāsanāsamudghāta</s>), being free from defilements, he does not display conduct that resembles defilements—such as a worthy monk displaying stumbling and so forth.

body.text: mahākaruṇayā ṣaṭkṛtvā rātriṃdivasena lokaṃ vyavalokayati, ko hīyate kaḥ parihīyata ityevamādibhiḥ prakāraiḥ pratyavekṣaṇāt //
body.translated_text: Through great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), six times each day and night he surveys the world—reviewing through such modes as 'who is declining? who has declined?' and so forth.

body.text: āveṇikānāṃ buddhadharmāṇāṃ karmāsādhāraṇakāyavāṅmanaskarmapariśuddhisamṛddhāvityevamādilakṣaṇanirdeśādhikāreṇayojayitavyam //
body.translated_text: The unique <s>Buddha</s>-qualities (<s>āveṇika buddhadharma</s>) should be applied through the heading of the teaching of the characteristic of 'the accomplishment of the purity of bodily, verbal, and mental action that is unshared' and so forth.

body.text: sarvakārajñatayā sarvasattvānāṃ sarvasaṃśayān chinatti, sarvatrāvyāhatajñānatvāt / dharmanetrīṃ ca dīrghakālamavasthāpayati, tatra tatra vineyasaṃśayacchedanārtha deśitānāṃ dharmaparyāyāṇāṃ saṃgītikārairanukrameṇa saṃjñāpanāt /
body.translated_text: Through omniscience (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>), he cuts all the doubts of all beings—because of having unobstructed knowledge everywhere. And he establishes the eye of the <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmanetrī</s>) for a long time—for the purpose of cutting the doubts of those to be trained in every situation...

body.text: dharmanetrīṃ nisrityāparipakvāḥ sattvāḥ paripacyante paripakvāśca vimucyante //
body.translated_text: Relying on the eye of the <s>Dharma</s>, beings who are unripened become ripened, and those who are ripened become liberated.

body.text: viśiṣṭamārgalābhe hīnamārgavihānistadyathā phalasaṃgṛhītamārgalābhe pratipannakamārgo vihīna ityucyate, punarasaṃmukhīkaraṇāt / sakalaprahāṇaṃ ca sākṣātkaroti phalaprāptikāle tu tadvipakṣajātīyakleśapratipakṣadauṣṭhulyāśeṣaprahāṇādāśrayaparivṛttiviśeṣalābhataḥ samavasargavihānyā vijahātī[tya]tyantāsamudācāraṃ vijahā[tī]tyarthaḥ / no tu bodhisattvastathā vijahāti, sarvasattvaparinirvāṇābhiprāyapūrvakatvāttanmārgasya / ata eva bodhisattvā akṣayakuśalamūlā akṣayaguṇā ityucyante tadyathākṣamiti [sūtre] 'kṣayatānirdiṣṭeti //
body.translated_text: Upon attaining a superior path, the inferior path is abandoned. For example, upon attaining the path included in a fruit, the path of the practitioner [toward that fruit] is said to be 'abandoned,' because it is not brought into presence again. And one directly realizes complete abandonment...

body.text: śāśvato loka aśāśvata ityevamādiṣu praśneṣvavyākṛtavastuvyavasthānamanarthopasaṃhitatvenāyoniśatvāt / teṣāṃ teṣāṃ praśnānāṃ kīdṛśaḥ punaḥ praśno 'rthopasaṃhitaḥ / tadyathā catvāryāryasatyānyārabhya yaḥ praśnaḥ / tathāhi sahetuphalasaṃkleśavyavadānacintāntarbhūta iti //
body.translated_text: Regarding questions such as 'the world is eternal,' 'the world is not eternal,' and so forth—the establishment of unanswered matters (<s>avyākṛtavastu</s>) [is] because they are unwise (<s>ayoniśas</s>), being not conducive to purpose. What kind of question then is conducive to purpose regarding those respective questions?...

body.text: bodhisattvasya nyāmāvakrāntāvapi śrotāpannatvāvyavasthānam, apratiṣṭhitamārgapratilambhāt pratiśrotaḥ pratipattyapariniṣpannatāmupādāya //
body.translated_text: Even though a <s>Bodhisattva</s> has entered the certainty [of the path] (<s>nyāmāvakrānti</s>), the designation 'stream-enterer' (<s>srotāpanna</s>) is not established [for him]—because of having attained the non-abiding path (<s>apratiṣṭhitamārga</s>), and because the practice going against the stream has not been consummated.

body.text: jñeyaṃ ṣaḍvidhaṃ - bhrāntiryāvadabhrāntiniṣyandaśca / tatra bhrāntirgrāhyagrāhakābhiniveśaḥ / bhrāntyāśrayo yasminnāryajñā nagocare saṃskāranimittamātre 'bhūtaparikalpātmake sati bālānāṃ so 'bhiniveśaḥ pravartate / abhrāntyāśrayastathatā, nirvikalpasya jñānasya tadadhiṣṭhānatvāt / bhrāntyabhrāntilokottarajñānānukūlāḥ śrutamayyādayaḥ kuśalā dharmāḥ, jñeyavikalpanānnirvikalpajñānānukūlyācca / abhrāntirnirvikalpajñānam / abhrāntiniṣyanda āryamārgapṛṣṭhalabdhāḥ kuśalā dharmāḥ //
body.translated_text: The knowable (<s>jñeya</s>) is sixfold: error (<s>bhrānti</s>) and so on, up to the outflow of non-error (<s>abhrāntiniṣyanda</s>). Among these, error is the clinging to the apprehended and the apprehender (<s>grāhyagrāhakābhiniveśa</s>). The basis of error: that which, in the domain of noble knowledge, is the mere sign of conditioned phenomena—the unreal...

body.text: upāyakauśalyaṃ punaścaturvidham / sattvaparipākakauśalyaṃ catvāri saṃgrahavastūni, taiḥ saṃgṛhya kuśaleṣu dharmeṣu niyojanāt /
body.translated_text: Skill in means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>) is further fourfold. Skill in maturing beings (<s>sattvaparipākakauśalya</s>) consists of the four means of gathering [a following] (<s>saṃgrahavastu</s>)—because through gathering [beings] by those, one engages them in wholesome <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: buddhadharmaparipūraṇakauśalyaṃ prajñāpāramitā, dānapāramitāṃ yāvat sarvākāravarajñatāṃ paripūrayitukāmena bodhisattvena mahāsattvenāsyāmeva prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣitavyamiti vacanāt / kṣiprābhijñatākauśalyaṃ ṣaṭkṛtvā rātridivasaṃ pāpapratideśanā puṇyānumodanā buddhādhyeṣaṇā kuśalamūlapariṇāmanā ca yathākra[ma]māryamaitreyaparipṛcchāyām / dharmānupacchedakauśalyaṃ cāpratiṣṭhitanirvāṇatayā punaḥpanaranuparatamatyantaṃ ca samantāllokadhātuṣu yathāvineyaṃ buddhabodhisattvacaryāsaṃdarśanāditi //
body.translated_text: Skill in fulfilling <s>Buddha</s>-qualities (<s>buddhadharmaparipūraṇakauśalya</s>) consists of the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>)—because a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> wishing to fulfill the perfection of giving up to the all-knowing knowledge endowed with all aspects [should practice] this very perfection of wisdom...

body.text: abhūtaparikalpo daśavidhaḥ / tatra mūlavikalpa ālayavijñānam, sarvavikalpānāṃ bījabhūtatvāt / nimittavikalpo dehapratiṣṭhābhogapratibhāsā vijñaptayaḥ, grāhyanimittabhūtatvāt / tāḥ punaryathākramaṃ rūpīndriya bhājanalokarūpādiviṣayalakṣaṇā draṣṭavyāḥ / nimittapratibhāsasya vikalpaḥ ṣaḍvijñānakāyāḥ manaśca, yathoktagrāhyanimittākāratvāt / nimittavikāravikalpo yathoktadehādinimittasyānyathātvenotpādaḥ / nimittapratibhāsavikāra vikalpo yathoktasya cakṣarvijñānādinimittapratibhāsasya sukhādyavasthāntareṇotpādaḥ / paropanīto vikalpo deśanāsaṃgṛhītanāmapadavyañjanakāyalakṣaṇaḥ / sa punardvividhaḥ - durākhyātadharmavinayātmakaḥ svākhyādharmavinayātmakaśca / atastadadhipateyamanaskārasaṃgṛhītau yathākramaṃ yoniśovikalpo 'yoniśovikalpaśca veditavyaḥ / abhiniveśavikalpo 'yoniśovikalpādvāṣaṣṭidṛṣṭigatasaṃgṛhīto yo vikalpaḥ / vikṣepavikalpaḥ yoniśo vikalpādabhāvādigrāhalakṣaṇo yo vikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: Unreal conceptualization (<s>abhūtaparikalpa</s>) is tenfold. Among these, the root-conceptualization (<s>mūlavikalpa</s>) is the <s>ālaya-vijñāna</s> (store consciousness)—because it is the seed-ground of all conceptualizations. The sign-conceptualization (<s>nimittavikalpa</s>) consists of the cognitions appearing as body, posture, and exertion—the signs of the apprehended...

body.text: sa punardaśavidhaḥ - abhāvavikalpaḥ yāvadyathārthanāmavikalpaśca / sa eṣa daśavidho vikalpaḥ prajñāpāramitādinirdeśamadhikṛtya veditavyaḥ / yathoktam iha śāriputra bodhisattvo bodhisattva eva san bodhisattvaṃ na samanupaśyati /
body.translated_text: That [conceptualization] is further tenfold: the conceptualization of non-existence (<s>abhāvavikalpa</s>) and so on, up to the conceptualization of names corresponding to reality (<s>yathārthanāmavikalpa</s>). This tenfold conceptualization should be understood with reference to the teaching of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and so forth. As stated: 'Here, <s>Śāriputra</s>...

body.text: bodhisattvanāma na samanupaśyati / prajñāpāramitāṃ na samanupaśyati / bodhiṃ na samanupaśyati / caratīti na samanupaśyati / na caratīti na samanupaśyati / tathāhi nāma svabhāvena śūnyaṃ na śūnyatayā, rūpaṃ svabhāvena śūnyaṃ na śūnyatayā yāvadvijñānaṃ svabhāvena śūnyaṃ na śūnyatayā / tatkasya hetoḥ / yā rūpasya śūnyatā na tadrūpam, nāpyanyatra, rūpācchanyatā, rūpameva śūnyatāḥ, śūnyataiva rūpam, evaṃ yāvadvijñānam / tatkasya hetoḥ / nāmamātramidaṃ yaduta bodhisattvanāmeti bodhisattva iti prajñāpāramiteti bodhiriti rūpamiti yāvadvijñānamiti / svabhāvasya hi notpādo na nirodho na saṃkleśo na vyavadānam / prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caran bodhisattva utpādamapi na samanupaśyati yāvadvayavadānamapi na samanupaśyati / tatkasya hetoḥ / kṛtrimaṃ nāma prati prati te dharmāḥ kalpitā āgantukena nāmnānuvyavahriyante / [yathā yathānuvyavahriyante] tathā tathābhiniviśanti / tāni bodhisattvaḥ sarvanāmāni na samanupaśyati, asamanupaśyannābhiniviśate / tatra abhāvavikalpapratipakṣeṇāha - bodhisattvo bodhisattva eva sannityevamādi, sacchabdasya bhāvārthatvāt / bhāvavikalpapratipakṣeṇāha - bodhisattvaṃ na samanupaśyati yāvadvayavadānamapi na samanupaśyati yāvanna caratīti na samanupaśyati pudgaladharmabhāvapratiṣedhāt / samāropavikalpapratipakṣeṇāha - tathāhi nāma svabhāvena śūnyamiti, abhūtaparikalpasya svabhāvapratiṣedhāt / apavādavikalpapratipakṣeṇāha - na śūnyatayeti, tasminnāmni tena parikalpitena parikalpita svabhāvena virahitatāyāḥ sarvadāstitvāt / ekatvavikalpaprati pakṣaiṇāha - yā rūpasya śūnyatā na tadrūpaṃ yāvadvijñānamiti, bhāvāntaratvāt / rūpādayo hi parikalpitaḥ svabhāvaḥ śūnyatā pariniṣpanna iti / pṛthakatvavikalpapratipakṣeṇāha - nāpyanyatra rūpācchūnyatāyā rūpam, yāvacchanyataiva vijñānamiti, parikalpitasvabhāvasyā lakṣaṇatvāttadvyatirekeṇa tadbhā vāsaṃbhavataḥ / svabhāvavikalpapratipakṣeṇāha - nāmamātramidaṃ yaduta rūpamiti yāvadvijñānamiti, abhilāpavyatirekeṇābhilāpyasvabhāvābhāvāt / viśeṣavikalpapratipakṣeṇāha - svabhāvasya notpādo yāvadvayavadānamapi na samanupaśyatīti, utpādādiviśeṣalakṣaṇapratiṣedhāt / yathānāmārthavikalpapratipakṣeṇāha - kṛtrimaṃ
body.translated_text: does not perceive the name '<s>Bodhisattva</s>.' Does not perceive the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Does not perceive awakening (<s>bodhi</s>). Does not perceive 'one practices.' Does not perceive 'one does not practice.'...

body.text: nāma prati prati te dharmāḥ kalpitā āgantukena nāmnā vyavahriyante ityevamādi / yathārthanāmavikalpapratipakṣeṇāha - tāni bodhisattvaḥ sarvanāmāni na samanu paśyannābhiniviśata iti, yathārthaṃ nāmnāmadarśanā[na]bhiniveśāt //
body.translated_text: means: regarding those <s>dharmas</s>, [names] are imagined—they are designated by adventitious names, and so forth. As the antidote to the conceptualization of names corresponding to reality, [the text] says: 'The <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not perceive all those names...'

body.text: nirvikalpanāt tridhā saṃtuṣṭinirvikalpanādibhiḥ / tatra pṛthagjanā yadi [a]nityatādikāṃ kāṃcidevadharmatāmārabhya cittaparyavasānaṃ nītvā labdhaparitoṣā bhavantyevametaditi niścinvantaḥ sā teṣāṃ saṃtuṣṭinirvikalpatetyucyate, tatra sarvatarkākhyavikalpoparateḥ / śrāvakāḥ skandheṣu nityādiviparyāsapratipakṣeṇa yathāvadrūpādikaṃ dharmadhātuṃ parīkṣamāṇā lokottareṇa jñānena nairātmyaṃ pratividhyantyataḥ sā teṣāmaviparyāsanirvikalpatetyucyate / bodhisattvāstadapi rūpādidharmamātraṃ prapañca iti viditvā sarvadharmanimittāni vibhāvayantaḥ paramaśāntena lokottareṇa jñānena sarvatragāṃ tathatāṃ pratividhyantyataḥ sā teṣāṃ niṣprapañcanirvikalpatetyucyate / kathaṃ punarasau niṣprapañcanirvikalpatetyucyate / yadyamanaskāratastena suptamattādīnāṃ nirvikalpatāprasaṅgaḥ, teṣāṃ dharmanimittāmanaskārāt / atha samatikramatastena dvitīyadhyānāt prabhṛti sarvatra nirvikalpatā prāpnoti, [vi]tarkavicāravikalpānāṃ samatikramāt, tataśca vikalpasya śarīraṃ hi cittacaittāḥ traidhātukā ityasya virodhaḥ / atha vyupaśamatastena saṃjñāveditanirodhasamāpattirnivikalpatā prāpnoti, tatra cittacaitavikalpavyupaśamāt, tataśca jñānābhāvaḥ prasajyate / atha svabhāvatastena rūpaṃ nirvikalpatā prāpnoti, tasyāvikalpasvabhāvatvāt / athālaṃbane 'bhisaṃskārastena savikalpataiva nirvikalpatā prāpnoti, nirvikalpametadityetasyābhisaṃskārasya nimittavikalpalakṣaṇatvāt / tasmānnaibhiḥ prakāraiḥ nirvikalpatā draṣṭavyā / api tvālaṃbane 'nabhisaṃskāratādraṣṭavyā / kathaṃ kṛtvā / yadā hyasya bodhisattvasyānulomikamavavādamāgamya prakṛtyā sarvadharmanimittānyapariniṣpannānīti vicārayatastadvicāraṇābhyāsabalādhānāt pratyātmamanabhisaṃskāreṇaiva yathāvanniṣprapañcadhātau sarvadharmatathatāyāṃ cittaṃ samādhīyate sāsāvucyate niṣprapañcanirvikalpateti //
body.translated_text: Non-conceptuality (<s>nirvikalpatā</s>) is threefold, through contentment-non-conceptuality (<s>saṃtuṣṭinirvikalpatā</s>) and the rest. Among these, ordinary persons (<s>pṛthagjanas</s>), having taken up some quality of <s>dharmas</s> such as impermanence and the rest and bringing their investigation to a conclusion of mind, become satisfied and determine 'it is just so'—that is called their contentment-non-conceptuality, because there is the cessation of the conceptuality called 'all reasoning.' <s>Śrāvakas</s>, examining the <s>dharma</s>-realm of form and the rest as they truly are in the aggregates, as the antidote to the inversions of permanence and the rest, penetrate selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>) through supramundane knowledge—therefore that is called their non-inversion non-conceptuality (<s>aviparyāsanirvikalpatā</s>). <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, knowing that even that mere <s>dharma</s> of form and the rest is elaboration (<s>prapañca</s>), while contemplating the signs of all <s>dharmas</s>, penetrate the all-pervading <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) through supremely peaceful supramundane knowledge—therefore that is called their non-elaboration non-conceptuality (<s>niṣprapañcanirvikalpatā</s>). Now, how is that called non-elaboration non-conceptuality? If through non-attention (<s>amanaskāra</s>), then non-conceptuality would absurdly follow for those who are asleep, intoxicated, and so forth, because they have non-attention to the signs of <s>dharmas</s>. Or if through transcending (<s>samatikrama</s>), then non-conceptuality would obtain everywhere from the second <s>dhyāna</s> onward, because of the transcending of the conceptualities of initial and sustained thought (<s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s>)—and then there would be a contradiction with the statement that 'the body of conceptuality is mind and mental factors of the three realms.' Or if through pacification (<s>vyupaśama</s>), then the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling (<s>saṃjñāveditanirodhasamāpatti</s>) would be non-conceptuality, because of the pacification of the conceptuality of mind and mental factors therein—and then the absence of knowledge would absurdly follow. Or if through intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāva</s>), then form (<s>rūpa</s>) would be non-conceptuality, because of its intrinsically non-conceptual nature. Or if through mental construction with respect to the object (<s>ālambane abhisaṃskāra</s>), then conceptuality itself would be non-conceptuality, because the mental construction 'this is non-conceptual' has the character of sign-based conceptuality (<s>nimittavikalpa</s>). Therefore, non-conceptuality should not be understood through these modes. Rather, it should be understood through non-construction with respect to the object. How so? When, having resort to the concordant instruction, this <s>Bodhisattva</s> who reflects that by nature all signs of <s>dharmas</s> are unestablished (<s>apariniṣpanna</s>)—through the force of habituating that reflection, by the power of personal non-construction itself, the mind becomes concentrated in the non-elaboration realm (<s>niṣprapañcadhātu</s>), in the <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) of all <s>dharmas</s>, just as it truly is—that is called non-elaboration non-conceptuality.

body.text: prakṛtyā tīkṣṇendriyo bodhisattva ityuktaṃ prākkathaṃ tena kālena kālamindriyāṇyutāpayitavyānītyucyate / svajātīyānāṃ mṛdvāditraividhyāduttarottarābhinirhāratastaduttāpanaṃ veditavyam / anyathā tīkṣṇendriyagotrāṇāmindriyāṇāmaikavidhye sati bodhisattvānāmindriyakṛto viśeṣo naivopalabhyate / sa copalabhyata iti //
body.translated_text: It was said earlier that the <s>Bodhisattva</s> has sharp faculties (<s>tīkṣṇendriya</s>) by nature. How then is it said that the faculties should be sharpened from time to time? The sharpening should be understood through progressive development from the threefold division of dull and so forth among those of the same class. Otherwise, if the faculties of those of the sharp-faculty lineage were uniform, no distinction based on faculties among <s>Bodhisattvas</s> could be found at all. But such distinction is indeed found.

body.text: sāṃkathyaviniścayo nāma pañcamaḥ samuccayaḥ
body.translated_text: The fifth compendium, called the Determination of Discussions (<s>Sāṃkathyaviniścaya</s>).

body.text: saptavidhasāṃkathyaviniścaye 'rthaviniścayaḥ svabhāvārthādīn ṣaḍarthānārabhya veditavyaḥ / tatra -
body.translated_text: In the sevenfold determination of discussions, the determination of meaning is to be understood with respect to six meanings beginning with the meaning of intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāvārtha</s>). Among them:

body.text: svabhāvastrayaḥ svabhāvāḥ parikalpitaḥ paratantraḥ pariniṣpannaśca //
body.translated_text: Intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāva</s>): the three natures are the imagined (<s>parikalpita</s>), the dependent (<s>paratantra</s>), and the thoroughly established (<s>pariniṣpanna</s>).

body.text: hetvarthastrayo hetavaḥ / utpattihetustathā hetusamanantarālaṃbanādhipatipratyayāḥ, tataḥ sarvasaṃskṛtanirvartanāt / pravṛttihetustadyathāvidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārā yāvatsamudayo nirodhaśca bhavatītyetayānupūrvyā saṃkleśavyavadānapravṛtteḥ / siddhihetuḥ pratyakṣopalambhānupalambhasamākhyānasaṃgṛhītaḥ, tena sādhyasyāpratītasyārthasya sādhanāt //
body.translated_text: The meaning of cause (<s>hetvārtha</s>): there are three causes. The cause of arising (<s>utpattihetu</s>), namely the conditions of cause (<s>hetu</s>), immediately preceding (<s>samanantara</s>), object-support (<s>ālambana</s>), and dominant (<s>adhipati</s>)—because all conditioned things are produced from those. The cause of activity (<s>pravṛttihetu</s>), such as 'conditioned by ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) are formations (<s>saṃskāras</s>),' up to 'there is both arising and cessation'—because of the sequential operation of defilement and purification. The cause of proof (<s>siddhihetu</s>), included in direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), non-apprehension (<s>anupalambha</s>), and verbal testimony (<s>samākhyāna</s>)—because through it, an unaccepted meaning that is to be proved is established.

body.text: phalārthaḥ pañca phalāni / vipākaphalaṃ tadyathālayavijñānam / niṣpandaphalaṃ tadyathā pūrvotpannānāṃ kuśalādīnāṃ dharmāṇāṃ tatsāntānikā uttara kuśalādayo dharmāḥ / adhipatiphalaṃ tadyathā sarvasattvasādhāraṇaṃ karmādhipatyena bhājanalokaḥ / puruṣakāraphalaṃ tadyathā sasyādayaḥ visaṃyogaphalaṃ tadyathāryamārgeṇānuśayasamudghātaḥ //
body.translated_text: The meaning of fruit (<s>phalārtha</s>): there are five fruits. The maturation-fruit (<s>vipākaphala</s>), such as the store-consciousness (<s>ālayavijñāna</s>). The outflow-fruit (<s>niṣyandaphala</s>), such as subsequent wholesome and other <s>dharmas</s> belonging to the same continuum as previously arisen wholesome and other <s>dharmas</s>. The dominant-fruit (<s>adhipatiphala</s>), such as the receptacle-world (<s>bhājanaloka</s>) produced by the dominance of <s>karma</s> shared by all beings. The effort-fruit (<s>puruṣakāraphala</s>), such as crops and the like. The separation-fruit (<s>visaṃyogaphala</s>), such as the eradication of latent tendencies (<s>anuśaya</s>) through the noble path (<s>āryamārga</s>).

body.text: karmārthaḥ pūrvavaddraṣṭavyastadyathā karmasaṃkleśanirdeśe //
body.translated_text: The meaning of action (<s>karmārtha</s>) should be understood as before, namely as in the exposition of <s>karma</s> and defilement (<s>karmasaṃkleśanirdeśa</s>).

body.text: yogārthaḥ pañca yogāḥ sāmūhiko yogastadyathā gṛhakāṣṭheṣṭakādīnām / ānubandhiko yogastadyathā[nu]śayādihetuḥ, tathāhi tasmin satyasamudācaradbhirapi kleśādibhiryukta ityucyate / sāmbandhiko yogastadyathā svajanmanāṃ parasparam / āvasthiko yogastadyathānugrahādyāḥ saṃtānavyavasthāḥ, tathāhi tāsu vartamānaḥ sukhena yukto yāvadduḥkhāsukhena yukta ityucyate / vaikāriko yoga āgantukopakleśādika saṃmukhībhāvaḥ, tathāhi tasmin sati rāgādibhiḥ śraddhādibhiśca yukta ityucyate //
body.translated_text: The meaning of connection (<s>yogārtha</s>): there are five connections. Collective connection (<s>sāmūhika yoga</s>), such as [the connection] of a house, timber, bricks, and the like. Continuity-connection (<s>ānubandhika yoga</s>), such as the cause of latent tendencies (<s>anuśaya</s>) and the like—for even when the defilements and so forth are not actively manifesting, one is said to be 'connected' with them, because they exist as latent tendencies. Relational connection (<s>sāmbandhika yoga</s>), such as the mutual relationship of one's births. Situational connection (<s>āvasthika yoga</s>), such as the states of the continuum like benefit and the rest—for one dwelling in those states is said to be 'connected with happiness,' up to 'connected with neither-suffering-nor-happiness.' Transformational connection (<s>vaikārika yoga</s>): the coming into presence of adventitious secondary defilements (<s>upakleśa</s>) and the like—for when that occurs, one is said to be 'connected with desire (<s>rāga</s>)' and 'connected with faith (<s>śraddhā</s>)' and the like.

body.text: vṛttyarthaḥ pañca vṛttayaḥ / lakṣaṇavṛttiḥ saṃskṛtasya trīṇi lakṣaṇānyutpādādīni, taiḥ prakārairvartanāt / avasthānavṛttirādheyasyādhāre
body.translated_text: The meaning of activity (<s>vṛttyārtha</s>): there are five activities. The activity of characteristics (<s>lakṣaṇavṛtti</s>)—the three characteristics of the conditioned, beginning with arising (<s>utpāda</s>), because things operate in those modes. The activity of position (<s>avasthānavṛtti</s>)—the establishment of what is supported in its support

body.text: vyavasthānam / viparyāsavṛttiḥ sāṃkleśikānāṃ dharmāṇāmayathābhūtaṃ vartanāt / aviparyāsavṛttirvyāvadānikānāṃ dharmāṇām / prabhedavṛttiḥ sarvasaṃskārāṇāmatītānāgatapratyutpannādhyātmikabāhyādiprakārairvartanāt //
body.translated_text: establishment. The activity of inversion (<s>viparyāsavṛtti</s>)—because defiling <s>dharmas</s> operate not as they truly are. The activity of non-inversion (<s>aviparyāsavṛtti</s>)—that of purifying <s>dharmas</s>. The activity of classification (<s>prabhedavṛtti</s>)—because all formations (<s>saṃskāras</s>) operate in modes such as past, future, present, internal, external, and so forth.

body.text: vyākhyāviniścayo yena sūtrāntānāmarthaṃ nirdiśati / sa punaḥ parijñeyavastvādīnāṃ ṣaṣṇāmarthānāṃ pratisūtraṃ yathāsaṃbhavaṃ pratipādanāt / tatra parijñeyaṃ vastu skandhādi / parijñeyo 'rtho 'nityatādi / parijñopaniṣacchīlendriyaguptadvāratādi / parijñā bodhipakṣyā dharmāḥ / parijñāphalaṃ vimuktiḥ / tatpravedanā vimuktijñānadarśanamiti //
body.translated_text: The determination of exegesis (<s>vyākhyāviniścaya</s>) is that by which one expounds the meaning of the <s>sūtrāntas</s>. Moreover, this is through the explanation, in accordance with each <s>sūtra</s> as applicable, of the six meanings beginning with the thing to be fully known (<s>parijñeya</s>). Among these: the thing to be fully known is the aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>) and the rest. The meaning to be fully known is impermanence and the rest. The basis for full knowledge (<s>parijñopaniṣad</s>) is moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>), guarded sense-faculties, and the rest. Full knowledge (<s>parijñā</s>) is the factors conducive to awakening (<s>bodhipakṣya dharmas</s>). The fruit of full knowledge is liberation (<s>vimukti</s>). The realization thereof is the knowledge and vision of liberation (<s>vimuktijñānadarśana</s>).

body.text: api khalu caturdaśa mukhāni vyākhyāyāḥ //
body.translated_text: Moreover, there are fourteen methods of exegesis.

body.text: vyākhyāsaṃgrahamukhaṃ yatra sūtrasyotpattiprayojanaṃ padārtho 'nusandhirabhiprāyaścodyaparihāraśca varṇyate //
body.translated_text: The comprehensive-explanation method (<s>vyākhyāsaṃgrahamukha</s>): where the <s>sūtra</s>'s origin and purpose, word-meaning, connection, intention, and objection-and-refutation are expounded.

body.text: vastusaṃgrahamukhaṃ yatra sūtramukhaṃ śikṣāryasatyavastvādiṣu pratipādyate / tadyathā sarvapāpasyākaraṇamiti gāthā tisraḥ śikṣā[ma]dhikṛtyetyevamādi //
body.translated_text: The subject-matter method (<s>vastusaṃgrahamukha</s>): where the import of the <s>sūtra</s> is explained with respect to the trainings (<s>śikṣā</s>), noble truths (<s>āryasatya</s>), and so forth. For example, the verse 'the non-performance of all evil'—this is with reference to the three trainings, and so forth.

body.text: aṅgopāṅgamukhaṃ yatraikena padenoddeśaḥ śeṣairnirdeśa iti pradarśyate / tadyathā dvādaśakṣaraṇasaṃnipātadeśanāyāmātmasampatparasampadityanayordvayoryathākramaṃ pañcabhiḥ pañcabhiruttaraiḥ padairnideśa iti //
body.translated_text: The principal-and-subsidiary method (<s>aṅgopāṅgamukha</s>): where it is shown that one phrase serves as the heading and the rest serve as the exposition. For example, in the teaching of the twelve-session discourse (<s>dvādaśakṣaraṇasaṃnipātadeśanā</s>), self-accomplishment (<s>ātmasampat</s>) and other-accomplishment (<s>parasampat</s>)—these two are each expounded in order by five subsequent phrases respectively.

body.text: uttarottaranirhāramukhaṃ yatrottarasyottarasyābhinirharaṇāśrayatvādette dharmā evaṃ deśitā iti pradarśyate / tadyathā pañcendriyāṇi / tathāhi śraddadhāno vīryamārabhate, ārabdhavīryasya smṛtirupatiṣṭhate, upasthitasmṛteścitaṃ samādhīyate, samāhitacitto yathābhūtaṃ prajānātīti //
body.translated_text: The progressive-development method (<s>uttarottaranirhāramukha</s>): where it is shown that these <s>dharmas</s> were taught in this way because each subsequent one serves as the basis for the development of the next. For example, the five faculties (<s>pañcendriyāṇi</s>): thus, one who has faith exerts effort; for one who has exerted effort, mindfulness is established; for one whose mindfulness is established, the mind becomes concentrated; one whose mind is concentrated knows as it truly is.

body.text: pratikṣepamukhaṃ yatredamārabhyedaṃ pratikṣipyata iti pradarśyate / tadyathā vāsyaupamyasūtre āsravakṣayamārabhya catvāraḥ pudgalāḥ pratikṣipyante / ito bāhyaka ihadhārmikaḥ śrutacintāmātrasaṃtuṣṭaḥ bhāvanāyāṃ paritasyamāno 'paripūrṇasaṃbhāraśca / jānataścāhaṃ bhikṣavaḥ paśyataścāsravāṇāṃ kṣayaṃ vadāmītyevamādinā sūtrakhaṇḍenādyaḥ pudgalaḥ pratikṣiptaḥ / bhāvanāyogamanuyuktasyetyevamādinā dvitīyaḥ / vāsyaupamyadṛṣṭāntena tṛtīyaḥ / naudṛṣṭāntena caturtha iti //
body.translated_text: The rejection method (<s>pratikṣepamukha</s>): where it is shown that 'beginning from this, this is rejected.' For example, in the <s>Vāsyaupamya Sūtra</s>, beginning from the destruction of outflows (<s>āsravakṣaya</s>), four types of persons are rejected: the outsider, the one established in the <s>dharma</s> here but content with mere hearing and reflection, the one satisfied with mere hearing and reflection who shrinks from cultivation, and the one with incomplete accumulations. By the <s>sūtra</s>-passage 'I declare the destruction of the outflows for one who knows and sees, O <s>bhikṣus</s>' and so forth, the first person is rejected. By 'for one engaged in the practice of cultivation' and so forth, the second. By the simile of the adze (<s>vāsī</s>), the third. By the 'not like the adze' example, the fourth.

body.text: akṣarapaṇimamukhaṃ yatrānyasminnarthe prasiddhānyakṣarāṇyanyasmin pariṇāmyante / tadyathāśraddhaścākṛtajñaśceti gāthāyām /
body.translated_text: The letter-transformation method (<s>akṣarapariṇāmamukha</s>): where letters well-known in one meaning are applied to another meaning. For example, in the verse 'one who is faithless (<s>aśraddha</s>) and ungrateful (<s>akṛtajña</s>)' —

body.text: nāśānāśamukhaṃ tatra praṇāho 'praṇāśastadubhayopāyastadubhayaprabhedaśca pradarśyate / tadyathā sujātasūtre praṇāśo bāhyādhyātmikopadhyavasānam / tatra bāhya upadhirgṛhakalatrādilakṣaṇaḥ, ādhyātmikaḥ pañcopādānaskandhalakṣaṇaḥ / apraṇāśastadubhayādhyavasānavigamaḥ / praṇāśopāyo 'pravrajanaṃ pravrajitasya cāsravakṣayaṃ prati pramādaḥ / viparyayādapraṇāśopāyo draṣṭavyaḥ / tatrobhayato vatāyaṃ sujātaḥ kulaputraḥ śobhate yacca keśaśmaśrūṇyavahārya yāvat pravrajito yaccāsravāṇāṃ kṣayādyāvatprajānāmītyanenāpraṇāśatadupāyāpadeśena tadviparītalakṣaṇapraṇāśatadupāyau sūcitau bhavataḥ / apraṇāśaprabhedo gāthānugītena darśitaḥ - "śobhate vata bhikṣurayamupaśānto nirāśrava" iti / tadevaṃ pravrajanamāsravakṣayaśca paridīpitaḥ / sa punarāsravakṣayaḥ -
body.translated_text: The loss-and-non-loss method (<s>nāśānāśamukha</s>): where loss, non-loss, the means for both, and the classification of both are shown. For example, in the <s>Sujāta Sūtra</s>: loss is the clinging to external and internal possessions. Among these, external possessions are characterized as houses, wives, and the like; internal possessions are characterized as the five aggregates of clinging (<s>pañcopādānaskandha</s>). Non-loss is the departure from clinging to both. The means of loss is not going forth (<s>pravrajana</s>), and for one who has gone forth, heedlessness (<s>pramāda</s>) regarding the destruction of outflows. The means of non-loss should be understood as the opposite. Therein, 'On both sides does this well-born (<s>Sujāta</s>) son of good family shine: both in having shaved off hair and beard... having gone forth, and in having destroyed the outflows... he knows'—by this indication of non-loss and its means, the contrarily characterized loss and its means are implied. The classification of non-loss is shown by the appended verse: 'This <s>bhikṣu</s> indeed shines, calmed and free from outflows.' Thus going forth and the destruction of outflows are illuminated. And furthermore, that destruction of outflows—

body.text:
vītarāgo visaṃyukto hyanupādāya nirvṛtaḥ /
dhārayatyanti maṃ dehaṃ jitvā mārasya vāhinīm //
body.translated_text: Free from desire, disjoined, and without clinging, one has attained cessation; bearing this final body, having conquered the army of <s>Māra</s>.

body.text: ityanena laukikamārgavairāgyataḥ, lokottareṇa mārgeṇāvarabhāgīyasaṃyojanaprahāṇataḥ, ūrdhvabhāgīyasaṃyojanaprahāṇataḥ, ādhyātmikopadhiprahāṇataśca paridīpitaḥ / hetuphalakṣayādhikārāccāyaṃ nirdeśo draṣṭavyaḥ / etadviparyayeṇa praṇāśaprabhedaḥ sūcito draṣṭavyaḥ iti //
body.translated_text: —is illuminated through dispassion by the mundane path, through the abandonment of the lower fetters (<s>avarabhāgīyasaṃyojana</s>) by the supramundane path, through the abandonment of the upper fetters (<s>ūrdhvabhāgīyasaṃyojana</s>), and through the abandonment of internal possessions (<s>ādhyātmikopadhi</s>). This exposition should be understood as having the topic of the destruction of cause and fruit. The classification of loss should be understood as implied by the opposite of this.

body.text: pudgalavyavasthānamukhaṃ yatreyataḥ pudgalānadhikṛtyedaṃ bhāṣitamiti pradarśyate / tadyathā audakopame sūtre dvividhau pudgalau tricatuḥprabhedānadhikṛtya bhāṣitam - pṛthagjanaṃ dṛṣṭasatyaṃ ca / pṛthagjanastribhedaḥ - aśuklo 'lpaśuklaḥ bahuśuklaśca / dṛṣṭasatyaścatuḥprabhedaḥ - catvāraḥ pratipannakāḥ, catvāraḥ phalasthāḥ, trayaḥ śekṣāḥ, eko 'śaikṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: The person-classification method (<s>pudgalavyavasthānamukha</s>): where it is shown that 'with reference to these persons, this has been spoken.' For example, in the <s>Audakopama Sūtra</s>, the discourse is spoken with reference to two types of persons having threefold and fourfold classifications: the ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) and one who has seen the truths (<s>dṛṣṭasatya</s>). The ordinary person has three divisions: one without merit (<s>aśukla</s>), one with little merit (<s>alpaśukla</s>), and one with much merit (<s>bahuśukla</s>). One who has seen the truths has four divisions: the four who are on the path (<s>pratipannaka</s>), the four who are established in the fruit (<s>phalastha</s>), the three trainees (<s>śaikṣa</s>), and the one beyond training (<s>aśaikṣa</s>).

body.text: prabhedavyavasthānamukhaṃ yatra catuṣkoṭikadibhiḥ praśnairartho varṇyate / tadyathānityasūtre - yaḥ sadidaṃ samanupaśyati sarvo 'sau rūpaṃ samanupaśyati, yo vā rūpaṃ samanupaśyati sarvaḥ sa sadidaṃ samanupaśyatīti catuṣkoṭikaḥ / prathamā koṭirvedanārdīścaturaḥ skandhānnityaśucisukhātmaviparyāsairasamāropya parijñeyaprahātavyāṃśca samanupaśyataḥ / dvitīyā koṭī rūpaṃ nityaśucisukhātmaviparyāsaiḥ samāropyāparijñeyāprahātavyaṃ ca samanupaśyataḥ / tṛtīyā koṭī rūpaṃ nityaśucisukhātmaviparyāsairasamāropya parijñeyaprahātavyāṃśca samanupaśyataḥ caturthīkoṭirvedanādīṃścaturaḥ skandhānnityaśucisukhātmaviparyāsaiḥ samāropyāparijñeyāprahātavyaṃ ca samanupaśyataḥ / yathā rūpe catuṣkoṭika evaṃ vedanādau sarvatra vistareṇa draṣṭavyam / yāvadyasya kṛtaṃ karaṇīyaṃ sarvaḥ sa nāparamasmādbhavaṃ prajānāti, yāvannāparamasmādbhavaṃ prajānāti sarvasya tasya kṛtaṃ karaṇīyam / āha catuṣkoṭikam / prathamā koṭiryāvajjīvaṃ sucaritacāriṇaḥ pṛthagjanasya / dvitīyocchedadṛṣṭayādīnām / tṛtīyā aśaikṣasya / caturthī tānākārān sthāpayitvā //
body.translated_text: The categorical-distinction method (<s>prabhedavyavasthānamukha</s>): where the meaning is expounded through <s>catuṣkoṭika</s> (tetralemma) and other questions. For example, in the <s>Anitya Sūtra</s>: 'Does everyone who views this rightly view form? Or does everyone who views form rightly view this?'—this is a <s>catuṣkoṭika</s>. The first lemma: one who views the four <s>skandhas</s> of feeling and the rest without superimposing the inversions of permanence, purity, happiness, and self, and as to-be-fully-known and to-be-abandoned. The second lemma: one who views form by superimposing the inversions of permanence, purity, happiness, and self, and as not-to-be-fully-known and not-to-be-abandoned. The third lemma: one who views form without superimposing the inversions of permanence, purity, happiness, and self, and as to-be-fully-known and to-be-abandoned. The fourth lemma: one who views the four <s>skandhas</s> of feeling and the rest by superimposing the inversions of permanence, purity, happiness, and self, and as not-to-be-fully-known and not-to-be-abandoned. As the <s>catuṣkoṭika</s> applies to form, so it should be understood in detail for feeling and the rest, everywhere. Up to: 'Does everyone whose task is done know that there will be no more of this existence? Does everyone who knows that there will be no more of this existence have his task done?'—this is a <s>catuṣkoṭika</s>. The first lemma: an ordinary person who has practiced good conduct throughout life. The second: those with the view of annihilation (<s>ucchedadṛṣṭi</s>) and the rest. The third: one beyond training (<s>aśaikṣa</s>). The fourth: setting aside those aspects.

body.text: nayamukhaṃ yatra ṣaḍbhirnayairartho varṇyate - tattvārthanayena prāptinayena deśanānayenāntadvayavivarjanānayenācintyanayenābhiprāyanayena ca / eṣāṃ ca ṣaṇṇāṃ nayānāṃ pūrvakāstrayo nayā uttaraistribhirnayairyathākramamanugantavyāḥ / tadyathāsvādanasūtre - asti bhikṣavaḥ rūpe āsvāda ityevamādināpavādāntaṃ samāropāntaṃ ca varjayitvā tattvārthanayo 'bhidyotitaḥ / astyāsvāda ādīnavo niḥsaraṇamityanenāpavādānto varjitaḥ, rūpe yāvadvijñāna ityanena samāropāntaḥ, skandhamātre saṃkleśo vyavadānaṃ cānātmanīti pradarśayatā yāvaccāhaṃ bhikṣavaḥ yāvadanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddho 'smītyadhyajñāsiṣamityanena prāptinayo 'cintyanayena paridīpitaḥ, pratyātmavedanīyādhigamasūcanāt / sarvamevedaṃ sūtraṃ deśanānayaḥ / sa cābhiprāyeṇānugantavyaḥ / sa parijñeyaṃ vastu, parijñeyamartham, parijñām, parijñāphalam, tatpravedanāṃ cābhipretyedaṃ sūtraṃ bhāṣitamiti / tatra parijñeyaṃ vastu rūpādikam / parijñeyo 'rtha āsvādādikaḥ, tena prakāreṇa tasya rūpādikasya vastunaḥ parijñānāt / parijñaiṣāṃ pañcānāmupādānaskandhānāmevaṃ triparivartena yathābhūtaparijñānam / parijñāphalamasmāt sadevakāllokādyāvat sadevamānuṣāyāḥ prajñāyā vimuktiryāvadvipramuktiḥ / tatpravedanānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddho 'smītyadhyajñāsiṣamiti //
body.translated_text: The <s>nayamukha</s> (method of approach) is where the meaning is explained through six methods: the method of the true meaning, the method of attainment, the method of teaching, the method of avoiding both extremes, the method of the inconceivable, and the method of implicit intention. Among these six methods, the first three should be understood through the latter three respectively. For example, in the <s>Āsvādanasūtra</s> — 'There is, <s>bhikṣus</s>, enjoyment in form' and so forth — by avoiding both the extreme of denial and the extreme of superimposition, the method of the true meaning is illuminated. 'There is enjoyment, danger, and escape' — by this, the extreme of denial is avoided. 'In form, up to consciousness' — by this, the extreme of superimposition is avoided. By showing that there is defilement and purification in the mere aggregates, without a self — up to 'I have, <s>bhikṣus</s>, fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening' — by this, the method of attainment is illuminated through the method of the inconceivable, because it indicates an attainment to be personally experienced. This entire <s>sūtra</s> is the method of teaching. And it should be understood through implicit intention: this <s>sūtra</s> was spoken with the intention of the object to be fully known, the meaning to be fully known, full knowledge, the fruit of full knowledge, and the proclamation thereof. Among these, the object to be fully known is form and the rest. The meaning to be fully known is enjoyment and the rest, because through that mode there is full knowledge of that object of form and the rest. Full knowledge is the true understanding of these five aggregates of clinging through the threefold turning. The fruit of full knowledge is liberation from this world including the <s>devas</s>, up to the wisdom including <s>devas</s> and humans, up to complete liberation. The proclamation thereof is 'I have fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening.'

body.text: parijñādimukhaṃ yatra tattvalakṣaṇamāramya parijñālakṣaṇena, prahāṇalakṣaṇena, sākṣātkriyālakṣaṇena, eṣāmeva tattvalakṣaṇādīnāṃ prakārabhedalakṣaṇena, āśrayāśritasaṃvandhalakṣaṇena, parijñādīnāmāntarāyikadharmalakṣaṇena, āmulomikadharmalakṣaṇena, aparijñādiṣu cādīnavānuśaṃsālakṣaṇena cārtho nirdiśyate / tadyathātraivāsvādanasūtre / tatra tattvalakṣaṇamupādānaskandhasaṃgṛhītaduḥkhasatyam / parijñālakṣaṇaṃ tasyaivāsvādādinā yathābhūtaṃ, parijñānam / prahāṇalakṣaṇaṃ sākṣātkriyālakṣaṇaṃ ca sarvasmāllokādvimuktiḥ, āvaraṇaprahāṇe nāśrayaparivṛttisākṣātkaraṇāt bhāvanālakṣaṇaṃ viparyāsāpagatena cetasā bahulavihāraḥ / prakārabhedalakṣaṇam - tattvalakṣaṇasya pañcadhā bhedo rūpaṃ yāvadvijñānamiti / parijñālakṣaṇasya tridhā bheda āsvādaṃ cāsvādayato yāvanniḥsaraṇaṃ ca niḥsarato yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / prahāṇalakṣaṇasya sākṣātkriyālakṣaṇasya dvidhā bhedaḥ kleśavimuktirduḥkhavimuktiśca / tatra sadevakāllokādyāvatsadevamānuṣāyāḥ prajāyā vimuktiḥ kleśebhyo vimokṣādata eva tadviśeṣaṇārthamāha niḥsṛta iti / tadyathā hyanyatra sūtre - niḥsaraṇaṃ katamadbhayaḥ / chandarāgavinayaḥ chandarāgaprahāṇaṃ chandarāgasamatikrama ityuktam / evamanāgataduḥkhābhinirvartaka kleśavisaṃyoge sati duḥkhādapi vipramukto bhavatīti viśeṣaṇārthamāha - visaṃyukto vipramukta iti / bhāvanālakṣaṇasya dvidhā bhedo darśanamārgo bhāvanāmārgaśca / tatra viparyāsāpagatena cetaseti darśanamārgaṃ darśayati, bahulaṃ vyahārṣamityanena bhāvanāmārgam / āśrayāśritasaṃbandhalakṣaṇaṃ tatvalakṣaṇādīnāmuttarottarāṇāmāśrayatvasūcanāt / parijñādīnāmāntarāyikalakṣaṇamevaṃ triparivartena yathābhūtamaparijñānam / anulomikalakṣaṇaṃ yathāvyavasthānameṣāmeva rūpādīnāmāsvādādito vicāraṇā / aparijñānādīnavalakṣaṇamavimuktiryāvadanuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodherasaṃbodhaḥ / viparyayādanuśaṃsalakṣaṇaṃ veditavyamiti //
body.translated_text: The <s>parijñādimukha</s> (method of full knowledge and the rest) is where, beginning with the characteristic of reality, the meaning is indicated through: the characteristic of full knowledge, the characteristic of abandonment, the characteristic of direct realization, the characteristic of the varieties of these very characteristics of reality and the rest, the characteristic of the relationship of support and supported, the characteristic of the <s>dharmas</s> that obstruct full knowledge and the rest, the characteristic of the <s>dharmas</s> that are favorable, and the characteristic of the danger in non-knowledge and the benefit in knowledge and the rest —

body.text: balābalamukhaṃ yatraikena padenānucyamānenāyamartho na gamitaḥ syāditi pratyekaṃ sarveṣāṃ padānāṃ sāmarthya pradarśyate / tadyathā pratītyotpādasūtre 'smin satīdaṃ bhavatyasyotpādādidamutpadyate, yadutāvidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārā ityevamādi, eṣāṃ ca padānāṃ pratyekaṃ sāmarthya pūrvavadveditavya yathā pratītyasamutpādasya lakṣaṇanirdeśe //
body.translated_text: The <s>balābalamukha</s> (method of strength and weakness) is where, because a single term when cited does not convey the full meaning, the power of each and every term is demonstrated individually. For example, in the <s>Pratītyotpādasūtra</s>: 'This being, that comes to be; from the arising of this, that arises — namely, conditioned by <s>avidyā</s>, the <s>saṃskāras</s>' and so forth. The power of each of these terms should be understood as before, as in the —
