body.text: pratyāhāramukhaṃ yatra sūtrasyaikaṃ padaṃ gṛhītvā vistareṇārthaḥ pratinirdiśyate / tadyathā ṣaḍbhirdharmaiḥ samanvāgato bhikṣurhimavantamapi parvatarājaṃ mukhavāyunā cālayet, kaḥ punarvādaḥ savāsanāyā avidyā[yā]ḥ / katamaiḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ / iha bhikṣavo bhikṣuścittasyotpādakuśalo bhavati iha bhikṣurviviktaṃ kāmairyāvaccaturthadhyānamupasaṃpadya viharati / evaṃ hi bhikṣuścittasyotpādakuśalo bhavati / kathaṃ ca bhikṣuścittasya sthitikuśalo bhavati / iha bhikṣurāsevanānvayādyaddhānabhāgīyaṃ dhyānaṃ tat sthitibhāgīyaṃ karoti / evaṃ bhikṣuḥ sthitikuśalo bhavati / kathaṃ ca bhikṣurvyutthānakuśalo bhavati / iha bhikṣurāsevanānvayādyatsthitibhāgīyaṃ dhyānaṃ tadviśeṣabhāgīyaṃ karoti / evaṃ hi bhikṣurvyutthānakuśalo bhavati / kathaṃ ca bhikṣurāyakuśalo bhavati / iha bhikṣuranutpannānāṃ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāmiti vistareṇa dve samyakprahāṇe / evaṃ hi bhikṣurāyakuśalo bhavati / kathaṃ ca bhikṣurapāyakuśalo bhavati / iha hi bhikṣurutpannānāṃ pāpakā nāmakuśalānāmiti vistareṇa dve samyakprahāṇe / evaṃ hi bhikṣurapāyakuśalo bhavati / kathaṃ hi bhikṣurupāyakuśalo bhavati / iha hi bhikṣuśchandasamādhipradhānasaṃskārasamanvāgatamṛddhipādaṃ bhāvayatīti vistareṇa catvāra ṛddhipādāḥ / evaṃ hi bhikṣurupāyakuśalo bhavatīti //
body.translated_text: The <s>pratyāhāramukha</s> (method of condensation) is where, taking a single term of a <s>sūtra</s>, the meaning is explained in detail. For example: 'A <s>bhikṣu</s> endowed with six <s>dharmas</s> could shake even <s>Himavān</s>, the king of mountains, with the breath of his mouth — what need is there to speak of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) together with its imprints? Which six? Here, <s>bhikṣus</s>, a <s>bhikṣu</s> is skilled in the arising of the mind; here, a <s>bhikṣu</s>, being secluded —'

body.text: abhinirhāramukhaṃ yatra pratipadaṃ catuṣkādibhirnirdiśyate / teṣvapi catuṣkādiṣvekaikaṃ padamaparaiścatuṣkādibhiraparyanto hi nirhāro veditavyaḥ / tadyathā buddhākṣepasūtre - catvāra ime bodhisattvānāṃ bodhipariśodhakā dharmāḥ - śūnyatābhāvanā, sarvasattveṣvapratihatacittatā, bodhisattvānāṃ nityaṃ hitopasaṃharaṇatā, nirāmiṣeṇa cittena dharmadānasaṃprakāśanatā ceti / catuṣkaḥ svārtha paramārtha cārabhya bodhipariśodhanāya caturvipakṣapratipakṣeṇa veditavyaḥ / catvāro vipakṣāḥ - samāpattyāsvādanā, vyāpādaḥ, mānaḥ, tṛṣṇā ca lābhasatkāre //
body.translated_text: The <s>abhinirhāramukha</s> (method of elaboration) is where each term is explained through tetrads and the like. In those tetrads and the like, each individual term should be understood as being further elaborated endlessly through other tetrads and the like. For example, in the <s>Buddhākṣepasūtra</s>: 'These are four <s>dharmas</s> that purify the awakening of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>: the cultivation of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), an unobstructed mind toward all beings, always bringing benefit to <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and —'

body.text: aparaḥ paryāyaḥ - prathamena dharmeṇa kleśaprahāṇapratipakṣaḥ / śeṣairhīnayānaparivarjanā paridīpitāstribhiḥ kāraṇaiḥ bodhicittena sarvasattvopādānataḥ, avatīrṇaparipācanataḥ, anavatīrṇāvatāraṇataśca //
body.translated_text: Another interpretation: through the first <s>dharma</s>, the antidote for the abandonment of defilements is shown. Through the remaining three, the avoidance of the inferior vehicle is illuminated through three reasons: through <s>bodhicitta</s>, from the taking up of all beings; from the maturation of those who have entered; and from the introduction of those who have not yet entered.

body.text: aparaḥ paryāyaḥ - prathamena jñānasaṃbhārastribhiḥ puṇyasaṃbhāraḥ paridīpitaḥ, upādānaparipācanāvatāraṇaiḥ, pratyekaṃ puṇyaviśeṣaprasavanataḥ //
body.translated_text: Another interpretation: through the first, the accumulation of knowledge is illuminated; through the three, the accumulation of merit is illuminated — through taking up, maturing, and introducing — because each produces a distinctive merit.

body.text: punardvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāmāśayataśca maitracittatayā, pratipattitaścādhigamāgamopadeśābhyām /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, through two reasons: from the standpoint of disposition, through having a mind of loving-kindness; and from the standpoint of practice, through instruction in realization and scripture.

body.text: caturbhirdharmaiḥ samanvāgatā bodhisattvāḥ śūnyatāṃ bhāvayanti - adhyātmaṃ cittāvikaṃpanatayādhimuktipravicayabalādhānatayā, sarvadharmāṇāṃ yathātmyaprativedhataḥ, sarvāvaraṇavimokṣataśca / yadāśritya yathā ca bhāvayanti tadetena paridīpitam / kimāśritya / dhyānapāramitām / kathaṃ bhāvayanti / pṛthagjanamārgeṇa śrutacintābalādhānataḥ śaikṣamārgeṇāśaikṣamārgeṇa ca //
body.translated_text: <s>Bodhisattvas</s> endowed with four <s>dharmas</s> cultivate <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness): through the unshakability of the mind within, through the strength of conviction and investigation, through the penetration of the true nature of all <s>dharmas</s>, and through liberation from all obscurations. What they rely on and how they cultivate — this is illuminated by this. What do they rely on? The <s>dhyānapāramitā</s> (perfection of meditation). How do they cultivate? Separately —

body.text: caturbhirdharmaiḥ samanvāgatā bodhisattvāḥ sarvasattveṣvapratihatacittā bhavanti maitrībhāvanayā, pratipatyavikopanatayā, nimittāvikalpanatayā, khedasahiṣṇutayā ca / atrāpi yadāśritya yathā cāpratihatacittā bhavanti tatparidīpitaṃ bhavati / kimāśritya / paurvajanmikīṃ maitrībhāvanām / kathamapratihatacittā bhavanti / mithyāpratipattisthiteṣu svacitāvikopanataḥ, apakāriṣvapakāranimittāvikalpanataḥ, parahitārthaṃ vyāyāmāparikhedataśca //
body.translated_text: <s>Bodhisattvas</s> endowed with four <s>dharmas</s> have unobstructed minds toward all beings: through the cultivation of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), through the non-deviation from practice, through the non-conceptualization of signs, and through the tolerance of fatigue. Here too, what they rely on and how they have unobstructed minds is illuminated. What do they rely on? The cultivation of loving-kindness from previous lives. How are they unobstructed? —

body.text: caturbhirdharmaiḥ samanvāgatā bodhisattvā bodhisattvānāṃ nityaṃ hitamupasaṃharanti - ātmanaḥ paritulanatayā, samyagavavādapravartanatayā, saurabhyasukhasaṃvāsanatayā, pūjālābhasatkāraparicaryopasaṃharaṇatayā ca / atrāpi yadāśritya yathā copasaṃharati tatparidīpitam / kimāśritya / nihatamānatām / kathamupasaṃharati / yathoktaṃ tribhiḥ prakārairhīnasamaśiṣṭānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ yathākramam //
body.translated_text: <s>Bodhisattvas</s> endowed with four <s>dharmas</s> always bring benefit to other <s>Bodhisattvas</s>: through considering others as equal to oneself, through engaging in proper admonition, through pleasant and agreeable companionship, and through providing worship, offerings, honor, and service. Here too, what they rely on and how they bring benefit is illuminated. What do they rely on? The defeat of pride. How —

body.text: caturbhirdharmaiḥ samanvāgatā bodhisattvā nirāmiṣeṇa cittena dharmadānaṃ saṃprakāśayanti - antarāyasukhaprativedhatayā, mohalayāpanayanakauśalyatayā, nāthakaradharmārāmatayā ca / atrāpi yadāśritya / yathā ca saṃprakāśayanti tatparidīpitam / kimāśritya / lābhasatkārasyāntarāyakaratvaprativeghatām / kathaṃ saṃprakāśayanti / saṃdarśanato mūḍhānām, samādāpanataḥ samuttejanataśca pramādasaṅgānātmaparibhavena vā līnānām, saṃpraharṣaṇataḥ samyakpratipannānām, prakṛtyaiva ca dharmārāmatayā / prathamasyānyacatuṣkaḥ padaprabhedādibhirnirhāro veditavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Bodhisattvas</s> endowed with four <s>dharmas</s> proclaim the gift of <s>dharma</s> with a disinterested mind: through the penetration that worldly happiness is an obstacle, through the skill of removing the resting-place of delusion, and through the delight in the <s>dharma</s> that serves as a protector. Here too, what they rely on and how they proclaim is illuminated. What do they rely on? The penetration that gain and honor are obstructive. How —

body.text: prabhidyasaṃdarśana[vi]niścayo yathānirdiṣṭeṣu skandhādiṣu dharmeṣu yathāyogamekāvacārakādīni / tatra -
body.translated_text: The <s>prabhidyasaṃdarśana</s> (demonstration through analysis) is the determination regarding the <s>dharmas</s> such as <s>skandhas</s> and the rest as indicated, through the single-category and other question formats as appropriate. Among these —

body.text: ekāvacārako nāma praśno yenaikaṃ dharmaṃ pariśiṣṭaiḥ saha pratyekaṃ praśnayitvā tamapahāya dvitīyaṃ tenānyaiśca saha praśnayatyevamekaikasyaiva sarvān praśnayati / tadyathā yaścakṣurāyatanena samanvāgato rūpāyatanenāpi saḥ, yo vā rūpāyatanena cakṣurāyatanenāpi sa iti pūrvapādakaḥ / yaścakṣurāyatanena samanvāgataḥ śrotrāyatanenāpi sa ityatra catuṣkoṭikam / evaṃ yāvanmanaāyatanenāpi sa ityatra yathāyogaṃ yojayitavyam / dharmāyatanenāpi sa ityatra pūrvapādakaḥ / yo rūpāyatanena samanvāgataścakṣurāyatanenāpi saḥ, yo vā cakṣurāyatanena rūpāyatanenāpi sa iti paścātpādakaḥ / yo rūpāyatanena samanvāgataḥ śrotrāyatanenāpi sa ityatra cāpi paścātpādakaḥ / evaṃ yāvaddharmāyatanena yathāyogaṃ yojayitavyam / yaḥ śrotrāyatanena samanvāgataścakṣurāyatanenāpi sa ityatra catuṣkoṭikam / evaṃ yāvaddharmāyatanenā[pi] yojyam / evamekaṃkāmarṣeṇānukramaśaḥ sarvāṇyāyatanāni parasparaṃ yojayitavyāni /
body.translated_text: The <s>ekāvacāraka</s> (single-category question) is a question by which, having inquired about one <s>dharma</s> together with the remaining ones individually, one sets that aside and inquires about a second one together with the others — thus inquiring about each one with all the others. For example: 'Is one who possesses the <s>cakṣurāyatana</s> (eye sense base) also possessed of the <s>rūpāyatana</s> (form sense base)? Or is one who possesses the form sense base also possessed of the eye sense base?' — this is the forward-footed format. 'Is one who possesses the eye sense base —'

body.text: pūrvapādakaṃ dvayordharmayoḥ kathaṃcideva dharmamārabhya parasparaṃ pṛṣṭayoḥ pūrvadharmamadhiṣṭhāya yadvayākriyate / tadyathā yajjñānaṃ jñeyamapi tadyadvā jñeyaṃ jñānamapi taditi / pūrvapādakam - yattāvajjñānaṃ jñeyamapi taditi / syājjñeyaṃ na jñānam, tadanye dharmā iti //
body.translated_text: The <s>pūrvapādaka</s> (forward-footed) — regarding two <s>dharmas</s>, when both are asked about each other with respect to some <s>dharma</s>, the answer is given by first establishing the former <s>dharma</s>. For example: 'Is knowledge also what is to be known? Or is the knowable also knowledge?' — the forward-footed answer: 'First, whatever is knowledge is also what is to be known.' But there may be what is to be known that is not knowledge — namely, other <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: paścātpādakaṃ tathaiva dvayordharmayoḥ parasparaṃ pṛṣṭayoryatpaścimamadhiṣṭhāya vyākriyate / tadyathā yadgrāhyaṃ grāhakamapi tadyadvā grāhakaṃ grāhyamapi taditi / paścātpādakam - yattāvadgrāhakaṃ grāhyamapi tat / syādgrāhyaṃ na grāhakam, rūpādayaḥ pañca viṣayā dharmāyatanaṃ ca saṃprayuktakavarjyam //
body.translated_text: The <s>paścātpādaka</s> (backward-footed) — likewise regarding two <s>dharmas</s>, when both are asked about each other, the answer is given by establishing the latter. For example: 'Is what is apprehended also the apprehender? Or is the apprehender also what is apprehended?' — the backward-footed answer: 'First, whatever is the apprehender is also what is apprehended.' But there may be what is apprehended that is not the apprehender — namely, the five objects of form and the rest, and the <s>dharmāyatana</s> excluding the associated.

body.text: dvikoṭikaṃ yatra dve koṭī vyākriyete tadanyāsaṃbhavāt tadyathā skandhasya vyavasthānaṃ dhātuvyavasthānaṃ ca nigamayyocyate - yā skandhasaṃkhyā dhātusaṃkhyāpi sā, yā vā dhātusaṃkhyā skandhasaṃkhyāpi seti / dvikoṭikam - syāt skandhasaṃkhyā na dhātusaṃkhyā, rūpaskandho vijñānaskandhaścaḥ / tathāhi naiko dhāturasti yaḥ sakalarūpaskandhalakṣaṇo vā syāt sakalavijñānaskandhalakṣaṇo vā / dhātusaṃkhyā na skandhasaṃkhyāḥ, dharmadhāturiti //
body.translated_text: The <s>dvikoṭika</s> (two-alternative) is where only two alternatives are answered, because the others are impossible. For example, by concluding the establishment of <s>skandhas</s> and <s>dhātus</s> — 'Is what is a <s>skandha</s>-enumeration also a <s>dhātu</s>-enumeration? Or is what is a <s>dhātu</s>-enumeration also a <s>skandha</s>-enumeration?' — the two-alternative: there can be a <s>skandha</s>-enumeration that is not a <s>dhātu</s>-enumeration — the <s>rūpaskandha</s> (form aggregate) and the <s>vijñānaskandha</s> (consciousness aggregate). For there is no single <s>dhātu</s> that would have the character of the entire form aggregate or of the entire consciousness aggregate. A <s>dhātu</s>-enumeration that is not a <s>skandha</s>-enumeration — the <s>dharmadhātu</s>.

body.text: trikoṭikaṃ yatra tisra eva koṭayo vyākriyante / tadyathā yā skandhasaṃkhyāyatanasaṃkhyāpi sā, yā vāyatanasaṃkhyā skandhasaṃkhyāpi seti / trikoṭikam - syāt skandhasaṃkhyā nāyatanasaṃkhyā, rūpaskandhaḥ / syādāyatanasaṃkhyā na skandhasaṃkhyā, dharmāyatanam / syāt skandhasaṃkhyāyatanasaṃkhyā ca vijñānaskandho manaāyatanaṃ ca / anubhayasaṃkhyāyāḥ skandhāyataneṣvasaṃbhava eveti //
body.translated_text: The <s>trikoṭika</s> (three-alternative) is where only three alternatives are answered. For example: 'Is what is a <s>skandha</s>-enumeration also an <s>āyatana</s>-enumeration? Or is what is an <s>āyatana</s>-enumeration also a <s>skandha</s>-enumeration?' — the three-alternative: there can be a <s>skandha</s>-enumeration that is not an <s>āyatana</s>-enumeration — the <s>rūpaskandha</s>. There can be an <s>āyatana</s>-enumeration that is not a <s>skandha</s>-enumeration — the <s>dharmāyatana</s>. There can be both a <s>skandha</s>-enumeration and an <s>āyatana</s>-enumeration — the <s>vijñānaskandha</s> and the <s>manāyatana</s> (mind sense base). The alternative of neither is impossible in the <s>skandhas</s> and <s>āyatanas</s>.

body.text: catuṣkoṭikaṃ yatra catasro 'pi koṭayo vyākriyante / tadyathā yaścakṣurindriyeṇa samanvāgataḥ śrotrendriyeṇāpi saḥ, yo vā śrotrendriyeṇa samanvāgataścakṣurindriyeṇāpi sa iti / catuṣkoṭikam - prathamā koṭirutpannāvihīnacakṣurbadhiraḥ / dvitīyotpannāvihīnaśrotro 'ndhaḥ / tṛtīyotpannāvihīnacakṣuḥśrotraḥ / caturthī tānākārān sthāpayitvā //
body.translated_text: The <s>catuṣkoṭika</s> (four-alternative) is where all four alternatives are answered. For example: 'Is one who possesses the eye faculty also possessed of the ear faculty? Or is one who possesses the ear faculty also possessed of the eye faculty?' — the four-alternative: the first alternative is one whose eye has arisen and not been lost, but who is deaf. The second is one whose ear has arisen and not been lost, but who is blind. The third is one whose eye and ear have both arisen and not been lost. The fourth is setting aside those modes.

body.text: oṃkāritaṃ yatra praśne vyākaraṇamomiti kriyate evametadityabhyupagamyata ityarthaḥ / tadyathā ye 'nityāḥ sarve te saṃskārāḥ, ye vā saṃskārāḥ sarve te 'nityā iti pṛṣṭena omiti vyākartavyam //
body.translated_text: The <s>oṃkārita</s> (affirmative answer) is where the answer to a question is given as 'yes' — meaning it is accepted as 'it is so.' For example: 'Are all impermanent things <s>saṃskāras</s> (conditioned phenomena)? Or are all <s>saṃskāras</s> impermanent?' — the one questioned should answer 'yes.'

body.text: prātikṣepikaṃ yatra neti pratikṣipyate / tadyathā skandhavinirmuktāḥ saṃskārāḥ katibhiḥ satyaiḥ saṃgṛhītā iti / prātikṣepikam - na santi skandhavinirmuktāḥ saṃskārā iti //
body.translated_text: The <s>prātikṣepika</s> (rejective answer) is where 'no' is given as rejection. For example: '<s>Saṃskāras</s> apart from the <s>skandhas</s> — by how many truths are they included?' — the rejective answer: 'There are no <s>saṃskāras</s> apart from the <s>skandhas</s>.'

body.text: saṃpraśnaviniścayaḥ - aṣṭākāraḥ kāpadeśastadyathā ko nopalabhate / prajñāpāramitālābhī bodhisattvaḥ / kiṃ nopalabhate / grāhyalakṣaṇaṃ grāhakalakṣaṇaṃ ca / kena nopalabhate / prajñāpāramitayā / kasmai nopalabhate / sarvasattvaparitrāṇārthamanuttarāyai samyaksaṃbodhaye / kuto nopalabhate / buddhotpādārāgaṇataḥ saddharmaśravaṇato yoniśomanaskārato dharmānudharmapratipattitaśca / kasya nopalabhate / sarvadharmāṇām / kutra nopalabhate / adhimukticaryābhūmau yāvaddaśamyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau / kativighaścānupalambhaḥ / ekādaśavidhaḥ - utpannaviruddhaḥ, anutpannaḥ, saṃmukhībhūtaḥ, hetuvalotpannaḥ, mitrabalotpannaḥ, sarvadharmānupalambhaḥ, śūnyatānupalambhaḥ, sāsmimānaḥ, nirasmimānaḥ, asaṃbhṛtasaṃbhārasya, [saṃbhṛtasaṃbhārasya] ca / ete cānupalambhā yat kiṃcidatītānāgatapratyutpannaṃ yāvadyadvā dūre yadvāntika ityetadanukramānusāreṇa draṣṭavyāḥ //
body.translated_text: The determination through questioning — the eightfold <s>kāpadeśa</s> (presentation): 'Who does not apprehend?' A <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has attained the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>. 'What does one not apprehend?' The characteristic of the apprehended and the characteristic of the apprehender. 'By what does one not apprehend?' By the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>. 'For what purpose does one not apprehend?' For the protection of all beings, for the sake of unsurpassed —

body.text: yathā kāpadeśa evaṃ yāpadeśaḥ / yo nopalabhate yadyena yasmai yato yasya yatra nopalabhate yāvadvividhaścānupalambha iti //
body.translated_text: Just as the <s>kāpadeśa</s>, so the <s>yāpadeśa</s>: 'The one who does not apprehend, that which, by which, for which, from which, of which, and wherein one does not apprehend' — up to the twofold non-apprehension.

body.text: api khalu catvāro viniścayamārgā dūṣakādayaḥ / tatra dūṣakaḥ durākhyātasya parapakṣasyāsādhurayamiti pratiṣedhakaḥ / sādhakaḥ svākhyātasya svapakṣasya sādhurayamiti pratiṣṭhāpakaḥ / chedakaḥ pareṣāmutpannotpanneṣu saṃśayeṣu niścayadāyakaḥ / bodhakasteṣvartheṣu samūḍhānāṃ tadarthavyutpādakaḥ //
body.translated_text: Moreover, there are four paths of determination beginning with the refuter and the rest. Among these, the <s>dūṣaka</s> (refuter) refutes the opposing position that is badly proclaimed — 'this is not correct.' The <s>sādhaka</s> (establisher) establishes one's own position that is well proclaimed — 'this is correct.' The <s>chedaka</s> (resolver) gives certainty regarding doubts that arise one after another in others. The <s>bodhaka</s> (illuminator) —

body.text: kṛtyānuṣṭhānaviniścayo laukikānāmanyonyaṃ jīvikopāyādisamarthanaprayojanam / avatāraviniścayastrayāṇāṃ yānānāṃ katamasminyāne 'vatareyamavatārayeyaṃ ceti vicāraṇā / adhimuktiviniścayaḥ śrutamayyā prajñayā yathādeśanaṃ saṃpratyayaḥ / yuktiviniścayaḥ cintāmayyā prajñayā paurvāparyeṇābhiprāyaparitulanam / sāṃkathyaviniścayo yathāśrutacintitānāṃ praśnapratipraśnakriyāyogenānyonyaṃ dharmasaṃbhogaḥ / prativedhaviniścayo darśanamārgastena satyaprativedhāt / viśuddhiviniścayo bhāvanāmārgastenāvaśeṣa kleśa viśoghanāt / abhinirhāraviniścayo viśeṣamārgastena vaiśeṣikaguṇābhinirhārāt / padaprabhedaviniścayo dvikatrikacatuṣkādiprakārābhinirhāramukhenāparyantā dharmadeśanā / anābhogābhogamātrasarvārthasiddhiviniścayastathāgataṃ jñānam, vinā pūrvābhogena sarveṣvartheṣvābhogasahakālamasaṃgāpratihatajñānadarśanapravṛtteḥ //
body.translated_text: The determination of functional activity is the purpose of establishing livelihood and other means for worldly people among each other. The determination of entry is the deliberation 'in which of the three vehicles should I enter and should I cause others to enter?' The determination of conviction is faith in accordance with the teaching, through wisdom born of hearing. The determination of reasoning is —

body.text: vādaviniścayo vādavādādhikaraṇādiṣu kauśalyam //
body.translated_text: The determination of debate is skill in debate, disputation, adjudication, and the rest.

body.text: tatra sarvaṃ vacanaṃ vādaḥ / prakāraśo loke vādaḥ pravādaḥ / viruddhayorvādo vivādaḥ / apavādo garhito vādaḥ / anukūlo vādo 'nuvādaḥ sāṃkathyaviniścayaḥ / avagamāya vādo 'vavādaḥ //
body.translated_text: Among these, all speech is <s>vāda</s> (discourse). Discourse by type in the world is <s>pravāda</s> (assertion). Discourse between opponents is <s>vivāda</s> (dispute). <s>Apavāda</s> (denial) is censured discourse. Favorable discourse is <s>anuvāda</s> (concordance) — a determination through conversation. Discourse for the purpose of understanding is <s>avavāda</s> (instruction).

body.text: vādādhikaraṇam
body.translated_text: The <s>vādādhikaraṇa</s> (venue of debate) — that in which debate takes place. A royal court where the king himself is present; an appointed court where those appointed by the king preside; an assembly such as a merchants' assembly and the like. The <s>prāmāṇikas</s> (authorities) are the assistants whose words neither the proponent nor the opponent doubts. And <s>śramaṇas</s> and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> skilled in <s>dharma</s> and meaning — those are —

body.text: atra vādaḥ kriyata iti kṛtvā / rājakulaṃ yatra rājā svayaṃ saṃnihitaḥ yuktakulaṃ yatra rājñādhiyuktāḥ sabhā vaṇik sabhādi / prāmāṇikāḥ sahāyakāḥ yeṣāṃ vacanaṃ vādiprativādinau na saṃśayataḥ / dharmārthakuśalāśca śramaṇabrāhmaṇā ye teṣu śāstreṣu granthataścārthataśca vyutpannabuddhayaḥ //
vādādhiṣṭhānaṃ yadadhiṣṭhāya vādaḥ kriyate tadyathā sādhyaṃ sādhanaṃ ca //
body.translated_text: The <s>vādādhiṣṭhāna</s> (basis of debate) is that upon which debate is conducted — namely, the proposition and its proof.

body.text: tatra svabhāvaḥ sādhya ātmasvabhāvo dharmasvabhāvaśca nāstīti vāstīti vā //
body.translated_text: Among these, the intrinsic nature as proposition — whether the intrinsic nature of the self or the intrinsic nature of <s>dharmas</s> exists or does not exist.

body.text: viśeṣaḥ sādhya ātmaviśeṣo dharmaviśeṣaśca sarvagato na sarvagato nityānityo rūpyarūpītyevamādibhiḥ prakāraiḥ //
body.translated_text: The distinction as proposition — the distinction of the self or the distinction of <s>dharmas</s> — in such modes as: pervading all or not pervading all, permanent or impermanent, having form or formless, and so forth.

body.text: pratijñā sādhyasya svarucitārthasya parasaṃprāpaṇavijñāpanā / sādhyagrahaṇaṃ yadi na kriyeta siddhasyāpi svapakṣasya pareṣāṃ deśanā pratijñā prasajyeta / svarucitārthagrahaṇaṃ na kriyeta parapakṣasyāpi sādhyasya vacanaṃ pratijñā prasajyeta / paragrahaṇaṃ na kriyeta ekākino 'pi tadvacanaṃ pratijñā prasajyeta / saṃprāpaṇagrahaṇaṃ na kriyeta kāyenāpi tadarthābhinayanaṃ pratijñā prasajyeta / vijñāpanāgrahaṇaṃ na kriyetāvijñāte 'pi tadarthe śrotṛbhiḥ pratijñā prasajyeta / yathokte tu vyavasthāne sarva ete doṣā na bhavanti, tasmādevamasyā vyavasthānaṃ veditavyam /
body.translated_text: The <s>pratijñā</s> (thesis) is the communication and notification to others of the meaning one holds regarding the proposition. If the qualification 'proposition' were not included, even the teaching of an already established position to others would absurdly become a thesis. If the qualification 'meaning one holds' were not included, even the statement of the opponent's proposition would absurdly become a thesis. If the qualification 'to others' —

body.text: hetustasminneva sādhye 'pratītasyārthasya saṃpratyayanimittaṃ pratyakṣopalaṃbhānupalaṃbhasamākhyānama / saṃpratyayanimittārtha iha hetvartha iti darśayati / tathāhi pratyakṣānupalaṃbhādupalaṃbhādvetyanena samākhyānena tasmin sādhye 'pratītasyārthasya saṃpratyaya utpadyate / tena tatsamākhyātaṃ tannimittatvāddheturityucyate / pratyakṣopalaṃbhānupalaṃbhau punaḥ svabhāvaṃ liṅgaṃ cādhikṛtya veditavyau //
body.translated_text: The <s>hetu</s> (reason) is the statement that is the ground for generating conviction regarding the unaccepted meaning in that very proposition — being the announcement of the perception or non-perception through direct experience. That the meaning of <s>hetu</s> here is the ground for generating conviction is what is shown. For through the statement 'because of the direct non-perception or perception' regarding the unaccepted meaning in that proposition —

body.text: dṛṣṭānto dṛṣṭenāntenādṛṣṭasyāntasya samīkaraṇasamākhyānam, pratītena bhāgenāpratītasya bhāgasya pratyāyanāya samākhyānamityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: The <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example) is the statement that equalizes the unseen side through the seen side — meaning, the statement for the purpose of demonstrating the unaccepted aspect through the accepted aspect.

body.text: upanayaḥ śiṣṭatajjātīyataddharmopagamāya nayatvasamākhyānam / yathā sādhyo 'rthastribhiravayavaiḥ sādhitastathā śiṣṭānāmapi tajjātīyānāṃ sādhyānāṃ sādhitārthadharmopagamāya nayatvena samākhyānaṃ yuktyātideśa upanayaḥ //
body.translated_text: The <s>upanaya</s> (application) is the statement of applicability for the purpose of accepting the property of the proved in what remains and is of the same type. Just as the proposition has been proved through the three members, so for the remaining propositions of the same type, the statement applying the property of the proved meaning as applicable is the application through extension of reasoning.

body.text: nigamanaṃ niṣṭhāgamanasamākhyānam / yasmādevaṃ yuktyā sūpapannaṃ tasmāditthamevedamityetannigamanaṃ veditavyam //
body.translated_text: The <s>nigamana</s> (conclusion) is the statement of arriving at the final determination. 'Since it is well established through this reasoning, therefore it is exactly so' — this should be understood as the conclusion.

body.text: eṣāṃ pratijñādīnāmidamudāharaṇamātraṃ pradarśyate // tadyathā
body.translated_text: Here, merely an illustration of the thesis and the rest is shown. Namely:

body.text: nairātmyavādinastadrūpe 'dhikaraṇe saprativādike nāstyātmeti vacanaṃ pratijñā //
body.translated_text: For one who advocates <s>nairātmya</s> (selflessness), in such a forum with an opponent, the statement 'there is no self' is the <s>pratijñā</s> (thesis).

body.text: skandhavijñaptau caturvidhadoṣopalaṃbhāditi hetuḥ / sa hyātmā prajñapyamānaḥ skandhalakṣaṇo vā prajñapyeta, skandheṣu vā, anyatra vā skandhebhyaḥ, askandhako vā / tadyadi skandhalakṣaṇastenāsvatantrāḥ skandhāḥ pratītyasamutpannā udagavyayadharmāṇastallakṣaṇa ātmānopapadyata iti doṣaḥ / atha skandheṣu tenānityaskandhāśrita ātmānityaḥ prāpnotīti doṣaḥ / athānyatra skandhebhyastena nirdehaka ātmā niṣprayojana iti doṣaḥ / athāskandhakastena prakṛtyaiva muktasya kevalino mokṣārthaprayatnavaiyarthyamiti doṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Because four defects are observed in the designation within the <s>skandhas</s>' — this is the <s>hetu</s> (reason). For that self, when being designated, would be designated either as having the character of the <s>skandhas</s>, or as within the <s>skandhas</s>, or as apart from the <s>skandhas</s>, or as having no <s>skandhas</s>. If it has the character of the <s>skandhas</s>, then since the <s>skandhas</s> are not independent, being dependently originated and subject to arising and cessation, that —

body.text: vartamāne 'tītaprajñaptivaditi dṛṣṭāntaḥ / taddhayatītaṃ vidyamānalakṣaṇatvena prajñapyamānaṃ vartamānalakṣaṇaṃ vā prajñapyeta, vartamāne vā anyatra vā vartamānāt vartamānanirapekṣaṃ vā / tadyadi vartamānalakṣaṇaṃ tena vartamānamutpannāniruddhatallakṣaṇamatītamutpannā niruddhātmakamiti doṣaḥ / atha vartamāne tenāniruddhe niruddhātmakasya saṃbandho na yujyata iti doṣaḥ / athānyatra vartamānāttena vartamānaṃ hitvā na kiṃcittadvastūpalabhyate yatra tatprajñapyata iti doṣaḥ / atha vartamānanirapekṣaṃ tenāsaṃskṛtamapyatītaṃ prāpnotīti doṣaḥ / taccātītaṃ bhraṣṭalakṣaṇatvāllakṣaṇato nāstīti siddham / ato 'nena vartamānaprajñaptau caturdoṣeṇa siddhenāsiddha ātmā nāstīti skandhaprajñaptau caturvidhadoṣopalaṃbhāt prasādhyate nāstīti //
body.translated_text: 'Like the designation of the past in the present' — this is the <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example). For the past, when being designated as having the character of the existent, would be designated either as having the character of the present, or as within the present, or as apart from the present, or as independent of the present. If it has the character of the present, then the present, being arisen and not ceased, has that character —

body.text: evamātmaviparyāsaṃ pratiṣidhyaitayaiva yuktyā nityādayo 'pi na santītyatideśa upanayaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus, having refuted the distortion of self, by this very reasoning 'permanence and the rest also do not exist' — the extension is the <s>upanaya</s> (application).

body.text: yasmādetadevaṃ tasmādanityāḥ pañca skandhāḥ yāvadanātmāna iti nigamanamiti //
body.translated_text: 'Since it is thus, therefore the five <s>skandhas</s> are impermanent, and so forth up to without self' — this is the <s>nigamana</s> (conclusion).

body.text: pratyakṣaṃ svasatprakāśābhrānto 'rthaḥ / tatra svo 'rthastadyathā cakṣuṣo rūpam / sadgrahaṇaṃ ghaṭādidravyāṇāṃ loke pratyakṣasaṃmatānāṃ pratyakṣatvavyudāsārtha prajñaptimātratvāt / prakāśagrahaṇamāvṛtatvādibhiranupalabdhikāraṇairanābhāsagataviṣayavyudāsārtham / abhrāntagrahaṇamalātacakramāyāmarīcikādivyudāsārthamiti //
body.translated_text: <s>Pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception) is the object that manifests its own existence, without error. Among these, 'its own' means, for example, form for the eye. The qualification 'existent' is for the purpose of excluding things such as pots and the like that are conventionally considered directly perceived, because they are merely designations. The qualification 'manifesting' is for the purpose of excluding objects that do not appear due to being covered and other reasons for non-perception —

body.text: anumānaṃ pratyakṣaśiṣṭasaṃpratyayaḥ / pratyakṣādyadanyacchiṣṭamapratyakṣaṃ niyamena tatsahavarti prasiddhaṃ draṣṭuḥ pūrvaṃ tasya tatpratyakṣamīkṣamāṇasya tadanyasmin śiṣṭasaṃpratyaya utpadyate tenāpyatra bhavitavyametat sahavartineti tatpratyakṣapūrvakamanumānam / tadyathā dhūmaṃ paśyato 'gnāviti //
body.translated_text: <s>Anumāna</s> (inference) is the conviction regarding the remainder based on direct perception. What is other than direct perception — the remainder that is not directly perceived — is necessarily seen to coexist with something well-known. For one who has previously observed that direct perception, when looking at the other, conviction arises regarding the remainder — 'this too must be here because it coexists with that' — this, preceded by direct perception —

body.text: āptāgamastadubhayāviruddhopadeśaḥ / yatropadeśe tatpratyakṣamanumānaṃ ca sarvathā na virudhyete na vyabhicarataḥ sa āptāgamaḥ saṃpratyayitvāt //
body.translated_text: <s>Āptāgama</s> (authoritative scripture) is instruction that does not contradict both of those. When in a teaching, direct perception and inference are in no way contradicted and do not deviate, that is authoritative scripture, because it generates conviction.

body.text: vādālaṃkāro yena yukto vādī vādaṃ kurvāṇo 'tyarthaṃ śobhate / sa punaḥ svaparasamayajñatādiḥ / tatra svaparasamayajñatā svasiddhāntaṃ parasiddhāntaṃ cārabhya granthataścārthataśca paurvāparyeṇa nirantaraṃ vyutpattiparipākaḥ / vākkaraṇasaṃpat śabdavādino vakṣyamāṇakathādoṣaviparyayeṇānākulādivāditā / vaiśāradyamanekodāhārābhiniviṣṭavidvajjanasamāvarte 'pi bruvato nirāsthatā gatavyathatā / sthairyaṃ prativādino vacanāvasānamāgamayyātvaramāṇabhāṣitā / dākṣiṇyaṃ prakṛtibhadratā prāśnikaprativādicittānuvartitā //
body.translated_text: <s>Vādālaṃkāra</s> (ornament of debate) is that which adorns a debater so that one shines exceedingly when conducting a debate. It consists of knowledge of one's own and others' doctrines, and the rest. Among these, knowledge of one's own and others' doctrines is the maturation of thorough learning, continuously and in due order, regarding one's own established position and the other's established position, both in terms of text and meaning. The excellence of vocal expression —

body.text: vādanigraho yena vādī nigṛhīta ityucyate / sa punaḥ kathātyāgādibhiḥ / tatra kathātyāgo 'sādhu mama sādhu tavetyevamādibhiḥ prakāraiḥ svaparavādadoṣaguṇābhyupagamaḥ / kathāsādo 'nyenānyapratisaraṇādibhiḥ vikṣepa ityarthaḥ / yathoktaṃ sūtre - āyuṣmāṃścundikastīrthikaiḥ saha vādaṃ kurvannavajānitvā pratijānāti pratijānitvāvajānātīti / kathādoṣa ākulā divacanam / tatra ākulaṃ yadadhikāramutsṛjya vicitrakathāpratānanam / saṃrabdhaṃ yatkopoddhavaṃ dravoddhavam / agamakaṃ yaddharmato 'rthataśca parṣadvādibhyāmagṛhītam / amitaṃ yadadhikaṃ punaruktārthaṃ jñātārthaṃ ca / anarthamanarthayuktam, tatpañcākāraṃ draṣṭavyam / nirarthakam, apārthakam, yuktibhinnam, sādhyasamam, jāticchalopasaṃhitam, arthānupalabdhito 'saṃbaddhārthato 'naikānti[ka]taḥ sādhanasyāpi sādhyato 'yoniśo 'sabhyasarvavādānugamataśca / akālayuktavacanaṃ yatpūrvakaṃ vaktavyaṃpaścādabhihitam, paścādvaktavyaṃ pūrvamabhihitam /
body.translated_text: <s>Vādanigraha</s> (defeat in debate) is that by which a debater is said to be defeated. It is through abandonment of the thesis and so forth. In this regard, <s>kathātyāga</s> (abandonment of the thesis) is the acceptance of faults in one's own position and merits in the opponent's position through such modes as 'mine is wrong, yours is right.' <s>Kathāsāda</s> (disruption of the discourse) means distraction through diverting to something else, and so forth. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The venerable <s>Cundika</s>, while debating with the <s>tīrthikas</s>, acknowledges without having been defeated, and having acknowledged, then rejects.' <s>Kathādoṣa</s> (fault in speech) is confused speech. Of these, 'confused' (<s>ākula</s>) is when one abandons the topic at hand and extends into various irrelevant narratives. 'Agitated' (<s>saṃrabdha</s>) is what arises from anger or panic. 'Unconvincing' (<s>agamaka</s>) is what is not accepted by the assembly and others either in terms of doctrine or meaning. 'Unmeasured' (<s>amita</s>) is what is excessive, repetitive in meaning, or states what is already known. 'Meaningless' (<s>anartha</s>) is what is joined with purposelessness; this should be seen as fivefold: devoid of meaning, contrary to meaning, contrary to logic, equivalent to what is to be proved, and associated with sophistry and quibbling — due to non-apprehension of meaning, incoherent meaning, non-conclusiveness, the proof itself requiring proof, being illogical, and following all arguments of those unworthy. 'Untimely speech' (<s>akālayuktavacana</s>) is when what should be said first is said afterward, and what should be said afterward is said first.

body.text: asthiraṃ yatpratijñāyāvajñātamavajñāya pratijñātamatitvaramāṇayā vācā hi tūrṇaparāmṛṣṭaḥ / [a]pradīptavacanaṃ yacchandalakṣaṇasamatikrāntamapratyanubhāṣyottaravihittam, saṃskṛtenārabhya prākṛtenāvasitam, prākṛtenārabhya saṃskṛtena paryavasitaṃ ca / aprabaddhaṃ yadantarādhiṣṭhitavicchinnaṃ vākpratibhānamiti //
body.translated_text: 'Unsteady' (<s>asthira</s>) is when what was acknowledged in the thesis is then rejected, or what was rejected is then acknowledged, through hurried speech that grasps too quickly. 'Unclear speech' (<s>apradīptavacana</s>) is that which transgresses the characteristics of meter, which provides a response without repeating the opponent's statement, which begins in Sanskrit and concludes in Prakrit, or begins in Prakrit and concludes in Sanskrit. 'Disconnected' (<s>aprabaddha</s>) is when the flow of speech is interrupted and broken off midway.

body.text: vādaniḥsaraṇaṃ yena vādānniḥsarati, akaraṇena vā guṇadoṣau vicārya vādasya nigrahasthānānāsādanāt, karaṇena vā nirvahanāditi / tatra prativādinyabhājanatākuśalātsthānādvyutthāpya kuśale sthāne pratiṣṭhāpayitumaśakyatā / parṣado vaiguṇyamasabhyābhiniviṣṭapakṣapātitādinā / ātmano 'kauśalyaṃ vāde yāvadvādālaṅkāre 'vyutpattiḥ viparyayātprativādibhājanatādīni veditavyāni //
body.translated_text: <s>Vādaniḥsaraṇa</s> (escape from debate) is that by which one extricates oneself from debate — either by not engaging, having considered the merits and faults and thereby not reaching the grounds of defeat, or by engaging and carrying through to completion. In this regard, the incapacity of the opponent means being unable to dislodge them from an unskillful position and establish them in a skillful position. The deficiency of the assembly is due to the assembly being partial, attached to biased views, and so forth. One's own lack of skill extends to inexperience in debate ornamentation. The opposite — the opponent's capacity and so forth — should be understood accordingly.

body.text: vāde bahukarā dharmā ye vāde 'vaśyamupayujyante / tadyathā svaparasamayajñatā vāde bahukaro dharmo yena sarvatra kathāvastuni vādaṃ karoti / śeṣaṃ sugamam //
body.translated_text: The qualities that are greatly helpful in debate are those that are necessarily employed in debate. For example, knowledge of one's own and others' doctrinal systems is a quality greatly helpful in debate, by which one debates on every subject of discussion. The rest is easy to understand.

body.text: kuśalapakṣaprayuktenetyuktvā pratipattisārakeṇeti vacanamāśayaviśuddhijñāpanārthaṃ na lābhasatkārādinimittaṃ śrutādikuśalapakṣe prayuktenetyarthaḥ / sattvasaṃgrāhakeṇeti śrāvakādiviśeṣaṇārthaṃ parahitapratipattipradhānenetyarthaḥ / evaṃ ca svahitaparahitapratipannaḥ kṣipramanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyata ityayameṣāṃ padānāmanusaṃdhirveditavyaḥ / avigṛhyāpi tāvadvāde kriyamāṇe prakṛtigambhīratvānmahāyānadharmasya durlabhājñā prāgeva vigṛhya / yaiśca saha vigṛhya vādaḥ kriyate te 'pi pratipattāro nājñābhiprāyāḥ pratibruvanti kiṃtarhyupālambhābhiprāyāḥ / yeṣvapi prāśnikeṣu sa vādaḥ kriyate te vāsabhyā avyutpannā vā bhavantyabhiniviṣṭā vā / sarvo 'pi ca vādā prāyeṇa ṣaḍbhirdoṣairyukto bhavati / tathāhi vādaṃ kurvāṇaḥ kadācidatirabhasenāsatpakṣamapi parigṛhyābhiniveśena chalajātinigrahasthānānyapi prayukte / vacanaparyavasānamanigamayyāpyakālena vaktumārabhate / samyagapyuktāṃ prativādinaḥ kathāmapapātayati paṃsayatītyarthaḥ / paruṣamapi bruvate, yena prativādyādayaḥ cittaṃ pradūṣayanti / svayaṃ ca teṣu cittaṃ pradūṣayatītyebhiḥ ṣaḍbhirdoṣairyukto bhavati //
body.translated_text: Having said 'one engaged in the wholesome side,' the statement 'one whose essence is practice' is for the purpose of indicating purity of intention — meaning one engaged in the wholesome side of learning and so forth, not for the purpose of gain, honor, and the like. 'One who gathers beings' is a qualifier distinguishing from <s>Śrāvakas</s> and others, meaning one whose primary concern is practice for the benefit of others. Thus, one who practices for one's own benefit and the benefit of others quickly fully awakens to unsurpassed perfect enlightenment — this should be understood as the connection of these terms. Even without dispute, when debate is being conducted, understanding of <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>dharma</s> is difficult to obtain due to its naturally profound nature, how much more so when disputing. Moreover, those with whom one debates while disputing — they too do not respond with the intention of understanding, but rather with the intention of finding fault. And the examiners before whom that debate is conducted are either unworthy, uneducated, or biased. Furthermore, all debate is generally accompanied by six faults. For when debating, one sometimes, through excessive zeal, grasps even a false position, and out of attachment employs sophistry, quibbling, and points of defeat. Without bringing the speech to a conclusion, one begins to speak at an inappropriate time. One overthrows and disparages even the opponent's correctly stated thesis. One speaks harshly, whereby the opponents and others corrupt their minds. And one oneself corrupts one's mind toward them — thus debate is accompanied by these six faults.

body.text: upaśāntasya ca durlabho vādaḥ / sati cānupaśame durlabhaṃ paracittānurakṣaṇaṃ svacittānurakṣaṇaṃ ca yena pare prasādaṃ labheran vimuktyāyatanayogena svacittaṃ samādhīyate / prāyeṇa vāde kathamahaṃ jayeyaṃ pare parājīyerannityevaṃ cittaṃ samudācarati / sati ca tasmin paridāhaduḥkhasaṃkleśaḥ / tasminsatyasparśavihāraḥ / tato nirantarakuśalapakṣaprayogāsāmarthyāttato viśeṣādhigamaṃ pratyaprāptiparihāṇiriti //
body.translated_text: For one who is peaceful, debate is difficult to obtain. And in the absence of peace, it is difficult to guard others' minds and one's own mind — whereby others would gain faith, and one's own mind would be composed through application to the basis of liberation. Generally in debate, the thought arises: 'How shall I win, and how shall others be defeated?' And given that, there is the affliction of the suffering of inner torment. Given that, there is non-abiding in tranquil experience. From that, due to the inability to continuously engage in wholesome practice, there is failure to attain and deterioration with respect to higher attainment.

body.text: mātaraṃ pitaraṃ hatvā ityasyāṃ gāthāyāṃ loke yadatyarthamavadyaṃ pātakaṃ tadabhidhāyīnyakṣarāṇyetāni viśuddhau pariṇāmitāni / kiṃ ca loke 'tyarthamavadyaṃ saṃmatam / gurujanaghāto mahājanaghātaśca / sa punargurujano dvividhaḥ pratiniyato loka[sādhāraṇaśca] / lokasādhāraṇo 'pi punardvividhaḥ - paripālako dakṣiṇīyaśca / tatra pratiniyato gurujano mātā pitā ca, pālako rājā, dakṣiṇīyaḥ śrotriyabrāhmaṇāḥ, teṣāṃ śuddhatarasamatatvāt / tadeṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ ghāto gurujanaghāta ityucyate / mahājanaghāto rāṣṭrasya sānucarasya ghātaḥ / anucarāḥ punaḥ gavāśvamahiṣoṣṭrādayo veditavyāḥ //
body.translated_text: In the verse 'Having killed mother and father,' the syllables that in the world designate what is extremely blameworthy and sinful are here transformed to the meaning of purity. What then is considered extremely blameworthy in the world? The killing of elders and the killing of great persons. The elders are of two kinds: specific and common to the world. Those common to the world are also of two kinds: protectors and worthy of offerings. Among these, the specific elders are mother and father; the protector is the king; those worthy of offerings are learned <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, on account of their purer equality. The killing of all these is called elder-killing. The killing of great persons is the killing of a kingdom together with its retinue. The retinue should be understood as cattle, horses, buffalo, camels, and so forth.

body.text: kathaṃ punaretānyakṣarāṇi viśuddhau pariṇāmyante / mātrādighātavacanasya tṛṣṇādiprahāṇapariṇāmanādyathākramaṃ tṛṣṇām, karmabhavam, sopādānaṃ vijñānam, dṛṣṭiśīlavrataparāmarśadvayam, ṣaḍāyatanaṃ ca sagocaramadhikṛtya mātrādayo draṣṭavyāḥ, tatsādharmyāt / tatra tṛṣṇā nirvṛttihetuḥ / karmabhava utpattihetuḥ / sa ca bhāvanābījāghānayogena pitṛbhūto draṣṭavyaḥ / ābhyāṃ hetubhyāṃ sopādānaṃ vijñānaṃ pravartate / tasyaivaṃ pravartamānasya satyapi mokṣābhilāṣe mokṣaprāptivighnakarāvanupāyāgraśuddhipratyāyakau parāmarśau / śrotriyasādharmyamanayoretadeva veditavyaṃ yadutāgraśuddhayabhiniveśaḥ / tasyaiva punarvijñānasyāśrayālaṃbanabhāvena ṣaḍāyatanaṃ sagocaraṃ veditavyamiti //
body.translated_text: How then are these syllables transformed to the meaning of purity? Through the transformation of the words denoting killing of mother and so forth into the abandonment of craving and so forth. In sequence: mother, father, the consciousness with its basis, the two kinds of clinging to views and to rules and rituals, and the six <s>āyatanas</s> together with their objects should be seen as corresponding to mother and so forth, due to their similarity. In this regard, <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) is the cause of complacent rebirth. <s>Karmabhava</s> (karmic becoming) is the cause of arising. And this should be seen as the 'father' through the analogy of destroying the seed of future existence through cultivation. Through these two causes, consciousness with its basis operates. For that consciousness thus operating, even though there is a desire for liberation, the two kinds of clinging — to views and to rules and rituals — are obstacles to attaining liberation, producing belief in wrong methods and false purity. The similarity of these two to 'learned brāhmaṇas' should be understood as precisely this: the attachment to false purity. And the six <s>āyatanas</s> together with their objects should be understood as the support and object of that very consciousness.

body.text: aśrāddhaścākṛtajñaścetyasyāṃ gāthāyāṃ hīnārthābhidhāyīnyakṣarāṇyuttamārthe paridīpitāni / hīno loke caturvidhaḥ - manaskarmahīnaḥ kāyakarmahīno vākkarmahīna upabhogahīnaśca / manaskarmahīnaḥ punardvividhaḥ kuśalapravṛttivailomyena cāśrāddhaḥ, paralokādyasaṃpratyayena dānādiṣvaprayogāt / akuśalapravṛttyānukūlyena cākṛtajñaḥ, yatropakārānapekṣitvena mātṛvadhādiduścarite nirmaryādatvāt / kāyakarmahīnaścauraḥ saṃdhicchedakaḥ atyarthaṃ garhitajīvitatvāt / vākkarmahīno mṛṣāvādādipradhānaḥ, tadrūpasya sabhādiṣu praveśābhāvāt / upabhogahī naḥ śvā kā kaḥ preto vetyevamādikaḥ, charditabhakṣaṇāditi //
body.translated_text: In the verse 'Faithless and ungrateful,' syllables designating what is lowly are illuminated in the supreme meaning. A lowly person in the world is of four kinds: one lowly in mental action, one lowly in bodily action, one lowly in verbal action, and one lowly in enjoyment. One lowly in mental action is of two kinds: 'faithless' (<s>aśrāddha</s>), through opposition to wholesome mental engagement, due to non-application to giving and so forth through disbelief in the next world and the like; and 'ungrateful' (<s>akṛtajña</s>), through conformity with unwholesome mental engagement, because through disregard for kindness received, one has no boundaries in committing evil deeds such as matricide. One lowly in bodily action is a thief, a burglar, because of having an extremely despicable livelihood. One lowly in verbal action is one predominantly given to false speech and the like, because such a person is not admitted into assemblies and so forth. One lowly in enjoyment is like a dog, a crow, a hungry ghost, and so forth, because of eating what has been vomited.

body.text: kathaṃ punaretānyakṣarāṇyuttamārthe pariṇāmyante / aśrāddhādivacanānāmarhati pariṇāmanāt / tatrāśrāddho vimuktijñānadarśanayogena svapratyayatvāt / akṛtajño 'saṃskṛtanirmāṇajñānāt / saṃdhicchettā punarbhavapratisaṃdhihetukleśaprahāṇāt / hatāvakāśa āyatyāṃ sarvagatiṣu duḥkhānabhinirvartanāt / vāntāśo dṛṣṭe dharme upakaraṇabalena kāyaṃ saṃdhā rayato 'pi bhogajīvitāśābhāvāditi //
body.translated_text: How then are these syllables transformed to the supreme meaning? Through the transformation of the words 'faithless' and so forth into the meaning of an <s>Arhat</s>. In this regard, 'faithless' — through the application of knowledge and vision of liberation, because of being self-assured. 'Ungrateful' — through knowledge of the unconditioned and knowledge of transformation. 'Burglar' — through the abandonment of the afflictions that are the cause of connection to future existence. 'One whose opportunity is destroyed' — through not producing suffering in any future destiny. 'One who has vomited his food' — because in this present life, even while sustaining the body through material requisites, there is no desire for enjoyment or life.

body.text: yathā coktam - asāre sāramataya iti / asyā gāthāyāḥ pūrvavadarthanirdeśo draṣṭavyaḥ / śarīraṃ punarasyāḥ samādhiṃ niśritya bodhisattvā darśanabhāvanāmārgābhyāṃ mahābodhiṃ spṛśantīti //
body.translated_text: As it is also said: 'Those who see essence in the essenceless.' The meaning of this verse should be indicated as before. The body of this verse is that <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, relying on <s>samādhi</s>, touch great awakening through the paths of seeing and cultivation.

body.text: mātsaryadharmatāmanuvṛṃhayatīti savāsanamātsaryānuśayaprahāṇena tattathatāśrayaparivṛttisākṣātkaraṇāt / dānena ca parikhidyate, dīrghakālaṃ dānanimittaṃ paramaduṣkaraśramābhyupagamāt / yācanakaṃ ca dveṣṭi, svayaṃ grāhābhirucitatayā yācanakaprātikūlyāt / na kiṃcit kadāciddadāti, sarvasya vastunaḥ sarvadā dānāt / dūre ca bhavati dānasya, āsādyadānādiparivarjanāt //
body.translated_text: 'One who nourishes the nature of stinginess' — through the abandonment of the latent tendency of stinginess together with its imprint, and the direct realization of the transformation of the basis through that <s>tathatā</s> (suchness). 'And one who is wearied by giving' — because for a long time one undertakes the supreme hardship of difficult practice for the sake of giving. 'And one who hates supplicants' — because of one's own preference for grasping, there is aversion toward supplicants. 'One who never gives anything' — because of giving all things at all times. 'And one who is far from giving' — because of the abandonment of approachable giving and the like.

body.text: tatra parameṇa brahmacaryeṇa samanvāgata iti lokottareṇa mārgeṇetyarthaḥ / nānyatra maithunānmaithunasya niḥsaraṇaṃ paryeṣata iti tasyaiva yathābhūta parijñānena tatprahāṇāt / yathābhūtaparijñānaṃ punarasya tathatāpratibedhādveditavyam / maithunaprahāṇenopekṣako bhavati, abrahmacaryaprahāṇopekṣaṇāt / utpannaṃ ca maithunarāgamadhivāsayati, kāmarāgasyādhyātmamutpannasya bahiḥpravāsanāt / maithunapratipakṣeṇa ca dharmeṇottrasyati tatpratipakṣeṇa mārgeṇa sarvasattvottaraṇāya vyavasyatīti kṛtvā / abhīkṣṇaṃ ca dvayadvayaṃ samāpadyate saṃkleśavyavada nadvayena phalahetubhedena catuḥsatyātmakena [śamathavipaśyanādvayena] punaḥpunarlaukikalokottaramārgadvayaṃ samāpadyata iti kṛtvā //
body.translated_text: In this regard, 'endowed with the supreme holy life' means endowed with the supramundane path. 'One does not seek escape from sexual intercourse through anything other than sexual intercourse' means the abandonment of that through its direct knowledge as it truly is. The direct knowledge as it truly is should be understood as the penetration of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness). 'Through the abandonment of sexual intercourse, one becomes equanimous' means through the equanimous abandonment of unchaste conduct. 'One endures arisen sexual desire' means the outward expulsion of sensual desire that has arisen internally. 'One is frightened by the <s>dharma</s> that is the antidote to sexual intercourse' — considering that through that antidote path, one resolves to deliver all beings. 'And one repeatedly attains the pair' — one repeatedly attains the pair of the mundane and supramundane paths, through the twofold [method] of defilement and purification, by the division of result and cause that constitutes the four truths, and through the pair of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight).

body.text: kimupādāyedaṃ śāstramabhidharmasamuccaya iti nāma labhate / niruktinyāyena / sametyoccayatāmupādāya tattvamabhisametyādhigamya bodhisattvaṃḥ saṃkalanādityarthaḥ / samantāduccayatāmupādāyābhidharmasūtrataḥ sarvacintāsthānasaṃgrahādityarthaḥ / samyaguccayatvāyāyatanatāṃ copādāyetyaviparītenopāyena yāvadbuddhatvaprāpaṇādityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: On what basis does this treatise obtain the name <s>Abhidharmasamuccaya</s>? By the method of <s>nirukti</s> (etymology). On the basis of 'collecting after having met' — meaning, having directly realized the truth, the collection of <s>Bodhisattva</s> [teachings]. On the basis of 'collecting from all sides' — meaning, from the <s>Abhidharma</s> <s>sūtras</s>, the comprehensive gathering of all topics of reflection. And on the basis of 'collecting correctly, leading to the sphere of' — meaning, through the unerring method, leading up to the attainment of Buddhahood.

body.text: ityabhidharmasamuccaye bhāṣyataḥ sāṃkathyaviniścayo nāma pañcamaḥ samuccayaḥ samāptaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus concludes the fifth <s>samuccaya</s> called <s>Sāṃkathyaviniścaya</s> (Determination of Discussion) from the commentary on the <s>Abhidharmasamuccaya</s>.

body.text: likhāpitamidaṃ paṇḍitavaidyaśrī amaracandreṇa jagadbuddhatvasaṃpada iti //
body.translated_text: This was caused to be written by the learned physician <s>Śrī Amaracandra</s>, for the attainment of Buddhahood of all beings.
